cards.note: Masculine. Nouns ending in -age are almost always masculine: le voyage, le fromage. Exceptions: la page, la plage, l'image (f).
The final -e makes these look feminine, but every noun in -isme is masculine. Cynisme and fascisme follow the same rule as the more obvious organisme and mécanisme.
Every -eau noun here is masculine. Oiseau is the one that hides its gender in speech because you say l'oiseau, and all six form their plural with -x, not -s.
All six -age nouns are masculine. The trap comes later: a small group with the same ending is feminine, such as la page, la plage and l'image, so the rule is reliable but not absolute.
Nouns in -ment are masculine, including appartement and vêtement where the final t is silent. Événement is the one to spell carefully: it carries two accents before the ending.
All six -ance nouns are feminine. La vacance in the singular means a vacancy; for a holiday you always say les vacances in the plural.
The -ette ending is a diminutive and is always feminine, so all six take la. Two of them are mostly heard in the plural in real use: les lunettes for glasses and les toilettes for the bathroom.

These abstract nouns in -té are all feminine even though they end in a stressed vowel with no -e after it, which is what makes learners guess le. Note liberté and société keep the same ending despite the different vowels before it.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine, so all six take la. Watch attention: you normally meet it as l'attention, where the elision hides the gender, but it is still la.
Masculine despite the final -e. Nouns of Greek origin ending in -ème are masculine: le système, le thème.
Nouns ending in -ence and -ance are feminine. The indefinite article is used here because l'expérience hides the gender. Exception: le silence.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine: la liberté, la santé, la société. The exceptions are le côté and l'été (m).
An important exception: nouns ending in -eau are normally masculine, but l'eau is feminine. So une eau minérale and l'eau est froide.

cards.de: The government has announced a reform.
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ment are masculine: le gouvernement, le bâtiment, le changement. The ending is a reliable clue, so use it.
Mouvement is masculine, because nouns ending in -ment always are.

cards.fr: Le nature est magnifique en automne.
cards.answer: La nature est magnifique en automne.
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ure are feminine: la nature, la voiture, la culture. Le mur is not an exception, as it has no -ure.

accept: Cette décision a été une erreur.
cards.note: Like -tion, the ending -sion is feminine: la décision, la télévision, la discussion. Hence cette décision, not ce décision.

cards.de: I found a nice picture on the internet.
cards.fr: J'ai trouvé ___ belle image sur Internet.
cards.note: Image is one of the few exceptions to the rule that -age nouns are masculine. Also feminine: la page, la plage and la cage.

cards.de: On Saturday we are going to the beach.
cards.answer: Samedi, nous allons à la plage.
accept: Samedi, on va à la plage.
Samedi nous allons à la plage.
cards.note: Plage is feminine even though it ends in -age. That is why it is à la plage and not au plage.
Nouns ending in -eau are masculine: le château, le bureau, le gâteau. The article and the adjective have to follow: ce château ancien. The one important exception is l'eau.
Most French nouns ending in er are masculine (le dîner, le loyer), but la mer is feminine. Do not confuse it with le maire (the mayor), which sounds the same.
cards.hint: ends in er but is not masculine

cards.note: Le lait is masculine, like le fait and le portrait. Learn it with its article: un verre de lait.
Nouns ending in ent are usually masculine (le moment, le vent), but la dent is feminine: j'ai mal à une dent.
cards.hint: one of the feminine ent nouns

cards.note: Le pont is masculine, like le front and le mont. Also learn faire le pont, meaning to take the day off between a holiday and the weekend.
Nouns ending in aise are feminine: la chaise, la falaise, la fraise. Say une chaise, not un chaise.
La planète is feminine. Common phrase: sauver la planète.
Le don is masculine: avoir un don pour la musique means to have a gift for music. Le don also means a donation, so un don de sang is a blood donation.
cards.hint: nouns in on are often masculine

cards.note: Le rat is masculine and the final t is silent, so it sounds like ra. The feminine form la rate exists but also means the spleen.
Le pardon is masculine. Note the construction demander pardon à quelqu'un, to ask someone for forgiveness, with no preposition before pardon.
cards.hint: nouns in on are often masculine

cards.note: Nouns ending in isse are feminine: la cuisse, la saucisse. Une cuisse de poulet is a chicken leg.
Nouns ending in ine are feminine: la colline, la cuisine, la machine. En haut de la colline means at the top of the hill.
Le dessus is masculine, like le dessous. Le dessus de la table est tout rayé. (The top of the table is all scratched.) Avoir le dessus means to have the upper hand.
La lune is feminine, like la dune and la fortune. Un clair de lune is moonlight.

cards.de: The butter is in the fridge.
cards.note: Nouns ending in eur are often feminine (la couleur, la peur), but le beurre is masculine. Learn it together with le lait and le fromage.
La clé is feminine, so the possessive is ma, not mon. The spelling la clef is older but sounds exactly the same.
French uses one masculine singular noun, un escalier, where English says stairs in the plural. Before a vowel sound ce becomes cet.

cards.de: My trip to Spain was wonderful.
cards.fr: Ma voyage en Espagne était merveilleuse.
cards.answer: Mon voyage en Espagne était merveilleux.
cards.note: Nouns ending in age are masculine (le voyage, le fromage, le message), with a few exceptions like la plage. The possessive and the adjective must both be masculine.

cards.de: I do not share your opinion.
cards.fr: Je ne partage pas ta avis.
cards.answer: Je ne partage pas ton avis.
cards.note: Un avis is masculine, and before a vowel you always use mon, ton, son, even with feminine nouns. À mon avis means in my opinion.
Feminine. Careful: le page means a page, meaning a young servant at court.
Le livre is a book. La livre is a pound, both the weight and the British currency.
Only the feminine means fashion: à la mode. Masculine le mode means way, method or mode, as in le mode d'emploi (instructions for use).

cards.de: I'm popping to the post office.
cards.note: La poste is the post or the post office. Le poste is a job, a position or a device such as a TV set.

cards.de: I didn't like the end of the film.
cards.answer: La fin du film ne m'a pas plu.
cards.note: La fin is feminine, so it takes la. Note too that French says the film's end did not please me, so the thing you liked becomes the subject of plaire.

cards.de: Our house is old, but very beautiful.
cards.answer: Notre maison est vieille, mais très belle.
cards.note: Maison is feminine, so the adjectives must become vieille and belle. English adjectives never change, so this agreement is easy to forget.
Oreille is feminine: une oreille, les oreilles. Say avoir mal aux oreilles for to have earache.
A final -e tempts learners to guess feminine, but uniforme is masculine, like problème and groupe.
Nouns ending in -ance and -ence are feminine. Very common in the plural: dans ces circonstances.
La cave is feminine and means cellar, not a cave in the ground, which is une grotte. Une cave à vin is a wine cellar.
Nouns ending in -ette are feminine. Une assiette creuse is a soup plate.
Nouns ending in -age are almost always masculine: le paysage, le village, le fromage.
Le banc is masculine. Do not mix it up with la banque, which is a bank for money.
La botte is feminine and usually used in the plural: des bottes de pluie. It also means a bunch, as in une botte de radis.
Nouns ending in -ière are feminine. Une rivière flows into another river, un fleuve flows into the sea.
Despite the final -e, disque is masculine. Un disque dur is a hard drive.
English uses boutique without any article, so remember that French needs la. A bigger shop is un magasin.
Examen is masculine: un examen difficile. Careful: passer un examen means to sit an exam, while to pass it is réussir un examen.
Nouns ending in -ine are feminine. À l'origine means originally, être d'origine anglaise means to be of English origin.
Égard is masculine even though it starts with a vowel, so you write un égard and cet égard. It is common in à l'égard de, meaning towards.
La barbe is feminine. Se raser la barbe means to shave off one's beard, and la barbe! is a casual what a pain.

cards.de: the link (bond between people or things)
cards.note: Le lien is masculine. It is also the word for an internet link: cliquer sur le lien.
Nouns ending in -ment are masculine. It also means a connection when travelling: un changement à Lyon.
Learn the article with the word. Nouns ending in -te are usually feminine: une perte de temps.
Nouns in -ade are feminine. Say faire une promenade, not making a walk word for word.
Nouns in -ière are feminine. Note faire carrière (to have a career) drops the article, and the same word also means quarry.
Nouns in -esse are feminine. Tenir sa promesse means to keep one's promise.
Abstract nouns in -eur are feminine (la peur, la douleur, la sueur), unlike job words in -eur which are masculine. Idiom: avoir des sueurs froides.
Masculine, with the -é ending of many masculine nouns (le café, le marché). Keep it apart from la pêche, the peach or fishing.
A silent -e does not mean feminine. Le groupe, le voyage and le fromage are all masculine.
Feminine, like other abstract nouns in -eur. Common phrase: des objets de valeur.
Every noun in -ance or -ence is feminine. In history, la Résistance refers to the wartime movement.
Masculine, like most nouns ending in a pronounced or silent consonant. As an adjective, désert means deserted, empty.
A consonant ending usually means masculine, but la clé (also spelled la clef) is feminine. Une clé USB is a memory stick.
cards.hint: ends in a silent consonant, still feminine

cards.de: the pass (throwing the ball to a teammate)
cards.note: Feminine: la passe, une passe décisive au football. Keep it apart from le passé, the past, and from le passage.
Feminine, even though the ending -x looks masculine. Say: sa voix est douce.
All nouns in -té are feminine (la liberté, la santé). Les curiosités de la ville also means the sights.
Masculine: on dit minuit pile, exactly midnight. Usually appears bare, as in à minuit, without any article.
Nothing in the ending helps here, so memorise the article: la main droite, se laver les mains.
Feminine despite the consonant ending. In avoir soif (to be thirsty) it takes no article: j'ai très soif.
Feminine. Faire une chute means to have a fall, and une chute d'eau is a waterfall.
Nouns in -ence are feminine. En apparence means seemingly: les apparences sont trompeuses.
Masculine, like most nouns in a silent consonant. It belongs to raconter: faire le récit de quelque chose.
Masculine, like almost all nouns ending in -at (le résultat, le climat). Un chocolat chaud is a hot chocolate.

cards.de: the end (of a film, of the day)
cards.note: Feminine even though it ends in a consonant sound, which learners often read as masculine. Adjectives agree: une fin heureuse.
cards.hint: short word ending in -in, but feminine

cards.note: Masculine although it ends in -e, and it is a collective word with no plural in this sense. Étendre le linge means to hang out the washing.
Feminine. The same word means a leak: une fuite d'eau, and prendre la fuite means to flee.
Masculine despite the final -e, which usually suggests feminine. Tomber dans le piège means to fall into the trap.
Feminine: la jupe. Related is le jupon (petticoat), and the phrase "une jupe plissée" means a pleated skirt.
Masculine, like nearly all nouns ending in -ier. It also means a class or workshop: un atelier d'écriture.
Masculine, like most nouns ending in -on. It covers both the heel of your foot and a shoe heel: des talons hauts.
Masculine, and so is its opposite le plancher (the floor). Figuratively, un prix plafond is a maximum price.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Un chiffre is a single figure, un nombre is a number as a quantity; le chiffre d'affaires means turnover.
Masculine: le mille, un mille nautique, parcourir trois milles. The number mille, a thousand, never takes an s.
Most nouns in -age are masculine (le fromage, le voyage), but la cage, la page, la plage and une image are feminine. In football la cage is also the goal.
Masculine, like most shortened words ending in -o (le vélo, le resto). Prendre le métro, une station de métro.
Feminine, like every noun ending in -sion or -tion. Faire pression sur quelqu'un means to put pressure on someone, and une pression is also a draught beer.
Feminine: la nuque. Distinct from le cou, the whole neck; la nuque is only the back of it.
Masculine, like most nouns in -et. Careful: un cabinet is an office or practice, not a kitchen cabinet, which is un placard.
Feminine. The plural les moustaches covers an animal's whiskers, as in les moustaches du chat.
Feminine, like nearly all nouns ending in -ure (la voiture, la nature). La ceinture de sécurité is the seat belt.
Feminine, like other nouns in -inte or -einte (la plainte, la teinte). Les empreintes digitales are fingerprints.
Feminine and normally used in the plural, even though rubbish is uncountable in English: sortir les ordures. Applied to a person, une ordure means a swine.
cards.hint: Feminine, and French keeps it plural

cards.note: Masculine, like l'espoir and le devoir. En désespoir de cause means as a last resort.
Nouns in -eau are masculine (le bureau, le château) and add x in the plural: les drapeaux. The famous exception is l'eau, which is feminine.
cards.hint: Ends in -eau; plural takes an x

cards.note: Masculine: le flingue, very informal for a firearm. The verb flinguer means to shoot someone down.
Masculine, even though the ending -e looks feminine. Say: j'ai un doute.
Masculine, like l'ordre from which it is built. Very common in ta chambre est en désordre.
Nouns in -ée are feminine (la journée, l'idée, la soirée). The main exceptions are le musée and le lycée.
Nouns in -euil are masculine, like le fauteuil and l'écureuil. Also figurative: le seuil de pauvreté, the poverty line.
Feminine: une grande armoire. Careful, not every -oire noun is feminine: le laboratoire and le territoire are masculine.
Nouns in -ente are feminine, like la détente and la vente. Être sur une mauvaise pente means to be going downhill in life.
Masculine: le pré, like le blé, le degré, le marché. Les vaches sont dans le pré. Nearby but feminine: la prairie.

cards.de: the language (way of speaking, e.g. legal jargon)
cards.note: Masculine, like le fromage and le voyage. Use la langue for a specific tongue (le français) and le langage for how people speak: le langage familier.
Nouns in -et are masculine, like le billet and le jouet. Un coup de pistolet is a gunshot.
Masculine: le sourcil, with a silent final l. Keep it apart from le cil, the eyelash; froncer les sourcils means to frown.
Le canard stays masculine; the female bird is une cane. Informally, un canard also means a newspaper.
Nouns in -ent are masculine, like le moment and l'accident. A queue of people is la queue, never le serpent.
Feminine: une bague en or. A wedding ring is une alliance, not une bague de mariage.
Learn it as le tiroir. Nouns in -oir are reliably masculine: le couloir, le miroir, le comptoir.
Masculine: le zéro. Used in "repartir de zéro", to start again from scratch.
Feminine, like other nouns in -ête (la fête, la quête, la conquête). Une tempête dans un verre d'eau is a fuss about nothing.
Feminine, like other nouns in -ouille (la grenouille, la citrouille). Very crude register; also heard in casse-couilles for someone deeply annoying.

cards.de: the counter (in a cafe or shop)
cards.note: Masculine like other -oir nouns. Un café au comptoir, drunk standing at the bar, costs less than at a table.
Many -ice nouns are feminine (la justice, la police), but un exercice is masculine. Say faire des exercices difficiles.
Nouns in -eau are masculine apart from l'eau and la peau. Plural is les carreaux, and the word also means windowpane.
Nouns in -ée are normally feminine: la vallée, la journée, la soirée. Compare the masculine le val kept in place names like Val de Loire.
All nouns in -ment are masculine: un enterrement, un appartement, un moment. The word contains terre, earth.
Nouns in -ier are masculine. Le courrier is the mail you receive, while the postal service itself is la Poste.
Masculine: le rein. In the plural, les reins often means the lower back, as in avoir mal aux reins.
Nouns in -ume are feminine: la brume, la plume, la coutume. Thick fog is the masculine le brouillard.
Short nouns ending in -i are masculine: le pli, le cri, le tapis. Prendre le pli means to get into the habit.

cards.de: the morning (the whole stretch of it)
cards.note: Feminine like other -ée nouns. Use la matinée for the duration (toute la matinée) and le matin for the point in the day (ce matin).
Nouns in -ente are feminine: la vente, la pente, la détente. Common phrases are en vente and mettre en vente.
Feminine, and spelt with double l and double p, unlike English envelope. Say une enveloppe timbrée.
Nouns in -ade are feminine: la salade, la promenade, la limonade. Colloquially raconter des salades means to talk nonsense.
Feminine, and it has nothing to do with English can or cane sugar only. Une canne à pêche is a fishing rod.
Nouns in -ique are feminine: la brique, la musique, la boutique. Say un mur en brique.
Learn it with the article: la poubelle. Nouns ending in -elle are feminine. Say jeter quelque chose à la poubelle to mean throw something in the bin.
Nouns in -erie are reliably feminine: la plaisanterie, la boulangerie. Useful phrases: faire une plaisanterie, and sans plaisanter for joking aside.
Do not assume abstract nouns are feminine: le mépris is masculine. The verb is mépriser quelqu'un.
cards.hint: Masculine, with a silent s at the end.

cards.note: Every noun ending in -tion is feminine in French. Note the article in avoir bonne reputation, where French drops it: avoir bonne / mauvaise réputation.
Nouns in -ment are masculine: le traitement, le gouvernement. Also used for software: traitement de texte means word processing.
Nouns in -té are feminine, like la liberté and la beauté. The adjective takes de: être fier de quelque chose.
Nouns in -sme are masculine: un enthousiasme, le tourisme, le rythme. Common phrase: avec enthousiasme.
Feminine like all -tion nouns. Say faire une proposition à quelqu'un. In grammar it also means clause: proposition subordonnée.
Feminine: la grève. French drops the article in faire grève, and uses être en grève for to be on strike.
Feminine like every -tion noun. La protection de l'environnement means environmental protection.
Abstract nouns in -eur are feminine (la terreur, la peur, la douleur), while nouns for people in -eur are masculine (le vendeur).
Masculine, and countable unlike English information: demander un renseignement à quelqu'un. In the plural, les renseignements can mean the intelligence service.
Slang and feminine: être en taule. It sounds exactly like la tôle, which means sheet metal.
Feminine like all -tion nouns, and often countable in French: avoir de grandes ambitions.
Feminine and rather formal, used for an imposing house. The fixed phrase à demeure means permanently.
The final e does not make it feminine: le foie. Keep it apart from la foi (faith) and une fois (once), which sound the same.
cards.hint: Masculine, even though it ends in -e.

cards.note: Masculine and singular, unlike the English form crossroads with its s. Figuratively it means a meeting point or turning point.
Feminine: la pâte. In the plural les pâtes means pasta, and without the accent la patte is an animal's paw.
Masculine, like most nouns built from a verb: le mélange, le change, le partage. The verb is mélanger.
Abstract nouns in -sion and -tion are feminine. A common phrase is prendre possession de quelque chose.

cards.de: the flea (also a chip in a card or phone)
cards.note: Feminine: la puce. "Ma puce" is a common term of endearment, and "une carte à puce" is a chip card.
Nouns in -ée are usually feminine: la tranchée, la journée, l'idée. La guerre des tranchées means trench warfare.
Masculine, like most nouns in -ier. It also means a dog's collar, so un collier de chien.
Masculine. Do not mix it with the verb bouger, to move, or with la bougie, the candle.
Masculine, as are most nouns borrowed with a final -a (le cinéma, le opéra). For the building you say aller à l'opéra.

cards.de: the support (something to lean on, backing)
cards.note: Masculine: un appui. Useful phrases are prendre appui sur quelque chose and des preuves à l'appui, meaning with supporting evidence.
Nouns in -ance and -ence are feminine: une ambulance, la patience. Call one with appeler une ambulance.

cards.de: the exit (way out, also the outcome)
cards.note: Feminine, and it does not mean an issue in the English sense of a problem. You see it on signs as une issue de secours, an emergency exit.
Masculine: le pari, from the verb parier. Say je te parie que tu vas gagner.
Masculine, even though la feuille inside it is feminine. In politics it also means a minister's brief.
Feminine: une tentative de vol, an attempted theft. A laboratory experiment is une expérience, not une tentative.

cards.de: the mourning (grief for someone who died)
cards.note: Masculine: être en deuil means to be in mourning, and faire son deuil de quelque chose means to let something go.
Nouns in -ment are masculine. Le règlement intérieur is the house rules, and le règlement d'une facture is payment of a bill.
Masculine: le futur. For the future in general French more often says l'avenir, which is also masculine.
Masculine, like most nouns in -on. Usually plural: respirer à pleins poumons, to breathe deeply.
Masculine despite the final -e: un tube de dentifrice. Informally un tube is also a hit song.
Feminine: la flèche. It also means the spire of a church, and partir comme une flèche means to shoot off.
Many learners assume a word ending in -e is feminine, but le liquide is masculine. Payer en liquide means to pay cash.
cards.hint: Final -e here does not mean feminine.

cards.note: Masculine despite the -e ending. Do not confuse it with le magasin, which means shop, not magazine.
Feminine, like une science and une patience. Avoir de l'influence sur quelqu'un means to have influence over someone.
cards.hint: Words in -ence are almost always feminine.

cards.note: The -tion ending is a reliable feminine signal, so say la construction, la question, la solution. It also works grammatically: la construction d'une phrase.
Feminine. The matching verb is trahir quelqu'un, to betray someone.
cards.hint: Nouns in -aison are feminine, like la saison.

cards.de: the crew (of a ship or plane)
cards.note: Masculine because of the -age ending. Keep it apart from une équipe, which is a team.
Masculine. It is the opposite of une entreprise in ads, and as an adjective particulier means particular or private.
Masculine, with an x in the plural: des troupeaux. Un troupeau de moutons is a flock of sheep.
Masculine, ending in -us like le virus and le bus. Un éclat d'obus is a piece of shrapnel.
Masculine, and the h blocks elision, so it stays le hall and never l'hall. It means a lobby, not a hall for concerts, which is une salle.
cards.hint: An English loanword with h aspiré.

cards.note: Most nouns in -ence are feminine, but le silence is masculine. Garder le silence means to keep quiet.
cards.hint: An -ence word that is not feminine.

cards.note: Masculine, and the s is silent, so singular and plural sound identical. The verb is refuser de faire quelque chose.
The -age ending usually signals masculine, but une image, la page, la plage and la cage are feminine exceptions.

cards.de: the episode (of a series or story)
cards.note: Masculine: un épisode, like un problème and un programme. Note "le dernier épisode".
Feminine. Avoir coutume de faire quelque chose means to be in the habit of doing something.
Masculine. The spelling is odd: oi is pronounced like o here, so it sounds like o-gnon.
Masculine. Informally, quel chantier! means what a mess.
Feminine, like la jeunesse and la vitesse. In the plural, les richesses means treasures or natural resources.
Masculine because le tour is masculine; note that la tour with a feminine article means tower. It is mostly used in faire demi-tour, to turn back.
cards.hint: Built on le tour, which is masculine.

cards.note: Lean on the ending: le tablier, le cahier, le quartier. The word comes from table, a cloth held in front of the body.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -ier are almost always masculine.

cards.note: Le matelas is masculine and the final s is silent. Singular and plural look identical: un matelas, deux matelas.
Say le travail, but des travaux for building works. The gender has to be learned by heart.
cards.hint: Nouns in -ail are masculine and form the plural in -aux.

cards.note: La descente is feminine, like its opposite la montée. Une descente de police means a police raid.
Le savon is masculine, and un savon means a single bar of soap. Passer un savon à quelqu'un means to tell someone off.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -on are usually masculine.

cards.note: Une cheville is feminine. Note also se fouler la cheville, to sprain your ankle, where French uses la where English says your.
Le pigeon is masculine whatever the bird's sex. Colloquially un pigeon is a sucker, someone who has been tricked.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -on are usually masculine.

cards.note: The -tion ending is one of the safest rules in French: la réception, la question, la solution. It also means the front desk of a hotel: demandez à la réception.
cards.hint: Every noun ending in -tion is feminine.

cards.note: Masculine: le crépuscule, as with le véhicule and le spectacle. Its counterpart at the other end of the day is l'aube, feminine.
Le sapin is masculine, like le jardin and le matin. Le sapin de Noël is the Christmas tree.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -in are usually masculine.

cards.note: Masculine, as nearly all nouns in -age are: le voyage, le message. Rendre hommage à quelqu'un is the standard phrase.
La chaleur, la douleur and la peur are feminine, while people in -eur such as un acteur are masculine. Remember j'ai chaud for I am hot, never je suis chaud.
cards.hint: Abstract nouns ending in -eur are feminine.

cards.note: Feminine: une ardeur. Nouns in -eur naming a quality are feminine: la chaleur, la douceur, la peur. Travailler avec ardeur is to work with real drive.
Un blouson en cuir is a leather jacket. Une veste is the smarter kind of jacket, and it is feminine.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -on are usually masculine.

cards.note: La fontaine is feminine, like la semaine and la plaine. An office water cooler is une fontaine à eau.
You say un otage about a man or a woman. The set phrase is prendre quelqu'un en otage.
cards.hint: Nouns in -age are masculine, and this one stays masculine for a woman too.

cards.note: Le milliard is masculine: deux milliards d'euros. English billion is un milliard, while un billion in French means a thousand billion.
cards.hint: Masculine, and it needs de before the noun that follows.

cards.note: La banlieue is feminine and usually singular where English uses the plural suburbs: habiter en banlieue.
La révolte is feminine. The matching verb is se révolter contre quelqu'un or quelque chose, to rebel against.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -te like this one are feminine.

cards.note: Masculine: le pin. Don't confuse it with le pain (bread), which sounds the same; "une pomme de pin" is a pine cone.
Feminine: la mâchoire. Nouns in -oire are often feminine, like la victoire and la baignoire. Serrer la mâchoire means to clench your jaw.
Feminine: une étoffe, as in une étoffe de soie. Figurative phrase: avoir l'étoffe d'un chef, to have what it takes to lead.
Masculine, from calculer. Le calcul mental is mental arithmetic, and un calcul rénal is a kidney stone.
Feminine, like practically every abstract noun ending in -té: la beauté, la liberté, la société.

cards.de: the crest (of a bird or of a ridge)
cards.note: Feminine: la crête, with a circumflex. Used for a cockerel's comb and for the crest of a wave or a mountain ridge.
Feminine, from the verb réussir à faire quelque chose. Careful: the near synonym le succès is masculine.
Masculine: dans un délai de trois jours. It does not mean a delay in the English sense; a train's delay is un retard.
Feminine, like almost all nouns ending in -ure: la voiture, la nature, la culture.
Masculine, like every noun ending in -ment: le gouvernement, le moment, le bâtiment. Un établissement scolaire is a school.
Feminine even with no -e at the end. Do not confuse it with le tribut (the tribute), which sounds the same.
Masculine: relever un défi means to take up a challenge. The verb is défier quelqu'un.
Masculine, like le four and le jour. The player is un tambour too, or un batteur in a band.
Feminine, like every noun ending in -tion. Say une intervention chirurgicale; the verb is intervenir.

cards.de: the saddle (for a horse or bike)
cards.note: Feminine: la selle, like la dentelle, la vaisselle, la poubelle. Se mettre en selle means to get in the saddle.
Feminine: écrire dans la marge. La marge de manœuvre means room for manoeuvre.

cards.de: a puff (of smoke), a wave (of heat)
cards.note: Feminine, like nearly all nouns in -ée: une journée, une année, une idée. Une bouffée d'air frais, une bouffée de chaleur.
Masculine, although most nouns in -eur are feminine (la peur, la couleur, la douleur). Le cœur and le bonheur go the other way.
Feminine, and it means a row between people, not a formal dispute. The verb is se disputer avec quelqu'un.

cards.de: the terminal (post or marker, e.g. a charging point)
cards.note: Feminine: la borne, used for "une borne de recharge" (charging point) and "dépasser les bornes", to go too far.

cards.de: the fur (animal coat or fur garment)
cards.note: Feminine: la fourrure, like la voiture, la nature, la ceinture. Un manteau de fourrure is a fur coat.
It is the diminutive of le camion (lorry), yet the -ette ending makes it feminine: une petite camionnette blanche.
Masculine: le chêne. Like most trees (le pin, le hêtre, le peuplier) it is masculine; note the circumflex, and do not mix it up with la chaîne (chain).
A final -e does not mean feminine: un timbre à deux euros. The word also means the timbre of a voice.
Abstract nouns are not automatically feminine in French: le soutien, from soutenir. The word le soutien-gorge means bra.
Nouns in -eau are usually masculine (le bureau, le couteau); la peau and l'eau are the exceptions to remember.
Learn la casserole. A big pot without a handle is une marmite.
Not the season (le printemps) and not a water spring (la source). Also used in en dernier ressort, meaning ultimately.
A flash of light in the sky is un éclair, but the strike is la foudre. Remember coup de foudre, love at first sight.
La vigne is the plant; the wine growing area is le vignoble, which is masculine.
Masculine, like le service and le précipice. Faire un caprice is said of a child throwing a fit over something it suddenly wants.
Feminine, even though le programme and le problème are masculine. Donner l'alarme means to raise the alarm.
cards.hint: -me can go either way; here feminine

cards.note: Learn le refuge; chercher refuge chez un ami. In the mountains it means a hut.
Un bonnet de bain is a swimming cap. Watch the contrast with une casquette, a cap with a peak.

cards.de: the bust (upper body, or the sculpture of it)
cards.note: Masculine, like le geste. Keep it apart from la liste and la piste, which are feminine.
Le fouet also means whip, the older sense of the word. Say battre les œufs au fouet.
Un moulin à vent is a windmill and un moulin à café a coffee grinder.

cards.de: the tablet (pill; also a seal or stamp)
cards.note: Masculine: le cachet, like most nouns in -et (le paquet, le billet). Un cachet d'aspirine is a tablet, and avoir du cachet means to have real character.
French turns the verb aller into a masculine noun. Un aller simple is a one way ticket, un aller-retour a return ticket.
cards.hint: Infinitives used as nouns are masculine.

cards.note: Learn it with the article: donner l'alerte, une alerte à la bombe. As an adjective alerte means lively or spry.
Say le débat, un débat, like le résultat and le climat. Common phrases: un débat sur la santé, ouvrir le débat.
The -ment ending is a reliable sign of a masculine noun, like le changement and le gouvernement. Useful phrase: pousser un soupir de soulagement.
cards.hint: Every noun ending in -ment is masculine.

cards.de: the victim (a man or a woman)
cards.note: La victime stays feminine even when the person is male: la victime est un homme de trente ans. The same happens with une personne.
cards.hint: Always feminine, whoever it refers to.

cards.note: Feminine: la gorgée, from la gorge (throat). Nouns in -ée like la journée and la bouchée are feminine.
Learn it as le loisir, like le plaisir and le désir. In the plural, les loisirs means hobbies or leisure activities.

cards.de: the stem (of a plant, thin rod)
cards.note: Feminine: la tige, like la page, la plage, la cage. La tige d'une fleur holds up the flower.
Feminine: la miette, like other nouns in -ette (l'assiette, la serviette). En miettes means in pieces.
Every noun in -tion or -sion is feminine: la profession, la question, la décision. Exercer une profession means to practise a profession.
Feminine: la querelle, like other nouns in -elle (la poubelle, la ficelle). Chercher querelle à quelqu'un means to pick a fight with someone.
Masculine like le travail and le détail. The final consonant is not pronounced as in English rail; it sounds like raï.
Feminine, like other drinks borrowed from elsewhere: la tequila, la sangria, la bière. Une vodka orange is how you order it mixed.
English traffic is uncountable, but French says la circulation est dense. La circulation sanguine means blood circulation.
Feminine like la différence and la patience, though le silence is an exception. The diaeresis on the i keeps oi from sounding like wa.
Masculine like le bateau and le manteau, plural rouleaux. Un rouleau à pâtisserie is a rolling pin.
Nouns already ending in -s do not add another one: un parcours, des parcours. Un parcours professionnel is a career path.
cards.hint: Masculine, and the plural looks the same.

cards.note: Feminine like la boulangerie and la vie. It also means a bell ringing: la sonnerie a retenti.
Feminine: la jungle. Common in the phrase la loi de la jungle, the law of the jungle.
Le moral is your state of mind (avoir le moral = to be in good spirits), while la morale is the moral of a story or morality. English morale and moral map onto two different French words.
cards.hint: masculine here, and the feminine form means something else

cards.note: Feminine: garder rancune a quelqu'un means to hold a grudge against someone, and sans rancune! means no hard feelings.

cards.de: the journey, the trip from A to B
cards.note: Le trajet is the route or commute you cover (le trajet domicile-travail), while le voyage is a longer trip. Both are masculine.
Feminine: tondre la pelouse means to mow the lawn. Park signs read pelouse interdite, keep off the grass.
Compounds keep the gender of the main noun, and le sol is masculine. In a shop you go au sous-sol, down to the basement level.
Le titre is masculine, so le sous-titre is too. Usually plural: un film en version originale avec sous-titres.
An exception: le legume and le bitume are masculine, but amertume is feminine. It covers both a bitter taste and bitter feelings.
cards.hint: feminine, even though -ume words are usually masculine

cards.note: Abstract nouns in -te are feminine (la liberte, la societe). After la majorite des gens the verb can be singular or plural.
Nouns in -illon are masculine. Used for free samples and in statistics: un echantillon representatif.

cards.de: the old outer district, the faubourg
cards.note: Masculine and rather old fashioned, kept in Paris street names such as le faubourg Saint-Antoine. For modern suburbs say la banlieue.
Nouns in -ant are masculine (le restaurant, le moment). It also means a bend in a road: un tournant dangereux.

cards.de: the pâté (the meat paste, in a terrine)
cards.note: Masculine. Keep three words apart: le pâté is the meat paste, la pâte is dough or pastry, and les pâtes are pasta. Il a acheté du pâté de campagne. (He bought some country pâté.)
Masculine: payer le loyer. The rental flat itself is la location, and to rent is louer.
All nouns in -tion are feminine. The opposite is la benediction, the blessing.
Feminine in French. The idiom perdre sa salive means to waste your breath talking.
Masculine: le frein a main is the handbrake, and the verb is freiner. Figuratively, mettre un frein a quelque chose is to put a brake on something.
Feminine, and it means a big chest, not a suitcase (la valise). The trunk of a car is le coffre.
cards.hint: feminine, double l plus silent e

cards.note: Learn the article with the word: le maquillage. The related verb is se maquiller, to put on makeup.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -age are almost all masculine.

cards.note: Masculine: le rempart. Often plural, les remparts de la ville, the walls ringing an old town.
Masculine: le cil, les cils. Do not confuse it with le sourcil, the eyebrow.
Le syndicat is a labour union. Watch out: un syndicat d'initiative is a tourist information office.
Le bronze, like le fer, le cuivre, l'or. Une médaille de bronze, a bronze medal.

cards.de: the association, the club (non profit group)
cards.note: Une association sportive. The same reliable rule gives la question, la solution, la nation.
cards.hint: Every noun ending in -tion is feminine.

cards.note: Masculine, like le ticket and le paquet. Un coup de sifflet is a blast of the whistle; the verb is siffler.
The plural adds an x: les pinceaux. The two famous exceptions to the -eau rule are l'eau and la peau, both feminine.
Feminine: l'estime. Common in "avoir de l'estime pour quelqu'un" and "l'estime de soi", self-esteem.
Une fourmi, des fourmis. Idiom: avoir des fourmis dans les jambes, to have pins and needles.
cards.hint: Feminine even though it does not end in -e.

cards.note: La conquête comes from conquérir. Same pattern: la fête, la tempête, la quête.
Masculine, and the h is aspirate: le haricot, les haricots with no liaison. Green beans are des haricots verts.

cards.de: the intention (aim, purpose one has in mind)
cards.note: Masculine: le dessein. Don't confuse it with le dessin, a drawing. Common in à dessein, meaning on purpose.
Faire une objection à quelque chose. In conversation you can simply say Objection!
Faire une remise de 10 %. It comes from remettre and can also mean a handover or a shed.
Feminine: faire une farce à quelqu'un, to play a trick on someone. La farce is also stuffing in cooking.
Une corbeille à papier is a wastepaper basket, while le panier is more a shopping or carrying basket.
On the plate you mostly hear les petits pois. À pois means spotted: une robe à pois, a polka dot dress.
cards.hint: Masculine, and it already has an s in the singular.

cards.note: Avoir recours à quelque chose means to resort to something; en dernier recours means as a last resort.
cards.hint: Masculine, with an s even in the singular.

cards.note: Le citron, un jus de citron, une tarte au citron. Careful: nouns in -tion and -son (la maison) are feminine.
cards.hint: Nouns ending in -on are usually masculine.

cards.de: the tax (money paid to the state)
cards.note: Masculine: un impôt, l'impôt sur le revenu, payer des impôts.
Feminine: la baleine. The shark is masculine, le requin, so the two animals take different articles.
Nouns ending in -esse are feminine: l'ivresse, la vitesse, la politesse. Official wording: conduite en état d'ivresse.
Feminine, but before a vowel you hear only l'éponge, so the gender is hidden. Passer l'éponge means to let something go.
cards.hint: feminine, though you only hear l'

cards.note: Masculine: un site web, un site internet. Most tech nouns follow: un mail, un réseau, un ordinateur.
Masculine: le péril, a formal word. Set phrase: "à vos risques et périls".

cards.de: the cam (mechanical part driving a movement)
cards.note: Feminine: la came, as in un arbre à cames, a camshaft. In slang it also means drugs, from camelote.
Nouns in -age are usually masculine, but la plage, la page, la cage and la nage are feminine.
Masculine: un gilet de sauvetage is a life jacket, and les gilets jaunes were the yellow vest protesters.
Masculine: sous le règne de Louis XIV. The verb is régner.
Masculine: le crabe. Marcher en crabe means to walk sideways.
Masculine and the final d is silent. The frog, la grenouille, is feminine, so do not copy the article across.

cards.de: the embankment (sloping bank of earth beside a road or field)
cards.note: Masculine: le talus, with the final s silent and unchanged in the plural, like le jus and le refus. La voiture a fini dans le talus.

cards.de: the porch (covered entrance of a building)
cards.note: Masculine, despite looking close to la porte, which is the door itself. S'abriter sous le porche means to shelter in the entrance.

cards.de: the flat, the apartment (colloquial short form)
cards.note: Colloquial clipping of appartement, so it stays masculine. You also see it written appart'.

cards.de: the notion, the idea of something
cards.note: Every noun in -tion is feminine: la notion, la question, la nation. In the plural, avoir des notions d'espagnol means to have a basic grasp.
Masculine: au ralenti means in slow motion, or ticking over at low speed.
Feminine even though it starts with é and you usually hear l'épave. Also used of a person: c'est une épave.
cards.hint: feminine, though you only hear l'

cards.note: Nouns in -age are almost always masculine: le virage, le voyage, le fromage. Un virage serré is a sharp bend.
Learn the article with the word. Nouns ending in -ière are reliably feminine, like la lumière and la rivière.
The word is feminine whatever the animal's sex, so a male frog is still la grenouille. Nouns in -ouille are feminine.
Learn the article with the word. Nouns ending in -ente are feminine: la fente d'une tirelire is the slot of a piggy bank.
Nouns ending in -on are usually masculine, as in le balcon and le plafond. Say attendre sur le perron, to wait on the front steps.
A final -e often signals a feminine noun, but not here: le vote joins le groupe and le problème. The verb is voter pour or contre quelqu'un.
Most nouns in -ge are masculine, like le village and le cierge. An ordinary household candle is la bougie, which is feminine.
Nouns ending in -ée are feminine, like une idée and une journée. A distress flare is une fusée de détresse.
Every noun in -erie is feminine, like la boulangerie and la cavalerie. The horse is le cheval and the rider le cavalier.
Nouns in -elle are feminine, so it is une petite étincelle. Faire des étincelles means to shine or do brilliantly.
Unusually for a noun in -ge, this one is feminine: une berge boueuse. The seashore is le rivage, which is masculine.
Nouns in -ère are feminine, so it is une cuillère propre. The spelling la cuiller is also correct.

cards.de: the sudden shift (of wind or mood)
cards.note: It is feminine even though the related verb sauter looks neutral. You meet it mostly in une saute de vent and une saute d'humeur.
All nouns ending in -ment are masculine, like le gouvernement and un avertissement. The verb is avertir quelqu'un de quelque chose.
Nouns in -ion are feminine, so use une and not un. Common phrase: être victime d'une agression.
You hear l'écharpe and cannot tell the gender, so store it as une écharpe. It also means a sling: avoir le bras en écharpe.
cards.hint: starts with a vowel, so l' hides the gender

cards.note: Nouns in -ence and -ance are feminine, like la patience and la résidence. Résidence principale and résidence secondaire are main and second home.
Nouns in -aison are feminine, like la maison and la saison. En comparaison de quelque chose means in comparison with something.
Le raisin is fresh grapes, used in the singular: une grappe de raisin. An English raisin is un raisin sec.
Masculine, with the plural les poux. The saying laid comme un pou means as ugly as sin.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine in French, with no exceptions worth worrying about at B1. Prendre une résolution means to make a resolution, and it also means screen resolution.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Nouns ending in a double s plus e, like secousse, are feminine. Une secousse sismique is an earth tremor.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Tree names in -ier are masculine: le palmier, le pommier, le cerisier. Un palmier dattier is a date palm.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Nouns in -esse are feminine: la noblesse, la politesse, la vitesse. It also means nobility of character.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Nouns formed from a verb with no ending added, like le retrait from retirer, are masculine. It also means a retreat or pulling back.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: The article l' hides the gender, so learn it as une écume, feminine. Foam on beer or in a bath is la mousse.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article
cards.hint: starts with a vowel, so use une to show the gender

cards.note: Nouns in -ane such as la caravane and la cabane are feminine. The same word also means a camel caravan.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.de: the soft spot (avoir un ... pour qn)
cards.note: An adjective turned into a noun takes le, so avoir un faible pour quelqu'un means to have a soft spot for someone. Weakness as a lack of strength is la faiblesse.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article
cards.hint: an adjective used as a noun

cards.de: the report, the feature (in the press or on TV)
cards.note: Nouns in -age are almost always masculine: le reportage, le voyage, le message. The exceptions to know are la page, la plage and une image.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Nouns in -ée are feminine: la montée, la journée, une idée. The opposite is la descente.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Nouns in -ment are masculine: le développement, le gouvernement, le changement. A common phrase is les pays en voie de développement.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Nouns in -ine are feminine, and here l'épine hides that, so store it as une épine. L'épine dorsale is the spine.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article
cards.hint: ends in -ine, and starts with a vowel

cards.note: Most nouns in -on are masculine, which makes this one a trap: la mousson is feminine, like la maison and la chanson. Say la saison des moussons.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article
cards.hint: ends in -on but is an exception

cards.note: Nouns in -aire for places and things are usually masculine: le vestiaire, le dictionnaire, le commentaire. It covers both a theatre cloakroom and a sports changing room.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: This short noun has no helpful ending, so memorise la trêve. Sans trêve means non stop, and trêve de plaisanteries means enough joking.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article
cards.hint: no ending rule, just learn la

cards.note: Nouns in -aille are feminine: la ferraille, la bataille, la volaille. Bon pour la ferraille means fit for the scrapyard, even though le fer is masculine.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: The -ment ending makes it masculine. Le Débarquement with a capital letter is the Normandy landings of 1944, and the opposite is l'embarquement.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: A final e here signals the feminine: une poutre en bois. In gymnastics la poutre is the balance beam.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Short nouns ending in a consonant sound are usually masculine, so it is le pic. It also means a pickaxe, and tomber à pic means to come at just the right moment.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Nouns in -ard are masculine: le lézard, le renard, le brouillard. Even a female lizard stays le lézard.
cards.task: Translate into French with the article

cards.note: Learn it as la paye. Both spellings paye and paie are correct, as in le jour de paye.
Learn it with the article: le cordon. Common uses are le cordon ombilical and un cordon de police.
The final -e tempts learners to guess feminine, but it is un missile. A space rocket or a firework is la fusee, spelled la fusée.
Say la colle, and note that in school slang une colle also means detention or a trick question.
The -ette ending is reliably feminine, literally a little apple from pomme. Often plural: des pommettes saillantes.
The adjective naturel becomes a masculine noun, le naturel. Avec naturel means in a natural, unforced way.
cards.hint: masculine when used as a noun

cards.note: Say la toux, with a silent x, pronounced like tou. The verb is tousser.
Order un coca, not une coca. Drinks such as le cafe and le the are masculine too.
The -age ending signals masculine, as in le fromage and le voyage. It comes from the verb éclairer, to light up.
The -ée ending is feminine, built on la bouche. Mettre les bouchées doubles means to work twice as hard.

cards.de: the sentry, the guard on duty
cards.note: The word stays feminine whatever the soldier's sex, like la personne and la victime. Être en sentinelle means to stand guard.
cards.hint: always feminine, even for a man

cards.note: The -ment ending is a safe masculine clue. Common phrase: avoir un mauvais pressentiment.
Say la mare for a pond. Do not mix it up with la mer, the sea, or le maire, the mayor, which all sound similar.

cards.de: the strike, the blow (in sport or warfare)
cards.note: It is la frappe, from frapper. Une frappe aérienne is an air strike and une faute de frappe is a typo.
French treats it as one masculine singular item: un jean, deux jeans, never une jean. English plural jeans misleads learners here.
Say la crasse. As an adjective it intensifies, as in une ignorance crasse, utter ignorance.
Learn le mollet for the leg muscle, not to be confused with le veau, the animal. Un œuf mollet is a soft boiled egg.
The -ure ending is feminine, like la voiture and la nature. It also means the closing of something, as in la clôture de la séance.
Masculine thanks to the -ment ending. It sounds literary, so in everyday French use la punition.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine in French: la protestation, la question, la nation. Often used in the plural: malgre les protestations des habitants.
Masculine, like almost all nouns in -et (le ticket, le paquet, le billet). The full phrase is le béret basque.

cards.de: the stop (short break in a journey)
cards.note: Feminine. Common in faire une halte, to stop off for a while; the h is aspirated, so you say la halte, not l'halte.

cards.de: the carcass (animal body or bare frame of a thing)
cards.note: Feminine: une carcasse. Nouns ending in -asse are feminine: la classe, la masse, la paillasse. Used for an animal skeleton and for the frame of a car or building.
Masculine: un nichon, crude slang; the neutral word is le sein. Nouns in -on like le ballon and le poisson are usually masculine.
Nouns in -ance and -ence are feminine: la confiance, la patience, la différence. Say avoir confiance en quelqu'un, with no article.
All nouns in -tion and -sion are feminine. Faire une suggestion means to make a suggestion or proposal.
Feminine. In everyday speech Quelle tuile! means What rotten luck!
Masculine, formed from the past participle of recevoir. Nouns made this way are masculine: un reçu, un résumé. Demandez un reçu!

cards.de: the indication (sign or piece of guidance)
cards.note: Feminine: une indication, like every noun in -tion (la direction, la solution). Suivre les indications means to follow the instructions.
The diminutive ending -ette is always feminine: la mallette, la fourchette, la maisonnette. It comes from la malle, a trunk.
Abstract nouns in -eur are feminine: la saveur, la couleur, la douleur. For the sense of taste or for good taste, use le goût.
The singular la bretelle is feminine. It also means a dress strap and a motorway slip road.

cards.de: the respite (short break from something hard)
cards.note: Masculine. It lives in the phrase sans répit, meaning relentlessly, and the final t stays silent.
Masculine and the s is not pronounced. Prendre le relais means to take over from someone.
Feminine. Passer la douane means to go through customs; the officer is le douanier.
Masculine, like nearly all -age nouns. It covers both the surrounding area and the neighbours taken together.
Feminine because it is short for la photographie; same with la moto and la radio, while le vélo and le stylo are masculine.
cards.hint: short form of a longer word

cards.note: Masculine: un fantasme, like l'enthousiasme and le sarcasme. Note the s: le fantôme is the ghost.
Feminine, like la bouche and la mouche. It also means family stock: être de vieille souche means to come from an old line.
Masculine: le désarroi. Nouns in -oi are masculine too: un emploi, un tournoi, un convoi. Common phrase: être en plein désarroi.
The ending -age signals masculine: le tatouage, le message, le garage. The verb is tatouer, and se faire tatouer means to get a tattoo.

cards.de: the bowl (a pet's food dish, or a mess tin)
cards.note: Feminine: la gamelle, with the -elle ending shared by la poubelle and la vaisselle. Remplir la gamelle du chien is the everyday use.
Nouns in -ot are masculine: un escargot, un chariot, un haricot. On a menu: des escargots de Bourgogne.
Masculine: le devant, the opposite of le derrière. Le devant de la maison est peint en bleu. (The front of the house is painted blue.) Also in prendre les devants, to take the initiative.
Masculine, plural fardeaux, in the family of le bureau, le manteau and le cadeau. Porter un lourd fardeau works for luggage and for worries alike.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine, with no exceptions worth worrying about: la contradiction, la question, la solution. Common phrase: être en contradiction avec quelque chose.
Currency names are masculine: un euro, le dollar, le franc, le yen. The odd one out is la livre sterling, feminine, because la livre is a pound.
La moyenne is the average, while le moyen is a means or a way, so the gender changes the meaning. Very common: en moyenne, on average.
A final -e does not guarantee feminine: l'hymne national is masculine. Only a church hymn can be feminine, une hymne.
Feminine: la valse. Danser une valse, and the verb valser goes with it.
Before a vowel the article hides the gender in l'étable, so learn it as une étable, feminine. A stable for horses is une écurie.
cards.hint: ends in -able, starts with a vowel

cards.note: Nouns in -ite are feminine: la faillite, la limite, la visite. Note that faire faillite, to go bankrupt, takes no article.
Compounds built on a masculine noun stay masculine: le sang-froid, from le sang. Set phrase: garder son sang-froid, to keep one's cool.
Nouns in -eau are masculine, plural in -x: le maquereau, des maquereaux. In slang maquereau also means pimp, so context matters.
Nouns in -aire are usually masculine: un itinéraire, un dictionnaire, un salaire. The main exception is la grammaire.
Nouns ending in -é are masculine (l'été, le café, le thé), but those in -té are feminine (la santé, la beauté). Use en été for in summer.
Nouns in -el are masculine: le rappel, l'appel, le sel. Un rappel de vaccin is a booster shot.
English marks no gender, so you have to store it: nouns ending in -tion are reliably feminine (la potion, la question, la solution).
French uses a masculine singular noun where English uses a plural: un pantalon, not des pantalons, for one pair. The same goes for un jean.
Nouns ending in -ance or -ence are feminine (la croyance, la patience). Religious faith as trust is la foi.
Masculine: le museau. Ends in -eau like le bateau and le chapeau, and the plural takes an x: les museaux.
Une fleur is feminine, but un tree is le fleuve? No: note that le fleuve (river) is masculine and looks similar, so keep la fleur and le fleuve apart.
cards.hint: no ending clue, just learn it

cards.note: La frange is feminine, while the hair itself is masculine plural: les cheveux. Also means the fringe on a scarf.
Words borrowed from English are almost always masculine in French: le film, le week-end, le parking, le sandwich.
Nouns ending in -ment are masculine. Careful: an email attachment is une pièce jointe, not un attachement.
Masculine and often used in the singular: un caleçon propre. Like le savon and le blouson, nouns in -on here are masculine.
The silent -e makes learners guess feminine, but un acide is masculine. As an adjective, acide means sour.

cards.de: the stick (in hockey), also the butt of a rifle
cards.note: Feminine, like la bosse and la brosse. Une crosse de hockey is the curved stick.

cards.de: the mush (soft boiled food, baby cereal)
cards.note: Feminine, formed from bouillir, to boil. The phrase réduire en bouillie means to reduce something to a pulp.
Nouns in -age are nearly always masculine: l'esclavage, le courage, le message.
Most nouns in -on are masculine: le melon, le citron, le poisson. Watermelon is la pastèque.
Write it une leçon with the cedilla. Nouns in -on are usually masculine, but leçon, façon, chanson and maison are feminine.

cards.de: the edge (of the sea, of a road)
cards.note: Le bord is masculine: au bord de la mer means at the seaside. The related la bordure (border strip) is feminine.
Nouns in -ier are masculine: le fichier, le dossier (folder), le cahier.
Masculine: le comté de Nice. Le comté is also a famous cheese; keep it apart from le comte, the nobleman, and la comtesse.
Une balade with one l is a walk; une ballade with two l is a poem or song. The verb is se balader.
Write it une équipe. It is feminine and takes a singular verb: l'équipe a gagné, where English often says the team have won.
A final -e often signals a feminine noun in French, but axe is masculine. Also used for roads: un axe routier is a main traffic route.
Feminine: une argile rouge. A clay pot is un pot en argile.
Nouns ending in -erie are reliably feminine: la boulangerie, la tapisserie. Note that faire tapisserie means to be a wallflower at a party.
This noun exists only in the plural and is masculine, so you never say un alentour. Aux alentours de means near or roughly around.
Masculine and unchanged in the plural: le taux, les taux. Common phrases are le taux de change and le taux d'intérêt.
cards.hint: masculine, already ends in -x in the singular

cards.note: The ending -ée is a good sign of a feminine noun, as in une journée or une idée. Typical use: les vitres sont couvertes de buée.

cards.de: the parapet (low wall on a bridge)
cards.note: The ending -et is dependably masculine: le ticket, le parapet. Typical use: s'accouder au parapet, to lean on the parapet.
Learn it with its article, la gomme. The related verb is gommer un mot, to rub out a word.
cards.hint: feminine, ends in -omme like la pomme

cards.note: Because it starts with a vowel you cannot hear the gender in l'averse, so store it as une averse. Example: être surpris par une averse.
cards.hint: feminine, so une averse not un averse

cards.note: Feminine: une teinte plus claire. It comes from teindre, to dye, and is not the same as le teint, which means complexion.
La pousse (feminine) is a sprout, while le pouce (masculine) is the thumb, and they sound identical. Example: des pousses de bambou.
cards.hint: feminine; its homophone le pouce is masculine

cards.de: the display (goods in a shop window)
cards.note: The ending -age is masculine apart from a few exceptions such as la page, la plage and l'image. Figuratively, faire étalage de qc means to show something off.

cards.de: the isolation (being cut off from others)
cards.note: The ending -ment is always masculine. Do not reach for l'isolation, which in French means the insulation of a building.
Masculine like all -ment nouns. It also covers the act of loading, including loading a file on a computer.
Nouns in -que are usually feminine (la banque, la musique), but le moustique is masculine. A mosquito bite is une piqûre de moustique.

cards.de: the toil (hard, formal word for labour)
cards.note: Many abstract nouns in -eur are feminine (la peur, la douleur), but le labeur is masculine. It sounds literary, so in everyday French say le travail.
cards.hint: masculine, unlike la peur or la couleur

cards.note: Masculine with the irregular plural les totaux. Au total means in total or all in all.
The ending -aie is feminine, as in la plaie or la monnaie. The same word also means stripe and the fish called a ray.
Masculine: un bilan positif. The set phrase faire le bilan de qc means to take stock of something.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine, so it is une obstination. The matching verb is s'obstiner à faire qc, to persist in doing something.

cards.de: the squadron (military unit of cavalry or vehicles)
cards.note: Masculine: un escadron, like un bataillon, un avion, un camion. Un escadron de gendarmerie is a familiar phrase in the news.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. In a cafe, une consommation is a drink you order.
Masculine: l'enlèvement d'un enfant. Nouns in -ment such as le changement and le paiement are masculine; the verb is enlever.
Masculine, and countable in French: il m'a donné un conseil. English advice has no plural, but French says des conseils.
Feminine: une poussée, from pousser. Nouns in -ée are feminine: une montée, une arrivée, une percée. Used for une poussée de fièvre, a spike of fever.
Nouns in -sion are feminine. Watch the spelling too: French occasion has one c, unlike English occasion.
Feminine, like la botte and la carotte. Une crotte de chien on the pavement is the everyday use, and une crotte en chocolat is a sweet.

cards.de: the slate (roofing stone or writing tablet)
cards.note: Feminine: une ardoise grise. Also used for a running tab in a café: avoir une ardoise chez le boulanger.

cards.de: the andouille (tripe sausage; also a fool)
cards.note: Feminine, sharing the -ouille ending with la grenouille. Calling someone espèce d'andouille means you idiot, said fairly gently.
Nouns in -ment are masculine. Note the two accents: un événement important.
Nouns in -age are masculine: un voyage, un garage, un message. The few exceptions are la plage, la page, la cage, l'image.
Nouns in -sion are feminine. French says prendre une décision, not faire une décision.
Feminine: une exclamation, in the big family of -tion nouns. Un point d'exclamation is the punctuation mark.

cards.de: the shuttle (vehicle running back and forth)
cards.note: Feminine, like almost all nouns in -ette (la baguette, la recette). Used for la navette spatiale and for a bus doing a short return route.
Masculine, like the tree names le pommier and le cerisier. Un panier en osier is the phrase you meet most often.
La mort is feminine even though it ends in a consonant. The adjective mort, morte is separate: il est mort.
Masculine, so you say un environnement agréable. The elided l' hides the gender, and the word also means a person's surroundings.
cards.hint: the article is hidden by elision

cards.note: Masculine: un bouillon de légumes. From bouillir, to boil; compare la soupe, which is feminine.

cards.de: the fraction (in maths, or a small part)
cards.note: Feminine: une fraction de seconde. Every noun in -tion is feminine, like la nation and la question.
Masculine: se faire un massage. Nouns in -age like le voyage and le fromage are masculine, with rare exceptions such as la plage.
Feminine: la rosée, like la matinée, la soirée, la pensée. Do not confuse it with la rose, the flower. Une goutte de rosée.

cards.de: the lime tree (linden; also its herbal tea)
cards.note: Masculine: le tilleul. Une tisane de tilleul is drunk in the evening, and the word also names the pale green colour.

cards.de: The television in the living room is broken.
cards.fr: La poste de télévision du salon est en panne.
cards.answer: Le poste de télévision du salon est en panne.
cards.note: As a device, poste is masculine: un poste de télévision, un poste de radio. The feminine la poste means the post office.
La mémoire is memory, including computer memory. Le mémoire is a dissertation or report.

cards.de: I have a bad memory for names.
cards.fr: J'ai un mauvais mémoire pour les noms.
cards.answer: J'ai une mauvaise mémoire pour les noms.
cards.note: Memory is feminine: une mémoire. The masculine un mémoire is a written thesis or report.

cards.fr: J'ai acheté un kilo de cerises au marché.
cards.answer: J'ai acheté une livre de cerises au marché.
cards.note: La livre is the pound (weight or currency) and is feminine. Le livre is the book.
Faire un petit somme means to take a nap. La somme is a sum or an amount.

cards.de: A guard is watching the entrance to the museum.
cards.answer: Un garde surveille l'entrée du musée.
accept: Un garde surveille l'entrée du musée .
Un garde surveille l'entrée du musee.
cards.note: Le garde is the person, the guard. La garde is the duty of guarding: monter la garde.
Feminine it is the flower; masculine le rose is the colour pink.
Feminine it is the sleeve; masculine le manche is a handle or shaft. La Manche is the English Channel.
Le voile is a veil; la voile is a sail (and faire de la voile is to go sailing). The article carries the whole difference.
cards.hint: masculine here, but the same word is feminine with another meaning

cards.note: La crème is cream, both dairy and cosmetic; un crème (masculine) is a coffee with milk.
Masculine le vase is a vase; feminine la vase is mud or silt.
The fruit is feminine, the colour masculine: le orange. As an adjective orange never changes: des chaussures orange.
La manœuvre is a manoeuvre; le manœuvre is an unskilled labourer.
La vapeur is steam, le vapeur is a steamship. A common phrase: des légumes à la vapeur.

cards.de: the morals (ethics, also the moral of a story)
cards.note: Careful: le moral is your mood or spirits, and avoir le moral means to be in good spirits.
Le critique, by contrast, is the critic, the person.
La mousse is foam or moss, while le mousse is a ship's boy.

cards.de: the office (public bureau, e.g. tourist office)
cards.note: Masculine: un office de tourisme, and also a church service. Feminine une office is the pantry next to the kitchen. Remember faire office de (to serve as).
Masculine for the material: un sac en plastique. La plastique instead refers to someone's figure or body shape.
Feminine it is the frying pan, masculine le poêle is a stove. Pronounced [pwal].
Watch the gender: le physique means someone's physical appearance (il a un physique agréable).
Masculine it means basketball, feminine la basket is a trainer or sneaker, usually plural: des baskets.
La trompette is the instrument, le trompette is the trumpeter (military, old-fashioned).
La casse is breakage or damage, and also a scrapyard. Le casse, by contrast, is criminal slang for a break-in.
Feminine une enseigne is a shop sign, and also a retail chain. Masculine un enseigne is a naval ensign (officer rank).
The pancake is feminine: la crêpe. Masculine le crêpe means crepe as a fabric or rubber.

cards.de: the clock (pendulum clock on a wall or mantelpiece)
cards.note: The gender changes the meaning: le pendule is a pendulum, la pendule is a clock.
Watch the gender: le capital is financial capital, la capitale is a capital city. Plural: les capitaux.

cards.de: the guy, the bloke (colloquial, also a pet name)
cards.note: Colloquial: mon coco is used as a term of endearment. La coco, by contrast, means cocaine.

cards.de: the balance (of an account, remaining amount)
cards.note: Feminine la solde is a soldier's pay. In the plural, les soldes means the sales.
The gender decides: la moule is the mussel, le moule is a baking tin or mould. A classic dish: moules-frites.
La cartouche is a cartridge, le cartouche is a decorative inscription panel. Une cartouche d'encre is an ink cartridge.

cards.de: the beer (small glass in a café)
cards.note: Le demi is a glass of beer (about 25 cl), while la demie means the half hour.
With la it is a scythe, with le it means what is false or a forgery. The plural is unchanged: les faux.
The gender decides: le pique is spades in cards, la pique is a pike or a cutting remark.
The gender decides: la coke is cocaine (slang), le coke is coke the fuel.
l'œil, les yeux. One of the very few completely irregular plurals in French.

All six add -x rather than -s, and the pronunciation does not change at all. Eau and peau are feminine, so the article shifts to les eaux, les peaux while the ending behaves the same as for the masculine ones.

The singular -al is replaced by -aux, so there is no -s anywhere and no l left in the plural. Hôpital keeps its circumflex on the o; note that a few -al nouns like bal and festival simply add -s instead.

cards.de: The animals at the zoo are well cared for.
cards.fr: Les ___ du zoo sont bien soignés.
cards.note: animal becomes animaux. A plural in -als would be wrong here.

cards.de: In summer there are lots of festivals in France.
cards.fr: En été, il y a beaucoup de ___ en France.
cards.note: A few nouns in -al are exceptions and simply add -s: les festivals, les bals, les carnavals, les récitals.

cards.de: After the run my knees hurt.
cards.fr: Après la course, j'ai mal aux genous.
cards.answer: Après la course, j'ai mal aux genoux.
cards.note: Seven nouns in -ou take -x: bijou, caillou, chou, genou, hibou, joujou, pou. All the others take -s, for example les trous.
le bijou, les bijoux. It belongs to the small group of -ou nouns whose plural ends in -x.

cards.de: The children are playing with the horses.
cards.answer: Les enfants jouent avec les chevaux.
accept: Les enfants jouent avec des chevaux.
cards.note: le cheval becomes les chevaux. You hear the l in the singular but not in the plural.

cards.fr: Ce journal régional est très ancien.
cards.task: Put the whole sentence into the plural.
cards.answer: Ces journaux régionaux sont très anciens.
cards.note: Adjectives ending in -al also change to -aux in the masculine plural: régional becomes régionaux.
With monsieur, madame and mademoiselle both parts change: messieurs, mesdames, mesdemoiselles.
Nouns in -eau always take -x: les bateaux, les gâteaux, les châteaux.
Before an adjective that comes in front of a plural noun, des becomes de. In everyday speech you will often hear des as well.

cards.answer: Je n'ai pas acheté de pommes.
accept: Je n'ai pas acheté de pommes
Je n'ai pas acheté de pommes .
cards.note: In the passé composé too, des becomes de after a negation. The ne and pas wrap around the auxiliary only.

cards.de: She is a doctor and her husband is a teacher.
cards.fr: Elle est une médecin et son mari est un professeur.
cards.answer: Elle est médecin et son mari est professeur.
cards.note: After être, jobs and nationalities take no article, unlike English which needs "a". With c'est you do need one: C'est un médecin.
After sans the indefinite and partitive articles disappear: sans sucre, sans voiture, sans amis.
-er becomes -ère: boulanger, boulangère; infirmier, infirmière.
Four of these take -eur → -euse (visiteuse, chanteuse, serveuse, pêcheuse), while cuisinier follows the -ier → -ière pattern with its grave accent, and espion just doubles the n before -e.
Chasseur and danseur take -euse since they come from chasser and danser, while lion, champion and baron double the n. Portier is the only one that changes -ier to -ière, adding a grave accent.

Chien, patron and rayon just double the n before -e, while acteur and inspecteur switch -teur to -trice. Chauffeur is the odd one out of the -eur group: it becomes chauffeuse because it comes from the verb chauffer.
Nouns ending in -teur usually form the feminine in -trice: acteur, actrice; directeur, directrice.
A final -f becomes -ve: veuf, veuve; sportif, sportive.

cards.de: She has been a widow for two years.
cards.fr: Elle est veuf depuis deux ans.
cards.answer: Elle est veuve depuis deux ans.
cards.note: For a woman you need the feminine form veuve. After être the word stands without an article.
The ending -ien becomes -ienne with a double n: pharmacien, pharmacienne; likewise musicien, musicienne.

cards.de: My sister is a teacher at a secondary school.
cards.answer: Ma sœur est professeure dans un lycée.
accept: Ma sœur est professeur dans un lycée.
Ma sœur est prof dans un lycée.
Ma sœur est enseignante dans un lycée.
Ma sœur est professeure au lycée.
cards.note: Today une professeure is the usual feminine form. After être, job titles take no article, so there is no equivalent of "a".

cards.de: My friend (female) is a shop assistant in a bookshop.
cards.fr: Mon amie est vendeur dans une librairie.
cards.answer: Mon amie est vendeuse dans une librairie.
cards.note: Mon amie calls for the feminine vendeuse. The feminine ending is easy to forget.

cards.fr: Mon frère est acteur et son ami est boulanger.
cards.task: Put everything into the feminine (frère becomes sœur).
cards.answer: Ma sœur est actrice et son amie est boulangère.
accept: Ma sœur est actrice et son amie est boulangère .
cards.note: Two patterns in one sentence: -teur becomes -trice, -er becomes -ère. Ami also becomes amie.

cards.fr: Un sportif et un traducteur habitent dans cet immeuble.
cards.answer: Une sportive et une traductrice habitent dans cet immeuble.
cards.note: sportif becomes sportive (-f to -ve) and traducteur becomes traductrice (-teur to -trice).

cards.de: She is a doctor in a hospital in Nice.
cards.fr: Elle est ___ dans un hôpital à Nice.
cards.note: médecin does not change form: you say une médecin. La médecine, by contrast, is medicine as a subject.
héros and héroïne are irregular. You say le héros with an aspirated h, but l'héroïne with elision.

cards.de: She is wearing a white blouse.
cards.note: The feminine of blanc is blanche. chemise is singular, so the adjective stays singular too.

Naturel and personnel double the l, moyen doubles the n, and étranger takes the grave accent -ère. The two to memorise are public → publique (qu keeps the k sound) and bref → brève, which changes f to v and adds an accent.
Léger, secret and fier all end in a grave accent plus -e, and secret doubles nothing but shifts its accent. Neuf and vif swap f for v, while sec becomes sèche with both an accent and a ch.

Pareil and gentil add a silent -le, so the feminine sounds the same as the masculine; ancien doubles the n. Cher, entier and fier all take the grave accent (-ère), while fou → folle is the odd one, using the second masculine form fol.

Bon doubles the n, and premier and dernier both swap -er for -ère with a grave accent. The three to watch are beau → belle (the hidden form bel), long, which gains a u to keep the hard g sound, and blanc, where the c turns into ch.
The feminine is always belle, even before a vowel. Only the masculine has the special form bel.
nouvel exists only in the masculine before a vowel. With a feminine noun you always use nouvelle.
The masculine stays sec with no accent. The accent grave only appears in the feminine: sèche.

cards.fr: Un vieux monsieur attend devant la porte.
cards.task: Put into the feminine: une dame.
cards.answer: Une vieille dame attend devant la porte.
cards.note: vieux becomes vieille in the feminine. Other adjectives with their own feminine forms: roux → rousse, doux → douce.
bel is also used before a silent h, because the h is not pronounced. You can hear the link: un bel homme.
Before the noun, ancien means former. After the noun it means old or ancient: une maison ancienne.
To mean clean, propre goes after the noun. Before the noun it would mean own and would need a possessive: ma propre chemise.

cards.de: She comes from a poor family with no money.
cards.note: When money is really the point, pauvre goes after the noun. Before the noun it would only express pity.
When it means expensive, cher always comes after the noun. Before the noun it means dear or beloved.

cards.de: A woman living on her own lives next door to us.
cards.answer: Une femme seule habite à côté de nous.
accept: Une femme seule vit à côté de nous.
À côté de nous habite une femme seule.
cards.note: une femme seule is a woman who lives alone. une seule femme would mean just one single woman.

cards.de: Her brother is a tall man, almost two metres.
cards.fr: Son frère est un ___, presque deux mètres.
cards.note: For physical height, grand goes after the noun. un grand homme means a great man.

cards.task: Rearrange it so that it means an old, historic castle.
cards.note: un ancien château is a former castle that is something else today. un château ancien is a very old castle.

cards.de: Last year we were in Lyon.
cards.note: In time expressions, dernier follows the noun: la semaine dernière, le mois dernier. Before the noun it means the last one in a series: le dernier train.
After the noun, vrai means true in the sense of factual. Before the noun it means real or genuine: un vrai ami.

cards.de: She sings better than I do.
cards.note: mieux is the adverb (how something is done). meilleur is the adjective (what something is like): une meilleure chanteuse.

cards.de: This wine is better than the other one.
cards.note: After être you are describing a quality, so you need the adjective meilleur. It agrees in gender and number: meilleure, meilleurs, meilleures.

cards.de: The weather is worse than yesterday.
cards.note: mauvais has the irregular comparative pire. plus pire is wrong, since pire is already a comparative.

cards.de: She speaks French better than I do.
cards.fr: Elle parle français plus bien que moi.
cards.answer: Elle parle français mieux que moi.
cards.note: The adverb bien does not take plus; its comparative is mieux. plus bien does not exist.

cards.de: That's the best film of the year.
cards.fr: C'est le plus bon film de l'année.
cards.answer: C'est le meilleur film de l'année.
cards.note: bon becomes meilleur, never plus bon. The superlative is le meilleur, la meilleure.

cards.de: I'm feeling better than last week.
cards.answer: Je vais mieux que la semaine dernière.
accept: Je me sens mieux que la semaine dernière.
cards.note: With aller for how you feel, French uses the adverb: aller mieux. Je vais meilleur would be wrong.

cards.de: Of all the pupils, she works the best.
cards.fr: De tous les élèves, c'est elle qui travaille ___.
cards.note: The superlative of the adverb is always le mieux and never changes form, even when referring to a woman.

cards.task: Put into the superlative: ... de toutes.
cards.answer: Cette solution est la meilleure de toutes.
cards.note: The superlative of bonne is la meilleure. The adjective agrees with the noun, unlike the invariable adverb le mieux.
lent is the big exception. Despite its -ent ending, the adverb is lentement, built on the feminine form lente.
