It works both ways: guérir un malade (to cure someone) and il est guéri (he has recovered).
The same form is used for men and women, only the article changes. Le secrétaire can also mean a writing desk.
Feminine form la louve. Avoir une faim de loup means to be ravenously hungry.
With de it becomes a preposition: Leur maison se trouve au-delà de la frontière. (Their house is beyond the border.) As a noun, l'au-delà is the afterlife.

cards.de: the fiancé (man engaged to be married)
cards.note: Feminine une fiancée. The verb is se fiancer avec qn, to get engaged to someone.

cards.de: the avenue (path in a park or garden)
cards.note: It comes from aller, to go. It also means the aisle between rows of seats or shelves.
The verb pattern is menacer qn de qc, to threaten someone with something.
Feminine form affreuse. Very common in speech: c'est affreux !
Same form for masculine and feminine. Use être coupable de qc, and as a noun le coupable means the culprit.
Linked to the verb blesser, to injure. Also figurative: une blessure d'amour-propre, a wound to one's pride.
Usually lutter contre qc, to fight against something, or lutter pour qc, to fight for something. Il faut lutter contre le racisme. [We must fight against racism.]
Key phrase: prendre en charge, to take on or to cover the cost for someone.
For a woman it is une imbécile, with no change to the word itself. It also works as an adjective: une idée imbécile.
en principe means in theory or in principle, and par principe means on principle.
Il est interdit de cracher par terre dans le métro. [It is forbidden to spit on the ground in the metro.] cracher sur qn means to spit at someone, and figuratively to have contempt for them.
Elle s'est contentée de hausser les épaules. [She just shrugged.] The h is aspirate, as in le haussement.
Always followed by à: participer à une réunion.
The feminine is now usually une écrivaine; older usage was femme écrivain.
Borrowed from English and masculine. Plural matchs or matches; faire match nul means to draw.
French counts furniture: un meuble is one piece, les meubles covers furniture in general. The adjective meublé gives une chambre meublée, a furnished room.
Built on droit, straight. Le médecin m'a dit de me redresser sur ma chaise. [The doctor told me to sit up straight in my chair.] Reflexive se redresser also means to recover economically.
Feminine complète. On signs, complet means fully booked or no vacancies.
Feminine mystérieuse. Adjectives ending in -eux regularly change to -euse in the feminine.
J'aime voyager en train en été. [I like travelling by train in summer.] A -ger verb, so the e stays before o: nous voyageons. Passé composé with avoir: j'ai beaucoup voyagé.

cards.de: to gaze at (look at in absorption)
cards.note: More elevated than regarder and often admiring. Nous sommes restés une heure à contempler la mer. [We stayed an hour gazing at the sea.]
Singular and plural look the same: un vers, des vers. Do not confuse it with the preposition vers (towards, around).
Feminine: une énergie, l'énergie. Very common: les énergies renouvelables (renewable energy).
Feminine: la réserve. It also means restraint, and sans réserve means without reservation.
Formed from apparent; the ending -emment is pronounced like -amment. Apparemment, il a raté son train. (Apparently, he missed his train.)
Mostly figurative. Ce documentaire a réussi à éveiller ma curiosité. [This documentary managed to awaken my curiosity.] To wake a person up is réveiller.
The pattern is ordonner à qn de faire qc. Le capitaine peut nous ordonner de partir tout de suite. [The captain can order us to leave right away.] It can also mean to arrange or put in order.
Comparison takes à, not que: supérieur à la moyenne. The feminine form is supérieure.

cards.de: sometimes ... sometimes (now one way, now another)
cards.note: Usually used in pairs: tantôt ... tantôt. Elle est tantôt gentille, tantôt insupportable. (She is sometimes nice, sometimes unbearable.) Regionally it can also mean later today or earlier today.
Written as one word. Je prends quelquefois le bus pour aller au travail. (I sometimes take the bus to work.) The synonym parfois is slightly more common.
Usually reflexive: Je dois me raser avant l'entretien. [I have to shave before the interview.] It also means to raze to the ground and, informally, to bore someone.
Used as grimper à un arbre or grimper sur le toit. It normally takes avoir in the passé composé.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Smaller craft are called le bateau.
Il aime foncer sur l'autoroute. [He likes racing along on the motorway.] foncer sur qn means to charge at someone. It can also mean to make a colour darker.
Le premier venu peut s'inscrire. [Just anybody can sign up.] As an adjective it also appears in bien venu (welcome, fitting) and mal venu (out of place).
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. Les Nations unies means the United Nations.
No preposition needed: demain matin, demain soir. As a goodbye: à demain!

cards.de: the stake (in a game, in betting)
cards.note: It comes from mettre. Also found in set phrases: la mise en scène, la mise en place.
The feminine form is fameuse. Informally it also means great: pas fameux means not very good.
poser un lapin à qn means to stand someone up. A hare is le lièvre.
The plural is plateaux. It also means plateau (high ground) and a film or TV set.
Feminine form: une patiente. The same word is also the adjective meaning patient.

cards.de: to appear (be listed, e.g. on a list)
cards.note: Used as figurer dans un livre, sur une liste. Reflexive se figurer qc means to imagine something.

Son courage peut inspirer toute l'équipe. [His courage can inspire the whole team.] Pattern: inspirer qc à qn, and s'inspirer de qc = to take inspiration from something. In medical use it also means to breathe in.
From léger: the feminine légère plus ment. Il a été légèrement blessé dans l'accident. (He was slightly injured in the accident.)
prendre la mouche = to take offence. A bow tie is le nœud papillon, not une mouche.
Formal; in everyday speech people say s'habiller. Past participle vêtu: elle était vêtue de noir.
As a noun, le déjeuner = lunch. To have breakfast is prendre le petit-déjeuner.
La Révolution française refers to 1789. In technical use it also means one full turn.
Always followed by de: une centaine de personnes. Formed like dizaine and douzaine.
Same form for both genders: un collègue, une collègue. Common phrase: un collègue de travail.
Spelled with double t in the present: je rejette. Say rejeter une offre, rejeter une idée.
Un angle droit is a right angle. It also means corner: à l'angle de la rue.
As an adjective it never changes: elle est bien, ils sont bien. Don't confuse it with bon, which does agree.
Je suis censé travailler means I'm supposed to be working. Don't confuse it with sensé, which means sensible.
Same form for masculine and feminine. As a noun, la ferme means farm.
A false friend: it means reading, not a lecture (that's un cours). Common phrase: la lecture d'un roman.
Also used in colloquial phrases: être trempé comme une soupe = to be soaked through.
Pattern: réclamer qc à qn. Les clients commencent à réclamer un remboursement. [The customers are starting to demand a refund.] Stronger than demander; it suggests insistence.
With children, sois sage means be good. English sage keeps only the wise sense.
Il faut conserver le fromage au frais. [You have to keep the cheese somewhere cool.] À conserver au frais appears on food packaging. Also figurative: conserver son calme.
Month names are masculine and take no article: en mai or au mois de mai. They are also written in lower case.
Same form for masculine and feminine. It usually follows the noun: une femme extraordinaire.
The accent changes in the present tense: il règne. Used with sur: régner sur un pays.
Colloquial, often used as an exclamation: c'est dingue! The neutral word is fou.
Same form for both genders: une propriétaire. Used with de: propriétaire d'une maison.

cards.de: to mix up, to confuse (two things)
cards.note: The pattern is confondre qc avec qc. Il est facile de confondre ces deux mots. [It is easy to mix up these two words.] It follows répondre, with the past participle confondu.
The feminine form is furieuse. You are furieux contre qn, angry at someone.
The final s stays silent and the plural looks the same. Faire un procès à qn means to sue someone.

cards.de: the test, the exam paper (also: an ordeal)
cards.note: Feminine. Often in mettre qn à l'épreuve, to put someone to the test.

cards.de: to fall again, to fall back
cards.note: Takes être in the passé composé: elle est retombée. Fais attention à ne pas retomber malade. [Be careful not to fall ill again.]
Same form for both genders. As a noun, une minuscule is a lower-case letter, the opposite of majuscule.
Feminine. It also means a grid: la grille de mots croisés, the crossword grid.
Elle a préféré détourner les yeux. [She preferred to look away.] détourner un avion means to hijack a plane.
The feminine form is jalouse. Use être jaloux de qn, to be jealous of someone.
The feminine la sorcière means witch. A common phrase is ce n'est pas sorcier, it's not rocket science.
Mostly reflexive: Elle s'est fâchée contre son frère. (She got angry with her brother.) Note that être fâché avec qn means to have fallen out with someone.
Same form in the masculine and the feminine. The opposite is visible.
The chicken on your plate is le poulet. Colloquially, ma poule is a term of endearment.
Conjugated like écrire: je décris, nous décrivons, j'ai décrit.
The pattern is avertir qn de qc. Related noun: un avertissement, a warning.

cards.de: the river (large one flowing into the sea)
cards.note: A fleuve flows into the sea, while a rivière flows into another river. English just says river for both.

cards.de: beautiful, handsome (special form before a vowel, e.g. ... homme)
cards.note: beau becomes bel before a vowel or silent h: un bel arbre, un bel hôtel. The feminine is belle.

cards.de: the guest (person who has been invited)
cards.note: Feminine: une invitée. A guest in a hotel or restaurant is le client instead.

cards.de: the favour (something you do for someone)
cards.note: Feminine. Common uses: demander une faveur à qn and en faveur de (in favour of).
You say signer un contrat. A CDI is a permanent employment contract.

cards.de: to write down, to enter (on a list)
cards.note: Conjugated like écrire: j'inscris, nous inscrivons. Je vais m'inscrire à un cours de danse. (I'm going to sign up for a dance class.)

cards.de: to spoil, to ruin (also to waste)
cards.note: Very common: gâcher sa vie, gâcher la soirée, ne pas gâcher la nourriture.

cards.de: to note, to observe (to notice something is the case)
cards.note: Often followed by que: je constate que rien n'a changé. A bit more formal than voir.
Usually reflexive: se détendre, to relax oneself. Opposite: tendre, to tighten.
Stronger than chercher, used for police work or research: être recherché par la police.

cards.de: the singing, the song (as an art or activity)
cards.note: Sounds exactly like champ (field). Un cours de chant is a singing lesson.
To go for a swim or bathe yourself is se baigner: on se baigne dans la mer.
Masculine despite the -e ending: porter un masque.
The pattern is être responsable de qc. As a noun, le/la responsable means the person in charge.
Masculine despite the -e. Common phrase: dans le domaine de la santé.
Also religious: les dix commandements, the Ten Commandments. Nouns ending in -ment are masculine.
Conjugated like finir. There are two past participles: béni (blessed) and bénit in l'eau bénite (holy water).
Often concrete: faire une bêtise means to do something silly. Related adjective: bête, stupid.
Feminine noun. Remember the phrase avoir de la fièvre, to have a temperature.
Addressed as Monsieur le curé. A Protestant minister is le pasteur.

cards.de: the period, the stretch of time
cards.note: Feminine, despite the -ode ending. Very common: pendant cette période.

cards.de: to manage, to cope, to get by
cards.note: Very common in speech: je me débrouille = I'm managing fine. Also se débrouiller en français = to get by in French.
The past participle of fatiguer. Je suis trop fatigué pour sortir ce soir. (I'm too tired to go out tonight.) Careful: fatigant, with -ant, means tiring.
Feminine form juive. Lower case as an adjective, capitalised as a noun: un Juif, une Juive.
Today it survives mainly in set phrases: tant pis = never mind, too bad; de pis en pis = worse and worse.
From the verb craindre qc. Set phrase: de crainte que + subjonctif = for fear that.
Used as être incapable de faire qc. The opposite is capable de.
conseiller à qn de faire qc: je te conseille de partir tôt. The same form is also a noun: le conseiller = the adviser.
Feminine une alliée. Les Alliés (capitalised) means the Allies in wartime.
Le prof mesure la table avant de la déplacer. (The teacher measures the table before moving it.) Also used for height: il mesure 1,80 m means he is 1.80 m tall.
Transitive: Ce bruit dans la nuit m'a effrayé. (That noise in the night frightened me.) Reflexive s'effrayer de qc means to get frightened by something, and effrayant means frightening.

cards.de: to work, to function (of a machine)
cards.note: Mon ordinateur ne fonctionne plus depuis hier. (My computer hasn't been working since yesterday.) In everyday speech people usually say ça ne marche pas instead.
Sounds formal and slightly disparaging. The neutral option is une personne âgée.

cards.de: to wipe, to dry (with a cloth)
cards.note: Watch the spelling: j'essuie, nous essuyons. Common: essuyer la vaisselle, s'essuyer les mains.
Informal and invariable: une fille cool, des gens cool. Also used as an exclamation: Cool!

cards.de: to deprive (to take something away from someone)
cards.note: Used as priver qn de qc: Ses parents l'ont privé de dessert. (His parents deprived him of dessert.) Reflexive se priver de qc means to go without something.
The feminine doubles the l: sexuelle. Common: harcèlement sexuel, éducation sexuelle.
Related to entreprendre. It can also mean an undertaking: une entreprise difficile.

cards.de: the plate (flat sheet of metal, sign)
cards.note: Very common in plaque d'immatriculation (number plate) and plaque chauffante (hotplate).

cards.de: the chicken (the meat, a young bird)
cards.note: La poule is the live hen. In slang un poulet also means a cop.
Masculine. Do not confuse it with la mentonnière (chin strap) or mentir (to lie).
Common phrase: se faire des illusions (to kid oneself). Also un tour d'illusion for a magician's trick.
Watch the spelling: rythme has a y and no h after the r. Au rythme de means in time with.
It comes from prendre. Other meanings: prise de sang (blood test), prise de décision (decision making).

cards.de: the code (numbers or a set of rules)
cards.note: Masculine. Set phrases: le code postal, le code de la route (the highway code).
It takes a direct object with no preposition: dominer qn/qc. In a spatial sense it means to overlook: la colline domine la ville.
Feminine totale, masculine plural totaux. As a noun, le total means the sum.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. Assumer la responsabilité de qc means to take responsibility for something.
C'est évident, il ment depuis le début. (It's obvious, he's been lying from the start.) But ce n'est pas évident colloquially means it's not easy.
Masculine. You say sur le boulevard, not dans.
Nouns in -té are feminine. As a form of address it is Votre Majesté, even for a king.
Always feminine. Common: vivre dans la misère. Also un salaire de misère, a pittance of a wage.
Feminine sainte. As a noun un saint, une sainte; in place names it is hyphenated: Saint-Michel.

cards.de: the fat man (informal, for a fat person)
cards.note: Feminine la grosse; it is slangy and can be insulting. Also note en gros, meaning wholesale or roughly speaking.
Formed from direct. Common: aller directement à, to go straight to.
Masculine despite the final -e. Se ronger les ongles means to bite your nails.

The pattern is appliquer qc à qc: Nous appliquons la même règle à tous les élèves. (We apply the same rule to all the pupils.) Reflexive s'appliquer à faire qc means to make an effort to do something.
Note the spelling change: J'emploie souvent ce mot au travail. (I often use this word at work.) Also employer qn, to employ someone, which gives un employé.
Same form for both genders. Careful: it is a false friend, since sensible in English is sensé in French. Use sensible à qc for sensitive to something.
The word is identical for a woman: une journaliste. Only the article shows the gender.
viser qc takes a direct object with no preposition: il vise la cible. Before a verb you need à: viser à faire qc, to aim to do something.
avoir des difficultés à faire qc means to have trouble doing something. It is often used in the plural.
Vulgar and very colloquial: Le chien a pissé sur le tapis. (The dog pissed on the rug.) The neutral options are faire pipi or the formal uriner.
Applied to people the word is sensitive, so origine is preferred. un chien de race is a pedigree dog.
Same form for both genders. Say célèbre pour qc, famous for something; the noun is la célébrité.
Masculine despite the -e ending. en échange de qc means in exchange for something.
Almost always plural, just like in English: Félicitations! The matching verb is féliciter qn.
La voiture ne démarre pas, the car won't start. Also figurative: le projet démarre bien.
The final z is silent and the plural looks the same as the singular. Colloquially, mettre les gaz means to step on it.
Used politically too, exactly as in English: un sommet européen, an EU summit.
The feminine doubles the l: cruelle. The adverb is cruellement.
Un sucre can also mean a sugar cube. The adjective sucré means sweet or sweetened.
Conjugated like vendre: il répand, ils répandent, participle répandu. Se répandre means to spread (by itself).
Unlike English, French months are written in lower case and take no article: en juin, in June.
Feminine une inconnue, which in maths is also the unknown quantity. It works as an adjective too: un lieu inconnu.
The pattern is reprocher qc à qn: Il me reproche mon retard. (He blames me for being late.)
Plier une feuille, plier le linge. Se plier means to bend or to give in.
Same form for masculine and feminine. The noun is l'humidité, dampness or humidity.
Same form in the masculine and feminine. Common uses: un argument solide, une amitié solide.
Written with an accent circonflexe, from the verb bâtir, to build. Le bâtiment also means the construction industry.
Don't confuse it with le cou, the neck. Jouer des coudes means to elbow your way through.
La roue de secours is the spare wheel. Don't confuse it with la rue, the street.
Pronounced pa-si-ans, with a silent final e. The adjective is patient, feminine patiente.

cards.de: to set against (oppose one thing to another)
cards.note: Most often used reflexively: Les voisins s'opposent à ce projet. (The neighbours oppose this project.)
This is a feeling in the body, not an emotion, which is le sentiment. Also faire sensation, to cause a stir.
Je dois gonfler les pneus de mon vélo. (I have to pump up my bike tyres.) Used intransitively it means to swell up.
Nouns ending in -ence are feminine. Les sciences humaines are the humanities.
The feminine is voisine. Used as a noun, le voisin means the neighbour.
The h is aspirated, so there is no liaison in la hâte. Very common: j'ai hâte de te voir, I can't wait to see you.
The feminine form is irregular: une impératrice.
The final c is pronounced. Don't mix it up with la mer, the sea.
Formed from facile, keeping the silent e before -ment. The opposite is difficilement. J'ai trouvé la gare facilement. (I found the station easily.)
The feminine is la gardienne with a double n. Le gardien de but is the goalkeeper.
Formal or literary, common in storytelling. The final s is pronounced.
Feminine précieuse, plural stays précieux. Common phrase: une aide précieuse.
Feminine intérieure. As a noun l'intérieur means the inside, and à l'intérieur de means inside of.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. dans l'obscurité means in the dark.
Masculine noun. Watch the pronunciation: the x sounds like ks.
Written without a final d, unlike the verb cauchemarder. faire un cauchemar means to have a nightmare.
Also means to run over: il s'est fait renverser par une voiture. And politically: renverser le gouvernement.

cards.de: the ridge (highest point of a roof)
cards.note: Spelled with a circumflex and pronounced exactly like la fête. Figuratively: le faîte de la gloire, the height of glory.
Literally on top of that, but also figurative: je suis d'accord là-dessus. Always written with a hyphen.

cards.de: to constitute (to make up, to amount to)
cards.note: Often means to represent: cela constitue un risque. Reflexive se constituer prisonnier means to give oneself up.
As an adverb it never changes: allez tout droit. Do not confuse it with the noun le droit, meaning right or law.

From the adjective franc, franche. Franchement, je préfère rester à la maison ce soir. (Honestly, I'd rather stay home tonight.) Colloquially it also intensifies: c'est franchement nul, that's really rubbish.
Feminine grasse. Faire la grasse matinée means to have a lie-in.
Conjugated like faire: Ce résultat ne satisfait pas le directeur. (This result doesn't satisfy the director.) Satisfaire à une condition means to meet a condition.
Feminine, like almost all nouns ending in -ance. It also means self-confidence: parler avec assurance.
The standard phrase on meeting someone: Enchanté, je suis le frère de Marie. (Pleased to meet you, I'm Marie's brother.) Literally it means enchanted.
Ce camion transporte des légumes vers le marché. (This lorry carries vegetables to the market.) Related words: le transport and les transports en commun, public transport.

cards.de: to be late in coming, to delay
cards.note: Tarder à faire qc means to take a long time to do something: Il tarde à répondre à mes messages. (He's slow to answer my messages.) Il me tarde de te voir means I can't wait to see you.

cards.de: to carry out (an order, a task)
cards.note: Les ouvriers exécutent les ordres du chef. (The workers carry out the boss's orders.) It also means to execute someone, and reflexive s'exécuter means to comply.
Elle frotte la casserole depuis dix minutes. (She's been scrubbing the pan for ten minutes.) Se frotter les mains means to rub your hands, both literally and figuratively.

cards.de: to distrust, to be wary of
cards.note: Only used reflexively: se méfier de qn/qc. Je me méfie de ses promesses. (I'm wary of his promises.) Méfie-toi! means Watch out!

Emprunter qc à qn means to borrow something from someone, so French uses à where English says from. J'ai emprunté cinquante euros à mon frère. (I borrowed fifty euros from my brother.) The opposite is prêter (to lend).
Only for film and video. A stills camera is un appareil photo.
Always feminine, even when a male being is meant. Nouns ending in -ure are usually feminine.
Feminine form innocente. The opposite is coupable (guilty).
faire usage de qc means to make use of something. Common phrases: hors d'usage (unusable), à usage unique (single-use).
Feminine italienne, with a double n. As a language name it stays lowercase: il parle italien.
All nouns ending in -té are feminine. En activité means in active service, still working.
faire le ménage means to do the cleaning, and une femme de ménage is a cleaning lady.
The drink is masculine, while the region La Champagne is feminine. Une coupe de champagne.
Masculine: le 15 août. Pronounced [u] or [ut], with the a not spoken. For the month use en août.
Usually reflexive: se venger de qn means to take revenge on someone. Il veut se venger de son ancien patron. (He wants to take revenge on his former boss.) La vengeance is revenge.

cards.de: at length (for a long time and in detail)
cards.note: Formed from long. Do not confuse it with longtemps (a long time). Nous avons parlé longuement de son projet. (We talked at length about her project.)
The ending -esse is always feminine, as in la politesse. The adjective is triste.
Same form for a woman: une peintre. Un peintre en bâtiment is a decorator.
Also a column in a newspaper or a table. La colonne vertébrale is the spine.
Used as le manque de qc, or par manque de temps (for lack of time). The verb is manquer.
Sounds just like soi (oneself) and sois. Un foulard en soie is a silk scarf.
punir qn de or pour qc. Regular like finir: je punis, nous punissons.
semblable à qc/qn, slightly formal. In everyday speech people say pareil à.
aller à un concert, en concert. The piece of music is un concerto.
Feminine gaie, pronounced like [gé]. The spelling gay means homosexual.
bloquer la route, bloquer un compte. Reflexive se bloquer means to jam or get stuck.
Irregular feminine: maligne. Faire le malin means to show off.

cards.de: to make up, to put together
cards.note: Se composer de qc means to consist of something. L'équipe se compose de six joueurs. (The team consists of six players.) Also composer un numéro, to dial a number.
Used as se disputer avec qn. Il se dispute souvent avec son frère. (He often argues with his brother.) Informally, disputer qn means to tell someone off.

cards.de: Monday (as a day of the week)
cards.note: No article and no preposition: lundi means on Monday. With the article, le lundi means on Mondays.
confirmer un rendez-vous. Often used in the passive: la nouvelle est confirmée.
It also means rabies. Une rage de dents is a raging toothache.
Informal register. Je me suis cogné la tête contre la porte. (I banged my head on the door.) Se cogner la tête contre qc means to bang your head on something.
The final s is silent. The opposite is l'enfer (m), hell.
Always with de: jouir d'une bonne santé. On its own the verb also has a sexual meaning, so use it with care.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Parcels are marked Fragile in French too.
Prendre le bus, venir en bus. The final s is pronounced here.
Feminine: la marchande. Un marchand de légumes sells vegetables.
From sérieux, sérieuse. Tu dois réfléchir sérieusement à cette offre. (You need to think seriously about this offer.) As a question, Sérieusement ? means Seriously?
Un fer à repasser is an iron. Je dois repasser ma chemise avant l'entretien. (I have to iron my shirt before the interview.) Repasser also means to come back round or drop by again.
It organises what you say: Bref, je n'y vais pas. As an adjective, bref, brève means brief.
Only used of women, so there is no masculine form: elle est enceinte de trois mois. As a noun, une enceinte is a loudspeaker.
Usually used in the plural: une paire de gants. Ça te va comme un gant means it fits you perfectly.
Feminine because it is short for l'automobile. In everyday speech la voiture is more common.
Always masculine, even about a woman: elle est un modèle célèbre. Prendre qn pour modèle = to take someone as a role model.
Borrowed from English and therefore masculine. The usual verb is passer un test (to take a test).
In sport it means a card: un carton jaune, un carton rouge (yellow card, red card).
Feminine, and the initial h is silent (h muet), so it becomes l'huile d'olive.
The same word also covers a towel (serviette de bain) and a briefcase.
It also means a bookcase. Do not confuse it with la librairie, which is a bookshop.

Exposer qc à qn means to set something out for someone. Elle expose ses tableaux dans une petite galerie. (She is exhibiting her paintings in a small gallery.) S'exposer à un danger means to expose oneself to danger.
The feminine is déserte: une rue déserte. As a noun, le désert means the desert.
The final f stays silent: [nɛʁ]. Taper sur les nerfs de qn = to get on someone's nerves.
Masculine, and pronounced [ɔtɔn] with a silent m. En automne = in autumn.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Structure: être digne de confiance (trustworthy).

cards.de: to make an effort, to strive
cards.note: Only used reflexively: s'efforcer de faire qc means to try hard to do something. Je m'efforce de parler français tous les jours. (I make an effort to speak French every day.)
Same form for masculine and feminine. As a noun, un noble is a nobleman.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Structure: être fidèle à qn/qc.
Always plural and masculine: les frais de port (postage costs). Do not confuse it with the adjective frais = fresh, cool.
La salle de séjour is the living room. To wish someone well, say bon séjour!
Here the t is pronounced [nɛt], and the feminine is nette. Le prix net = the net price.
As in accent aigu, accent grave. Mettre l'accent sur qc means to stress or emphasise something.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. It covers both a body or group and the act of planning.
Feminine. Very common: le bruit court que ... or la rumeur court que ...
Remember the phrase être à la disposition de qn, to be at someone's disposal.
Usually plural and placed before the noun: divers problèmes. Feminine form diverse.

cards.de: to go ashore (to get off a boat)
cards.note: The opposite of embarquer. Informally it also means to turn up unannounced: il a débarqué chez moi.
A standard reply to an offer: Volontiers! The final s stays silent. Je viendrais volontiers avec toi demain. (I'd gladly come with you tomorrow.)
Feminine form muette. An h muet is a silent h that still allows liaison.
You take a shower with prendre une douche, never faire. Se doucher works too.

cards.de: to dry (to become or make dry)
cards.note: The é changes to è before a silent ending: je sèche. Le linge sèche vite au soleil. (The washing dries quickly in the sun.) Informally, sécher un cours means to skip a class.
Feminine. En fonction de means depending on or according to.
Masculine. Femme au foyer means housewife, and in a theatre le foyer is the lobby.
Same form for both genders: un esclave, une esclave. Être esclave de qc means to be a slave to something.
Feminine, like other nouns in -ion. The adjective is religieux, religieuse.

cards.de: to maintain (to look after, to service)
cards.note: Conjugated like tenir: j'entretiens. Mon voisin entretient très bien son jardin. (My neighbour looks after his garden very well.) S'entretenir avec qn means to have a conversation with someone.
From poing, fist. Une poignée de main is a handshake, and une poignée is also a door handle.

cards.de: to conceal (to hide, to keep secret)
cards.note: Used as dissimuler qc à qn. Il a dissimulé la vérité à ses parents. (He concealed the truth from his parents.) A little more formal than cacher.
Month names are masculine and written in lower case, unlike in English. In September is en septembre.
Feminine form délicate. It also means delicate or sensitive: une peau délicate.
Usually placed before the noun: son futur mari. As a noun, le futur means the future.
Month names are masculine but normally appear without an article: en juillet, le 14 juillet.

cards.de: to lie in wait for (watch closely, on the lookout)
cards.note: Guetter qn/qc takes no preposition. Le chat guette les oiseaux depuis la fenêtre. (The cat is watching the birds from the window.) Also used for waiting for something: guetter l'occasion.
Also used of places: regagner sa place, regagner Paris = to get back to.
embarquer dans un avion. Used transitively it means to load, and colloquially to take along or cart off.
Feminine form familière. A second meaning is familiar: un visage familier.
être au régime = to be on a diet. The same word also means a political regime or an engine's speed.
The pattern is informer qn de qc. Le directeur nous a informés de sa décision. (The director informed us of his decision.) Reflexive s'informer sur qc means to find out about something.
The plural is irregular: les métaux.
Barre ce mot, il est faux. (Cross out that word, it is wrong.) Route barrée means road closed. Colloquially se barrer means to clear off.

cards.de: to consider (judge, reckon something to be the case)
cards.note: estimer que takes the indicative. It also means to think highly of someone: j'estime beaucoup ce collègue.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Very common in une carte d'identité.

cards.de: to take off (a garment, a hat)
cards.note: Slightly formal; everyday French prefers enlever. Il ôte son chapeau en entrant dans l'église. (He takes off his hat as he enters the church.) Ôter qc à qn means to take something away from someone.
Masculine, plural les week-ends. No preposition is used: ce week-end, le week-end dernier.
exercer une influence sur qn. Reflexive s'exercer à qc = to practise something.
An invariable borrowing from English, used colloquially: c'est très in. The opposite is out.
Masculine. Common phrase: jouer d'un instrument, to play an instrument.

cards.de: to fly away, to fly off
cards.note: Only used reflexively. Les oiseaux se sont envolés dès que je suis arrivé. (The birds flew away as soon as I arrived.) Also figurative: les prix s'envolent, prices are soaring.
Also means to break or violate. Cette entreprise a violé la loi plusieurs fois. (This company has broken the law several times.) In the sense of rape the word is strong, so use it carefully.
Masculine despite the -e ending. The feminine is une poétesse or une poète.
Ce long voyage m'a complètement épuisé. (This long journey completely exhausted me.) Very common as a participle: je suis épuisé, I'm completely worn out.
Reflexive with sur: se concentrer sur qc. Je n'arrive pas à me concentrer sur mon travail avec ce bruit. (I can't concentrate on my work with this noise.)

Le plancher craque quand on marche dessus. (The floor creaks when you walk on it.) Colloquially also to crack up or give in: je craque, I can't take it any more. Craquer pour qn means to fall for someone.
The accent shifts: je repère, nous repérons. J'ai repéré un bon restaurant près de la gare. (I spotted a good restaurant near the station.) Se faire repérer means to get caught.
Il travaille dans le secteur privé depuis dix ans. (He has worked in the private sector for ten years.) En privé means in private, just between us.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine. De génération en génération = from generation to generation.
La pluie a mouillé tous mes vêtements. (The rain got all my clothes wet.) Se mouiller = to get wet, and colloquially to stick your neck out.
Masculine despite the final -e, like many nouns in -ème (le problème, le système).
Ses parents l'ont armé de patience avant l'examen. (His parents equipped him with patience before the exam.) Armer qn de qc = to equip someone with something; the opposite is désarmer.
Slang for voiture, very common in everyday speech but not in formal writing.
Also pomp: en grande pompe, with great ceremony. Les pompes funèbres = the undertaker's.
Masculine despite the -e. The female is une guenon; payer en monnaie de singe = to pay in empty promises.
In the plural, les échecs means chess. The verb: échouer à un examen, to fail an exam.
Short for professeur and very informal. For a female teacher: la prof.
Feminine prudente. The opposite is imprudent. Very common: Sois prudent!

cards.de: the sword (also the épée in fencing)
cards.note: Feminine. Idiom: un coup d'épée dans l'eau, a wasted effort.
The final c is silent. Un bureau de tabac is the tobacconist's, where you can also buy stamps.
Feminine délicieuse. Used for food, but also for a délicieux moment, a lovely moment.
Le poulet est bien doré et sent très bon. (The chicken is nicely golden brown and smells great.) From dorer, to gild, so it works for gold colour and for food.

cards.de: to pierce, to drill through (make a hole)
cards.note: Je vais percer un trou dans le mur pour l'étagère. (I'm going to drill a hole in the wall for the shelf.) The c becomes ç before a and o: nous perçons. Se faire percer les oreilles means to get your ears pierced.
Le professeur est intervenu pour arrêter la dispute. (The teacher stepped in to stop the argument.) Conjugated like venir and takes être in the passé composé.
Almost only used in faire semblant de faire qc, to pretend to do something.
Same form for masculine and feminine. The adverb is extrêmement.

cards.de: to specify, to state more precisely
cards.note: Often followed by que: il a précisé que... Se préciser means to become clearer or take shape.

cards.de: half (invariable before the noun: half an hour)
cards.note: Before a noun it takes a hyphen and never changes: une demi-heure. After the noun it agrees: deux heures et demie.
Je m'identifie beaucoup à ce personnage du film. (I identify a lot with this character in the film.) S'identifier takes à, not avec.

cards.de: the gendarme (police officer in rural areas)
cards.note: The gendarmerie is a military force covering areas outside the big cities, while la police works in the towns.

cards.de: to tilt, to incline (hold at an angle)
cards.note: Elle incline la tête pour mieux entendre. (She tilts her head to hear better.) S'incliner devant qn means to bow to someone or to admit defeat.
Also figurative: dévorer un livre, to devour a book. Much stronger than manger.
Usually plural for the remains of a building: les ruines d'un château. Also financial: c'est ma ruine.
Conjugated like finir. Reflexive s'unir à/avec qn means to join forces with someone.
Also a gleam or sheen, for example in someone's hair. The verb is refléter, to reflect.
From entier, whole. Je suis entièrement d'accord avec toi. (I completely agree with you.)
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. You say une réaction à quelque chose.
More everyday than English discussion; it often just means a chat. The verb is discuter de quelque chose.
Set phrase: sous prétexte de faire quelque chose, on the pretext of doing something.
To be at the wheel is être au volant. The same word also means a frill on a dress and a badminton shuttlecock.
Same word as the cut of meat, a fillet, and also un filet d'eau, a thin trickle of water.
The feminine is une employée. Common combinations: un employé de banque, un employé de bureau.

cards.de: the flaw, the fault (character defect, blemish)
cards.note: Not a mistake in a calculation; that would be une faute or une erreur. Useful phrase: à défaut de, for want of.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -tude. The verb is s'inquiéter de quelque chose, to worry about something.
Masculine, like all nouns ending in -age. The opposite is un inconvénient.
Il a mal réagi à ma remarque. (He reacted badly to my comment.) Conjugated like finir, and you react à quelque chose, never sur.

cards.de: the division (splitting, or the maths operation)
cards.note: From the verb diviser, to divide. Also used in the military and in sport: la première division is the top league.
As an adverb it never changes: parler bas. It also works for position: plus bas means further down.
Désolé, je suis pressé, on parlera demain. (Sorry, I'm in a hurry, we'll talk tomorrow.) Careful: un citron pressé is a freshly squeezed lemon juice.
A small stone is une pierre, and a pebble is un caillou.
From vague, meaning unclear. Very common: je me souviens vaguement.
Use consacrer qc à qn/qc, and se consacrer à qc for devoting yourself to something. Je consacre une heure par jour à mes révisions. (I devote an hour a day to my revision.)
Its counterpart is heureusement, luckily. Malheureusement, le magasin était déjà fermé. (Unfortunately, the shop was already closed.)
Very crude, only for very informal speech. The feminine form is une connasse.

cards.de: to persuade, to talk someone into something
cards.note: Ils m'ont persuadé de rester encore une nuit. (They talked me into staying one more night.) It appeals to feelings, while convaincre convinces with arguments.
avoir la possibilité de faire qc. Every noun ending in -té is feminine.
Feminine. A broad street in town, often tree lined: habiter avenue de la République.
dans le cadre de means within the framework of. Un cadre is also a manager or executive.
The surname is le nom or le nom de famille.
La monnaie is loose change or currency, not money in general. Money is l'argent: Je n'ai pas de monnaie means I have no small change.

cards.de: to slip on (a piece of clothing, quickly)
cards.note: J'enfile un pull et j'arrive. (I'll slip on a sweater and I'm coming.) The basic sense is to thread: enfiler une aiguille.
en vertu de means by virtue of, under. It can also mean healing power: les vertus d'une plante.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Electricity is l'électricité, and electric current is le courant.
Son rire emplit toute la maison. (Her laughter fills the whole house.) Formal and literary; in everyday French you say remplir.
The feminine is une blonde, which in colloquial French also means a lager.
en bloc means as a whole. A notepad is un bloc-notes.
Mon petit frère imite tout ce que je fais. (My little brother copies everything I do.) Takes a direct object with no preposition; the noun is une imitation.
A verb in -ger: nous nageons keeps the e before o. Aller à la piscine pour nager.
Irregular plural: les tribunaux. Aller au tribunal means to go to court.
Une tasse de café. Colloquially, boire la tasse means to swallow water while swimming.
Pronounced with an open ending: [ʁevɔlvɛʁ]. More generally you can say une arme or un pistolet.
A free-standing wardrobe is l'armoire (f). Ranger qc dans le placard.
Always followed by de: une dizaine de personnes. Same pattern as une douzaine, une vingtaine.
Feminine: une policière. Used as an adjective in un roman policier, a crime novel.
A little more formal than avant. It stands on its own, with nothing following it. Nous nous étions rencontrés deux jours auparavant. (We had met two days before.)
Le prix est trop élevé pour mon budget. (The price is too high for my budget.) Use haut for physical height; bien élevé means well brought up.
Masculine, with the plural les whiskys or les whiskies. Un whisky sans glace.
Feminine: une université. Colloquially people say la fac: je vais à la fac.
The feminine doubles the l: habituelle. Related expression: comme d'habitude, as usual.
The final s is there in the singular too. Passer un concours means to sit a competitive exam.
Feminine. L'intelligence artificielle is AI.
Masculine, and normally used with the article: dans l'ouest de la France, à l'ouest de Paris.
The final c is silent: [pɔʁ], sounding like port. On a menu you will see côte de porc.
Conjugated like rendre: je fonds, nous fondons. fondre en larmes means to burst into tears.

cards.de: to become again (to turn back into something)
cards.note: Conjugated like devenir and takes être in the passé composé: il est redevenu calme.
For men you would rather say le slip or le caleçon.
Very common in the set phrase en revanche, which means on the other hand.
J'ai signalé le problème au responsable. (I reported the problem to the manager.) Pattern: signaler qc à qn, not signalling with a device.
Personne n'a décroché quand j'ai appelé. (Nobody picked up when I called.) The opposite is raccrocher; it also means to take down a picture and, informally, to land something.
The masculine plural is irregular: centraux; the feminine is centrale.

cards.de: the session (meeting, also a cinema showing)
cards.note: une séance de cinéma is a film showing, une séance de sport a workout.
Pattern: pourvoir qn de qc. With à it means to provide for: pourvoir aux besoins de la famille.

Rare as a noun; usually an adverb: dehors means outside. En dehors de means apart from or outside of. Les enfants jouent dehors depuis ce matin. (The children have been playing outside since this morning.)
The ending -ée is typically feminine. A puppet, by contrast, is la marionnette.
faire une gaffe means to put your foot in it. Informally, fais gaffe! means watch out!
Informally, avoir de la veine means to be lucky.
In the plural, les habits simply means clothes. The h is silent: l'habit, with a liaison in les habits.

cards.de: to comprise (to consist of, to include)
cards.note: Reflexive se comporter means to behave: il se comporte bien.
As an adjective before the noun it means former (mon ancienne voiture), after the noun old or antique.

cards.de: to submit (to put forward for consideration)
cards.note: Nous soumettons notre projet au directeur demain. (We're submitting our project to the director tomorrow.) Conjugated like mettre; se soumettre à means to submit to something.

cards.de: the cabin (on a ship, on a plane)
cards.note: Also a fitting room in a shop. Une cabine téléphonique is a phone box.
Le sel et le poivre go together. After a quantity the article drops: un peu de sel.
The pattern is enseigner qc à qn: j'enseigne le français aux enfants.
Elle a publié son premier roman l'année dernière. (She published her first novel last year.) Regular like parler, and the related noun is la publication.
Used as an adverb it never changes: ça coûte cher, payer cher. As an adjective it does: chère, chers.
Very common in speech: ça pue ici. It can take an object too: Ses chaussures puent le fromage. (His shoes stink of cheese.)
Conjugated like recevoir: je déçois, nous décevons. The participle is déçu: je suis déçu de toi.
Une planche à repasser is an ironing board, and faire la planche means to float on your back.

cards.de: the drama (a serious play or event)
cards.note: Masculine despite the -e ending. En faire un drame means to make a big deal of it.
La cérémonie de mariage is the wedding ceremony. Sans cérémonie means without any fuss.
Usually placed before the noun, and feminine is maudite. Ce maudit ordinateur ne marche jamais. (This damned computer never works.) It is the participle of maudire.
Consulter un médecin, un dictionnaire, ses mails. Le médecin consulte le matin means he holds surgery hours.
Feminine is douloureuse. It belongs to la douleur, pain.
A single subtitle is le sous-titre, plural les sous-titres.
Conjugated like prendre: j'entreprends, nous entreprenons. Pattern: entreprendre de faire qc. Il a entrepris de réparer la voiture tout seul. (He set about repairing the car on his own.)

S'exciter means to get worked up: Les enfants s'excitent avant les vacances. (The children get worked up before the holidays.) Careful: être excité often sounds sexual, so for looking forward to something say être impatient.
Same form for both genders. C'est absurde! is a very common exclamation.
From le voile, the veil. Le ciel se voile peu à peu. (The sky is slowly clouding over.)
Masculine, and the final c is silent. Avoir mal à l'estomac means to have a stomach ache.
Feminine, like almost all nouns ending in -tion. Common phrase: selon la tradition.
The adjective form is de luxe, as in un hôtel de luxe. Note the x, not ss.
Feminine. Very common in à merveille (wonderfully): ça marche à merveille.
The pattern is soupçonner qn de qc, so French uses de where English uses of. La police le soupçonne du vol. (The police suspect him of the theft.) Noun: le soupçon.

cards.de: the pair (two things that go together)
cards.note: Feminine: une paire de chaussures. A pair of people is un couple instead.
You say prendre un médicament. The pharmacist is le pharmacien.
Le ballon is the big inflated ball, la balle the small one (tennis). It also means balloon.
Pattern: suggérer qc à qn. Je te suggère un autre restaurant. (I suggest another restaurant to you.) After suggérer que the subjonctif is often used.
Feminine: la cloche. Informally une cloche also means an idiot.
Also used of water: to make it cloudy. Son regard me trouble beaucoup. (His look really unsettles me.) Reflexive: se troubler, to get flustered.
Feminine form officielle with a double l. Adverb: officiellement.
Masculine. In a French meal the cheese comes before dessert.

cards.de: to hang up (end a phone call)
cards.note: Literally to hang back up, from accrocher. Elle a raccroché sans dire au revoir. (She hung up without saying goodbye.) Opposite: décrocher, to pick up.
Feminine. Learn the set phrase par conséquent (consequently).
To have an operation is se faire opérer. Le médecin m'a opéré du genou. (The doctor operated on my knee.) More generally it can mean to bring about or to go about something.
Usually plural in French, unlike the English uncountable: faire ses bagages (to pack). The singular is also figurative: bagage culturel.
Feminine: la rive gauche in Paris. By the sea you would rather say le rivage or la côte.
Masculine. It also means appearance: sous cet aspect (from this point of view). The final t is silent.
Une station de métro, but a train station is la gare. Also une station de ski (ski resort).
The feminine is la lionne. Common phrase: avoir un appétit de lion.

cards.de: the outfit (a particular set of clothes)
cards.note: Une tenue de soirée, en tenue de sport. Tenue also means good behaviour: un peu de tenue!
Masculine. Set phrases: à mon grand regret, sans regret, j'ai des regrets.
Colloquial for comprendre: Désolé, je n'ai rien pigé. (Sorry, I didn't get any of it.) Use comprendre in writing.
La pile also means a pile or stack (une pile de livres). As an adverb it means sharp: à huit heures pile.
Masculine: l'océan Atlantique. The accented e is pronounced as its own syllable: o-cé-an.
From profond, with é before -ment. Dormir profondément, respirer profondément.
Irregular: je vaincs, il vainc, nous vainquons, past participle vaincu. Vaincre qn takes a direct object.
Slang for killing someone: Ils ont buté le témoin. (They bumped off the witness.) In neutral use, buter contre qc means to bump into or trip over something.
Feminine. Une paille is also a drinking straw: boire à la paille.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. La libération d'un prisonnier; the verb is libérer.
Very common in the negative: pas forcément means not necessarily. Si tu es fatigué, ce n'est pas forcément grave. (If you are tired, it is not necessarily serious.)
Farm vocabulary: la ferme, la grange, l'étable. Don't mix it up with orange.
avoir accès à qc means to have access to something. The final s is silent.
suspendre qc à qc. Second meaning: to suspend or break off (la séance est suspendue).
Le public a sifflé le joueur pendant tout le match. (The crowd booed the player the whole match.) In a stadium siffler qn means to boo. The noun is un sifflet, a whistle.
Feminine form: la portière. Careful, la portière also means a car door.
Colloquial, roughly like calling someone a girl or a chick. The male counterpart is un mec.
La mariée is the bride, and les mariés are the newlyweds.
prendre qc au sérieux means to take something seriously. The form is the same in the singular and the plural.
affronter qn/qc takes a direct object with no preposition, unlike English to face up to. Il faut affronter la réalité. (We have to face reality.)

cards.de: the dish (fine food served at a meal)
cards.note: Formal in tone, often un mets raffiné. Singular and plural look the same, and it is not the verb form tu mets.
Fairly literary. Irregular: il luit, il a lui. Related to la lumière and luisant.
On fête l'anniversaire de ma sœur samedi. (We are celebrating my sister's birthday on Saturday.) For going out and partying, everyday French says faire la fête.
The same word also means layer: une couche de peinture, la couche d'ozone.
tracer une ligne, un trait. Nowadays it also means to track: tracer un colis.
It comes from le poing (fist). Le poignet is also the cuff of a shirt.

cards.de: new (masculine form before a vowel, as in un ... appartement)
cards.note: nouveau becomes nouvel before a vowel or a silent h: un nouvel ami. The feminine is nouvelle.
The form is the same for both genders. Common phrase: une baguette magique (magic wand).
It comes from produire. It can also mean proceeds: le produit des ventes.
Formed from vieux and conjugated like finir. Used transitively: cette coiffure te vieillit (makes you look older).
It describes polite, obliging behaviour, not being lovable. Polite formula: c'est très aimable à vous.
Feminine form: une cochonne. As an adjective it is informal for dirty or filthy.
Usually plural: suivre les instructions. In the singular it can also mean education or schooling.
Same form for both genders. As a noun: la physique (the subject), le physique (someone's looks).
Masculine, pronounced [eko], with ch sounding like k. Idiom: se faire l'écho de qc (to pass something on).
Masculine, like almost all nouns ending in -age. Do not mix it up with orange.
Feminine, even though it comes from the Latin for father (pater). For everyday talk about home, say mon pays.
This is the adverb; for the adjective use tardif, and en retard for someone behind time. Il rentre toujours tard le vendredi soir. (He always gets home late on Friday evenings.)

cards.de: the flank (side of a body or a mountain)
cards.note: The final c is silent. Colloquially, tirer au flanc means to shirk or skive off.
J'épargne un peu d'argent chaque mois. (I save a little money every month.) It also means to spare someone, and épargner qc à qn means to spare someone something.
The final d is usually pronounced. Say dans le sud de la France, au sud de Paris.

cards.de: the connection, link (also a love affair)
cards.note: Feminine, like all nouns ending in -aison. It is also the linking of sounds in speech: faire la liaison.
This is the past participle of blesser used as a noun. Feminine: une blessée.
The ending -nct is silent, so it sounds like [ɛ̃stɛ̃]. Common phrase: d'instinct, instinctively.
Typical phrase: avoir la certitude que ... The opposite is le doute.
Derived from cheval, so literally a horseman. The feminine une chevalière is rare and usually means a signet ring.

cards.de: to seize, take possession of (grab something for oneself)
cards.note: Only used reflexively: s'emparer de qc. Also figurative: la panique s'empare de lui.
You say porter une cravate and nouer sa cravate, to knot your tie.

cards.de: that is to say, in other words
cards.note: It is often continued with que: c'est-à-dire que je ne peux pas venir. Written short as c.-à-d.
Masculine plural royaux, feminine royale. Le roi is the king.
Used as comparer qc à qc or avec qc. Ne compare pas ta vie à celle des autres. (Don't compare your life to other people's.) The noun is la comparaison.
Jouer la comédie means to act in a play, but also to put on an act for someone.
Plural with x: des choux. Mon chou is also a term of endearment, like sweetie.
Nouns ending in -sion are always feminine. The verb is exploser.
Spelled with a double n, from la raison. Also used for prices: un prix raisonnable.
From la glace, ice. L'eau du lac est glacée en avril. (The lake water is ice cold in April.) Un thé glacé is an iced tea, un accueil glacé an icy welcome.
Feminine, related to English barque. A bigger or more modern boat is le bateau.
Masculine, despite the -e ending. Au chapitre trois means in chapter three.
Feminine form absolue. The adverb absolument (absolutely, definitely) is far more common.
Rien ne justifie une telle violence. (Nothing justifies such violence.) Reflexive se justifier means to justify oneself. The word for justice is la justice.
Je fais chauffer de l'eau pour le thé. (I'm heating up water for the tea.) The related noun is le chauffage, heating.
With no article, vendredi means on Friday, while le vendredi means on Fridays. French writes days of the week in lower case.
Feminine form: la voyageuse. On trains you often hear avis aux voyageurs, attention passengers.
Feminine: divine. Also used as praise in everyday speech: c'est divin!
Usually singular as a collective noun: le matériel de camping. As an adjective, matériel means material.
It takes a direct object with no preposition, unlike English to approve of something. Le conseil a approuvé notre décision. (The board approved our decision.)
Formal; in everyday French people say fatigué. Feminine: lasse, and être las de qc means to be tired of something.
Often in the phrase tout particulièrement, most especially. Ce film m'a particulièrement plu. (I particularly liked this film.)
C'est une évidence means that is obvious. A key phrase is mettre en évidence, to highlight.
Capitalised for a person, but lower case for the language or the adjective: il parle italien, un plat italien.
Don't forget the cedilla, which keeps the c soft; without it the word would sound like a k. Also figurative: ce n'est qu'une façade.
Une lame de rasoir is a razor blade. Une lame de fond is a huge wave or groundswell.
French needs à where English uses a direct object. J'ai échoué à mon examen de conduite. (I failed my driving test.) Reflexive s'échouer means to run aground.
You say prendre l'ascenseur, literally to take the lift. The noun is masculine: un ascenseur.
Same form for masculine and feminine: une page vierge, un CD vierge. As a noun, la vierge means virgin.
Être assis describes the state of sitting, while s'asseoir is the action of sitting down. Il est assis au fond de la classe. (He is sitting at the back of the class.) Feminine: assise.
The pattern is autoriser qn à faire qc. Often passive: je ne suis pas autorisé à entrer.
The feminine is irregular: la veuve. You say être veuf with no article.
It follows the regular finir pattern: je rougis, nous rougissons. Elle rougit chaque fois qu'il lui parle. (She blushes every time he speaks to her.)
It also means the unit of length, an inch. Informally, manger sur le pouce means to grab a quick bite standing up.
Use guider qn with no preposition. Une amie nous a guidés dans la vieille ville. (A friend guided us through the old town.) The related noun is le guide, a guide or guidebook.
A military rank, often used as a form of address in films: Oui, sergent!
The same form serves both genders: un adulte, une adulte. It also works as an adjective: un film pour adultes.
It belongs to the verb tirer, to shoot. Le tir à l'arc is archery.
In a theatre, le balcon is the dress circle. You say sur le balcon.
The masculine plural is moraux. As a noun, le moral means spirits or mood: avoir le moral, to be in good spirits.

cards.de: to trim, to cut (a hedge, cloth, a pencil)
cards.note: Mon père taille la haie tous les printemps. (My father trims the hedge every spring.) Tailler un crayon means to sharpen a pencil, and informally se tailler means to clear off.
Far more common reflexively: se dérouler means to take place or unfold. L'histoire se déroule à Paris.
It works both with and without an object: augmenter les prix, but also les prix augmentent.
Ma soeur me coiffe avant chaque fête. (My sister does my hair before every party.) Se coiffer means to do your own hair, and le coiffeur is the hairdresser.

cards.de: to mess about, to talk nonsense
cards.note: Very colloquial and only used among friends. Arrête de déconner, on est en retard. (Stop messing about, we're late.) Sans déconner? means Seriously?
It usually goes before the adjective, and a synonym is complètement. Tu as totalement raison sur ce point. (You are totally right on that point.)
Every noun ending in -sion is feminine. You say à la télévision for on television, shortened to la télé.

cards.de: the judgement (court ruling, also judgement as a faculty)
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ment are masculine. It covers both a court's verdict and the ability to judge well.
Ce médicament soulage la douleur en dix minutes. (This medicine relieves the pain in ten minutes.) Soulager qn de qc means to relieve someone of something, and je suis soulagé means I am relieved.
Same form for both genders. Common: un prix fixe, une heure fixe, regarder qn fixement.
Ils ont fondé leur entreprise il y a dix ans. (They founded their company ten years ago.) Se fonder sur qc means to be based on something.

cards.de: popular (with the people, of the people)
cards.note: It covers both popular and folk. Une chanson populaire is a folk song, not just a hit.
Elle tord le linge avant de l'étendre. (She wrings the washing before hanging it out.) Very common as a reflexive: se tordre la cheville, to twist your ankle.
Le chat gratte la porte depuis ce matin. (The cat has been scratching the door since this morning.) Se gratter la tête means to scratch your head, and informally it also means to scrape off.
Common: avoir la conviction que. Parler avec conviction means to speak with conviction.
Une personne âgée is an elderly person. To give an age: être âgé de vingt ans.

cards.de: the atmosphere (mood or layer of air)
cards.note: Feminine despite the consonant ending. Une atmosphère détendue, a relaxed atmosphere.
En rond means in a circle, for example s'asseoir en rond. As an adjective, rond, ronde means round.
Un ami intime is a close friend, with no sexual meaning implied. Same form for both genders.
Prendre son élan means to take a run-up. The same word also means elk.
Masculine. Garder l'équilibre, to keep your balance, perdre l'équilibre, to lose it.
Masculine. Une table en marbre, a marble table.
Used for textiles, not for material or subject matter in general. Also biological: le tissu musculaire.
Feminine. Regular plural: des villas.
Construction: demander la permission de faire qc. In the army, une permission also means leave.
Feminine form expresse: une interdiction expresse. As an adverb, faire exprès means to do something on purpose.
Masculine. Not an accident, which would be un accident. Sans incident means without a hitch.

cards.de: the grain (single seed of cereal or sand)
cards.note: Un grain de sable, un grain de raisin (a grape). Do not confuse it with la graine, meaning a seed for planting.
Nouns ending in -gramme are masculine: le programme, le kilogramme, le télégramme.

cards.de: to parry, to ward off (a blow, an attack)
cards.note: Le boxeur a paré le coup avec son bras. (The boxer warded off the blow with his arm.) With a preposition, parer à qc means to guard against something.
Masculine. A common reflexive use is se muscler, to build up muscle.
The feminine form is la championne with double n. Le championnat is the championship.
passer une commande means to place an order. In the plural, les commandes can also mean the controls of a vehicle.
Only used reflexively: le mur s'est écroulé. It also works for people collapsing from exhaustion.
Feminine. Capitalised and in the plural, les Écritures means the Scriptures.
Very colloquial, even crude: la voiture est foutue. Before the noun, un foutu problème means a damn problem.
Elle a accepté de témoigner au procès. (She agreed to testify at the trial.) Témoigner en faveur de qn means to testify for someone, and témoigner de qc means to bear witness to something.
Above all learn the phrase en dépit de, meaning in spite of. par dépit means out of spite.
Masculine. à l'extérieur means outside or on the outside; the opposite is l'intérieur.
Careful: le studio usually means a one-room flat, not only a film or recording studio.
The plural takes x: les vœux. Meilleurs vœux! is what you say at New Year.
From étonner, to astonish. After c'est étonnant que you need the subjonctif.
Before the noun, demi never changes: deux demi-heures. After the noun it agrees: une heure et demie.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Ça fait une éternité! means It's been ages.
The feminine form is féminine. Le genre féminin is the grammatical gender.

cards.de: to visit regularly, to associate with
cards.note: No preposition is needed. Il fréquente cette fille depuis six mois. (He has been seeing that girl for six months.) Fréquenter qn means to spend time with someone, and often to be dating them.
Feminine. avec méthode means methodically, in a systematic way.
Conjugated like conduire: je traduis, nous traduisons, past participle traduit. The pattern is traduire de l'anglais en français.
Feminine form régulière. Opposite: irrégulier. Common uses: un rythme régulier, un client régulier (a regular customer).
Je balaie la cuisine après le dîner. (I sweep the kitchen after dinner.) An -ayer verb, so both je balaie and je balaye are correct. The related noun is le balai (broom).
Bare jeudi means on Thursday (one specific day), while le jeudi means on Thursdays in general.
Colloquial and a bit milder than énerver. Arrête d'embêter ton frère! (Stop bothering your brother!) Reflexive s'embêter means to be bored.
Masculine: le commerce. It can also mean a single shop: un petit commerce. Related adjective: commercial.
The accent shifts with stress: j'exagère but nous exagérons. Very common as an exclamation: Tu exagères!
Conjugated like mettre, past participle transmis. Pattern: transmettre qc à qn. Je transmettrai ton message à Julie. (I'll pass your message on to Julie.)
Used as bourrer qc de qc. Elle a bourré sa valise de vêtements. (She stuffed her suitcase with clothes.) Colloquially, être bourré means to be drunk.
In everyday speech it is almost always shortened to la photo. Nouns ending in -ie are feminine.
A regular -ir verb: je vomis, nous vomissons. Le petit a vomi toute la nuit. (The little one threw up all night.) It is never reflexive in French.
Also used as an adjective: une page vierge is a blank page, une forêt vierge a virgin forest.
Masculine: le garage. It also means a repair shop for cars.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. Common: la population locale, la population active (the working population).
Used for temperature: Il fait vingt degrés. Also figuratively: à un certain degré, au plus haut degré.
Ton nouveau travail m'impressionne beaucoup. (Your new job impresses me a lot.) Note the double n of the ending -onner. The adjective is impressionnant.
Masculine despite the silent -t. Common: l'écart entre les deux, à l'écart de (away from, apart from).
Feminine: l'Union européenne. Remember the saying L'union fait la force.
Elle déshabille son fils avant le bain. (She undresses her son before the bath.) Reflexive se déshabiller means to get undressed. Opposite: habiller.
Often faire des sacrifices pour qn. The victim of a crime is la victime, not le sacrifice.
Only exists as a reflexive verb: il s'écria: Au secours! Typical of narrative writing.
Feminine form: prisonnière. Also a noun, a prisoner: faire qn prisonnier.
Masculine despite the -ée ending, like le lycée and le trophée. You say aller au musée.
Built as se soucier de qc/qn. Very often negative: il ne s'en soucie pas.
Feminine la baronne with double n. Figuratively too: un baron de la drogue, a drug baron.
Nous envisageons de déménager à Lyon l'année prochaine. (We are considering moving to Lyon next year.) Usually envisager de faire qc. It contains visage (face), so literally to face up to something.
An -ir verb like finir: l'eau jaillit de la source. Also figurative, for ideas that suddenly burst out.
Feminine civile: la guerre civile. L'état civil means civil status or the registry office.
Borrowed from English and feminine: Miss France. Also a casual way to address a young woman.
Un panier à linge is a laundry basket. In basketball, un panier is also a scored basket.

cards.de: to entail (to have as a consequence)
cards.note: Also to involve: être impliqué dans une affaire. Don't mix it up with expliquer.
Takes a direct object with no preposition: heurter un mur. Figuratively se heurter à un problème.
Feminine la danseuse. Un danseur étoile is a principal dancer.
Also a loop or buckle: les boucles d'oreilles are earrings.
Les étudiants protestent contre la nouvelle loi. (The students are protesting against the new law.) Built as protester contre qc. The noun is une protestation.
Informal and always reflexive: on s'est bien marrés. Related adjective: marrant (funny).
Feminine discrète with an accent grave. Adverb: discrètement.
In slang, le blé also means money, like dough in English.
Son voisin l'a dénoncé à la police. (His neighbour reported him to the police.) Built as dénoncer qn à la police. Also used for terminating a contract.
Plural takes an x: les cailloux, like bijou and genou.
Common phrase: à la satisfaction générale, to everyone's satisfaction.
en direct means live on TV or radio, and un train direct runs without any changes.
The form stays the same in the feminine: une eau tiède. Figuratively too: un accueil tiède, a cool welcome.
It also means the hand of a clock: la grande aiguille.
As an adverbial phrase: d'ordinaire, usually.
Il est urgent de partir. After il est urgent que you need the subjonctif.
acheter à crédit means to buy in instalments.
Derived from roi, king. Le Royaume-Uni is the United Kingdom.
Il nie avoir pris l'argent. (He denies having taken the money.) Also used as nier que with the subjonctif.
To queue up is faire la queue, not faire la file. à la file means one after another.
Je perçois un changement dans son attitude. (I perceive a change in his attitude.) Conjugated like recevoir: je perçois. A second meaning is to collect taxes.
Note the accent circonflexe on the a. mettre des bâtons dans les roues means to put a spanner in the works.
Usually without an article when talking about the material: en acier inoxydable, made of stainless steel.
Also to show a feeling: manifester sa joie. Reflexive se manifester means to get in touch.
Don't mix it up with le casque, which is a helmet. Very common: une casquette de baseball.

cards.de: the human (as a member of the species)
cards.note: People usually say un être humain. As an adjective, humain means human or humane.
The feminine form is la joueuse. It also works as an adjective: il est très joueur, he is very playful.
Very often reflexive: se situer, to be located. Le magasin se situe près de la gare.
As an adjective it never changes: les roues avant. The opposite is arrière.
The feminine is confuse. It can also mean embarrassed: je suis confus, I'm sorry, how embarrassing.
The final s is always there, even in the singular. Very common: faire des progrès, to make progress.
From s'amuser, to have fun. Feminine: amusante.
Also the spark plug in an engine. Souffler les bougies means to blow out the candles.
Also a written stroke or line, and a bar of chocolate: une barre de chocolat.
Feminine form: une assistante. Une assistante sociale is a social worker.
Feminine form: la visiteuse. Do not confuse it with la visite, which is the visit itself.

cards.de: to buckle up, to fasten (a belt)
cards.note: Boucle ta ceinture avant de démarrer. (Fasten your seatbelt before starting.) From la boucle, a buckle, which also means a curl: cheveux bouclés, curly hair.
A colloquial equivalent of amusant. The related verb se marrer means to laugh your head off.
Month names are masculine and written in lower case, unlike in English. In October is en octobre.
Je trempe mon croissant dans le café. (I dip my croissant in the coffee.) Pattern: tremper qc dans qc. Être trempé means to be soaking wet.
Feminine: compliquée. Common phrase: c'est compliqué à expliquer.
Crude word. Informally it also means to break: le verre a pété. Péter les plombs means to lose it.
The French spelling takes an accent: shérif. The h is silent.
La galerie also means the upper circle in a theatre and a roof rack on a car.
It also means a caption under a picture and the key of a map, just like English legend.
Le groupe a enregistré son premier album à Paris. (The band recorded its first album in Paris.) Also means to register or log something, and to check in at the airport: enregistrer ses bagages.
Masculine noun. At the table people say Bon appétit !
It covers schooling too: l'Éducation nationale is the state education system.
Often used as sans motif, for no reason. It also means a pattern on fabric or wallpaper.
A feminine noun. Contrast en théorie with en pratique.
Feminine noun. Like English, it also means humaneness: traiter qn avec humanité.
Set phrase: un vol à main armée (armed robbery). Le béton armé means reinforced concrete.
In the plural, les dessous means underwear or the hidden side of an affair. Le dessous de la table est couvert de poussière. (The underside of the table is covered in dust.)
As a reply it means exactly so; related verb: préciser (to specify). C'est précisément ce que je voulais dire. (That is precisely what I wanted to say.)
Elle console son amie de cette mauvaise nouvelle. (She comforts her friend over this bad news.) Structure: consoler qn de qc. The reflexive se consoler means to console oneself.
annuler un rendez-vous, annuler une commande. Noun: une annulation.
Feminine: quotidienne. As a noun, le quotidien means daily life or a daily paper.
Feminine form: une ambassadrice. The embassy is une ambassade.
Structure: destiner qc à qn. Very common in the passive: ce livre est destiné aux enfants.
Figuratively it also means one part or strand of a plan: le volet social de la réforme.
Nouns ending in té are almost always feminine. Common phrase: la dignité humaine.
Attention, le lait déborde de la casserole! (Careful, the milk is overflowing from the pan!) Figuratively: déborder de joie, to be bursting with joy.
Do not confuse it with la marine (the navy) or the adjective marin (sea, as in air marin).
Plural: les tuyaux. Informally, un tuyau also means a tip or inside information.
précéder qn/qc takes a direct object with no preposition: les jours qui ont précédé son départ.
From tendre (to stretch). Common uses: une atmosphère tendue, être tendu avant un examen.
Very common in à portée de main (within reach). It also means a litter of young animals.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Of a slope or path it means steep: une pente raide.
Feminine: généreuse. Also used of portions: une part généreuse.
Le réveil sonne à sept heures. It also means waking up: au réveil.
Masculine. Le grand écran means the cinema, and écran total is sunblock.
Also a set phrase: une formule de politesse is the closing greeting in a letter.
Il est ressorti tout de suite après le dîner. (He went out again right after dinner.) Conjugated like sortir, with être. Figuratively: faire ressortir qc means to highlight something.
Cette chanson m'émeut à chaque fois. (This song moves me every time.) Irregular: j'émeus, participle ému. Very common as être ému, to be moved.
Le secteur public/privé. Colloquially also the mains: brancher sur secteur.
Feminine: lumineuse. Une idée lumineuse is a brilliant idea.
Masculine. In everyday use it sounds slightly disparaging: un individu louche, a shady character.
From brûler. Also figurative: une question brûlante, a burning issue.
Quantities take de with no article: un kilo de pommes.

cards.de: the interview (formal talk, e.g. a job interview)
cards.note: Un entretien d'embauche is a job interview. A second meaning is maintenance or upkeep (frais d'entretien).
Je me réjouis de te revoir bientôt. (I am delighted to see you again soon.) Usually reflexive: se réjouir de qc. Cela me réjouit means that makes me happy.
Also an exclamation in speech: quelle catastrophe! Of a person, c'est une catastrophe means he is hopeless.
Conjugated like recevoir: je conçois, nous concevons, j'ai conçu. A second meaning is to conceive of or imagine.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Proverb: l'habit ne fait pas le moine, roughly the clothes do not make the man.
Stronger than seulement: il pense uniquement à lui. It comes from unique, meaning sole.
Do not confuse it with dépendre de, to depend on. Reflexive se dépenser means to use up one's energy. Je dépense trop d'argent au restaurant. (I spend too much money at restaurants.)
From jouer. Nouns ending in -et are masculine: un jouet en bois.
Colloquial; the neutral word is laid. Also figurative: c'est moche ce qu'il a fait means that was a nasty thing to do.
Feminine form chinoise. The language is lower case: je parle chinois; the person is capitalised: un Chinois.
Usually un bouquet de fleurs. C'est le bouquet! colloquially means that's the last straw.
Mes chaussures sont complètement mouillées. (My shoes are completely wet.) Participle of mouiller, to wet; se mouiller means to get wet. For weather, use humide instead.
Same form for a woman: la pilote. Also pilote de course = racing driver and projet pilote = pilot project.
Ça y est, c'est fini! As an adjective also produit fini = finished product.
Nouns ending in -esse are feminine. Avoir un moment de faiblesse = to have a moment of weakness.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. Prendre des précautions; par précaution = as a precaution.
Capitalised for the person, but the language is lower case and masculine: l'arabe. The adjective arabe is lower case too.
Verb: se suicider = to take one's own life. Also figurative: c'est un suicide politique.
Masculine. A lightning strike is la foudre. En un éclair = in a flash, and un éclair is also a pastry.
Plural: les voyous. Often used as an insult for a cheeky boy: petit voyou!
Also used for floors: il habite au troisième. At school, la troisième is the final year of collège.
Quelqu'un a assassiné le maire hier soir. (Someone murdered the mayor last night.) Assassiner qn takes a direct object with no preposition. Related: un assassin, un assassinat.
Feminine: une habitante. Common phrase: une ville de 50 000 habitants.
From se moucher (to blow one's nose). A tissue is un mouchoir en papier.
Feminine, despite the short form. In economics: l'offre et la demande. A job ad is une offre d'emploi.
Le blessé gémit de douleur sur le sol. (The injured man is groaning in pain on the ground.) Regular -ir verb like finir: je gémis, nous gémissons. Noun: un gémissement.
Often plural: les cendres d'un feu. Do not confuse it with cendrier (ashtray).
Slightly formal; everyday speech uses soûl or bourré. Figuratively: ivre de joie (overjoyed).
A driving lesson is une leçon de conduite. Second meaning: behaviour, une bonne conduite.
Feminine: espagnole. Lower case as an adjective, capitalised only for a person: un Espagnol.
Abstract nouns of this type ending in -eur are feminine. Common: étudier une question en profondeur.
Feminine: rousse, plural: roux. Never use rouge for hair.
sacrifier qc à qn/qc. Reflexive: se sacrifier pour sa famille.
It also means scale: une carte à l'échelle 1/50 000, à grande échelle (on a large scale).

cards.de: to approach, to go up to (someone in the street)
cards.note: Je n'ose jamais aborder les gens dans la rue. [I never dare approach people in the street.] Aborder qn takes no preposition. Also used for topics: aborder un sujet (to bring up a subject).
Past participle of s'endormir (to fall asleep). Also figurative: une ville endormie, a sleepy town.
It also covers the meat, mutton. Idiom: compter les moutons, to count sheep.
The opposite of souvent, and it usually comes straight after the conjugated verb. Mon frère vient rarement nous voir. (My brother rarely comes to see us.)
Masculine. Very common in faire l'impossible, to do everything humanly possible.
La police a réussi à délivrer les otages. [The police managed to free the hostages.] Construction: délivrer qn de qc. In official language it also means to issue: délivrer un passeport.

Je dois communiquer la nouvelle à mes parents ce soir. [I have to pass the news on to my parents tonight.] Communiquer qc à qn, to pass something on to someone. With no object: to communicate with each other.
Colour names are masculine in French. As an adjective: vert, verte.
The everyday word today is la chaussure; soulier sounds old-fashioned or literary.

cards.de: to cut up, to cut out
cards.note: Je vais découper cet article dans le journal. [I'm going to cut this article out of the paper.] With meat it means to carve.
The final s is silent. Colloquially also electricity: il n'y a plus de jus.
Spelt with double t and an accent on the first e: littérature.
Feminine laide. It sounds exactly like le lait (milk).
The related verb is se venger de qn, to take revenge on someone.
Set phrase sain et sauf, safe and sound. Pronounced the same as saint (holy).
Masculine. prendre le large literally means to head for open water, and colloquially to clear off.
