Il a commencé à insulter le chauffeur du bus. [He started insulting the bus driver.] Takes a direct object with no preposition: insulter qn. The noun is une insulte.
Very common in the phrase à la rigueur, meaning at a pinch or if need be.

cards.de: to park (to leave a vehicle somewhere)
cards.note: Je cherche un endroit pour garer ma voiture. [I'm looking for somewhere to park my car.] You say garer sa voiture; when you park yourself, use the reflexive se garer.
Je commence à redouter cet examen de maths. [I'm starting to dread this maths exam.] Used as redouter qc or redouter que + subjonctif. A bit more formal than avoir peur de.
Feminine form: franche. Often heard in pour être franc (to be honest).
It follows the noun and never changes form: les sièges arrière, la roue arrière.
The final l is silent: [uti]. Une boîte à outils is a toolbox.
Also used for books of tickets: un carnet de tickets. Smaller than un cahier, which is an exercise book.
Le parlement vient d'adopter une nouvelle loi. [Parliament has just passed a new law.] So it is not just for children: adopter une loi means to pass a law.
Masculine, pronounced [ɔʁɡœj] with the rare spelling ueil. It usually suggests excessive or haughty pride.
Very common in the plural: les heures d'ouverture, opening hours.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. It can also mean a message or a phone connection.
Faire un scandale means to make a scene or protest loudly.
From casser (to break). Mon téléphone est cassé. Of a person, je suis cassé is colloquial for being exhausted.
Slightly more formal than vraiment and stresses that something genuinely happened. Je ne sais pas ce qui s'est réellement passé hier. (I do not know what really happened yesterday.)
Feminine: une cabane. Une cabane de jardin is a garden shed.

cards.de: to accommodate (to put up someone, also to live somewhere)
cards.note: Loger qn means to put someone up; loger chez qn means to stay at someone's place. Être logé et nourri means board and lodging included.
Si tu laisses ces fruits dehors, ils vont pourrir. [If you leave this fruit outside, it will rot.] An -ir verb conjugated like finir. The participle works as an adjective: un fruit pourri.

Est-ce que vous pouvez me renseigner sur les horaires ? [Can you give me some information about the timetable?] Pattern: renseigner qn sur qc. Very common reflexively: se renseigner sur qc, to find out about something.

cards.de: the dirty trick, the crap (nasty act, junk)
cards.note: Very colloquial, bordering on vulgar. Also used for shoddy goods: c'est de la saloperie.
Construction: être absent de l'école. Opposite: présent.
Je commence à envier ta vie tranquille. [I'm starting to envy your quiet life.] The person is the direct object: je t'envie. The thing envied takes à: envier qc à qn.
Un casque audio means headphones, so you hear the word a lot in everyday life.
Peux-tu citer un exemple concret ? [Can you give a concrete example?] So it is used both for quoting someone's words and for naming or giving something.
Irregular plural: les canaux. A TV channel is usually la chaîne.

cards.de: to undo, to unpack (a knot, a suitcase)
cards.note: Je n'ai pas encore eu le temps de défaire ma valise. [I haven't had time to unpack my suitcase yet.] It is the opposite of faire. Se défaire de qc means to get rid of something.
Plural: les maréchaux. It is the highest military distinction, not an ordinary rank.

cards.de: the mouse (animal, also for a computer)
cards.note: Always feminine, and already spelled with an s in the singular: la souris, les souris.

cards.de: the thought, the reflection (thinking something over)
cards.note: Faire une réflexion instead means to make a (often pointed) remark. Réflexion faite: on second thought.
Short for motocyclette, which is why it is feminine. You travel à moto.
Also used in maths: la racine carrée, the square root.
Au four means baked in the oven. Faire un four is colloquial for being a flop.
Être en tournée means to be on tour. C'est ma tournée means this round is on me.
Feminine form: la citoyenne. Do not confuse it with habitant, an inhabitant.
Pronounced like ...keuil, with the letter group ueil sounding as in oeil.

cards.de: the target (of an attack), the target board
cards.note: Le groupe cible is the target group. Not but, which is a goal you set yourself.
Avoir de l'affection pour qn. In medical language, une affection is an ailment.
Prendre d'assaut means to storm something, also figuratively about shops being mobbed.
Feminine form: mortelle. Colloquially, c'est mortel can also mean deadly boring.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Common in official language: le véhicule est immobilisé.
Very vulgar, typically used as an insult: espèce d'enfoiré ! Feminine form: une enfoirée.
In the plural it often means prospects: les perspectives d'avenir. Also en perspective = in the offing.
Feminine form: continue. Set phrases: en continu (non-stop), courant continu (direct current).
Don't confuse it with journal, which is a daily newspaper. Phrase: passer en revue = to review, to go through.
In casual speech la flotte also means water or rain: il tombe de la flotte.
From la paix. Same form for both genders: un quartier paisible, une vie paisible.
Ce restaurant est très connu dans le quartier. [This restaurant is very well known in the neighbourhood.] Past participle of connaître, often in bien connu. For famous you would rather say célèbre.
Only used reflexively, and with être in the passé composé: elle s'est évanouie. Colloquial: tomber dans les pommes.
Collocation: pousser un soupir (to let out a sigh). Verb: soupirer.
The final t is pronounced here. Feminine form: intacte.
Distraire qn de son travail. Reflexive se distraire = to amuse oneself; distrait means absent-minded.
Also used at the dentist: une couronne dentaire. Verb: couronner.
Feminine form: professionnelle. Common phrase: la vie professionnelle (working life).
Feminine: une criminelle. Also works as an adjective: un acte criminel.
Masculine. Faire un essai = to have a go; un coup d'essai = a first attempt.
Feminine. Watch out: une alliance is also a wedding ring.
De profil = seen from the side, as opposed to de face (from the front).
Colloquial and childlike, and sometimes slightly disparaging for an old woman. More neutral: mamie.
Avant de courir, j'aime étirer mes jambes. [Before running, I like to stretch my legs.] Reflexive s'étirer means to stretch oneself, as you do after waking up.
Same form for both genders: un partenaire, une partenaire.
Regular like parler. Filmer une scène = to shoot a scene.
Masculine noun. The final t stays silent.
Related noun: un défilé = a procession or parade, and also a fashion show.
Feminine. Un pull en laine = a wool jumper.
Sounds exactly like pleine (full), but the two words are unrelated.
Masculine plural: médicaux. Un certificat médical = a doctor's note.
Masculine despite the final e. Les phares are also a car's headlights.
Feminine. It also means an estate and a property in the sense of a quality (les propriétés d'un métal).
Only the building. A musical band is un orchestre or une fanfare.
From prêter (to lend). Don't confuse it with the adjective prêt (ready), which sounds identical.
Month names take no article: en avril. Poisson d'avril is the French April Fool's joke.
Ils veulent bâtir une école dans le village. [They want to build a school in the village.] Slightly more formal than construire. Un homme bien bâti means a well built man.
Un oiseau de proie is a bird of prey. Être en proie à la panique means to be gripped by panic.

cards.de: to insert, to introduce (put something in)
cards.note: Il faut introduire la carte dans la machine. [You have to insert the card into the machine.] Pattern: introduire qc dans qc. Reflexive s'introduire means to break in or slip in.
Fais attention à ne pas bousculer les gens dans le métro. [Be careful not to jostle people on the metro.] Also figurative: bousculer les habitudes, to shake up people's habits.
Always with à: cela correspond à mes attentes. Correspondre avec qn means to exchange letters with someone.

cards.de: the pillow (for the head in bed)
cards.note: It comes from oreille (ear). A cushion on the sofa is un coussin.
Pronounced with a v sound at the start, like vagon. Un wagon-lit is a sleeping car.
Usually a convent for nuns; entrer au couvent means to enter religious life. Spelled like ils couvent (they brood), but pronounced differently.
The verb appears almost only in this phrase. The h is aspirated: le hochement.
The final b is silent, so it sounds like plon. Essence sans plomb means unleaded petrol.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Common pairings: la vie nocturne, un animal nocturne.
Sounds exactly like tante (aunt). Planter la tente means to pitch the tent.

J'essaie d'encourager mon frère à continuer ses études. [I'm trying to encourage my brother to continue his studies.] The pattern is encourager qn à faire qc. In a stadium it also means to cheer someone on.

cards.de: the work (a book or written work)
cards.note: Masculine, unlike une œuvre (a work of art or an artist's whole output). Un ouvrage de référence is a reference work.
Colloquially, quel cirque! means what a fuss or what a circus.
Built from terminer (to end). Very common: une attente interminable.
Same form for both genders. It also means loose or slack (un nœud lâche); as a noun, un lâche is a coward.
Colloquially used for a house or flat too: sa baraque means his place.
The opposite is emménager (to move in). It takes avoir in the passé composé: Nous avons déménagé à Lyon le mois dernier. (We moved to Lyon last month.)
Vivre en province means to live outside Paris, with no dismissive tone in everyday use.
Remember à plusieurs reprises, meaning several times over. It also means a revival or a cover version of a song.
Used as mépriser qn/qc, with no preposition: Il méprise les gens qui mentent. (He despises people who lie.) The noun is le mépris (contempt).
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. Also used for fashion: la collection d'hiver.
Used as projeter de faire qc, and the stem changes: Nous projetons de partir en Italie cet été. (We're planning to go to Italy this summer.) It also means to project, as in showing a film.
Plural only and feminine, with a literary tone. In everyday French you would say le noir or l'obscurité.
In the plural, les transports en commun means public transport.
Feminine, and the -ée ending is a reliable clue here. l'Assemblée nationale is the French parliament.
The final s is pronounced: [urs]. Singular and plural look identical; un ours en peluche = a teddy bear.
The c stays silent. It also means the trunk of the body.
Feminine: attentive. Used as attentif à qc; the adverb is attentivement (écouter attentivement).
Traditionally second is used when there are only two items, deuxième when there are more. The c sounds like a g: segond.

cards.de: the leave (time off granted by an employer)
cards.note: Usually plural: prendre des congés. A holiday trip is rather les vacances.
Feminine la conseillère. Spelled like the verb conseiller (to advise): conseiller qc à qn.
Typical of hiking: un sentier de randonnée.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Also used of income: un salaire modeste.
Feminine la cuisinière, which also means a cooker. The head chef is le chef.
Masculine despite the final e. Common phrase: éteindre un incendie.

cards.de: the slab (stone paving on the ground)
cards.note: Colloquially, avoir la dalle means to be starving.
déclencher une alarme, une crise. Reflexive se déclencher means to go off or start up.
French uses à l'aéroport for both at the airport and to the airport.
Insulting but everyday: espèce de crétin! Feminine la crétine.
It is masculine, while the similar-looking la cigarette is feminine.

cards.de: to cook (food, by heat: boil, bake or fry)
cards.note: Irregular: je cuis, participle cuit. It refers to the food cooking, whereas cuisiner is preparing a meal: Le poulet cuit au four depuis une heure. (The chicken has been cooking in the oven for an hour.)
Sounds just like mer and mère. The town hall is la mairie.
Same form in both genders. In letters: sincères salutations.
From découvrir. Common phrases: faire une découverte, partir à la découverte de.
The feminine is la menteuse. From the verb mentir (à qn).
Used as sacrer qn roi, with no preposition before the title: On l'a sacré roi à vingt ans. (They crowned him king at twenty.) In Quebec French, sacrer also means to swear.
Always singular in French and takes a singular verb, unlike English staff. Spelled like the adjective personnel (personal).
sucer un bonbon, sucer son pouce. It also has a vulgar colloquial sense, so use it with care.
Also a salesperson's commission. In the plural, faire les commissions means to do the shopping.
Rarely used in the plural. Constructions: l'indifférence à l'égard de qn or envers qn.
payer par chèque. A bounced cheque is un chèque sans provision.
It also means a lecture or talk: faire une conférence sur qc. The speaker is le conférencier.
Use être marié avec qn or à qn: Ma sœur est mariée avec un Espagnol. (My sister is married to a Spaniard.) As a noun, les mariés means the bride and groom.
être pris de panique means to be seized by panic. The verb is paniquer.

Reflexive se développer means to develop or grow: L'entreprise développe un nouveau produit. (The company is developing a new product.) Note the double p and the accent aigu, unlike the English spelling.
Month names are masculine and written with a small letter in French. Usually used without an article: en novembre.
Nouns in -eur naming feelings are feminine. faire fureur means to be all the rage.

cards.de: the complaint (formal, also a legal charge)
cards.note: porter plainte contre qn means to file a complaint against someone. It can also mean a moan or groan.
Masculine despite the final -e. Les cuivres are the brass section of an orchestra.
Singular: le bijou. It belongs to the small group of -ou nouns that take -x in the plural (bijou, caillou, chou, genou).
The feminine form is irregular: grecque. The language is le grec.
Common phrases: déclaration d'impôts (tax return), déclaration d'amour. For explaining something, use explication instead.
Same form for masculine and feminine. The noun is la timidité.
Used as affecter qn/qc, with no preposition: Cette nouvelle m'a beaucoup affecté. (That news affected me a lot.) It can also mean to allocate or to feign.
A coloured pencil is un crayon de couleur. Écrire au crayon means to write in pencil.
Only used reflexively, and with être in the passé composé. Son voisin a essayé de se suicider l'an dernier. (His neighbour tried to take his own life last year.)
Masculine. A laptop is un ordinateur portable, often shortened to un portable.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. The related verb is respirer.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -ence. A common phrase is attendre avec impatience, to look forward to something eagerly.
Masculine as a noun: c'est un plus, that's a bonus. Here the final s is pronounced.
Highly offensive, so avoid using it yourself. The neutral words are un homosexuel or un gay.
This h is aspiré, so you say la hanche with no elision. Les mains sur les hanches means with hands on hips.
The feminine form is la chanteuse. For opera you would rather say un chanteur d'opéra.
The s is there in the singular too and stays silent. Un puits de pétrole is an oil well.
A colloquial word for livre. The related verb bouquiner means to read for pleasure.
Said of a person, il est pénible means he is annoying. It is related to la peine, effort or trouble.
Unlike English, month names are written in lower case and take no article: en mars or au mois de mars. All months are masculine.
Very common reflexively: ça se complique (things are getting complicated). Ne complique pas les choses ! (Don't make things complicated!) The adjective is compliqué.

cards.de: the person in love, the lover
cards.note: The feminine is une amoureuse. As an adjective: être amoureux de quelqu'un, to be in love with someone.

cards.de: to circulate, to be going round
cards.note: Also used for traffic and for rumours: le bruit circule. Les voitures circulent mal le matin. (Traffic moves badly in the morning.) Police say Circulez !, meaning Move along!
Also means carrying something out: mettre un plan à exécution, to put a plan into action.

cards.de: to contact, to get in touch with
cards.note: contacter quelqu'un takes no preposition. An alternative is prendre contact avec quelqu'un.
It can refer to a single poem, but un poème is the usual word for that. A poet is un poète.
The noun is la torture. Figuratively: Ce doute me torture depuis des semaines. (This doubt has been tormenting me for weeks.)

cards.de: the Chinese man, the Chinese person
cards.note: Capitalised for the person, but lower case as an adjective or the language: un plat chinois, il parle chinois.
Masculine plural is locaux (les produits locaux). As a noun, un local means premises or a room.
From pourrir, to rot. Colloquially it also means lousy: un temps pourri, dreadful weather.
Common combinations: une agence de voyages (travel agency), une agence immobilière (estate agency).

cards.de: to suck in, to breathe in
cards.note: With à it means to aspire to: aspirer à une vie plus calme. A vacuum cleaner is un aspirateur.
As a noun it only means one's fellow human: aimer son prochain. As an adjective prochain means next (la semaine prochaine).
It also means a wick or a fuse. Idiom: vendre la mèche, to let the cat out of the bag.
The opposite is atterrir, to land. Notre avion décolle dans une heure. (Our plane takes off in an hour.) Literally décoller means to unstick, from coller, to glue.
Nouns ending in -ment are always masculine in French. The verb is documenter, se documenter sur quelque chose.
The opposite is intérieur. As a noun l'extérieur is the outside: à l'extérieur means outdoors.
Feminine, like most nouns in -ie. Common phrase: comme par magie, as if by magic.
Slightly more formal than pourtant and often placed at the start of the sentence. Le film est long; toutefois, il vaut la peine. (The film is long; however, it is worth it.)

cards.de: to deeply upset, to turn upside down
cards.note: bouleverser qn means to shake someone up emotionally: Ce film m'a vraiment bouleversé. (That film really upset me.) Also used for plans: cela bouleverse tout.
Feminine. Worth learning: à l'exception de (with the exception of), sauf exception (barring exceptions).
Feminine: l'économie française. In the plural: faire des économies means to save money.

cards.de: to get (something for someone), to obtain
cards.note: procurer qc à qn = to get something for someone: Mon oncle m'a procuré un travail cet été. (My uncle got me a job this summer.) Reflexive: se procurer qc = to get hold of something for yourself.
Feminine. Very common in the phrase par excellence = the perfect example of.
Feminine. Aller à la piscine = to go to the pool.

cards.de: the main thing, what matters most
cards.note: Masculine, almost always with l': l'essentiel, c'est de participer. As an adjective: essentiel, feminine essentielle.
Feminine. Faire son apparition = to show up. Also used for ghostly apparitions.
Feminine courageuse; the masculine plural stays courageux.
Used as bavarder avec qn: J'ai bavardé avec ma voisine pendant une heure. (I chatted with my neighbour for an hour.) Related: un bavard = a chatterbox, and bavard as an adjective means talkative.
Don't confuse it with étranger (foreign, foreigner). Dans le film, l'homme essaie d'étrangler son voisin. (In the film, the man tries to strangle his neighbour.) S'étrangler = to choke.
Colloquial; the neutral word is cacher. Se planquer = to hide out.
Conjugated like finir: je bondis, nous bondissons. Bondir de joie = to jump for joy.
consentir à qc = to agree to something: Mes parents ont consenti à ce mariage. (My parents agreed to this marriage.) Conjugated like sentir: je consens.
Impersonal: il gèle = it's freezing. The stem becomes gèl-: je gèle, but nous gelons.
réciter un poème, une leçon. Don't confuse it with raconter (to tell a story).
passer une annonce means to place an ad; les petites annonces are the classifieds.
Takes a direct object: féliciter qn de or pour qc, so you congratulate someone on something. Je te félicite pour ton examen ! (Congratulations on your exam!)
Irregular plural: des bonshommes. Un bonhomme de neige is a snowman.
The same word also means a guidebook: un guide de voyage.
Colloquially, ce n'est pas très catholique means something seems a bit dodgy.

cards.de: to walk/take someone back (see them home)
cards.note: Typical uses: raccompagner qn chez lui or à la gare.
prolonger un séjour, un contrat. Se prolonger means to drag on.
Feminine form: la concierge. Classically the person in the lodge of a Parisian apartment block.
The final s belongs to the word and stays in the singular. velours côtelé is corduroy.
Colloquial, so keep it for friends: Elle l'a plaqué après deux ans. (She dumped him after two years.) In rugby plaquer means to tackle, and plaqué or means gold-plated.
As a noun, un solitaire is a loner. It usually follows the noun: une vie solitaire.
Masculine. demander l'asile politique means to apply for political asylum.
faire une pause, to take a break. An interval at the theatre is un entracte instead.
Note the ou spelling and the single n. From gouverner, to govern.

cards.de: the housing estate (on the edge of town)
cards.note: Feminine. In formal use it can also mean city, and cité universitaire is a student hall of residence.
From tranquille, with a double l. On a mangé tranquillement dans le jardin. (We ate calmly in the garden.) Often heard as fais ça tranquillement, take your time over it.
animer une émission, un débat. It also means to bring to life: un dessin animé is a cartoon.
Very common as a reflexive: se ronger les ongles, to bite one's nails. Also figurative: le doute le ronge.

cards.de: the ticket (small one for bus or metro)
cards.note: Used for the bus, the metro and the cinema. For train journeys you say le billet.
Capitalised for the person, lower case for the language: il parle espagnol, j'apprends l'espagnol.
Feminine vilaine. Said to a child it means naughty: ne sois pas vilain!
Conjugated like descendre. With no object it takes être, with an object avoir: il a redescendu les valises.
Don't confuse it with le capital, money or capital. En capitales means in capital letters.

cards.de: the copy (also: a pupil's exam paper)
cards.note: At school une copie is the sheet you hand in: rendre sa copie.

cards.de: to collect (information, donations) or to take in (someone)
cards.note: Conjugated like cueillir: je recueille, nous recueillons. Recueillir un enfant means to take a child into your home.
Reflexive se replier means to withdraw, including in a military sense. Je replie la carte avant de partir. (I fold the map back up before leaving.)

cards.de: the next one (next person in the queue)
cards.note: At a counter you hear Au suivant!, meaning next please. Feminine la suivante.
Mardi on its own means "on Tuesday", while le mardi means "every Tuesday". Mardi gras is Shrove Tuesday.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. Written with a capital A, l'Administration means the state bureaucracy.
Feminine form religieuse. As a noun, une religieuse is a nun, but also a choux pastry cake.
Feminine form définitive. Careful: définitivement means "for good", not "definitely" in the sense of certainly.
Month names are masculine and usually take no article: en décembre, le 5 décembre.
As an adjective, drôle means funny. Very common: un drôle de type, a strange guy.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Common phrase: des produits de première nécessité, basic essentials.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. Common: la disparition d'un enfant; in the press it can also mean someone's death.
Irregular, but conjugated like an -er verb: je cueille, nous cueillons, future je cueillerai.
Feminine form la serveuse. The same word means "server" in computing.
Careful: depending on context, hôte means either host or guest. A female host is l'hôtesse.
Used as distribuer qc à qn. Le professeur distribue les copies aux élèves. (The teacher hands out the papers to the students.) In card games, distribuer les cartes means to deal.
Feminine form la traîtresse. As an adjective, traître means treacherous: un virage traître.
Each ch is pronounced like English "sh". Elle m'a chuchoté un secret à l'oreille. (She whispered a secret in my ear.)
Same form in the masculine and the feminine. The opposite is invisible.
Also a legal term: un mandat d'arrêt is an arrest warrant. The final t stays silent.
Informal: c'est fichu means "it's all over". Placed before the noun, un fichu caractère means "a rotten temper".
Originally a chariot, which is why it also means a carnival float. In Quebec, char is a colloquial word for car.
Plural takes x: les panneaux. Also un panneau solaire (solar panel), un panneau publicitaire (billboard).
Related to chaussure. Usually used in the plural: une paire de chaussettes.
The final t is silent. Set phrases: tirer profit de qc, au profit de (in aid of).
Une plaie is the open wound itself, while une blessure is an injury more generally. Informally: quelle plaie ! (what a nuisance).
Used with avec qn or envers qn. Also for things: une critique sévère.
Do not confuse it with the verb lire (to read), which is spelled the same.

cards.de: the ring (plain band, also a link in a chain)
cards.note: Plural anneaux. A ring worn as jewellery is usually une bague.
avoir des soupçons sur qn. Un soupçon de sel also means a tiny pinch.

cards.de: to close (bring to an end, conclude)
cards.note: A defective verb, mostly seen as the participle clos and in fixed phrases. Le président a clos le débat après une heure. (The chairman closed the debate after an hour.) For doors use fermer.
Feminine chère. Placed before the noun, cher means dear: un cher ami, chère Madame.
Feminine élégante. Also figurative: une solution élégante.
Almost always reflexive: le toit s'est effondré. Also of people: elle s'est effondrée en larmes.
Masculine, but month names take no article and are written in lower case: en janvier, le 3 janvier.

cards.de: any (any one at all, no matter which)
cards.note: It follows the noun: un prétexte quelconque. In that position it can also mean mediocre.

cards.de: to try, to make an effort
cards.note: Used as tâcher de faire qc. Je vais tâcher d'arriver à l'heure. (I will try to arrive on time.) Mind the accent: tacher without it means to stain.
Two patterns: consister en qc and consister à faire qc. Mon travail consiste à répondre aux clients. (My job consists in answering customers.)
Feminine une espionne. The verb espionner qn takes a direct object, no preposition.
Le sofa is also heard informally. In cooking, un canapé is a small appetiser.
The most senior non commissioned rank, feminine une adjudante. Addressed as mon adjudant.
Feminine noun. It used to mean a small box for money or jewellery.

cards.de: to proceed (go about something step by step)
cards.note: Construction: procéder à qc means to carry something out, e.g. procéder à un vote. Conjugated like céder: je procède.
From frais, fraîche. Covers both the freshness of food and the pleasant cool of the evening.

cards.de: to seduce (also: to charm, to appeal to)
cards.note: Like conduire: je séduis, nous séduisons, séduit. Cette idée me séduit = the idea appeals to me.

cards.de: the floor (wooden floor of a room)
cards.note: Le plancher is the floor inside a room, while le sol is the ground in general. Idiom: le plancher des vaches = dry land.
Usually la paume de la main. Do not confuse it with la pomme (apple).
Masculine despite the -e ending. Common: remporter un triomphe, and porter quelqu'un en triomphe.
Countable in French: un légume is one kind of vegetable, and you usually say les légumes in the plural.

cards.de: the approach, the procedure (also: the paperwork, the official steps)
cards.note: faire les démarches nécessaires = to take the necessary steps or deal with the formalities. It also means a person's way of walking.
Far more common in the reflexive: s'apprêter à faire qc means to be about to do something. Je m'apprêtais à sortir quand tu as appelé. (I was about to go out when you called.)
Nouns ending in -iste have one form for both genders: un touriste, une touriste.
un cahier de brouillon is a rough book. A book is le livre and a small notebook is le carnet.

cards.de: late, deceased (formal, placed before the name)
cards.note: Formal and rare: feu mon père = my late father. Do not confuse it with le feu (fire).

cards.de: to practise, to do (a sport, a profession)
cards.note: pratiquer un sport, pratiquer la médecine. Un catholique pratiquant is a practising Catholic.

cards.de: the person in charge, the person responsible
cards.note: Same form for both genders: une responsable. Construction: être responsable de qc.
Masculine, and literally a doubling of bon. A piece of chocolate is un chocolat, not un bonbon.
Usually placed after the noun. C'est mon film préféré depuis l'enfance. (It has been my favourite film since childhood.) The verb is préférer qc à qc.
Formed from chaud. Je réchauffe la soupe au micro-ondes. (I am warming up the soup in the microwave.) The reflexive se réchauffer means to warm oneself up.
Before a noun it takes de: suffisamment de temps. Je n'ai pas suffisamment dormi cette nuit. (I did not sleep enough last night.)
The related verb is caresser (to stroke). Common: faire une caresse à quelqu'un.

cards.de: to eliminate, to get rid of
cards.note: Il faut éliminer le sucre de ton petit déjeuner. (You need to cut sugar out of your breakfast.) In sport, être éliminé means to be knocked out.
It keeps the final s even in the singular. A common phrase is avoir des remords.

cards.de: the debt (money you have to pay back)
cards.note: Usually plural: faire des dettes. Moral guilt or fault is la faute instead.
A second meaning is to line or border something, as in une route bordée d'arbres.
Formal in tone. The same form serves both genders: une autorité suprême.
The pattern is recommander qc à qn. Je te recommande ce restaurant italien. (I recommend this Italian restaurant to you.) Une lettre recommandée is a registered letter.
The masculine plural is irregular: idéaux.
It also means to overtake in traffic and to dub a film.
The sc is pronounced like a simple s sound. Cette histoire me fascine depuis des années. (This story has fascinated me for years.) The adjective is fascinant.

cards.de: to vote (cast a vote in an election)
cards.note: The pattern is voter pour quelqu'un. Dimanche, je vais voter pour la première fois. (On Sunday I am going to vote for the first time.) For choosing between things, use choisir.
Built on the verb admirer, to admire. The same form is used for both genders.
Often plural: les noces d'or, a golden wedding anniversary. Informally, faire la noce means to go out partying.
Feminine and used only in the singular, even though English says dishes. Faire la vaisselle means to do the washing-up.
A typical phrase is éprouver de la reconnaissance envers qn. The same word also means recognition and military reconnaissance.
The same form is used for both genders. Common: un geste brusque, un changement brusque.
Always with à: succéder à qn dans une fonction. Reflexive se succéder means to follow one another.
Ton cadeau a enchanté ma fille. (Your present delighted my daughter.) This is where the greeting Enchanté! comes from, meaning pleased to meet you. It also works literally, of magic.
Used as a title: l'abbé Martin, roughly like Father Martin. Le père abbé is the abbot of a monastery.
It belongs to se comporter, to behave. Common: le comportement envers les autres.
Irregular: j'acquiers, nous acquérons, j'ai acquis. Common: acquérir de l'expérience.
Masculine and spelled without a final e, unlike the verb oublier. Tomber dans l'oubli means to be forgotten.
Typical structure: ça grouille de. La plage grouille de touristes en août. (The beach is swarming with tourists in August.) Colloquially, se grouiller means to hurry up.
Formed from the adjective soigneux, soigneuse. Common phrase: ranger soigneusement ses affaires.
Takes a direct object: contrer une attaque, contrer qn. It is unrelated to rencontrer, to meet.
Nouns of this type ending in eur are feminine, like largeur and hauteur. À longueur de journée means all day long.

cards.de: the innocent person, the innocent one
cards.note: Feminine form: une innocente. Faire l'innocent means to play innocent.
Colloquially un régiment de means a huge number, as in un régiment d'enfants.

cards.de: to go for a stroll, to wander around (informal)
cards.note: The reflexive form is very common in everyday speech instead of se promener. On va se balader au bord de la rivière? (Shall we go for a stroll along the river?) Transitive balader qn means to take someone around.
Usually used without an object: errer dans les rues. To be mistaken is se tromper, not errer.
Feminine form: la pêcheuse. Do not confuse it with le pécheur, the sinner, which has no circumflex.
Feminine petite, where the t becomes audible. Used adverbially in petit à petit, little by little.
Derived from bon. Polite formula: auriez-vous la bonté de ..., would you be so kind as to ...

cards.de: to make stiffen, to congeal (movement, fat, blood)
cards.note: Mostly reflexive: se figer, to freeze or stiffen. Elle s'est figée en entendant le bruit. (She froze when she heard the noise.) Un sourire figé is a fixed, forced smile.
A military unit larger than a company. Also used figuratively: un bataillon de journalistes.
The opposite of boucher, to cork or block. Tu peux déboucher la bouteille de vin ? (Can you uncork the bottle of wine?) Also déboucher sur qc, to lead to something.
Often un dur à cuire, a hard nut. As an adjective, dur, dure means hard.

cards.de: to stuff, to shove (put somewhere, informal)
cards.note: Very colloquial: où as-tu fourré mes clés? It also means lined or filled: des gants fourrés, un gâteau fourré.
Feminine finale, plural finals or finaux. La finale is the final match.
Feminine la Grecque, spelled with qu. Written in lower case as an adjective or the language: le grec.
Slightly more formal than fêter. Célébrer un anniversaire, une messe, une victoire.
Informal, and also used as an exclamation: chouette! As a noun, la chouette is an owl.
Used as isoler qn de qc. La neige a isolé le village du reste du pays. (The snow cut the village off from the rest of the country.) Reflexive s'isoler means to withdraw.
Watch the circumflex on the i. La pluie a abîmé mes chaussures neuves. (The rain ruined my new shoes.) S'abîmer means to get damaged or go bad.
Same form in the feminine: la riche. Often plural: les riches et les pauvres.
Se boucher le nez means to hold your nose. Spelled the same: le boucher, the butcher.
Peser lourd means to weigh a lot. Il fait lourd means the weather is muggy.
Surmonter une difficulté, sa peur. It contains monter, the idea of climbing over something.
Feminine: gratuite. It can also mean unfounded: une accusation gratuite.
Conjugated like employer: je déploie. L'oiseau déploie ses ailes avant de s'envoler. (The bird spreads its wings before flying off.) Se déployer is used of troops too.

cards.de: until then / up to there (time or place)
cards.note: Always written with a hyphen. Jusque-là, tout allait bien. (Up to that point, everything was going well.) J'en ai jusque-là is colloquial for I've had it up to here.
Also political: in France l'Occupation refers to the German occupation of 1940 to 1944.
Pierre Dupont, dit le Grand. In official language ledit, ladite means the aforementioned.

cards.de: to go along, to run alongside
cards.note: Takes a direct object with no preposition. Nous longeons la rivière tous les matins. (We walk along the river every morning.) Note the e kept after the g in nous longeons.
Same form for both genders: une communiste. Also an adjective: le parti communiste.
Very colloquial, from la gueule (an animal's mouth). Politer option: dégoûtant.
Formal: aviser qn de qc. La direction nous a avisés de la fermeture du bureau. (Management notified us of the office closing.) Reflexive s'aviser de qc means to suddenly notice something.
Common phrase: être en admiration devant qn. The verb is admirer qn.
Spelled with f, not ph as in English. It also means supernatural: un film fantastique.
Mélanger qc à or avec qc. Je mélange la farine avec le sucre. (I mix the flour with the sugar.) Nous mélangeons keeps the e after the g.
Feminine aiguë, with a diaeresis. Also found in accent aigu.
From supporter (to put up with). Also used of people: cet enfant est insupportable.
For clothing or a person's height, French uses la taille instead. Grandeur nature means life-size.
Slang, from la gueule (an animal's mouth). Le voisin gueule encore dans le couloir. (The neighbour is yelling in the hallway again.) Gueuler contre qn means to shout at someone.
Same form in the masculine and feminine. Opposite: rugueux (rough).
Takes a direct object: agacer qn. Ce bruit agace tout le monde au bureau. (That noise annoys everyone at the office.) Very common: ça m'agace!
Sa voix résonne dans l'église vide. (His voice echoes in the empty church.) Sounds exactly like raisonner (to reason), but the two are unrelated.
Pattern: rembourser qc à qn. Le magasin m'a remboursé les chaussures. (The shop refunded me for the shoes.) At the pharmacy you'll hear c'est remboursé par la sécu.
Feminine noun. Common: une pension de retraite; la pension alimentaire means alimony or child support.
Formed from clair. Il a clairement dit non. (He clearly said no.)
Je dois imprimer mon billet de train ce soir. (I have to print my train ticket tonight.) Related words: une imprimante (printer) and une imprimerie (printing house).
Feminine noun. La tension artérielle is blood pressure: prendre la tension.
Plural: les neveux. The female equivalent is la nièce.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. It also means a public figure: une personnalité politique.

cards.de: the ordinary mortal (in: le ... des mortels)
cards.note: As a noun it appears almost only in le commun des mortels. Otherwise it is an adjective: commun = shared, as in en commun.
Feminine doubles the l: exceptionnelle. Adverb: exceptionnellement (as an exception).
A diminutive of la rue, so it is feminine too. Think of a narrow street in an old town.
From une tranche (a slice). Il tranche le pain avant le dîner. (He slices the bread before dinner.) Figuratively, trancher une question means to settle a question for good.
Set phrase: faire des reproches à qn (to reproach someone).
Feminine: la représentante. Un représentant de commerce is a sales rep.
Masculine: un obstacle. Common phrase: franchir un obstacle (to get over an obstacle).
Typical uses: un rude hiver, un travail rude. Of people it means blunt or gruff. It does not mean "rude" in the English sense of impolite.
Le vase a basculé et s'est cassé. (The vase tipped over and broke.) Also figurative: basculer dans la violence, to slide into violence.
Feminine form: la bergère. Un berger allemand is a German shepherd dog.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Informally it also means predictable: c'est classique!
Today people usually say le vélo. By bike: à bicyclette or en vélo.
Pattern: garantir qc à qn. Le vendeur me garantit une livraison rapide. (The seller guarantees me a fast delivery.) Also je te garantis que..., I promise you that...
Masculine. Very common as an exclamation: c'est un désastre!
Feminine, from allumer (to light). Une boîte d'allumettes is a box of matches.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -tion. Pattern: une invitation à dîner.
Extremely vulgar and used only as an insult. Worth recognising in films, but best left unsaid.
Masculine: un insecte. Une piqûre d'insecte is an insect bite or sting.
As a noun, le portable means a mobile phone, or a laptop depending on context.
Takes a direct object: flatter qn. Tu me flattes, mais je ne chante pas si bien. (You flatter me, but I don't sing that well.) Je suis flatté means I'm flattered.
La santé de ma mère me préoccupe beaucoup. (My mother's health worries me a lot.) Reflexive se préoccuper de qc means to concern oneself with something.

From blesser (to injure), so a false friend of English "blessed". Mon frère est blessé au genou depuis samedi. (My brother has had an injured knee since Saturday.) As a noun, un blessé is an injured person.
Feminine. It sounds exactly like ancre (anchor), which is also feminine.
Spelled like the English word but the ending is nasal. Figurative too: une gestion transparente, transparent management.
Set phrase: tomber en panne, to break down. Also être en panne d'essence, to have run out of petrol.
Feminine form infinie. As a noun l'infini is infinity, and à l'infini means endlessly.
A diminutive of fille. It sounds affectionate and is often used for girls up to about ten.
The final z is silent, so it sounds like ri. Don't mix it up with rire, to laugh.
The form stays the same in the feminine. As a noun: un communiste, une communiste.
Pronounced ray-sa-mahn: the emm sounds like a. J'ai récemment changé de travail. (I recently changed jobs.) It comes from the adjective récent.
Same form in the feminine. You know it from Victor Hugo's Les Misérables.
It contains terre, earth. Notre avion atterrit à Paris à midi. (Our plane lands in Paris at noon.) A regular -ir verb, with avoir in the passé composé: l'avion a atterri.
From le nœud, the knot. Elle noue ses cheveux avant de sortir. (She ties up her hair before going out.) Also figurative: nouer des liens, to build up ties.
One form for both genders, only the article changes: une adversaire. Common in sport and politics.
The feminine is une suspecte. It also works as an adjective: un comportement suspect, suspicious behaviour.
Also an adjective: un mètre carré, a square metre. Feminine form carrée.
The feminine is la coiffeuse. Where English says to the hairdresser's, French says aller chez le coiffeur.
It also means an actor's dressing room and the caretaker's lodge in a building.
A feminine noun. Une toile d'araignée is a spider's web or cobweb.
The final p is pronounced here. It also means a ship's course: mettre le cap sur, to head for.
Archaic and literary, often mocking for a dandyish young man. It is masculine; the female counterpart is la demoiselle.
Nouns ending in -té are almost always feminine. Common phrases: la communauté internationale, vivre en communauté.
Faire des grimaces means to make faces, while faire la grimace means to pull a face in displeasure.
Construction: dégoûter qn de qc, to put someone off something. Cette odeur me dégoûte complètement. (That smell completely disgusts me.) The adjective dégoûtant means disgusting.
Feminine form: la duchesse. Related: le duché, the duchy.
Nouns ending in -logue are masculine. Common phrase: engager le dialogue, to enter into dialogue.
honorer qn de qc means to honour someone with something. La ville honore ses pompiers chaque année. (The town honours its firefighters every year.) The h is silent: on l'honore.
In France le temple also means a Protestant church, as opposed to l'église for a Catholic one.
Set phrase: faire allusion à qc, to allude to something, with no article before allusion.
Feminine form récente. The adverb récemment means recently.

cards.de: the height, the last straw (peak, extreme)
cards.note: C'est le comble! means That's the last straw! In the plural, les combles means the attic.
Structure: préserver qn/qc de qc, to protect someone from something. Ces gestes simples préservent l'environnement. (These simple actions protect the environment.)
Elle a vivement réagi à ma question. (She reacted sharply to my question.) Also used to express eagerness: Vivement les vacances! means Roll on the holidays!
Often medical in everyday use: une analyse de sang, a blood test.

cards.de: the dizziness, vertigo (spinning feeling, fear of heights)
cards.note: avoir le vertige means to feel dizzy or to have a fear of heights. For a swindle, use l'escroquerie.
Colloquial intensifier: Ce gâteau est drôlement bon! (This cake is seriously good!) It rarely means funnily.

cards.de: to pass, to go by (of time)
cards.note: For time it is almost always reflexive: deux ans se sont écoulés. Without the pronoun, écouler des marchandises means to sell off goods.
Capitalised when it means the holy scripture. Figuratively: c'est ma bible, it's my go-to reference.
Structure: divorcer de qn. Elle a divorcé de son mari l'an dernier. (She divorced her husband last year.) It takes avoir in the passé composé.
Full title: le procureur de la République. The feminine is usually la procureure.
Note the double s and the final t. Common: un passeport en cours de validité, a valid passport.
Prendre la pilule means to be on the contraceptive pill. Figuratively: avaler la pilule, to swallow a bitter pill.
Feminine actuelle. Beware: actuellement means currently, not actually.
Je calcule le prix total avant de payer. (I work out the total price before paying.) Une calculatrice is a calculator. Le calcul means the calculation, not a bill.
Feminine form: la vendeuse. In legal contexts it means the seller of something, the opposite of l'acheteur.
From fumer in its old sense of to fertilise. As an insult, espèce de fumier means something like you swine.
Written with œ and pronounced like the vowel in French peu; the final d is silent. Faire un nœud means to tie a knot.
Feminine géante. As a noun le géant means the giant; in casual speech c'est géant means that's great.

cards.de: the passer-by (person walking in the street)
cards.note: Feminine une passante. As an adverbial phrase, en passing: en passant means in passing or by the way.
Cette éponge absorbe toute l'eau. (This sponge soaks up all the water.) Also used figuratively: être absorbé par son travail means to be completely wrapped up in your work.
It covers both light (la clarté de la lune) and how clear an explanation is.
Irregular masculine plural: musicaux. Common phrase: une comédie musicale, a musical.
l'Union soviétique is the Soviet Union. Note the accent on the e and the lower-case adjective.

cards.de: to start, to cut into (a loaf, a discussion)
cards.note: Very often used figuratively: entamer une discussion, entamer des négociations.
Je suis surpris de te voir ici. (I'm surprised to see you here.) Constructions: être surpris de qc, or surpris que followed by the subjonctif.
Used about children it means good behaviour. Une dent de sagesse, though, is a wisdom tooth.
Feminine: une institutrice. The official title nowadays is usually professeur des écoles.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Also a noun: quel imbécile ! means what an idiot.
Regular masculine plural fatals, not fataux. It often really does mean deadly, not just unfortunate.
Les députés débattent de la nouvelle loi. (The MPs are debating the new law.) Either débattre de qc or débattre qc. Careful: se débattre means to struggle or thrash about.
In school slang it is shortened to la philo, the final year at the lycée.

cards.de: the civil servant, the state employee (male)
cards.note: Same form for both genders; only the article changes: une fonctionnaire.
It ends in -e but is still masculine. The verb is murmurer, to whisper.
The final s is silent. Feminine: la marquise, a word that also means a canopy or awning.
Usually used in the plural: nos ancêtres. Note the circumflex on the ê.
Don't confuse it with le ministre, which is the minister, the person.
Same form for masculine and feminine. As a noun, l'arabe means the Arabic language.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. A common phrase is dans l'intimité, meaning among close family and friends.
This is the surface of a wall, as in une paroi rocheuse, a rock face. The wall of a room is usually le mur.
Unusual plural: banals, not banaux. Common phrase: une histoire banale.
Feminine form aérienne. Very common in le transport aérien and une compagnie aérienne, an airline.

cards.de: to release, to set free (a prisoner)
cards.note: La police a relâché le suspect hier soir. (The police released the suspect last night.) Also to loosen: relâcher sa prise. Se relâcher means to slacken off or let oneself go.
Masculine noun. Se cacher derrière un buisson means to hide behind a bush.

cards.de: listening, the act of listening in
cards.note: Feminine noun. Être à l'écoute de qn means to listen to someone; les écoutes téléphoniques are phone taps.
Masculine noun. Sans commentaire! means no comment.
Rétablir l'ordre, rétablir le courant. Se rétablir means to recover, to get well again.

cards.de: to fill in, to close (a gap)
cards.note: Combler un vide, combler un déficit. Combler qn de cadeaux means to shower someone with presents.
Un car is a coach, short for autocar. A car in the English sense is une voiture.
Le fromage de chèvre is goat's cheese, shortened to un chèvre, which is then masculine.
Expresses surprise or resignation: Décidément, tu ne changes pas!
Feminine la bourgeoise, and la bourgeoisie for the class itself. Often slightly disparaging.
Le double de qc: il gagne le double de moi, he earns twice as much as me. Also a duplicate, as in le double des clés.
Masculine, like all units ending in -mètre. It can also mean a tape measure.
Adjectives ending in -ique have the same form in the masculine and the feminine. Common phrase: prendre un air tragique.
Ces plantes peuvent empoisonner les chats. (These plants can poison cats.) From le poison. Informally, empoisonner la vie de qn means to make someone's life a misery.
It takes à: être indifférent à qc. Feminine form: indifférente.
The same word also means the index at the back of a book. The final x is pronounced.
Very colloquial. Faire la tronche means to sulk.
Nouns ending in -tion and -sion are always feminine: la conclusion, la décision. Tirer une conclusion: to draw a conclusion.
Feminine: une géante. As an adjective géant means gigantic, and colloquially awesome.
From enfant. C'est enfantin means it's child's play.

cards.de: the back, the wrong side (of a fabric)
cards.note: À l'envers means inside out or back to front. The same word is also a preposition: envers qn, towards someone.
Le prof aligne les chaises avant le cours. (The teacher lines up the chairs before class.) From la ligne. S'aligner sur qc means to bring oneself into line with something.
Arrête de me pincer le bras! (Stop pinching my arm!) The c becomes ç before a and o: nous pinçons. Colloquially, se faire pincer means to get caught.
Le chien grogne quand on approche. (The dog growls when you come near.) Used for animals and for people who grumble. Don't confuse it with grommeler (to mutter under your breath).
Always feminine, even for a man: il est une grande vedette. En vedette means in the spotlight.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Pronounced like orkestr.
Un collier de perles is a pearl necklace. Figuratively: cette secrétaire est une perle, this secretary is a gem.
This noun is masculine. Demander le divorce: to file for divorce.
Quelqu'un a dérobé les bijoux pendant la nuit. (Someone stole the jewels during the night.) More formal than voler. Se dérober à qc means to shirk or avoid something.
Feminine: immédiate. Very common as an adverb: immédiatement (immediately).
Idiom: clouer le bec à qn, to shut someone up.

cards.de: the volume (one book of a set)
cards.note: Le volume also means sound level and volume in the physical sense: baisser le volume.
Formal and usually placed before the noun: un ultime effort, une ultime tentative. Same form in masculine and feminine.

cards.de: to misuse, to use to excess
cards.note: Il abuse du café depuis des années. (He drinks far too much coffee, and has for years.) It takes de: abuser de qc. Colloquially, tu abuses! means that's going too far!
Ils ont orné la salle de fleurs blanches. (They decorated the room with white flowers.) The pattern is orner qc de qc. The related noun is l'ornement.
Feminine form: grossière. Une erreur grossière is a glaring mistake.
Feminine form: la servante. It sounds old-fashioned today; the modern term is l'employé de maison.
Feminine, related to English grotto. For an animal's den, French prefers la tanière.
Same form for both genders. As a noun, le sinistre means a claim or disaster in insurance language.
Ce bâtiment abrite un petit musée. (This building houses a small museum.) From un abri. Reflexive: s'abriter de la pluie, to take shelter from the rain.
Je vais emballer le cadeau ce soir. (I'm going to wrap the present tonight.) Colloquially it also means to thrill someone: ça ne m'emballe pas, I'm not wild about it.
Days of the week are written with a small letter in French. Le mercredi means on Wednesdays, while mercredi alone means this Wednesday.
Vulgar, only among close friends or in a row. Feminine form: une connasse.
Feminine noun. Set phrase: être rouge comme une tomate, to go bright red.
Covers both obedience and a field of study or a sport, just like the English word.
Masculine, with a silent h. Don't confuse it with l'humeur (mood, feminine): avoir de l'humour versus être de bonne humeur.
Same form in singular and plural: un permis, des permis. Passer son permis means to take the driving test.
Tout le monde vante la qualité de ce vin. (Everyone praises the quality of this wine.) Very often reflexive: se vanter de qc means to boast about something.
Le nageur émerge enfin de l'eau. (The swimmer finally surfaces from the water.) Usually émerger de qc. Also figurative: une idée émerge.
Same form for both genders. Typically used of children and animals: elle est adorable.

cards.de: the bench seat (in a car, in a café)
cards.note: la banquette arrière is the back seat of a car. A bank for money is la banque.
Invariable in the feminine: une femme chic. Colloquially, un chic type means a nice guy.
Feminine form chrétienne. As a noun it means a Christian: un chrétien, written with a small letter in French.
From effrayer, to frighten someone. Feminine effrayante.
Masculine despite the -e ending, like many words of Greek origin (problème, système).
avoir tendance à faire qc means to tend to do something.

cards.de: the liking, the fondness (feeling warmly towards someone)
cards.note: Use avoir de la sympathie pour qn. In messages of condolence it also means sympathy in the English sense.
J'arrose les plantes tous les matins. (I water the plants every morning.) Also used for celebrating: arroser son diplôme, to drink to your degree.
Le public applaudit la chanteuse pendant dix minutes. (The audience applauds the singer for ten minutes.) Takes a direct object with no preposition: applaudir qn.

cards.de: the blind man, the blind person
cards.note: Same form for both genders: une aveugle. Also an adjective: une confiance aveugle, blind trust.
In everyday French people say l'espoir instead. Fixed phrase: l'espérance de vie, life expectancy.
Its opposite is la cave, the cellar. Originally a grain store.
Strongly offensive and now only used in historical contexts. The neutral word is un Allemand.
Le train accélère après la gare. (The train speeds up after the station.) The accent shifts: j'accélère, nous accélérons. Note the double c at the start.

cards.de: to linger, to stay longer than planned
cards.note: Ne t'attarde pas, on part dans dix minutes. (Don't linger, we're leaving in ten minutes.) Almost always reflexive: s'attarder à faire qc or s'attarder sur un détail, to dwell on a detail.
Feminine, like most nouns ending in -ance. Common phrases: l'indépendance d'un pays, gagner son indépendance.
Feminine ennuyeuse. It can also mean annoying: c'est ennuyeux, j'ai oublié mes clés.
Sounds exactly like cœur (heart) but is spelled with ch. En chœur means in unison, all together.
Le téléphone est coupé depuis ce matin. (The phone has been cut off since this morning.) Past participle of couper. Route coupée means a closed road, vin coupé d'eau is wine diluted with water.
Feminine, like other nouns ending in -ure. The related verb is signer: signer un contrat.
Same form for both genders: un/une spécialiste. Construction: spécialiste de qc.
Feminine ennemie: l'armée ennemie. As a noun, un ennemi means an enemy.
Masculine: un nu de Picasso. As an adjective nu means naked, and pieds nus means barefoot.
Feminine: la manivelle. Tourner la manivelle means to turn the crank.

La panne a immobilisé tous les trains pendant deux heures. (The breakdown brought all the trains to a standstill for two hours.) Reflexive s'immobiliser means to come to a stop or freeze. Related to immobile (motionless).
The feminine form today is une ingénieure. Professions take no article after être: elle est ingénieure.
Followed by de: un verre rempli d'eau. Une journée bien remplie is a full, busy day.

cards.de: to endow with a gift (give a talent to)
cards.note: In practice only the participle is used, as in être doué pour les maths (to be gifted at maths). La nature semble l'avoir doué d'une mémoire extraordinaire. (Nature seems to have endowed him with an extraordinary memory.)
As a number, cent means hundred, and the plural deux cents takes an s. For coins people often say centime instead.
Only the article shows the gender: un/une photographe. Do not confuse it with la photographie (photography).
Fais attention, tu vas salir ta chemise blanche. (Be careful, you are going to get your white shirt dirty.) From sale (dirty), an ir verb like finir. Se salir means to get yourself dirty.
Set phrase: prêter serment, to take an oath. Do not confuse it with sermon (a sermon).

cards.de: sonny, my boy (informal way of addressing a son)
cards.note: An affectionate, colloquial form of fils, often used as a form of address: Salut, fiston!
Feminine. Médicament sur ordonnance means a prescription-only medicine.
Feminine parisienne. Lower case as an adjective, capitalised for a person: un Parisien.
Plural réseaux. Very common: les réseaux sociaux.
Often opens a sentence: Personnellement, je pense que ... Double n as in personne.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. Also used for film and music productions.

cards.de: to misplace (be unable to find something)
cards.note: Reflexive s'égarer means to get lost. J'ai égaré mes clés.

cards.de: to connect, to link (two points together)
cards.note: Built as relier qc à qc. Ce train relie Paris à Lyon.
Ce soir, je cuisine des pâtes pour toute la famille. (Tonight I am cooking pasta for the whole family.) Colloquially, cuisiner qn means to grill someone for information.

cards.de: the landing (floor area at the top of stairs)
cards.note: Also used for a stage or level: progresser par paliers, to progress in stages.
Masculine. Common phrase: à mon grand étonnement, to my great surprise.
Le tailleur is also a woman's suit. S'asseoir en tailleur means to sit cross-legged.

cards.de: the tide (the rise and fall of the sea)
cards.note: Marée haute is high tide, marée basse low tide. Also figurative: une marée humaine, a sea of people.
Very informal: avoir la trouille, to be scared stiff.

cards.de: the place setting (cutlery laid at a place)
cards.note: Mettre le couvert means to lay the table. As an adjective, couvert means covered or overcast.
The final f is usually silent: [sɛʁ]. Un cerf-volant is a kite.
Informal, with the matching verb se bagarrer, to scrap or fight.

cards.de: kindly, nicely (adverb: he answered me kindly)
cards.note: Irregular adverb from gentil: gentiment, never gentillement. Il m'a gentiment aidé à porter les valises. (He kindly helped me carry the suitcases.) It can also mean well behaved, like a good boy or girl.
Also a roadblock: un barrage de police. In sport, un match de barrage is a play-off.
Plural: des seaux. Sounds identical to sot (silly) and sceau (seal).
At the cinema, version originale (VO) means the original soundtrack with subtitles.
Colloquially, c'est le délire! means it's madness or it's wild. The verb is délirer.
As an adjective it has two senses: cowardly, but also loose (un nœud lâche, a loose knot).
Built as être coupable de qc. In court: plaider coupable, to plead guilty.

cards.de: to pile up, to heap up
cards.note: Il entasse ses vieux journaux dans le garage. (He piles up his old newspapers in the garage.) From un tas, a heap. Reflexive s'entasser means to cram together, for example dans le métro.

cards.de: to freeze, to chill (with cold or with fright)
cards.note: Ce cri dans la nuit m'a glacé. (That scream in the night chilled me.) Common phrase: ça m'a glacé le sang, it made my blood run cold. The participle glacé means icy or iced.
The opposite of juste. You say être injuste envers qn or avec qn.
Masculine plural: amicaux. Un match amical is a friendly match; for "friendly" meaning kind or nice, use gentil.
Usually appears in the plural: éclater en sanglots means to burst into tears.
Masculine: le miel. Une lune de miel is a honeymoon.
Feminine essentielle. Used as a noun, l'essentiel means the main thing; also il est essentiel de faire qc.
Originally a purse or money bag; une bourse d'études is a scholarship.
Son ton arrogant me déplaît beaucoup. (His arrogant tone really displeases me.) Like plaire, it takes à: cela me déplaît. A polite set phrase is ne vous en déplaise, roughly "if you don't mind".
Feminine fabuleuse. Also used of amounts: une somme fabuleuse is a huge sum.
Don't mix it up with le temps or le temple (a place of worship). Often plural: les tempes grises.
In speech it often means "in theory" or "supposedly": normalement, il arrive à six heures.
Also an insult for a fool: bête comme un âne.
The ending -que serves both genders: un film romantique, une soirée romantique.

cards.de: amply, easily (plenty, by a wide margin)
cards.note: Very common in the sense of "plenty": on a largement le temps means we have plenty of time.
Nouns ending in -tion and -sion are feminine: la dimension, la tension, la version. Les dimensions d'une pièce are the measurements of a room.
The plural takes -x: des aveux. Common phrases: faire des aveux, passer aux aveux.
Notre salon fait vingt mètres carrés. (Our living room is twenty square metres.) It follows the measurement. As a noun, le carré is a square.
Mostly plural: des difficultés innombrables. It sounds more formal than beaucoup de.
The past participle of abandonner: une maison abandonnée, un chien abandonné.
Feminine la passagère. As an adjective, passager means temporary: une douleur passagère.
Les garçons du fond ricanent pendant que je parle. (The boys at the back are sniggering while I talk.) Always negative, never simply laughing. Ricaner de qn means to mock someone.
The pattern is encombrer qc de qc. Very common as a participle: le couloir est encombré.
Feminine patiente, adverb patiemment. As a noun, le patient means a hospital patient.
Lower case as an adjective, capitalised for a person: un Romain. Do not confuse it with le roman, a novel.
Excusez-moi, cette place est prise. (Excuse me, this seat is taken.) This is the past participle of prendre. Je suis pris ce soir means I am busy tonight.
Irregular: je conquiers, nous conquérons, participle conquis.
Common phrase: faire une remarque à qn. The verb remarquer means to notice.
Very crude, only in rough slang. The neutral word is le pénis, the childish one le zizi.
Also figurative: ruiner sa santé, ruiner ses chances. Reflexive se ruiner means to ruin oneself financially.
J'ai expédié le colis à ma sœur hier matin. (I dispatched the parcel to my sister yesterday morning.) Used as expédier qc à qn. Colloquially it can also mean to rush a task through carelessly.
Usually reflexive: se crisper sur le volant. Ça me crispe is colloquial for that gets on my nerves.
Il tousse toute la nuit depuis dimanche. (He has been coughing all night since Sunday.) The noun is la toux, a cough, and it is feminine.
Nouns ending in -aille are always feminine. In sport: la médaille d'or, d'argent, de bronze.

cards.de: fine (in: il fait ..., the weather is nice)
cards.note: Il fait beau means the weather is fine. Also note avoir beau + infinitive, to do something in vain.
In swimming: nager le papillon. Colloquially un papillon is also a parking ticket left on the windscreen.
A colloquial insult, feminine une abrutie. From the verb abrutir, to dull someone's mind.
Very rare and used almost only in the participle: un hareng saur means a smoked herring.
Conjugated like conduire: je reproduis, nous reproduisons. Se reproduire means to breed or to happen again.
The same form works as an adjective: le service militaire. Feminine une militaire.

cards.de: the giving up (withdrawal from a competition, abandonment)
cards.note: laisser une maison à l'abandon means to let a house fall into neglect. The verb is abandonner qn/qc.
L'armée a maté la révolte en quelques jours. (The army crushed the revolt in a few days.) Used as mater une révolte, mater qn. In slang, mater also means to ogle or stare at someone.
faire un compliment à qn = to pay someone a compliment. In the plural, mes compliments! means congratulations!
The feminine is la lectrice. Note that un lecteur DVD is a playback device, not a person.
Conjugated like lire: je relis, nous relisons, j'ai relu. Se relire means to check over your own writing.

cards.de: the vocation (inner calling to a profession)
cards.note: Often used in avoir la vocation de faire qc. It can also mean the purpose or mission of an institution.
Plural in x: les ruisseaux. It is linked to the verb ruisseler, to trickle or stream.
Désolé, ce siège est déjà occupé. (Sorry, this seat is already taken.) La ligne est occupée means the line is busy. Être occupé à faire qc means to be in the middle of doing something.
The feminine is une adolescente. Informally shortened to un ado, une ado.
Also used figuratively: la barrière de la langue, the language barrier.
Short for faculté and very informal. The usual phrase is aller à la fac.

cards.de: the combination (way things are put together)
cards.note: It also means an overall or a wetsuit: une combinaison de plongée.
Do not mix it up with le poisson, fish, which has a sharp s sound. An antidote is un contrepoison.

cards.de: to glimpse, to catch sight of briefly; to foresee
cards.note: J'ai entrevu mon voisin à la gare ce matin. (I caught a brief glimpse of my neighbour at the station this morning.) Conjugated like voir: j'entrevois, j'ai entrevu. Also figurative: entrevoir une solution.

cards.de: to take refuge, to seek shelter
cards.note: Only used reflexively: se réfugier dans une cave, chez un ami.
Usually reflexive: se déguiser en sorcière. Figuratively it means to conceal: déguiser la vérité.
Feminine honteuse, plural honteux. The related noun is la honte, shame.
Faire un saut chez qn is a colloquial way of saying to pop round to someone's place.
Feminine, and formed from boire. In a restaurant: une boisson fraîche, a cold drink.
Same form for masculine and feminine. In speech people almost always say sympa, which never changes.

cards.de: the elder one, the firstborn (among siblings)
cards.note: The feminine is une aînée. The opposite is le cadet, the younger one. The circumflex stays in every form.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. In academic contexts, civilisation also covers the study of a country's culture and society.
Usually placed after the noun: la semaine précédente. The opposite is suivant.
Feminine. Very common in auberge de jeunesse (youth hostel).
Always written with -s, even in the singular. Don't confuse it with le fond (the bottom, the background).
Usually means almost, less often in practice. Le travail est pratiquement fini. (The work is practically finished.)

cards.de: the feeling of faintness, the dizzy spell
cards.note: Masculine. avoir un malaise means to feel faint or have a dizzy spell; figuratively it also means unease within a group.
Built with la capacité de faire qc or à faire qc. In the plural it can also mean the capacity of a room.
faire un détour means to make a detour. sans détour means bluntly, without beating about the bush.
ruban adhésif is sticky tape. For a music band you say groupe.
Accent circonflexe on the first e, as in extrême. It intensifies adjectives: Cet exercice est extrêmement difficile. (This exercise is extremely difficult.)

cards.de: Monsignor (form of address for a bishop or prince)
cards.note: It is a form of address, so it usually appears without an article. Plural: Messeigneurs.
Le coq gaulois is a symbol of France. A famous dish is le coq au vin.

cards.de: the gate, the portal (large entrance gate)
cards.note: Regular plural: des portails, unlike travail/travaux. Also used for a website portal.
Masculine despite the final -e, like many words of Greek origin (le problème, le système).

cards.de: the mount (in the names of mountains)
cards.note: Mainly used in names: le mont Blanc. Otherwise you say la montagne.
Arrête, tu massacres ma chanson préférée ! (Stop, you are butchering my favourite song!) Informally it means to do something very badly. The noun is le massacre.

cards.de: the clue, the piece of evidence
cards.note: Masculine despite the final -e. In statistics it also means index: l'indice des prix.
The feminine is la jumelle. Careful: les jumelles also means binoculars.
Followed by de with no article: une douzaine d'œufs. It often just means roughly twelve: une douzaine de personnes.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Also in set phrases: la bande sonore (soundtrack), un signal sonore.
As a noun it is masculine: un rien l'amuse (the slightest thing amuses him). Learn the phrase en un rien de temps (in no time).
Works for bodies and for rules: des horaires souples means flexible hours. Opposites: raide or rigide.
Ma mère m'a grondé parce que je suis rentré tard. (My mother told me off because I came home late.) Used with a direct object: gronder qn. Figuratively it means to rumble: le tonnerre gronde.

cards.de: the beef / the ox (animal or meat)
cards.note: Written with the ligature œ. The singular sounds like /bœf/, but the plural bœufs is pronounced /bø/.
Used as contraindre qn à faire qc. It follows craindre: je contrains, nous contraignons, participe contraint.

cards.de: the job (informal word for a position)
cards.note: Colloquial, borrowed from English; le boulot is just as common. Typical: un petit job d'été.
Nouns ending in -ance are always feminine. Common: une caméra de surveillance, être sous surveillance.
Colloquial short form of le laboratoire, just as photo stands for photographie.
The noun from venir, and it is feminine. Typical: la venue au monde d'un enfant, attendre sa venue.

cards.de: the objective (aim, goal you set yourself)
cards.note: Masculine: atteindre un objectif, se fixer un objectif. It also means the lens of a camera.

cards.de: the bill (invoice you have to pay)
cards.note: Typical: payer or régler la facture. For the bill in a restaurant, say l'addition.
Usually used in the plural: les ressources naturelles, les ressources humaines.
In politics usually plural: gagner les élections. A choice between options is le choix.
The feminine form is la deuxième. Second tends to be used when there are only two items.
Built from attendre, the opposite of attendu. Feminine: inattendue.
Le voleur a braqué une arme sur le caissier. (The thief pointed a weapon at the cashier.) Used as braquer une arme sur qn. Colloquially braquer une banque means to hold up a bank.
Idiom: forcer la dose means to overdo it.
Also the jack in a pack of cards: le valet de cœur.

cards.de: the unfortunate man (a person to be pitied)
cards.note: Feminine: une malheureuse. As an adjective, malheureux means unhappy.
Typical structure: demander l'autorisation de faire qc.

cards.de: to lead to (to end in a result)
cards.note: Used as aboutir à qc. With no complement it means to succeed: le projet a abouti.
Also figurative: le fossé entre les générations, the gap between generations.
In the plural it means further details: demander des précisions.
The final d stays silent. Un nid-de-poule is a pothole.
Conjugated like finir. Common phrase: enfouir son visage dans ses mains.

cards.de: to relive, to come back to life
cards.note: Conjugated like vivre: je revis, j'ai revécu.
Feminine: creuse. Les heures creuses are off-peak hours.
Often plural: les marchandises. Un train de marchandises is a freight train.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Common: un froid intense, une douleur intense.
The noun from arrêter qn, to arrest someone. Note that arrêter also simply means to stop.
Je veux améliorer mon français avant l'été. (I want to improve my French before the summer.) Reflexive s'améliorer means to get better: le temps s'améliore.
Structure: indispensable à qn/qc. Also il est indispensable de réserver.
In everyday speech people nearly always say le bus. Prendre le bus means to take the bus.
Le bébé commence à ramper dans le salon. [The baby is starting to crawl in the living room.] Used for snakes, babies and soldiers. Figuratively, ramper devant qn means to grovel to someone.
It means as one can see, and often opens a sentence: Visiblement, il est fatigué.
From the verb gêner qn, to bother someone. Do not confuse it with le gène, the gene.

cards.de: the ordinary (the usual, as a noun)
cards.note: Mostly in set phrases: sortir de l'ordinaire (to be out of the ordinary), d'ordinaire (usually).
H muet, so l'humble with no h sound. It is rather formal; for modest, French often uses modeste.
Both spellings, bistrot and bistro, are correct. It is a casual word for a simple café that also serves food.
Feminine: maligne. As an adjective malin means clever or sly, but in medicine it means malignant (une tumeur maligne).
gérer une entreprise, gérer son temps. Informally, je gère means I've got this under control.
un coup de tonnerre is a thunderclap. Lightning is l'éclair (m).
The opposite is la vertu. It also works as a prefix, as in le vice-président.
The feminine is violette with a double t. Une violette is also the flower, a violet.
rédiger une lettre, un rapport. The related noun is la rédaction (the writing, or an essay).
In court: prouver son innocence. The adjective is innocent, innocente.
A public hospital is l'hôpital (m). Clinique is also an adjective: un essai clinique.
On forms, néant means none or not applicable.
The plural is usually les maximums. Very common in the phrase au maximum (at most, as much as possible).
It also means stepfather. Plural: les beaux-pères; the female counterpart is la belle-mère.
prendre un engagement means to make a commitment, tenir ses engagements to keep one's promises. It also covers political commitment.
The feminine form is une éléphante. Figuratively: un éléphant dans un magasin de porcelaine, like a bull in a china shop.
Unlike English, French month names are written in lower case and take no article: en février or au mois de février.
It ends in -ire but is masculine. Also used figuratively for someone who drains others.
maîtriser une langue, maîtriser le feu. Reflexive se maîtriser means to control oneself.
More precisely un stylo à bille; le stylo-plume is a fountain pen.

cards.de: the bitch (insulting word for a woman)
cards.note: A crude, colloquial insult. The male equivalent is un salaud.
Only the unit of weight. A rubbish bin is la poubelle. des tonnes de means loads of.
Plural les pneus, with -s. un pneu crevé is a flat tyre.
Je limite mon café à deux tasses par jour. [I limit my coffee to two cups a day.] The pattern is limiter qc à qc. Reflexive se limiter à means to restrict oneself to.

cards.de: to hoist (raise a flag or sail)
cards.note: hisser le drapeau, hisser les voiles. se hisser means to haul oneself up.
Names of colours are masculine in French. le jaune d'œuf is the egg yolk.
Feminine form subtile. une différence subtile, un esprit subtil.

cards.de: the batch (of goods; also a prize lot)
cards.note: The final t is silent. gagner le gros lot means to hit the jackpot; un lot de marchandises is a batch of goods.
faire un bond is to leap; d'un bond means in one bound. The verb is bondir.
Masculine: le virus, and the plural les virus is unchanged. Also used for computers: un virus informatique.

cards.de: the brain (the soft matter; also as food)
cards.note: For the organ in a neutral, anatomical sense you say le cerveau. Remember se creuser la cervelle, to rack one's brains.
As a colour adjective it never changes: une robe café, des gants café. The noun is le café.
faire sa ronde means to do one's rounds. It also means a children's ring dance and, in music, a whole note.
Feminine ardente. Often in un désir ardent or un défenseur ardent.
Le voleur a assommé le gardien avec une bouteille. [The thief knocked out the guard with a bottle.] Used as assommer qn. Colloquially, tu m'assommes means you're boring me to death.
avoir des frissons means to feel shivery or have the chills. The related verb is frissonner.
The opposite of agréable, with the same form for both genders. Of people: être désagréable avec qn.
Fixed phrase la légitime défense, self-defence. Also une colère légitime, justified anger.
c'est courant means that's common. Other senses: l'eau courante, running water, and le mois courant, the current month.
Il m'a humilié devant toute la classe. [He humiliated me in front of the whole class.] Used as humilier qn devant les autres. Also se sentir humilié, to feel humiliated.
Masculine: un accueil chaleureux, a warm welcome. Online, la page d'accueil is the home page.
La pluie brouille la vue sur la route. [The rain blurs the view of the road.] Remember des œufs brouillés, scrambled eggs. Reflexive se brouiller avec qn means to fall out with someone.
appuyer sur une touche means to press a key. Also une touche de couleur, a touch of colour, and in football la ligne de touche, the touchline.

cards.de: to buy back (buy up, buy more of)
cards.note: Je rachète du pain, il n'y en a plus. [I'm buying more bread, there's none left.] Conjugated like acheter: je rachète. Reflexive se racheter means to redeem oneself.
Careful: l'assistance can also mean the audience present. Common in assistance technique and porter assistance à qn.

cards.de: the basin (pool of water, also the body part)
cards.note: Masculine: un bassin. Covers a swimming pool, the pelvis, and geographically le Bassin parisien.
Le directeur veut me convoquer à un entretien. [The manager wants to call me in for an interview.] Also convoquer une réunion, to call a meeting.
The opposite of la victoire. Often subir une défaite, to suffer a defeat.
The verb is massacrer, to slaughter. Informally quel massacre! describes something that went badly wrong.
Short for la publicité, so it stays feminine. Une pub can also mean a single advert or commercial.
Also spelled gaîté. Set phrase: ne pas faire qc de gaieté de cœur, to do something reluctantly.
Masculine plural: mondiaux. Common in à l'échelle mondiale and la guerre mondiale.
Feminine form: la spectatrice. In a stadium or cinema it is usually plural: les spectateurs.
In law it means aiding and abetting: complicité de meurtre. It can also be positive, the close rapport between two people.
Nouns ending in -ie are feminine. The adjective is tragique.
From la bande, a bandage: avoir les yeux bandés, to be blindfolded. Careful, in slang bander also means to have an erection.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -té. In the plural les extrémités also means the extremities of the body.

Ils vont démolir l'ancienne école cet été. [They're going to demolish the old school this summer.] Conjugated like finir: je démolis, nous démolissons. Informally it can also mean to tear someone apart.

cards.de: the hair (the whole head of hair)
cards.note: It refers to the hair on the head as a whole; a single hair is un cheveu.
Mettre la nappe means to lay the table. Also une nappe de pétrole, an oil slick.
