Feminine: la meurtrière. As an adjective meurtrier means deadly: un accident meurtrier.
The verb is torturer qn. Also used figuratively for anything agonising: c'est une vraie torture.

cards.de: to sniff (draw air noisily through the nose)
cards.note: Also means to sniff at something: le chien renifle une piste. Colloquially used about someone with a cold.
Masculine despite the final -e. The same word also means stage or phase: à ce stade de la discussion.
The adjective rusé, rusée means cunning: rusé comme un renard.
The -s belongs to the word, so singular and plural look the same. Common: un excès de vitesse, à l'excès (to excess).

cards.de: an equal (someone of the same kind)
cards.note: Usually an adjective: pareil, pareille (such a, the same). As a noun mainly in ne pas avoir son pareil = to be unmatched.
The -que ending does not change in the feminine. Careful: la pratique as a noun means practice.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. La création d'emplois = job creation.

La voiture a failli me frôler sur le trottoir. [The car almost brushed against me on the pavement.] It takes a direct object: frôler qc. Figuratively, frôler la mort means to come within an inch of death.

cards.de: one's innermost self (only in the phrase: deep down inside)
cards.note: Only in the fixed phrase en mon for intérieur = deep down inside. Do not confuse it with fort.
Feminine: bourgeoise. Cuisine bourgeoise = hearty home cooking, though the word often carries a slightly disparaging tone.
Same form in the feminine. Un remède efficace; the adverb is efficacement.
Feminine: monstrueuse. From le monstre; it can mean both enormous and hideous.
From se lever. Je suis levé depuis six heures. Also in à main levée = by a show of hands.
From redouter = to dread. Un adversaire redoutable = a formidable opponent.
The same word means drum kit: jouer de la batterie. La batterie est à plat = the battery is flat.
The pattern is être reconnaissant à qn de qc. Related to reconnaître.
J'ai sursauté quand le téléphone a sonné. [I jumped when the phone rang.] It takes avoir in the passé composé. The noun is un sursaut.
Feminine: suspecte; the final t is usually silent in the masculine. As a noun: un suspect = a suspect.
Feminine, like la route. You say sur l'autoroute, and there is often a péage (toll).
Je dois modifier mon billet de train. [I have to change my train ticket.] The pattern is modifier qc. Regular -er verb, but the stem ends in i: nous modifions.
Used as être conscient de qc. Feminine: consciente.
Typically un pan de mur, a section of wall. Also un pan de chemise, a shirt tail.
Short for football and very colloquial. jouer au foot, to play football.
Same form for both genders. être hostile à qc, to be opposed to something.
Elle chérit les lettres de sa grand-mère. [She cherishes her grandmother's letters.] Formal or literary in tone. Related to mon chéri, ma chérie, darling.
Nous devons nous hâter de partir avant la nuit. [We must hurry to leave before nightfall.] It is far more common reflexively: se hâter de faire qc.
Masculine, and the final m is pronounced: [albɔm]. un album photo, a photo album.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. The verb is détruire, to destroy.
Je commence à désespérer de trouver un travail. [I'm starting to despair of finding a job.] Désespérer de qn/qc means to give up hope in someone or something. The accent shifts: je désespère.
Feminine. être à l'affiche means to be showing or on the programme.
Nous allons négocier le prix avec le vendeur. [We're going to negotiate the price with the seller.] The pattern is négocier qc avec qn. The noun is les négociations.
Feminine mûre, which also means blackberry. Without the accent, mur means wall.
les pavés means cobbled paving. Informally it can also mean a doorstopper of a book.
Ma mère sait coudre ses propres robes. [My mother knows how to sew her own dresses.] Irregular: je couds, nous cousons, past participle cousu. Une machine à coudre is a sewing machine.
A wave on the sea is la vague. sur les ondes means on the air.
It also means a horse's hoof. Do not confuse it with le savon, soap.
Masculine despite the -e ending. un remède contre le rhume, a remedy for a cold.
Adjectives in -ique have one form for both genders. As a noun, l'historique means the record or history of something.
Feminine form: naïve. The diaeresis is kept in every form.
La mairie also means the local council or its administration. The mayor is le maire.
Masculine plural: mentaux. A common phrase is le calcul mental, mental arithmetic.
Feminine: molle, plural mous. Said of a person, it means limp or lacking energy.
Typically used as dans la pénombre, in the half-light. The tone is slightly literary.
Feminine: massive. As a noun, le massif is a mountain range or a flower bed.
Le jury va attribuer le prix à une jeune écrivaine. [The jury is going to award the prize to a young writer.] The pattern is attribuer qc à qn. S'attribuer qc means to claim something for yourself.
The h is aspiré, so it stays la haie with no elision. Le 110 mètres haies is the hurdles race.
La police disperse la foule. Reflexive se disperser means to scatter, or to spread yourself too thin.
An old short form of monsieur, now found only in court documents or used ironically.
As a masculine noun, l'avant is the front part or an attacking player. Its opposite is un arrière, a defender.
The pattern être impatient de faire qc means to be eager to do something.
Common phrase: en récompense de, as a reward for. The verb is récompenser qn.
Feminine: la musicienne. It can also work as an adjective: elle est très musicienne, she is very musical.
Masculine: l'organe. Do not confuse it with un orgue, the musical instrument.
Note the accent circonflexe. Pécher without it means to sin, and le pêcher is a peach tree.
Ton nouvel appartement est vraiment ravissant. [Your new flat is really lovely.] From ravir, to enchant. A very common compliment: une robe ravissante.

cards.de: to rise from the dead (also: to revive someone)
cards.note: Ce chef veut ressusciter les recettes de sa grand-mère. [This chef wants to revive his grandmother's recipes.] It can be transitive (ressusciter qn, to bring someone back to life) or intransitive with être.

cards.de: to string together (to link, chain up)
cards.note: From la chaîne, chain, so it also means to put in chains. Common uses: enchaîner les idées, enchaîner sur un autre sujet.
La serrure is the lock mechanism; the key is la clé. Le trou de la serrure is the keyhole.
Son front était luisant de sueur. [His forehead was shiny with sweat.] From the verb luire, to shine. Un ver luisant is a glow worm.
Spelled with an accent circonflexe on the u. Figuratively: la voûte céleste = the vault of heaven.
Like all nouns ending in -té, it is feminine. Une quantité de gens = a lot of people; its counterpart is la qualité.
Il ne faut pas négliger ses vieux amis. [You shouldn't neglect your old friends.] Use négliger qn/qc, but négliger de faire qc = to fail to do something.
Also figurative: faire vibrer le public = to thrill the audience.
Usually plural: les narines. Dilater les narines = to flare one's nostrils.
Plural in -aux: les caporaux, like journal/journaux.
La roche is rock as a material, while le rocher is a single boulder or crag.
Il est probable que takes the indicatif, but il est peu probable que takes the subjonctif.
Same form for both genders: un/une complice. Être complice de qc, and as an adjective: un sourire complice = a knowing smile.
Two senses: muddle or chaos, and mixing two things up, as in une confusion de dates.
Avoir le teint pâle = to have a pale complexion. Do not confuse it with la teinte (a shade of colour), which is feminine.
Used for Protestant ministers; a Catholic priest is le curé. Figuratively also shepherd: le bon pasteur.
Typical: la brigade criminelle, la brigade des mœurs. In restaurants, la brigade is the kitchen team.
It also means economical or cheap to run (une voiture économique). Very common: la crise économique.
Elle a réussi à accumuler assez d'argent pour partir. [She managed to amass enough money to leave.] Reflexive s'accumuler = to build up: les dettes s'accumulent.
L'entreprise veut multiplier ses ventes par deux. [The company wants to multiply its sales by two.] In arithmetic: multiplier par trois. Reflexive se multiplier = to multiply or breed.
Only for things, never for people. If a person feels comfortable, say être à l'aise.
Ces images risquent de choquer les enfants. [These images could shock children.] Very common in ça me choque (that shocks me). The adjective is choquant = shocking.
Feminine form maternelle. Key phrases: la langue maternelle (native language) and l'école maternelle (nursery school).

cards.de: the thing (informal, when you forget the name)
cards.note: Colloquial, like thingy or whatsit. For a person you say Machin = what's-his-name.

Je sentais le vent effleurer mon visage. [I could feel the wind brushing against my face.] effleurer qc takes a direct object, no preposition. Figuratively: cette idée m'a effleuré, the thought crossed my mind briefly.
un maillot de bain is a swimsuit. In the Tour de France: le maillot jaune.

cards.de: to trap, to lure into a trap
cards.note: Nous avons posé du fromage pour piéger la souris. [We put out some cheese to trap the mouse.] From un piège (a trap); spelling: je piège, nous piégeons. Une voiture piégée is a car bomb.
It comes from dent (tooth), because of the toothed edge. Typical: un col en dentelle, a lace collar.
The same word also means mermaid. Common: la sirène des pompiers.
Plural: les beaux-frères, both parts take the plural. Same pattern for la belle-sœur.
The ending -tie is pronounced [si]: démocra-sie.
From cacher (to hide). Common: en cachette = secretly, on the sly.

cards.de: to go easy on, to treat with care (a person or thing)
cards.note: ménager qn/qc; se ménager = to take it easy. Don't confuse it with déménager (to move house).
une tranche de jambon, a slice of ham. Also figurative: une tranche d'âge = an age group.

cards.de: to cover, to coat (with a surface layer)
cards.note: Nous allons revêtir le sol de carrelage. [We're going to cover the floor with tiles.] Conjugated like vêtir: je revêts, nous revêtons. In formal style also revêtir une grande importance.

Les policiers ont réussi à cerner le bâtiment. [The police managed to surround the building.] Also mental: bien cerner un problème = to get a clear grasp of a problem. avoir les yeux cernés = to have rings under your eyes.
On va décorer la salle de ballons rouges. [We're going to decorate the room with red balloons.] Pattern: décorer qc de qc. Second meaning: to award someone a medal.
Irregular plural: des cristaux. It also means crystal glass as a material.
The everyday short form is le labo.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -ité. Common: une panne d'électricité = a power cut.
Feminine: une chrétienne. The ch here is pronounced [k].
Il a voulu graver son nom dans la pierre. [He wanted to carve his name into the stone.] Modern sense: graver un CD means to burn a CD.
un litre de lait: after a quantity you use de with no article.
Playing an instrument takes de: jouer de la guitare.
From trembler (to tremble). Fixed phrase: un tremblement de terre, an earthquake.
Sounds just like le ballet but is spelled differently. donner un coup de balai means to give the place a quick sweep.
Feminine: une domestique. As an adjective: les travaux domestiques, housework.
Also the back of a coin and the backhand in tennis. Saying: le revers de la médaille, the other side of the coin.
On pourra en reparler demain matin. [We can talk about it again tomorrow morning.] Pattern: reparler de qc à qn.
Common phrase: porter une accusation contre qn. In court, l'accusation means the prosecution.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. The adjective takes à: fidèle à qn.
Colour names are always masculine in French. As an adjective: gris, grise.
Also used playfully with children: petit bandit, little rascal.
Usually un détective privé. The word itself does not change, only the article: une détective.
Only one r, unlike charrette. At the airport it is the luggage trolley.
On a computer: supprimer un fichier, to delete a file. Noun: la suppression.
Elle a dû s'agenouiller pour regarder sous le lit. [She had to kneel down to look under the bed.] Only used reflexively, from le genou, the knee. Passé composé with être: il s'est agenouillé.
With a following noun: au-dessous de la table. The opposite is dessus, above.
From the verb s'entraîner, to train. Don't forget the accent circonflexe on the i.
Of people it can also mean strong-willed or wilful: un enfant volontaire. As a noun: un volontaire, a volunteer.
A false friend: nothing to do with English ride. Adjective: ridé, wrinkled.
From the verb étendre, to spread out. Also figurative: l'étendue des dégâts, the extent of the damage.
Regular plural: des scénarios. Also used for a scenario or sequence of events.
Tu peux brancher la lampe sur cette prise ? [Can you plug the lamp into this socket?] Pattern: brancher qc sur qc. Colloquially, c'est branché means it's trendy.
Sounds identical to le compte (account) and le comte (count). Classic phrase: un conte de fées.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Common: une douleur atroce, un temps atroce.

cards.de: to hunt down, to track down
cards.note: La police continue de traquer le voleur. [The police are still hunting down the thief.] traquer qn/qc, with no preposition. Originally a hunting term.
La Belgique est un pays allié de la France. [Belgium is a country allied with France.] Feminine alliée. As a noun: un allié = an ally, les Alliés = the Allies.
Often used of weather: la pluie lui cinglait le visage. Fairly literary in tone.
Le prof doit corriger nos copies ce soir. [The teacher has to mark our papers tonight.] Like manger, it keeps the e: nous corrigeons. Reflexive se corriger = to mend one's ways.
Two senses: the piece of furniture and the spread of food. Le buffet de la gare is the station restaurant.
faire la charité à qn = to give alms to someone. Nouns ending in -té are almost always feminine.
Colloquially also to pinch something: on m'a fauché mon vélo. Être fauché = to be broke.
Plural des marteaux. Colloquially être marteau = to be crazy.
Feminine gamine. As a noun un gamin = kid, brat, informal.
Set phrase: un policier en civil = a plain-clothes police officer.
On a entendu une sirène retentir dans la rue. [We heard a siren ring out in the street.] Conjugated like finir: un coup de feu retentit. retentir de qc = to resound with something.
La ville veut renforcer la sécurité dans le métro. [The city wants to strengthen security on the metro.] Cedilla before a and o: nous renforçons.
Also un convoi funèbre = a funeral procession. Don't confuse it with the verb convoyer.
céder à la tentation = to give in to temptation. The verb is tenter.
frémir de peur, frémir d'horreur. Also used of water just below boiling: l'eau frémit.
Note the accent grave on the last e. avoir le privilège de faire qc.

cards.de: the car park, the parking garage
cards.note: Looks English but is not used this way in English. Un parking souterrain is an underground car park.
Classic trap: it means right now, not actually. For actually say en fait or en réalité. Je travaille actuellement dans une école. (I'm currently working in a school.)
Common in the phrase sans hésitation (without hesitation). Verb: hésiter à faire qc.
In theatre it also means "rehearsal": la répétition générale is the dress rehearsal.
Une brosse à dents is a toothbrush, and the verb is se brosser les dents.
Usually shortened to la pub in everyday speech. A single advert or commercial is une publicité.
Verb: révéler qc à qn. Also used of people: c'est la révélation de l'année.
Same form for masculine and feminine. As a noun, la technique means technique or method.
Typical phrase: entrer en conflit avec qn. An armed conflict is un conflit armé.
Souhaiter la bienvenue à qn means to welcome someone. As an exclamation: Bienvenue !
France is divided into départements. In companies or universities it also means department: le département des ventes.

cards.de: the deal (of cards in a game)
cards.note: Feminine. Very common figuratively: la nouvelle donne means the new situation.
J'ai tendance à associer cette chanson à mon enfance. [I tend to associate that song with my childhood.] Construction: associer qc à qc. Reflexive s'associer à qn means to team up with someone.
Il a essayé d'empoigner la corde à deux mains. [He tried to grab the rope with both hands.] From le poing (fist), so literally to grip with the fist. S'empoigner means to come to blows.
Feminine and usually plural. Une base de données is a database.
Slang for frère, a bit like "bro". Feminine form: la frangine (sister).
Être amateur de qc means to be very fond of something. Feminine form: une amatrice.
Une colonie de vacances (colo for short) is a summer camp for children.
The é becomes è before a silent ending: il reflète, but nous reflétons. Se refléter dans l'eau means to be reflected in the water.
Not a church mass, which is la messe. Colloquially, faire la foire means to go out partying.
It is masculine. Common phrases: avancer un argument (to put forward an argument), un argument de poids (a weighty argument).
The feminine form is surprenante. It belongs to surprendre (to surprise), past participle surpris.
The full form is le commissariat de police. You say aller au commissariat to go and report something.

cards.de: the distress (emotional, or being in danger)
cards.note: Set phrases: un signal de détresse (distress signal), un navire en détresse (a ship in distress).
Polite and rather formal. Je vous remercie infiniment pour votre aide. (Thank you ever so much for your help.)
From s'habiller (to get dressed). Il est arrivé très habillé pour un simple dîner. [He arrived very dressed up for a simple dinner.] Une tenue habillée means smart or formal wear.
Feminine, like almost all nouns ending in -ance. Common phrase: avec élégance.
The counterpart is la femelle. Used as an adjective, mâle means male.

cards.de: the general staff, the top leadership
cards.note: Masculine, plural des états-majors, with an s on both parts. Also used for a company's senior management.
From se baigner (to bathe). You say prendre un bain dans la baignoire.
It also means depiction or representation, as in les frais de représentation (entertainment expenses).

cards.de: to post up, to put on display (announce publicly)
cards.note: Related to une affiche (poster). Le professeur a affiché les résultats devant la salle. [The teacher posted the results outside the room.] Figuratively, afficher un sourire means to put on a smile for show.
As a colour adjective it is invariable: des vestes bleu marine. The noun la marine means the navy.

cards.de: the bog, the loo (crude, usually plural)
cards.note: Very vulgar, only among friends. The neutral word is les toilettes.
Also technical: une lance à incendie is a fire hose. Do not confuse it with the verb lancer.
Used with de, and watch out for its opposite au-dessus (above). Ce matin, il fait deux degrés au-dessous de zéro. (This morning it's two degrees below zero.)
Colloquial, formed from la vache, so avoid it in writing. Ton nouvel appartement est vachement bien. (Your new flat is really nice.)
Conjugated like conclure, past participle exclu. On l'a exclu du club après la bagarre. [They excluded him from the club after the fight.] The pattern is exclure qn de qc.
Related to fil (thread). A thicker rope is la corde.
Usually said as flaque d'eau. Also une flaque de sang, a pool of blood.
Feminine: criminelle. As a noun, un criminel means a criminal.
Formed from the adjective épais, épaisse. Nouns in -eur of this type are feminine.
Typical uses: brandir une arme, brandir un drapeau. An -ir verb conjugated like finir.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Common phrase: avoir le mérite de faire qc.
The present participle of sourire, used as an adjective. Feminine: souriante.
Feminine correcte, where the t is pronounced. Of people it can also mean decent or proper.
You can évacuer people or buildings: évacuer les habitants, évacuer la salle.
The matching adjective is gras, grasse. Une tache de graisse is a grease stain.
Built on le pied. Les spectateurs ont piétiné les fleurs du jardin. [The spectators trampled the flowers in the garden.] Without an object it means to make no progress: l'enquête piétine.
C'est le moins qu'on puisse dire ! (That's the least you can say!) As an adverb, au moins means at least.

cards.de: to hurt someone's feelings, to offend
cards.note: Ma remarque sur son travail l'a vexé. [My comment about his work hurt his feelings.] Reflexive se vexer means to take offence or sulk. It is stronger than English vex, which is closer to annoy.

From sous plus ligne, literally under the line. Le directeur a souligné l'importance de ce projet. [The director stressed the importance of this project.] Souligner que ... means to point out that ...

cards.de: the closing, the closure (also: the fastening)
cards.note: From fermer. Une fermeture éclair is a zip.

cards.de: the machine, the device (large piece of equipment)
cards.note: Masculine, and not an engine, which is le moteur. Common: engin de chantier, engin explosif.
Short for le réfrigérateur and far more common in everyday speech.
Only an animal's horn. The musical instrument is le cor.

cards.de: to arouse, to give rise to (reactions, interest)
cards.note: Slightly formal in tone: susciter l'intérêt, susciter des questions.

cards.de: to chat someone up, to hit on someone
cards.note: Informal: draguer quelqu'un. Il essaie de draguer ma sœur depuis une semaine. [He has been trying to chat up my sister for a week.] The original meaning is to dredge.

cards.de: the bar (of a cage or cell)
cards.note: Plural: les barreaux. Common in être derrière les barreaux, to be behind bars.
Conjugated like peindre: je feins, nous feignons. Pattern: feindre de faire qc.
Colloquial and dismissive: un salaire minable, un type minable.
Also used of sounds and voices: un bruit métallique.
In formal style it can simply mean ordinary or mere: un vulgaire morceau de papier.
The pillow you sleep on is l'oreiller.
Pattern: avoir l'obligation de faire qc. In finance it also means a bond.
Colloquial: flanquer une gifle à qn. The past participle also means flanked: flanqué de deux gardes.
Administrative register. à domicile means at home, or delivered to your door.
From réfléchir. In grammar, un verbe réfléchi is a reflexive verb.

cards.de: the clock (large wall or tower clock)
cards.note: h muet, so l'horloge, and the word is feminine. A wristwatch is la montre, an alarm clock le réveil.
Usually reflexive: se maquiller. Elle se maquille toujours avant de sortir. [She always puts on make-up before going out.] Figuratively it means to doctor or cover up: maquiller la vérité.
Only used reflexively: il s'accroupit derrière la voiture. For the position itself, être accroupi.
Slangy and a bit dated, close to wheels or motor. Note also le vol à la tire, pickpocketing.
From le clou, the nail. Mon père a cloué une planche sur la fenêtre cassée. [My father nailed a board over the broken window.] Often figurative: être cloué au lit, to be stuck in bed.
Conjugated like mettre. Cette erreur risque de compromettre tout le projet. [This mistake could jeopardise the whole project.] Se compromettre means to compromise yourself.

cards.de: to bawl out (tell someone off furiously)
cards.note: Very colloquial, from la gueule, an animal's mouth. Mon chef m'a engueulé parce que j'étais en retard. [My boss bawled me out because I was late.] S'engueuler avec qn means to have a shouting row.
As a noun it appears almost only in le clair de lune. The common adjective clair, claire means light or clear.
Very colloquial and often disparaging. The male counterpart is un mec.
Ce soir, nous allons griller des légumes au barbecue. [Tonight we are going to grill some vegetables on the barbecue.] Also figurative: griller un feu rouge means to run a red light.
An identical word means bay (the inlet): la baie de Somme. Also une baie vitrée, a large picture window.
Used for eating fast: il a englouti son repas. Often passive, of the sea: englouti par les flots.
It already ends in e, so the masculine and feminine forms are the same. Very common: un temps splendide.

cards.de: the manner, way (only in set phrases, à sa ...)
cards.note: It survives only in fixed expressions: à ma guise, as I please, and en guise de, by way of, instead of.
In legal language, le parquet means the public prosecutor's office.
Notre équipe a triomphé malgré la pluie. [Our team triumphed despite the rain.] With an object it takes de: triompher de qn/qc, to triumph over someone or something.
La chaleur nous accable depuis trois jours. [The heat has been overwhelming us for three days.] The pattern is accabler qn de qc, as in accabler qn de reproches.
Diviser qc en deux, but in arithmetic diviser par trois. Also to split people: la question divise le pays.
Mostly figurative: ébranler la confiance, ébranler des certitudes.
From tirer (to shoot). Un tireur d'élite is a sniper; the feminine is la tireuse.
The same word also means a blister (on your foot) and a medical ampoule. Changer une ampoule = to change a bulb.
Ce souvenir le tourmente encore aujourd'hui. [That memory still torments him today.] Reflexive se tourmenter means to worry, to fret.
From cadre (frame). J'ai fait encadrer la photo de mes grands-parents. [I had my grandparents' photo framed.] Figuratively it means to supervise or mentor: encadrer une équipe.
Related to la guerre (war). As an adjective, guerrier, guerrière means warlike.
The related noun is le désespoir. Construction: être désespéré de faire qc.

cards.de: the close relation (person close to you)
cards.note: Usually plural: ses proches = his family and close friends. As an adjective, proche de means close to.
Faire des achats = to do some shopping. The verb is acheter qc à qn.
From le sang (blood). Careful: a rare steak is saignant, not sanglant.
From la cire (wax). Il cire ses chaussures tous les dimanches. [He polishes his shoes every Sunday.] Cirer un parquet means to wax a wooden floor.
Common in je te remercie sincèrement. It also serves as a sign-off at the end of a letter.

cards.de: to express, to voice (an opinion, a wish)
cards.note: Conjugated like mettre: j'émets, nous émettons, j'ai émis. Also means to broadcast (radio) and to issue (money, stamps).
Être étonné de qc, but être étonné que + subjonctif.
Un conte de fées = a fairy tale. Related word: féerique (enchanting).
From brûler. Le gâteau est complètement brûlé. [The cake is completely burnt.] Ça sent le brûlé means something smells burnt.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine in French.
Feminine form: une associée. Verb: s'associer à or avec qn = to team up with someone.
Past participle of partir, used like an adjective: il est déjà parti. Colloquially also c'est bien parti (it's off to a good start).
Same form as an adjective: wild, shy. Un chat sauvage, une région sauvage.
Prendre la température = to take someone's temperature. Avoir de la température means to be running a temperature.
Le traité de paix. A private agreement is un contrat instead.
Masculine despite the final e. Often figurative: être au bord de l'abîme.
Crude slang, derived from sale. The feminine la salope is even more offensive.
From inquiéter. Reflexive s'inquiéter de qc = to worry about something.
Feminine la factrice. The same word also means factor: un facteur important.
Une maison hantée = a haunted house. Also figurative: ce souvenir me hante.
Tenir la rampe. The same word means ramp: rampe de lancement = launch pad.
Formation professionnelle, formation continue (further training). Also formation in the sense of forming: la formation d'un nuage.
Unlike English, the adjective is written in lower case; the language is le japonais. Feminine: japonaise.
Very common in speech, and it also means straight out. Ce film est carrément génial. (This film is absolutely brilliant.)
Les falaises d'Étretat. A single rock standing in the sea is un rocher.
From briser (to smash, to break). Le vase brisé est encore par terre. [The broken vase is still on the floor.] Figurative use: avoir le cœur brisé, to be heartbroken.
It stays invariable in fixed expressions: couper court à qc (to cut something short), s'arrêter court, tourner court.
Common phrase: se lancer à la poursuite de quelqu'un. In the plural, les poursuites means legal proceedings.

cards.de: to tolerate, to put up with
cards.note: Je ne tolère pas ce comportement. Also used medically: mal tolérer un médicament.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -tion. Second meaning: an inscription carved or written on something.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Don't mix it up with le papa (dad).
déterminer la cause d'un accident. The adjective déterminé means determined, resolute.
Mostly reflexive: ne t'affole pas, meaning don't panic. Cette nouvelle a affolé toute la famille. [This news threw the whole family into a panic.] Related to fou (mad).
From remarquer (to notice). Typical praise on a school report: un travail remarquable.
The form is the same in the feminine. Une lettre anonyme; une société anonyme is a public limited company.
Childish and familiar, roughly like uncie. The normal word is un oncle, and the female equivalent is tata (auntie).

cards.de: to light up, to illuminate brightly
cards.note: Double l, as in English illuminate. Also figurative: un sourire illumine son visage.
Same form for both genders. As a noun, la logique (logic) is feminine.
La grève a retardé tous les trains ce matin. [The strike delayed all the trains this morning.] Ma montre retarde means my watch is slow. Related expression: être en retard (to be late).
An intensifier just like English terribly. Ce restaurant est terriblement cher. (This restaurant is terribly expensive.)
The verb insulter quelqu'un takes a direct object with no preposition, unlike English to swear at someone.
Shortened to une expo in everyday speech. It also means exposure: l'exposition au soleil.
Circumflex on the o and no h, unlike English throne. monter sur le trône means to come to the throne.
Feminine, plural des pizzas. Pronounced with a voiced dz sound in the middle.
The ending -esque stays the same in the feminine. A bit stronger than énorme.
Un salon de coiffure is a hairdresser's; the person is le coiffeur, la coiffeuse.

cards.de: to go around, to bypass (walk or drive around something)
cards.note: Literally: contourner un obstacle, contourner la ville. Also figurative: contourner la loi, contourner le problème.
The related noun is le baptême (baptism). Informally it also means to name someone: on l'a baptisé Max.
Il a fini par me confesser la vérité. [He finally confessed the truth to me.] Used as confesser qc à qn. The reflexive se confesser means to go to confession.
Common phrase: un contrat à durée déterminée (a fixed-term contract). From the verb durer (to last).

cards.de: to break down, to smash in (by force, e.g. a door)
cards.note: Les pompiers ont dû défoncer la porte. [The firefighters had to break the door down.] Slang se défoncer means to get high or to go all out.

cards.de: the edition (of a book), the print run
cards.note: Feminine, like almost all nouns ending in -tion. Une maison d'édition is a publishing house.
Masculine noun. A kite that you fly is un cerf-volant, not un dragon.
Mon vélo rouille sous la pluie. [My bike is rusting in the rain.] From la rouille (rust). Figuratively, se rouiller means to get rusty, to lose practice.
Nouns ending in -at are usually masculine. Also figurative: un climat de confiance (a climate of trust).
The same word appears in le rez-de-chaussée (the ground floor). Road sign: chaussée glissante.
Same form as the adjective fort (strong). Idiom: ce n'est pas mon fort (that's not my strong point).

cards.de: to escape, to break out (of prison)
cards.note: Deux prisonniers se sont évadés cette nuit. [Two prisoners escaped last night.] Almost always reflexive: s'évader de prison. Related noun: une évasion (an escape).
Used in gravement malade, gravement blessé. For injuries the media often prefer grièvement blessé.
Now historical or jokey; today you say le coiffeur. Familiar from the opera "Le Barbier de Séville".
Feminine maladroite; the opposite is adroit (skilful). It also works for words: une remarque maladroite.
Usually means bustle or nervousness rather than political agitation. Verb: agiter (to shake, to stir up).
Feminine form: la conductrice. A ticket inspector or conductor on a train is le contrôleur.

cards.de: the French school-leaving exam (colloquial short form)
cards.note: Short for le baccalauréat: passer le bac, avoir son bac. The same word can also mean ferry or tub.
Un robot ménager is a food processor. The final t is silent.
Idiom: ne pas quitter qn d'une semelle, to stick to someone like glue.
Sounds old fashioned today and is mostly literary. The masculine le servant means an attendant, for instance on a gun crew or at the altar.
Verb: inventer qc. It can also mean a made up story, a lie.
Shortened to la fac in everyday speech, often just meaning uni: aller à la fac. A second meaning is ability.
Le prof adapte ses cours au niveau des élèves. [The teacher adapts his lessons to the students' level.] adapter qc à qc. The reflexive s'adapter à qc means to get used to something.
Very often it simply means suddenly or abruptly: il s'est arrêté brutalement.
Un monument historique is a listed building, un monument aux morts a war memorial.
From la pointe, the tip or point. Figuratively, une question pointue is a highly technical question.
The noun is feminine: l'artillerie lourde. Sortir l'artillerie lourde is a jokey way of saying to bring out the big guns.
The word is masculine. A common question is qu'est-ce qu'il y a comme dessert?

cards.de: the info, the piece of news (short form)
cards.note: Short for information and feminine. In the plural, les infos means the news bulletin: regarder les infos.
Used this way it never changes form and appears only in set phrases: c'est mal, être mal. Pas mal means not bad or quite a lot.
Mes parents veulent investir dans un appartement. [My parents want to invest in a flat.] The reflexive s'investir dans qc means to throw yourself into something.
Always takes à: nuire à qn, nuire à sa santé. The past participle nui never agrees.
Feminine: la cathédrale de Chartres. French uses this one word where English may say cathedral or minster.
A doctor's prescription is une ordonnance, not une recette. In the plural, les recettes can also mean takings or revenue.
Set phrase: prendre qc en considération. It can also mean regard or esteem.
Useful phrase: le casier judiciaire is a criminal record.
Ne panique pas, on a encore le temps. [Don't panic, we still have time.] Very common in speech. Used transitively it means to make someone panic.
Masculine in the singular but feminine in the plural: les délices sont grandes. C'est un délice! is what you say about good food.
Also an insurance premium. The English word prime is a false friend here.
Feminine impériale, masculine plural impériaux. From un empereur, un empire.

cards.de: to cheat (in a game, in an exam)
cards.note: Used with à: tricher à un examen, tricher aux cartes. A cheat is un tricheur.
It also means dispatch or shipping: les frais d'expédition are the shipping costs.
L'incendie a anéanti toute la forêt. [The fire wiped out the whole forest.] An -ir verb like finir: j'anéantis, nous anéantissons. Être anéanti also means to be devastated.

cards.de: the Japanese man (a person from Japan)
cards.note: Capitalised for the person: un Japonais. The language and the adjective are lower case: le japonais, un jardin japonais.
Masculine plural sentimentaux. La vie sentimentale means someone's love life, not sentimentality.
Un homme bizarre rôde autour de l'école. [A strange man is prowling around the school.] Watch the accent circonflexe: roder without it means to run in a machine.
Very colloquial, for use among friends. The neutral word is l'argent, and le fric is equally slangy.
Formal and literary; everyday French uses le rêve. The related verb songer à qc means to think about something.
Set phrase: à discrétion means as much as you like, at will.
Masculine plural postaux. The most common pairing is une carte postale.

cards.de: to devote (dedicate your life to something)
cards.note: Elle a voué sa vie à la recherche. [She devoted her life to research.] Constructions: vouer qc à qn/qc, se vouer à qc. Very common as a participle: être voué à l'échec means to be doomed to fail.
Je te défie de sauter dans l'eau froide. [I dare you to jump into the cold water.] défier qn de faire qc means to challenge someone to do something. Formal: se défier de qn means to mistrust someone.
You say faire une hypothèse. Set phrase: dans l'hypothèse où + conditionnel means in the event that.
From impressionner qn, to impress someone. Note the double n, as in impressionniste.

cards.de: the betrothed (dated, solemn word for fiancé)
cards.note: Feminine: la promise. Today it sounds jokey or literary; the normal word is le fiancé.
It also means an actor's line and a replica of an artwork. sans réplique means with no arguing back.
Quite harmless in everyday French: c'est débile means that's rubbish. Much milder than the English debile or imbecile sound.

Le trésor est caché sous le vieux pont. [The treasure is hidden under the old bridge.] Past participle of cacher: cacher qc à qn = to hide something from someone. The game of hide-and-seek is cache-cache.
un rasoir électrique = an electric shaver. Informally also an adjective: c'est rasoir = that's boring.
candidat à un poste = applicant for a job. Related: poser sa candidature = to apply.
Tu progresses vraiment en français. [You're really improving in French.] progresser en français = to get better at French. Also used physically: to advance.

cards.de: to carry out, to perform (a payment, a task)
cards.note: Formal in tone: effectuer un paiement, effectuer un contrôle. In everyday speech people just say faire.
Feminine form glorieuse. From the same family as la gloire = glory.
Only one g in French, unlike the English spelling. Feminine: agressive.
à la pelle = by the bucketload. Informally: ramasser une pelle = to take a tumble.
From sonner = to ring. appuyer sur la sonnette = to press the doorbell.

cards.de: the set meal (fixed menu in a restaurant)
cards.note: The list of dishes is la carte: manger à la carte or prendre le menu. As an adjective, menu means tiny or slight.
French uses the singular: un pyjama, where English says pyjamas. être en pyjama = to be in one's pyjamas.
Capitalised in the name of a state: la République française. Very common: le président de la République.
Common on signs: stationnement interdit, entrée interdite. As an adjective it can also mean speechless or taken aback: il resta interdit.

cards.de: to keep doggedly at it (not let up)
cards.note: Il s'acharne à réparer sa vieille voiture. [He keeps doggedly trying to fix his old car.] Almost always reflexive: s'acharner à faire qc, s'acharner sur qn (to keep laying into someone).
Informally la capote also means condom (capote anglaise). Nothing to do with a cape or a coat in modern usage.
Typical uses: à ma grande stupeur, frapper qn de stupeur. Feminine, like many nouns ending in -eur that name feelings.
Plural veaux. It also means veal: une escalope de veau.
Plural: les petits-fils. Feminine: la petite-fille, the granddaughter.
prendre l'initiative de faire qc = to take the initiative to do something. A syndicat d'initiative is a tourist information office.

cards.de: the bastard (illegitimate child, also an insult)
cards.note: Crude as an insult. It also means a mongrel dog and a type of loaf between a baguette and a pain.
From the adjective discret, discrète, with an accent grave. Elle est sortie discrètement pendant la réunion. (She left discreetly during the meeting.)
From hurler, to howl or yell. Also used for the howling of wolves or sirens. H aspiré, so: le hurlement.
par politesse means out of politeness. A formule de politesse is the closing phrase of a letter.
J'ai oublié mon parapluie dans le bus. [I forgot my umbrella on the bus.] Past participle of oublier. Remember the pattern oublier de faire qc, to forget to do something.
Note the accent circonflexe on the a. Figuratively: tâter le terrain, to test the waters.
Une caserne de pompiers is a fire station. The stress falls on the last syllable.
Feminine, spelled just like the adjective technique. For technology you would say la technologie.
Feminine form une accusée. But un accusé de réception is an acknowledgement of receipt.
Mostly used in faire pipi, to do a wee. Childish, and casual among adults.
Il s'est fait mal au derrière en tombant. [He hurt his bottom when he fell.] The same word is also a preposition: derrière la maison, behind the house.
Words ending in -tion are always feminine. It also means breathing in.
Same form in the feminine: une philosophe. As an adjective, philosophe means philosophical or unruffled.
It comes from la feuille, but words ending in -age are usually masculine.
J'ai grossi de trois kilos cet hiver. [I put on three kilos this winter.] Built from gros; the opposite is maigrir. Also transitive: la loupe grossit les lettres.
Feminine européenne with a double n. As a noun it takes a capital: un Européen.
Also major de promotion, the top student of the year.
Same form in the masculine and feminine. As a noun, la mécanique means mechanics.
Colloquially also an insult for a cheeky child: quelle peste!
Also used for groups at school or in politics: se diviser en deux clans, to split into two camps.
The related verb is cicatriser, to heal over.
Ses grands-parents le gâtent beaucoup trop. [His grandparents spoil him far too much.] Un enfant gâté is a spoilt child. Se gâter means to turn bad, as in the weather.
A colloquial word for pomme de terre. La patate douce is the sweet potato.
It follows ouvrir: je rouvre, past participle rouvert.

cards.de: the index card, the record card
cards.note: Also la fiche de paie, a payslip, and the plug on an electrical lead.
Feminine: incertaine. A typical use is l'avenir est incertain. For people you would rather say ne pas être sûr de soi.

cards.de: the warehouse, the depot (place for goods)
cards.note: It comes from déposer. Also faire un dépôt, to pay money in, and un dépôt de calcaire, a limescale deposit.
mettre, j'ai mis, feminine mise. As an adjective it appears in bien mis, well dressed.
Same form in the masculine and the feminine. Of people, être disponible means to have time.
Common phrases: en pratique, mettre en pratique. The identical-looking adjective pratique means practical.
Sans pudeur means shameless. Do not confuse it with la honte, the shame you feel over something you did.
Two spellings exist, saoul and soûl, both pronounced [su]. Feminine saoule. The more neutral word is ivre.
Feminine: une experte. The pattern is être expert en informatique.

cards.de: the distinctive feature, what is characteristic (le ... de qn)
cards.note: Le propre de l'homme is what is unique to human beings. Also au propre et au figuré, literally and figuratively.
Common phrases: avec prudence, par prudence. The adjective is prudent, prudente.
Un chiffon à poussière is a duster. The related chiffonné means crumpled.
J'ai reçu ta lettre ce matin. [I received your letter this morning.] The cedilla is needed: reçu. Une idée reçue is a received idea or prejudice, and un reçu is a receipt.

cards.de: to plunder, to strip someone of something
cards.note: Les voleurs l'ont dépouillé de tout son argent. [The thieves stripped him of all his money.] The pattern is dépouiller qn de qc. In a technical sense, dépouiller le scrutin means to count the votes.
It works both transitively and intransitively: stopper la voiture, la voiture a stoppé. The everyday word is arrêter.
From mitrailler, to fire a machine gun at. The gunner is le mitrailleur.
Same form in singular and plural: une noix, des noix. Une noix de coco = coconut, une noix de beurre = a knob of butter.
From gentil, gentille. Polite formula: avoir la gentillesse de faire qc = to be so kind as to do something.
Used with à: être inférieur à la moyenne = to be below average. Opposite: supérieur.
Masculine despite the final -e: l'évêque, un évêque.
Often avoir la manie de faire qc. Do not confuse it with the verb manier (to handle).
Masculine plural: originaux; feminine: originale. As a noun, l'original means the original (item).

cards.de: the heavens (plural of ciel, religious or literary)
cards.note: Irregular plural of le ciel; the form ciels is only used for skies in paintings or types of sky.
Masculine despite the final -e. Common phrase: avoir de bons réflexes = to react quickly.

cards.de: to whip, to flog (with a whip)
cards.note: From le fouet (whip, also whisk). Il faut fouetter les œufs avec le sucre. (You have to whisk the eggs with the sugar.) In cooking: la crème fouettée = whipped cream.
Feminine: positive. Common: un point positif, un test positif.
Slangy word for les vêtements, used almost always in the plural.
Takes a direct object with no preposition: mentionner qn/qc. Elle a mentionné ton nom pendant la réunion. (She mentioned your name during the meeting.)
Common: partir en patrouille = to go out on patrol. Related verb: patrouiller.
La routine quotidienne = daily routine; par routine = out of habit.
Plural: des agneaux. On a menu: gigot d'agneau = leg of lamb.
Masculine despite the final -e. Set phrase: torse nu = bare-chested.
Formal, literary register. Cette ville était naguère un petit village. [This town was, not long ago, a small village.] It strictly refers to the recent past; for the distant past use jadis.
Mon frère ronfle si fort que je ne dors pas. (My brother snores so loudly that I can't sleep.) Noun: le ronflement. Also used for engines that rumble or hum.
Refers only to the diplomatic mission. Note that une ambassade is never a message; that is un message.
Often used figuratively: sombrer dans l'oubli (sink into oblivion), sombrer dans le désespoir.
classer des documents means to file documents. Reflexive se classer premier means to come first.
Nouns ending in -cle are masculine. Mettre le couvercle sur la casserole.
Same form for masculine and feminine. In the plural it often comes before the noun: de multiples raisons.
Watch the construction: hériter de qc, or hériter qc de qn. Elle a hérité d'une vieille maison en Bretagne. (She inherited an old house in Brittany.)
Common phrase: être en quête de qc. In church, la quête is the collection.
Jouer aux billes means to play marbles. Un stylo à bille is a ballpoint pen.
It also means seriousness: la gravité de la situation.
Irregular like lire: j'élis, past participle élu. Les Français élisent leur président tous les cinq ans. (The French elect their president every five years.)
Généralement, je me lève à sept heures. [Generally, I get up at seven.] Often placed at the start of a sentence. Synonym: en général.
This is fresh sausage for cooking. Dry cured salami style sausage is le saucisson.
Une bulle de savon is a soap bubble. In comics, la bulle is the speech bubble.
Un ami imaginaire. Do not confuse it with imaginable, which means conceivable.
Used as strong everyday praise: C'était sublime! Same form for both genders.
Les heures supplémentaires means overtime.
Un brin d'herbe is a blade of grass. Un brin de also means a touch of: un brin de folie.
Le rhume des foins is hay fever.
The same word also means pomegranate: un jus de grenade.
Remember the accent circonflexe. Common phrase: obtenir un diplôme, to get a qualification.
Past participle of disparaître. Mon portefeuille a disparu ce matin. (My wallet disappeared this morning.) Set phrase: porté disparu, reported missing.
You say jouer au tennis. In the plural, des tennis is a colloquial word for trainers.
Nouns ending in -ment are almost always masculine. The related verb is cimenter, to cement.
Feminine form: une combattante. Un ancien combattant is a war veteran.
Very common in par écrit, in writing. L'écrit is also the written part of an exam, as opposed to l'oral.
Used as avoir l'audace de faire qc. Depending on tone it can praise courage or criticise cheek.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. À la perfection means perfectly, flawlessly.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Used as a noun, l'incroyable means the incredible.
Note the accent grave and the silent final s. The plural stays les congrès.

cards.de: the beat (of the heart, of wings)
cards.note: From battre, to beat. Un battement can also mean a gap or bit of spare time between two appointments.
The ending -tion makes it feminine. Un mur de séparation is a dividing wall.
Feminine: une écolière. The general word is élève, while at university you say étudiant.

cards.de: key, main (decisive, as in le maître mot)
cards.note: Feminine form: maîtresse. Le maître mot is the key word, and une maîtresse femme is a formidable woman.
For women usually une ivrogne. Clearly insulting; alcoolique is the neutral term.
The h is aspiré, so it stays le hangar with no liaison. It covers a warehouse, a barn or an aircraft hangar.
Related to fort, strong. The ending -esse is always feminine.
First é, then è: phénomène. Colloquially it also describes an oddball, quel phénomène!
Common in le conseil municipal (town council). Masculine plural: municipaux.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. Often heard as en toute simplicité (quite informally).
Fixed expression: faire la sieste.
un passager clandestin = a stowaway; le travail clandestin = undeclared work.
The -e ending covers both genders. les pompes funèbres = the undertaker's, funeral home.
The h is silent, so you say l'héritage. The related verb is hériter de qc, to inherit something.
Feminine: rase. Colloquial: en avoir ras le bol = to be fed up.
Pas spécialement = not particularly, a very common reply in conversation. Example: Tu aimes le foot ? Pas spécialement. (Do you like football? Not particularly.)

cards.de: the small bottle (for perfume or medicine)
cards.note: Masculine: un flacon de parfum. For drinks you use une bouteille instead.
Formed from quatre + -ième, dropping the final e: quatrième. le quatrième étage.

cards.de: to dispel, to clear away (fog, doubts)
cards.note: Reflexive se dissiper = to lift or clear: le brouillard se dissipe.

cards.de: video (as an adjective, e.g. video game)
cards.note: As an adjective it never changes: des jeux vidéo, une caméra vidéo.
contrarier qn = to upset someone; être contrarié = to be annoyed. Ça me contrarie quand tu arrives en retard. (It annoys me when you arrive late.) Also used for plans: contrarier un projet.
Same form for both genders: un fan, une fan. Colloquial: être fan de qc.
Feminine: floue (une photo floue). As a noun: le flou = blurriness, vagueness.
It is feminine: l'industrie automobile. Adjective: industriel, industrielle.
Feminine form: négative. Also a noun: le négatif = the negative of a photo.
Ce travail est difficile, voire impossible. [This job is difficult, or even impossible.] Do not confuse it with the verb voir.
Colloquially also an adjective: c'est bidon = it's fake or made up (invariable).
Second meaning: illegal trade, le trafic de drogue. Note the single f, unlike English traffic.
Literally twice-baked (bis + cuit). In the supermarket you usually see the plural: des biscuits.
Same form in the masculine and the feminine. Key phrase: une crise cardiaque = a heart attack.
Feminine form: une héritière. The verb takes de: hériter de qc.
Bureau de change = exchange office, le taux de change = the exchange rate. Change you get back is la monnaie.
From le peuple. Des immigrés ont peuplé cette région au siècle dernier. (Immigrants settled this region last century.) Reflexive se peupler = to fill up with people.
Watch the pronunciation: solennel sounds like so-la-nel. Feminine: solennelle.
Works transitively and intransitively. Les prix ont diminué depuis l'année dernière. (Prices have gone down since last year.)

cards.de: to come running, to rush up
cards.note: Conjugated like courir: j'accours, il accourt, il est accouru.
Plural: des taureaux. Also the star sign: je suis Taureau.
Construction: se résigner à qc or se résigner à faire qc.
From large. An -ir verb like finir: nous élargissons. Ce voyage a élargi mes horizons. (This trip broadened my horizons.) S'élargir = to get wider.

cards.de: to plead, to defend in court
cards.note: L'accusé a décidé de plaider coupable. (The defendant decided to plead guilty.) Plaider en faveur de qn = to speak up for someone.
Plural only and feminine. The final s was traditionally silent, but today it is often pronounced.
intimider qn, a direct object with no preposition. Son silence m'intimide un peu. (His silence intimidates me a little.) The participle intimidé means intimidated.
The l doubles in the stressed forms: je renouvelle. Je dois renouveler mon passeport avant l'été. (I have to renew my passport before the summer.)
Feminine close. Le procès s'est déroulé à huis clos. (The trial took place behind closed doors.) It is the participle of clore and survives mainly in set phrases.

cards.de: to kick out (of a horse, with its hind legs)
cards.note: Attention, ce cheval rue quand on l'approche. (Careful, this horse kicks when you come near it.) Reflexive se ruer sur qc means to pounce on something. Do not confuse it with rue (street).
Masculine: le jury. It also refers to an examining board or panel of judges.
Crude slang; the feminine salope is even harsher. It echoes sale (dirty).
Feminine la chirurgienne. Surgery is la chirurgie, and ch here sounds like sh.
It covers any mushroom or fungus; the common white button mushroom is a champignon de Paris.
Il a photographié toute la cérémonie. (He photographed the whole ceremony.) In everyday speech people say prendre en photo. A photo is une photo, feminine.
From the verb trembler. A common phrase is trembler de peur, to shake with fear.
Also the fencing discipline. Do not confuse it with sable (sand), just one letter apart.

cards.de: to fold down, to close (a lid, a flap)
cards.note: Conjugated like battre: je rabats, nous rabattons. Rabats le couvercle avant de partir. (Close the lid before you leave.)
As a noun it is masculine: le moi et le surmoi. Otherwise moi is the stressed pronoun meaning me.
Almost always plural in French: les dégâts, faire des dégâts. Note the circumflex on the a.
Often used with figures and quantities: une somme considérable, des dégâts considérables.
Built on éviter (to avoid). Il était inévitable que takes the subjonctif.

cards.de: the atmosphere (mood of a place or event)
cards.note: It describes the feel of a place or a party: il y a une bonne ambiance. A person's own mood is l'humeur.
Used with de: elle a accouché d'une fille. Colloquially, accouche! means "out with it!"
From tendre (tender, soft). Cette histoire m'a vraiment attendri. (That story really moved me.) Reflexive s'attendrir sur qc means to be touched by something.
The h is aspirate, so it stays la hache with no elision. Do not confuse it with haché (minced, as in viande hachée).
Il se plaint constamment de son travail. [He constantly complains about his job.] Adjectives ending in -ant form adverbs in -amment, here from constant. It sounds like "-aman".
The opposite of imprimé or à motifs. The same word also means united: les Nations unies.
The feminine form is la tigresse, also used figuratively for a fierce woman.
Mes parents cultivent des tomates dans leur jardin. (My parents grow tomatoes in their garden.) Also figurative: cultiver une amitié, to nurture a friendship. Se cultiver means to broaden your mind.
Feminine form active. La population active means the working population.
Past participle of cuire. Le poulet est bien cuit, on peut manger. (The chicken is well cooked, we can eat.) Colloquially c'est cuit means it's all over.
From éclater. Typical uses: un succès éclatant, une lumière éclatante.

cards.de: the row (things or people standing side by side)
cards.note: From rang (rank, row). Une rangée d'arbres. A queue of waiting people is la file.
Always takes à: contribuer à qc / à faire qc. Chacun a contribué à l'organisation de la fête. (Everyone contributed to organising the party.) Noun: la contribution.
Feminine form exquise. Used for food and for manners: une politesse exquise.
Past participle of aimer. Elle a toujours été aimée de ses élèves. (She has always been loved by her students.) Common in bien-aimé (dearly beloved).
Also a crab's claw. Une pince à épiler means tweezers.
Feminine form singulière. As a noun, le singulier means the singular.
Same form for both genders: être complice de qc. As a noun it means accomplice.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Adjective: vaniteux, vaniteuse.

cards.de: to leaf through, to flick through
cards.note: From la feuille (leaf, sheet of paper). Je feuillette un magazine dans la salle d'attente. (I am leafing through a magazine in the waiting room.) Note the double t in je feuillette.
Le vent a violemment secoué les arbres. [The wind violently shook the trees.] Adverb from violent; the ending -emment is pronounced like -amment.
Masculine form: un prostitué. Verb: se prostituer.
Abstract nouns ending in -eur are feminine. From lent, lente.
para- (protecting against) + pluie (rain). Built the same way: le parasol, le parachute.
Feminine form permanente. Often used in en permanence (constantly).
Usually made of thin fabric; a warm winter scarf is une écharpe.
Same form for both genders. As a noun: un/une scientifique, a scientist.
Note the accent aigu on the first e. Adjective: mélancolique.
Do not mix up with hôtel: l'autel stands in a church, l'hôtel on the street.
From bombarder. Also figurative: un bombardement de questions.
Usually positive, unlike the English noun exploit: réaliser un exploit. Can be ironic: Quel exploit!
From peigner (to comb), originally the cape worn while having your hair done.
Used literally and figuratively for impressing someone. Les phares de la voiture m'ont éblouie. (The car headlights dazzled me.) Adjective: éblouissant.
Same form for both genders. Common phrase: être habile de ses mains.
Conjugated like préférer: je transfère, nous transférons. Also used for moving patients or players.
Masculine, like almost all loanwords ending in o. Borrowed from Italian.
Strengthens comparisons: nettement mieux, nettement plus cher.
From exciter. Feminine: excitante. As a noun, un excitant is a stimulant.
Stronger than le mur: la Grande Muraille de Chine is the Great Wall of China.
capturer qn/qc, used for animals, fugitives or images. Les policiers ont capturé le voleur ce matin. (The police captured the thief this morning.) Also capturer une image.
Une déception is a disappointment, not a deception. Deliberate deceit is la tromperie, and to deceive someone is tromper quelqu'un.
Plural is usually idéaux. As an adjective: une solution idéale.
clin appears almost only in this phrase. en un clin d'œil means in a flash.
Built on grand. Nous voulons agrandir la cuisine l'année prochaine. (We want to enlarge the kitchen next year.) Reflexive s'agrandir means to grow bigger or expand.
Nouns ending in -ance are always feminine. Common: par ignorance (out of ignorance).
Conjugated like tenir: je détiens, nous détenons. Also détenir qn, to hold someone in custody.
Short for microphone, so it stays masculine. parler au micro = to speak into the mic.
It also means a remark: faire une observation à qn is to make a comment to someone.
Feminine: la travailleuse. As an adjective, travailleur means hard-working.
Takes à: identique à qc, never de. Same form for both genders.
commettre un attentat = to carry out an attack. attentat à la bombe = bombing.
Masculine plural: légaux. Opposite: illégal.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Related adjective: rituel.
Je ne me fie pas à ses promesses. [I don't trust his promises.] Always se fier à qn/qc, so the à cannot be dropped. Don't confuse it with the adjective fier, proud.
En substance means "in essence, basically", not "substantially".
Masculine despite the -e. Cortège funèbre = funeral procession.
Ce film m'a passionné du début à la fin. (That film gripped me from start to finish.) Reflexive with pour: se passionner pour qc = to be passionate about something.
S'arrêter net = to stop dead, refuser net = to refuse flatly. As an adverb it never changes form.
A regular -er verb. Il boite encore un peu depuis son accident. (He still limps a little since his accident.) Related: boiteux = limping, or wobbly for a table.
Feminine, and rather formal or official. In everyday speech people say la voiture.

cards.de: to load, to mark (dice or cards, to cheat)
cards.note: Il a triché: quelqu'un avait pipé les dés. (He cheated: someone had loaded the dice.) Des dés pipés = loaded dice. Ne pas piper mot = not to say a word.
From contenir. Le contenu d'une lettre, but le contenant = the container.
Elle a machinalement regardé son téléphone. [She looked at her phone without thinking.] Describes actions done out of habit, and it has nothing to do with machines or technology.
Feminine form: la tsarine. The spelling tzar also appears.
The opposite of sensé (sensible). Often heard as c'est insensé! = that's crazy!
Unlike English, the adjective is lower case; the person is capitalised: un Polonais. The language is le polonais.
Adjectives ending in -ible have the same form in the masculine and the feminine.
Almost always plural in French, unlike the English mass noun: être à court de munitions = to be low on ammunition.
Feminine. The same word also means etiquette in the sense of courtly manners.
Written with an accent circonflexe. La télévision par câble = cable television.
Colloquially, casser la croûte means to have a bite to eat.
Also used for the American prairie. A small field near a house is le pré.
Regular -er verb. On va tester la nouvelle application demain. (We are going to test the new app tomorrow.) The noun is un test or un essai.
Very common as an exclamation: quelle corvée! It originally meant feudal forced labour.
Usually plural: avoir des scrupules à faire qc means to have qualms about doing something.
Lower case for the drink, capital C for the town of Cognac.

cards.de: the full tank of fuel (faire le ...)
cards.note: Set phrase: faire le plein (d'essence) means to fill up the tank.
The fire brigade is les pompiers: appeler les pompiers.
Feminine form: la sénatrice. He sits in le Sénat, the upper house of parliament.
Note the spelling: no letter after the n, unlike English comfort. The adjective is confortable.

cards.de: to stain, to leave marks on
cards.note: From une tache (a stain). Attention, tu vas tacher ta chemise avec le café. (Careful, you are going to stain your shirt with the coffee.) Do not confuse it with tâcher de faire qc, to try to do something.
A feminine noun. Often used in vivre en harmonie avec la nature.
Known from la Légion étrangère (the Foreign Legion). Also figurative: une légion de fans.
Always masculine, even for a woman. It also means a shop window dummy.
From bras (arm). A watch strap is un bracelet de montre.
Le gouvernement veut abaisser les prix de l'électricité. (The government wants to lower electricity prices.) Reflexive s'abaisser à faire qc means to stoop to doing something.
un village isolé, se sentir isolé. The related noun is l'isolement (isolation, seclusion).
Feminine form: la prophétesse. Watch the accent grave in prophète.
Slightly more formal than le début, which is far more common.
A masculine noun used only in the plural. Do not confuse it with the verb vivre (to live).
proclamer les résultats, proclamer l'indépendance. More solemn in tone than annoncer.
Feminine: odieuse. Also used of people: il est odieux avec sa sœur (he is horrible to her).
Feminine: la naine. Also an adjective: une étoile naine (a dwarf star).
Used almost only in the participle. Je suis navré, je ne peux pas vous aider. (I am terribly sorry, I cannot help you.) Sounds polite and slightly formal.
Masculine noun. The related adjective is continental.
Masculine plural: commerciaux. Very common in un centre commercial (a shopping centre).

cards.de: to conceal, to hide from view
cards.note: Construction: masquer qc à qn (to hide something from someone). Also literal: la haie masque la vue.
Feminine noun. It can also mean a religious denomination or an admission of guilt.
Feminine: indienne. For Native American, the usual word today is amérindien.
Also an adjective: une lettre manuscrite, a handwritten letter.
A regular -er verb. Le professeur nous demande d'analyser ce poème. (The teacher is asking us to analyse this poem.) Related noun: une analyse, an analysis or a blood test.
Usually followed by de: de la confiture de fraises. Often plural on the breakfast table: des confitures.
Typical use: une somme dérisoire, a laughably small sum. The form is the same for both genders.
Common phrase: il y a une nuance, there is a subtle difference. Verb: nuancer, to qualify or shade.
Also un défilé de mode, a fashion show. Verb: défiler, to march past.
Irregular feminine: favorite (mon émission favorite). As a noun: le favori, the favourite.
Linked to l'Antiquité, classical antiquity. For antique furniture in a shop, the word is ancien.
Plural: des bourreaux. Figuratively: un bourreau de travail, a workaholic.

cards.de: as soon as (adverb, e.g. ... que je serai prêt)
cards.note: Sitôt que je serai prêt, je t'appellerai. [As soon as I'm ready, I'll call you.] Sitôt que takes the indicative. Also common in pas de sitôt, not any time soon.
Related to le bruit, noise. Feminine: bruyante, adverb: bruyamment.
Mon frère aîné, my older brother. The opposite is cadet, younger.
Use la rive for a riverbank and le rivage for the seashore. Nouns ending in -age are almost always masculine.
Related to le dégoût, disgust, and dégoûter quelqu'un. Informally it also describes mean behaviour.
Related to la jambe, leg. Un jambon-beurre is the classic ham baguette.
A collective noun that stays singular: la clientèle est fidèle. One person is le client, la cliente.

cards.de: to wobble (be loose, e.g. a tooth)
cards.note: Cette dent branle depuis hier soir. (This tooth has been wobbling since last night.) Careful: the reflexive se branler and "ne rien branler" are vulgar. For a neutral wobble use bouger or être branlant.
Elle l'a giflé devant tout le monde. (She slapped him in front of everyone.) Say gifler quelqu'un, with no preposition. The noun is une gifle.
Only the fruit; a light bulb is une ampoule. Informally une poire is also a sucker or fool.
Usually plural: les fidèles, the faithful. As an adjective fidèle means faithful: être fidèle à quelqu'un.
Directly transitive: commenter un match, commenter une photo. Unlike English, there is no "on" after it.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -ité. Common phrase: rester dans l'immobilité, to stay motionless.
The verb is punir quelqu'un. A sentence handed down in court is la peine instead.

cards.de: the small public garden (in a city neighbourhood)
cards.note: Despite the English look, it is not a town square but a little green space. Pronounced roughly "skwar".
Feminine constante, adverb constamment, constantly. Common: une pression constante.
Careful: in the plural les ciseaux means scissors (une paire de ciseaux).
From croître, to grow. Hence un croissant de lune, a crescent moon, and the adjective croissant, growing.
Invariable: une soi-disant amie. Strictly it applies to people, but informally it is also used adverbially: il est soi-disant malade.
The g is silent: [etɑ̃]. Bigger than une mare, a small pool, and smaller than un lac.
Past participle of tordre, to twist or wring. Le cadre est tout tordu depuis le déménagement. (The frame is completely bent since the move.) Informally être tordu means to be a bit warped.
Takes sur: enquêter sur une affaire. The noun une enquête means both an investigation and a survey.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Note payer en liquide = to pay cash, de l'argent liquide = cash.
The final c is pronounced. Common: le tir à l'arc (archery), un arc-en-ciel (rainbow).

cards.de: to shiver (tremble with cold or fear)
cards.note: Used with de: frissonner de froid, frissonner de peur. Noun: un frisson (a shiver).
Same form in masculine and feminine: un animal féroce, une bête féroce. Also figurative: une critique féroce.
Feminine in French: la phase finale. Also en phase avec quelqu'un (on the same wavelength as someone).
Nouns ending in -ence are always feminine. The verb is exiger qc de qn (to demand something of someone).
The male counterpart is le neveu. Watch the accent grave: nièce.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. Verb: signifier, as in que signifie ce mot?
Usually reflexive. Le chien s'est élancé vers son maître. (The dog dashed towards its owner.) Without the pronoun, ça m'élance means it throbs with pain.

cards.de: to rock (a child, in your arms or a cradle)
cards.note: Elle berce son bébé pour l'endormir. (She is rocking her baby to get him to sleep.) Not the same as weighing something, which is peser. Related: une berceuse, a lullaby.
Le vent a courbé les jeunes arbres du jardin. (The wind bent the young trees in the garden.) Often reflexive: se courber, to bend down. Adjective: courbé (bent, stooped).
Listed as an adjective in dictionaries, but used almost only as a noun. On board you address him as mon commandant.

cards.de: the promotion (a step up at work)
cards.note: Ends in -tion, so it is feminine. In a supermarket, en promotion means on special offer.
Feminine form: matérielle. As a noun, le matériel means equipment or gear.

cards.de: to add more (add again on top)
cards.note: Tu peux rajouter du sel dans la soupe ? (Can you add more salt to the soup?) It is an intensified form of ajouter and often interchangeable with it in speech. Idiom: en rajouter (to lay it on thick).

Very common in written texts and the news, often used to introduce examples. Elle parle plusieurs langues, notamment l'espagnol. (She speaks several languages, notably Spanish.) Pronounced like notamman.
Cette vieille porte commence à grincer. (This old door is starting to creak.) The c becomes ç before a and o: nous grinçons. Typical: grincer des dents (to grind your teeth).
Also a bite or sting from an insect. Note the accent circonflexe on the û; the verb is piquer.
Common in tomber avec fracas (to fall with a crash). Singular and plural sound the same, as the s stays silent.
Rare and formal as an adjective: une prière instante. The noun un instant (a moment) is far more common.
Formal, and often figurative: souiller la réputation de qn.
Usually plural. Colloquially it also means your gut feelings: prendre qn aux tripes means to move someone deeply.

cards.de: to develop (to evolve, change over time)
cards.note: La situation peut évoluer très vite. (The situation can change very fast.) Used without se: la situation évolue. For the direction of change, use vers: évoluer vers qc.
Like all nouns ending in -tion, it is feminine. Also used for biological evolution: la théorie de l'évolution.
From the verb livrer (to deliver). A common phrase is la livraison à domicile (home delivery).
Feminine une nazie, adjective nazi(e): le régime nazi. French writes it with a small n.
The h is silent, so un homme honorable links the sounds together. It can also mean decent or respectable: un résultat honorable.
Very common: un certificat médical (doctor's note). The related verb is certifier.
An irregular feminine form of le dieu: dieu, déesse.

cards.de: to fill with wonder (to amaze, delight)
cards.note: Ce spectacle va émerveiller les enfants. (This show is going to fill the children with wonder.) Reflexive with de: s'émerveiller de qc means to marvel at something. Related to la merveille (a marvel).
Found in set phrases: une table de chevet (bedside table), une lampe de chevet. Au chevet de qn means at someone's bedside.
From the verb convenir. Often means decent or presentable: une tenue convenable.
Plural les tombeaux. A plain grave is la tombe.
La police va questionner les témoins demain. (The police are going to question the witnesses tomorrow.) The pattern is questionner qn sur qc, with no preposition before the person.
Mon chien se met à baver dès qu'il voit sa gamelle. (My dog starts drooling as soon as he sees his bowl.) Colloquially en baver means to have a hard time of it. The related noun is la bave (drool).
Pronounced roughly ka-oot-choo, with the final c silent. Bottes en caoutchouc are wellington boots.
Il ne faut pas mal interpréter ses paroles. (You mustn't misinterpret his words.) Also used of performers: playing a role or singing a song. Watch the accent shift: il interprète.
Je ne voulais pas vous offenser. (I didn't mean to offend you.) The pattern is offenser qn, with no preposition. Reflexive: s'offenser de qc, to take offence at something.
Je suis satisfait de mon nouveau travail. (I'm happy with my new job.) The pattern is être satisfait de qc. It is the past participle of satisfaire.
Used figuratively too: un alibi en béton is a cast-iron alibi.
The opposite is définitif. The ending -oire is the same for both genders.
Short for pull-over, and masculine. Un pull en laine is a wool jumper.
Also une décharge électrique, an electric shock. In the phrase à sa décharge it means in his or her defence.
The same word means a milling cutter and a dentist's drill. Tarte aux fraises is strawberry tart.
mettre qc en gage means to pawn something. In the plural, les gages is the wages of domestic staff.
Written exactly like il aura from avoir, but here it is a feminine noun.
Feminine is stricte, and then the t is pronounced. Le strict minimum is the bare minimum.

cards.de: the start (sudden jolt of the body)
cards.note: Common in se réveiller en sursaut, to wake up with a start. The verb is sursauter.
Note the double n: feminine traditionnelle, adverb traditionnellement.
Masculine plural is vitaux. Une question vitale is a matter of life and death, nothing to do with being energetic.
explorer une grotte, une piste. The related noun is un explorateur, an explorer.
Le chat sort ses griffes. It also means a designer's label; the verb griffer means to scratch.
The counterpart is le mâle. It can also follow a noun like an adjective: un éléphant femelle.
Literally badly heard, from mal + entendre. Often: il y a un malentendu.
Almost always used in the plural. Set phrase: être en pleurs, to be in floods of tears.
On doit décharger la voiture avant la pluie. (We have to unload the car before the rain.) It is the opposite of charger. Also décharger qn de qc, to relieve someone of something.

Tu peux me résumer le film en deux phrases ? (Can you summarise the film for me in two sentences?) A false friend: it does not mean to resume, which is reprendre. Se résumer à qc means to come down to something.
The construction is être favorable à qc, to be in favour of something.
The opposite is mineur. It also means major or main: un problème majeur, un cas de force majeure.
Les phares peuvent aveugler les conducteurs. (Headlights can dazzle drivers.) It comes from aveugle, blind. Also figurative: la colère l'aveugle, anger blinds him.
Il fait tout pour exaspérer sa sœur. (He does everything to exasperate his sister.) Much stronger than énerver. Very common as ça m'exaspère.

cards.de: the pit (hole dug in the ground)
cards.note: The related le fossé is a ditch beside a road. La fosse d'orchestre is the orchestra pit.

cards.de: to stall (an engine), to come to a halt
cards.note: Ma voiture vient de caler au feu rouge. (My car just stalled at the red light.) Also to wedge or prop something up: caler une armoire. Informally je cale means I can't eat any more.
The feminine is ouvrière, hence la classe ouvrière. As a noun, un ouvrier is a manual worker.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Common phrase: à intervalles réguliers.
From the verb gémir, to moan. All nouns ending in -ment are masculine.

cards.de: the notary (lawyer for property and wills)
cards.note: For a woman, la notaire is now usual. You often hear passer chez le notaire when buying a house.
Built on la main, hand. Manier un outil, une langue. Don't mix it up with manger.
Familiar baby talk, like mémé for grandma. The neutral word is le grand-père.
Slightly formal, used for things that surprise you: un objet insolite, une rencontre insolite.
Colloquial, from bouffer, to scoff or wolf down. The neutral word is la nourriture.
Il m'écoutait, les bras croisés. (He listened to me with his arms folded.) Common in les bras croisés, with arms folded, and les mots croisés, a crossword.
Nous devons repenser tout le projet. (We need to rethink the whole project.) With a direct object: repenser le projet. With à, repenser à quelque chose means to think of something again.
La pluie a fini par inonder la cave. (The rain ended up flooding the cellar.) Also figurative: être inondé de courriels, to be swamped with emails.
La grève va paralyser toute la ville. (The strike is going to paralyse the whole city.) Often in the passive: être paralysé par la peur, to be frozen with fear.
Le simple dames, le simple messieurs. The counterpart is le double, doubles.
Masculine. Subir un interrogatoire means to be questioned; the verb is interroger.
Same form for a woman: une hérétique. It also works as an adjective: une idée hérétique.
Used as extraire quelque chose de quelque chose. Irregular like traire: j'extrais, nous extrayons, past participle extrait.
Colloquial: refiler quelque chose à quelqu'un, as in il m'a refilé son rhume (he gave me his cold).
Don't confuse it with la boucle (curl, buckle). Figuratively: servir de bouclier, to act as a shield.
Regular -ir verb like finir. Often définir quelque chose comme ... or se définir comme ...
From le voile (the veil): dévoiler un secret, un projet.
This noun is feminine: la vidéo. Used as an adjective it never changes: des jeux vidéo.
Feminine, related to un étage (floor, storey). Une étagère à livres is a bookshelf.
J'ai réussi à choper le dernier train. (I managed to catch the last train.) Colloquial. Choper un rhume means to catch a cold, se faire choper to get caught.
Feminine form la supérieure. The usual phrase is mon supérieur hiérarchique, my line manager.
Feminine intellectuelle, plural intellectuels. It also works as a noun: un intellectuel, an intellectual.

cards.de: the cork, the stopper (for a bottle)
cards.note: A second very common meaning is traffic jam: il y a un bouchon sur l'autoroute.

cards.de: to slip through, to weave one's way (through a crowd)
cards.note: Almost always reflexive: se faufiler dans la foule, se faufiler entre les voitures.

cards.de: the villain (bad guy in a film)
cards.note: From the adjective méchant (nasty, wicked): les gentils et les méchants, the goodies and the baddies.

cards.de: to clear up (a mystery), to lighten
cards.note: éclaircir un mystère. Reflexive: le ciel s'éclaircit (the sky is clearing), s'éclaircir la voix (to clear one's throat).
Masculine, usually with the article: l'infini. Set phrase: à l'infini, endlessly.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Adjective: cruel, cruelle. La cruauté envers les animaux.
Same form for both genders: le/la locataire. Its counterpart is le propriétaire, the owner or landlord.
Feminine: la farine. De la farine de blé, un kilo de farine.
Linked to the verb se méfier de qn/qc, to distrust someone: méfie-toi de lui!
Elle n'arrête pas de cligner des yeux. (She keeps blinking.) Used with the partitive: cligner des yeux. Cligner de l'œil means to wink at someone.
