Same form for a woman: la psychiatre. Pronounced roughly see-kya-tr, with no vowel sound before the k.
A seat with no back or arms, as in le tabouret de bar.
Formed from couper. Also used figuratively: une coupure de courant is a power cut.
Always followed by à: accéder à un site, accéder à la demande de qn (to grant someone's request).
Plural in x: les chameaux. As an insult, quel chameau means what a nasty piece of work.

Le patron va inspecter les cuisines demain matin. [The boss is going to inspect the kitchens tomorrow morning.] A regular er verb. The related noun is un inspecteur, in the police or in school inspection.
Colloquial for rater or manquer: j'ai loupé le train. Also louper un examen, to fail an exam.
Pronounced [ka-o]: the ch sounds like k and the final s is silent.

cards.de: to drop, to release (a bomb, ballast)
cards.note: Originally nautical (larguer les amarres, to cast off). Informally, larguer qn means to dump someone.
Je me sens gêné quand tout le monde me regarde. [I feel embarrassed when everyone looks at me.] From gêner (to bother). Être gêné means to feel uncomfortable or self conscious, not annoyed.
In law it sits between contravention and crime. Set phrase: en flagrant délit, caught red handed.
Short for professionnel; for a woman, la pro. Informal: c'est un pro.
Feminine. The related verb is cirer, as in cirer ses chaussures (to polish your shoes).
Cette injustice va indigner tout le village. [This injustice will outrage the whole village.] Usually reflexive: s'indigner de qc, to be outraged about something. Adjective: indigné.
Very common as le registre de langue, the level of language such as familier or soutenu.
C'est le top means that's brilliant. It is also a starting signal: au top, partez.
Same form for both genders. Used as contraire à qc; as a noun le contraire, and au contraire means on the contrary.

cards.de: the composition (of a substance, of a group)
cards.note: All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. At school, une composition is also an essay.

Il faut tasser la terre autour de la plante. [You have to pack down the soil around the plant.] Reflexive se tasser means to squeeze together, or colloquially to settle down: ça va se tasser, it'll sort itself out.
On va trinquer à ta nouvelle maison ! [We're going to drink a toast to your new house!] It comes from German trinken, to drink. Say trinquer à la santé de qn, to drink to someone's health.
Same form for masculine and feminine. As a noun, un adulte or une adulte, an adult.
Feminine polie, opposite impoli. The same word also means polished, from the verb polir.
Mostly used in the phrase en direct, live on TV or radio. In boxing, un direct is a straight punch.

cards.de: the ledge, the rim (projecting edge, e.g. a window sill)
cards.note: Very common: le rebord de la fenêtre, the window sill.
Cette application peut faciliter ton travail. [This app can make your work easier.] faciliter qc à qn means to make something easier for someone. Don't confuse it with féliciter, to congratulate.
Masculine, like nearly all nouns ending in -ment. Also used in the plural: les équipements sportifs, sports facilities.

cards.de: to have a feeling about, to sense in advance
cards.note: Conjugated like sentir: je pressens, nous pressentons. The related noun is un pressentiment, a premonition.
Feminine savante. As a noun, un savant is a scholar or scientist.

cards.de: the member of parliament, the deputy
cards.note: A member of the Assemblée nationale. The feminine form today is une députée.

cards.de: the insult, the term of abuse
cards.note: Feminine. Often plural: couvrir qn d'injures, to hurl abuse at someone.

cards.de: the access, the approach (to a person or a place)
cards.note: Mostly found in set phrases: d'abord means first, au premier abord at first sight. Il est d'un abord facile, he is easy to approach.
The h is silent, so you get l'humiliation and a liaison. The verb is humilier qn.
Feminine perpétuelle with double l. Often slightly negative: des plaintes perpétuelles, endless complaining.

cards.de: the plaster (the material, also a cast)
cards.note: Masculine despite ending in -e. Avoir le bras dans le plâtre means to have one's arm in a cast.

cards.de: to boil (of a liquid, to bubble)
cards.note: Irregular: je bous, il bout, nous bouillons. Very common: faire bouillir de l'eau, to boil water.
The feminine form is la fermière. The farm itself is la ferme.
The same word also means chopstick (manger avec des baguettes) and wand (baguette magique).
Also means unaware or reckless. As a noun, l'inconscient is the unconscious mind.
The final -ls is silent, so it sounds like pou. Set phrase: prendre le pouls de qn.
Un tiers de la population. It also means a third party, someone not involved.
Il va botter le ballon vers le but. [He's going to kick the ball towards the goal.] From la botte (boot). Colloquially, ça me botte means I like it.
Donner une claque à qn. Figuratively, prendre une claque means to suffer a heavy defeat.

cards.de: school (relating to school, as in school year)
cards.note: Same form for masculine and feminine. Common: l'année scolaire, les fournitures scolaires.
A curve in a road is le virage instead. As an adjective, courbe means curved.
Nouns of this type ending in -on are feminine. Also medical: la cloison nasale (nasal septum).

cards.de: the therapist (casual short form of psychologist)
cards.note: Short for psychologue or psychiatre. Feminine une psy. Aller chez le psy.
It sounds just like air and aire, so watch the spelling. Une nouvelle ère commence.
Suivre les consignes means to follow the instructions. It also means left luggage office and deposit on a bottle.
Usually said as rafale de vent. Also a burst of gunfire: une rafale de mitraillette.
Arrête de chialer pour un match perdu ! [Stop blubbering over a lost match!] Very colloquial and dismissive version of pleurer. Avoid it in formal situations.
Same form for masculine and feminine. The noun is la mélancolie.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. At the station: un train à destination de Lyon.
The word itself does not change, only the article: la dentiste for a woman. The final -e is silent.
Le médecin va me prescrire des antibiotiques. [The doctor is going to prescribe me antibiotics.] Conjugated like écrire: il prescrit, nous prescrivons. Pattern: prescrire qc à qn.
From éclairer (to light up), so it can also mean literally lit. Common: un esprit éclairé, le despotisme éclairé.
Je n'aime pas du tout le poisson cru. [I don't like raw fish at all.] Feminine: crue (la viande crue). Spelled the same as the past participle of croire.
Mon vélo a été volé devant la gare. [My bike was stolen in front of the station.] voler means both to steal and to fly, so context decides. Une voiture volée.

cards.de: to be delirious (rave with fever; informally: to talk nonsense)
cards.note: Tu commences à délirer, il est trois heures du matin. [You're starting to talk nonsense, it's three in the morning.] Very common as Tu délires ! = You're out of your mind! Noun: le délire.
Family and child language, the counterpart of papi. More formal: la grand-mère.

Tu peux me redonner mon stylo, s'il te plaît ? [Can you give me back my pen, please?] The prefix re means again, much like English re. Very common figuratively: redonner confiance à qn (to restore someone's confidence).
À neuf heures, mon fils est déjà couché. [At nine o'clock, my son is already in bed.] être couché means to be lying down, not sitting. Related verb: se coucher (to lie down, to go to bed).
An e is added before a and o: nous forgeons. Figuratively: se forger une opinion (to form an opinion).

Arrête d'épier les voisins par la fenêtre ! [Stop spying on the neighbours through the window!] Takes a direct object: épier qn. Close to espionner (to spy), not to be confused with épicer (to spice).

cards.de: sweetie (pet name for a person, informal)
cards.note: Colloquial, feminine la louloute. It is also the name of the Pomeranian dog breed.
A false friend: an editor of texts is le rédacteur. Feminine: une éditrice; a publishing house is la maison d'édition.
Il mange proprement, sans rien renverser. (He eats neatly, without spilling anything.) Note the set phrase proprement dit = strictly speaking, in the proper sense.
Nouns ending in -té are almost always feminine. Adjective: pur, pure.
The same word also means underage or a minor (une mineure). From la mine (mine).
Written with a circumflex. As an exclamation, Flûte! = Darn! Also une flûte de champagne (champagne glass).

cards.de: to disown (renounce a person or thing)
cards.note: Il refuse de renier ses amis d'enfance. [He refuses to disown his childhood friends.] renier qn/qc, for example renier sa foi (to renounce one's faith). Stronger than nier (to deny something).

La prof va nous dicter un texte très court. [The teacher is going to dictate a very short text to us.] Pattern: dicter qc à qn. Also figurative: dicter sa conduite à qn, to tell someone how to behave.
It ends in e and stays the same in the masculine and feminine. Typical: un paysage morne, une vie morne.
Also used for a schedule or timetable: le calendrier des travaux.
Va te faire enculer ! [Get lost, very crudely.] Very vulgar, and best known in the insult enculé. Better avoided in conversation.
Le feu est éteint depuis une heure. [The fire has been out for an hour.] Past participle of éteindre, opposite of allumé. Also used for a flat voice: une voix éteinte.
Je n'arrive pas à déchiffrer son écriture. [I can't decipher his handwriting.] Used for illegible handwriting, codes, and also sight reading music.
porter un toast à qn means to drink a toast to someone. The same word also means a slice of toasted bread.
Masculine plural: occidentaux. The opposite is oriental.
Borrowed from English and neutral in tone. Also a noun: un gay.
A pharmacist is le pharmacien. A bathroom medicine cabinet is une armoire à pharmacie.

cards.de: to obsess, to haunt (as a fixed idea)
cards.note: In French the idea is the subject: Cette idée m'obsède depuis des semaines. (This idea has been haunting me for weeks.) The accent shifts: il obsède, nous obsédons.
Built on tourner. Figuratively: un tourbillon de pensées, a whirl of thoughts.
Before a noun it takes de: énormément de gens. It also intensifies verbs: J'ai énormément travaillé cette semaine. (I worked an enormous amount this week.)

cards.de: to wind up, to roll up
cards.note: Pattern: enrouler qc autour de qc. Elle enroule son écharpe autour de son cou. (She winds her scarf around her neck.) Reflexive: s'enrouler dans une couverture, to wrap yourself in a blanket.
Feminine: la commerçante. Remember the cédille: it keeps the c soft before a.
It can also be neutral, meaning to use or to run: exploiter une ferme, exploiter les données.
From la caisse, the till. Le magasin encaisse l'argent à la fin de la journée. (The shop takes in the money at the end of the day.) Informally it also means to take a hit: encaisser un coup.
From gêner, to bother. Une situation gênante is an awkward situation.
Pattern: infliger qc à qn. Le juge lui a infligé une lourde amende. (The judge imposed a heavy fine on him.) Like all ger verbs it keeps the e: nous infligeons.

cards.de: the trail (a streak left behind, e.g. of blood)
cards.note: From traîner, to drag. Common uses: une traînée de sang, and se répandre comme une traînée de poudre, to spread like wildfire.
The same word works as an adjective: une punition exemplaire, an exemplary punishment.
Adjectives ending in -ique keep the same form in the feminine. Un document authentique, une émotion authentique.
Pattern: indépendant de qc. Feminine indépendante; travailleur indépendant means self-employed worker.

cards.de: in the long run, over time (set phrase)
cards.note: The noun la longue survives almost only in this phrase. The adjective is long, longue.
The final f is pronounced and the stress falls on the last syllable. Mettre en relief means to highlight.
Feminine: une survivante. The verb takes à: survivre à qc, to survive something.
Difference: assassinat is a planned killing, meurtre is a killing without premeditation.

cards.de: to embarrass, to make someone uncomfortable
cards.note: Ta question m'embarrasse un peu. (Your question makes me a bit uncomfortable.) Often used in the passive: être embarrassé, to be embarrassed. It can also mean to clutter up or get in the way.
Conjugates like ouvrir: j'entrouvre, participle entrouvert. Il entrouvre la fenêtre pour aérer la chambre. (He opens the window slightly to air the room.) Une porte entrouverte is a door ajar.
Colloquially, un faux jeton means a two-faced person.
La chaîne diffuse le match en direct ce soir. (The channel is broadcasting the match live tonight.) It also means to spread, as with news or a smell. Noun: la diffusion.
Masculine plural animaux, feminine animale. Le règne animal, la graisse animale.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. Verb: exciter qn.

cards.de: to liquidate, to wind up (also: to get rid of)
cards.note: Liquider un stock = to sell off stock. Colloquially it can also mean to kill someone.
Conjugates like naître: il renaît, with être as the auxiliary. Au printemps, la nature renaît. (In spring, nature comes back to life.) Renaître de ses cendres means to rise from the ashes.
Donner une gifle à qn = to slap someone; the verb is gifler qn.
Related noun: le frein, the brake. Il freine brusquement devant le feu rouge. (He brakes suddenly at the red light.) Also figurative: freiner l'inflation.
A regular -ir verb like finir: je polis, nous polissons. Also figurative: polir son style.
Masculine: le fragment. Common phrase: un fragment de conversation.
J'habite près de la gare. (I live near the station.) Don't confuse it with prêt à (ready to). Before numbers, près de means almost: près de mille personnes.
A defective verb, used almost only as il gît, ils gisent and ci-gît (here lies) on gravestones. Le blessé gît sur le trottoir. (The injured man is lying on the pavement.) Formal or literary.
Same form in the masculine and feminine. As a noun, un interne is a junior doctor or a boarding school pupil.
All words ending in -tion are feminine. Common phrase: avoir l'intuition que.
Traditionally it has no feminine form, so you say elle est le vainqueur, or the newer la vainqueure.
French note names are do, ré, mi, fa, sol, la, si, and they are all masculine.

In the phrase étant donné que it means since or given that: Étant donné que tu es fatigué, reste à la maison. (Given that you are tired, stay home.) And c'est donné is a colloquial way of saying it's dirt cheap.
An -ir verb like finir: Les arbres fleurissent déjà en mars. (The trees are already blossoming in March.) Figuratively for business, use florissant, thriving.
From la couronne (crown). Common phrase: ses efforts ont été couronnés de succès (his efforts were crowned with success).
A strong word, also used for food: une nourriture ignoble (disgusting food). Same form in masculine and feminine.
Feminine form directrice: l'idée directrice (the guiding idea), les lignes directrices (the guidelines).
Conjugated like venir and takes être in the passé composé: un problème est survenu.
Masculine despite the final -e. Common phrase: au bénéfice de (in aid of, for the benefit of).
Je bâille parce que je n'ai pas assez dormi. (I am yawning because I did not sleep enough.) Don't confuse it with bailler or bayer. Remember the circumflex: bâiller d'ennui, to yawn with boredom.
L'enfant agrippe la main de sa mère. (The child grips his mother's hand.) Often reflexive: s'agripper à qc, to cling on to something.
Masculine, with the irregular plural berceaux. It comes from bercer (to rock).
Feminine une intellectuelle with a double l. The colloquial short form is un intello.
Tu as laissé la lumière allumée dans la cuisine. (You left the light on in the kitchen.) The opposite is éteint. Colloquially, il est complètement allumé also means he's completely crazy.
Il déplie la carte sur la table pour trouver la route. (He unfolds the map on the table to find the road.) The opposite of plier, to fold; replier means to fold back up.
Feminine gracieuse. In the set phrase à titre gracieux it means free of charge.
Je médite dix minutes chaque matin. (I meditate for ten minutes every morning.) Used with sur for reflection: méditer sur qc, to ponder something.
Related to the noun l'épouvante (terror). Common use: un temps épouvantable (awful weather).
In a military context it also means a detachment of troops. The verb is se détacher de qc.
Feminine financière, e.g. une aide financière. As a noun it means a financier.
Very informal, borrowed from Arabic; the neutral word is le médecin.
La police reconstitue les faits avec les témoins. (The police are piecing together what happened with the witnesses.) Also used for restoring something lost, like reconstituer une collection.
Irregular plural: les bijoux. The shop is la bijouterie.
Feminine excessive, adverb excessivement.
The feminine form is identical. As a noun, le trouble means disturbance or unease.
Also used for a section inside a drawer or a bag.
Reflexive se décourager means to lose heart. Ne te décourage pas!
Also a Protestant church service. Very common: un film culte, a cult film.

cards.de: destiny (the course a life is meant to take)
cards.note: Alongside le destin; la destinée stresses the path a life is laid out to follow.
The pattern is être doué pour les langues or doué en maths.

cards.de: to embrace, to wrap your arms around
cards.note: Elle enlace son frère avant de partir. (She hugs her brother before leaving.) Reflexive s'enlacer means to hold each other in an embrace. From le lacet, a lace or cord.
The masculine plural is capitaux. Very common: d'une importance capitale.
Feminine collective, as in une décision collective.
The masculine is le jumeau. In the plural, les jumelles also means binoculars.

cards.de: the washbasin, the sink (in a bathroom)
cards.note: From Latin lavabo, I will wash. A kitchen sink is l'évier instead.
Often figurative: un silence pesant, une atmosphère pesante. For physical weight, lourd is usual.

cards.de: to persist stubbornly, to dig one's heels in (about something)
cards.note: Used only reflexively: s'obstiner à faire qc or s'obstiner dans son erreur.
Adjectives ending in -aire do not change in the feminine. Un prix littéraire, une œuvre littéraire.
From menacer; the cedilla keeps the c soft before a. Le ciel devient menaçant, rentrons vite. (The sky is turning threatening, let's go home quickly.) It works for people too: un regard menaçant.
Feminine universelle with double l. Le suffrage universel is universal suffrage.
Directly transitive: no preposition after it. Les enfants ont escaladé le mur du jardin. (The children climbed the garden wall.)
Shortened to le foot in everyday speech. The ball itself is le ballon.
From the adjective attentif, attentive. Lis attentivement les instructions avant de commencer. (Read the instructions carefully before starting.) Écouter attentivement means to listen closely.
In France, la quatrième is also a school year (roughly age 13). Written short as 4e.

cards.de: the monk, the member of a religious order
cards.note: The feminine une religieuse means a nun. Une religieuse is also a choux pastry cake.
Past participle of choisir, also used as an adjective: des mots choisis means well-chosen words.
The related verb: ça me répugne, it disgusts me. Much stronger than désagréable.
Feminine form une apprentie. Un apprenti boulanger is a trainee baker.
A regular -ir verb like finir. Le froid raidit mes doigts en quelques minutes. (The cold stiffens my fingers in a few minutes.) Reflexive se raidir means to stiffen up, also to tense up emotionally.
Capitalised for the person, lower case as an adjective: la cuisine indienne. Feminine une Indienne.
Note values are named by colour: la blanche is a half note, la noire a quarter note. The masculine le blanc means the white part or white wine.
The u stays in every form: je navigue. Nous naviguons le long de la côte depuis ce matin. (We have been sailing along the coast since this morning.) Also used online: naviguer sur Internet.
Feminine une professionnelle. As an adjective professionnel/professionnelle, as in la vie professionnelle.
From écarter (to move apart). Ils habitent dans un village écarté, loin de la ville. (They live in a remote village, far from the city.) Les jambes écartées means with legs spread apart.
Related to rêver (to dream), used as rêver de qc. Common phrase: perdu dans ses rêveries.
Adjectives ending in -ique are the same in masculine and feminine. Typical: un appel téléphonique, une cabine téléphonique.
Nouns of this type ending in -ice are feminine. Common: lutter contre l'injustice.

Past participle of rendre. J'ai déjà rendu les livres à la bibliothèque. (I have already given the books back to the library.) Colloquially je suis rendu can mean I have arrived or I am completely worn out.
Feminine noun. Key collocation: la convention collective, a collective labour agreement.
The form does not change: une disciple for a woman. Not a pupil at school, that is un élève.
You say jouer au billard. The final d is silent.
It goes straight before the word it modifies: Trouver un billet ce soir est quasi impossible. (Finding a ticket tonight is almost impossible.) In everyday speech quasiment is more common.
Une torche électrique is a flashlight. Do not confuse it with a tart, which is la tarte.
Feminine douteuse, masculine plural stays douteux. Une blague douteuse is a tasteless joke.
Feminine: une antenne. Être à l'antenne means to be on air.
A diminutive of fourche (pitchfork). Figuratively, une fourchette de prix is a price range.
Masculine plural infernaux, feminine infernale. Un bruit infernal is an unbearable racket.
Masculine, and the final l is pronounced. Vivre en exil, with the verb s'exiler.

cards.de: to mess up, to screw up
cards.note: Very colloquial and slightly crude, so avoid it at work. J'ai merdé mon entretien de ce matin. (I screwed up my interview this morning.)
It contains le poing (fist). Un coup de poignard is a stab with a dagger.
The adverb is ironiquement. Common phrase: un sourire ironique.

cards.de: to embrace tightly, to hug close
cards.note: Conjugated like peindre: j'étreins, nous étreignons. Elle a voulu étreindre son frère avant son départ. (She wanted to hug her brother tightly before he left.) The noun is une étreinte.
A regular -er verb like parler. Nous campons au bord du lac tous les étés. (We camp by the lake every summer.) Related: le camping, which is both the campsite and the activity.
Two r's and one s, as in résister. Same form for masculine and feminine.
Masculine: le pacte. Common phrase: conclure un pacte avec qn.
Used as peiner à faire qc. Je peine à comprendre ses explications. (I struggle to understand his explanations.) Transitively it means to sadden: cela me peine.
Also se poster, to station oneself somewhere. Don't confuse it with la poste, the post office.
Derived from un artiste. Common phrase: le patrimoine artistique.
Used as implorer qn de faire qc. Elle l'a imploré de rester encore un jour. (She begged him to stay one more day.) It is close in register to supplier, both sounding literary.
Feminine: la thèse. It also means a doctoral thesis: soutenir sa thèse.
Masculine, like all nouns ending in -ment. Faire un pansement, and un pansement adhésif is a plaster.
Masculine: le pilier. Figuratively: il est un pilier de l'entreprise, he is a mainstay of the company.
Colloquial, the everyday word for a stub. Common phrase: écraser son mégot.
Same form for both genders. Often heard as ce n'est pas dramatique, meaning it's not a big deal.
Nouns ending in -tion and -sion are feminine: une obsession, la passion, la pression. The related adjective is obsédé par quelque chose.
Built from the feminine form forte plus -ment. Often: je vous le conseille fortement.
Doubles the l in stressed forms: il ruisselle. Après la course, il ruisselait de sueur. (After the race, he was dripping with sweat.) It comes from le ruisseau, a stream.
A shade more formal than tout à coup. Often: il est mort subitement.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine in French. It can also mean a medal or award.
Feminine noun. Idiom: éclairer sa lanterne, to make something clear to someone.
The same word works as an adjective: c'est logique, that makes sense.

cards.de: bacon fat, lard (the cured pork fat)
cards.note: The final d is silent. Colloquially un gros lard is a fat bloke.

cards.de: the barrel, the cask (for wine or beer)
cards.note: Sounds exactly like fut, the passé simple of être. Bière à la pression comes from a fût.
Typical uses: remporter une victoire, remporter un prix. Literally it also means to take back away.
Feminine décisive. Often: un moment décisif, une preuve décisive.
Masculine noun. Un cocktail can also mean a drinks reception.
From the verb rassurer qn, to reassure someone. Feminine rassurante.
It also means a racetrack or a tour: un circuit touristique.

cards.de: the bump, the lump (on your head)
cards.note: Also a camel's hump. Avoir la bosse des maths means to have a gift for maths.
Feminine la bouchère, and the shop is la boucherie. Spelled the same as the verb boucher, to block up.
The form does not change in the feminine. As a noun: la critique the criticism or review, le critique the critic.
Forms: le tien, la tienne, les tiens, les tiennes. À la tienne! means Cheers!
Feminine affectueuse. Used to sign off letters: affectueusement, with love.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Une spécialité de la région, a regional speciality.
Feminine: marine. Typical uses: l'air marin, un courant marin. The noun un marin means a sailor.
An -ir verb conjugated like finir. Common: gravir une montagne, gravir les échelons (climb the career ladder).
Feminine. Often in the plural: des boîtes de conserve. The set phrase de conserve means together, side by side.
All nouns ending in -sion are feminine. The matching verb is s'évader (de prison).
Feminine, like almost all words ending in -ure. Common: une procédure judiciaire, suivre la procédure.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Structure: être avide de qc, for example avide de pouvoir (hungry for power).
Past participle of tomber, which takes être in the passé composé. Il est tombé dans l'escalier hier soir. (He fell on the stairs last night.) Familiar phrase: un ange tombé, a fallen angel.
The male is le cerf. Used as a term of endearment: ma biche, roughly my darling.
Feminine. For cows and pigs you say l'étable (f) instead.

cards.de: to convert (change one thing into another)
cards.note: Structure: convertir qc en qc. Je dois convertir mes euros en dollars avant le voyage. (I have to convert my euros into dollars before the trip.) Reflexive se convertir à means to convert to a religion.
Feminine: successive. Mostly used in the plural: trois échecs successifs. The adverb successivement means one after another.
Masculine. Colloquially, avoir le cafard means to feel down, to have the blues.
Very common in de préférence, preferably. The verb is préférer qc à qc.
Usually reflexive: se réconcilier avec qn. Elle s'est réconciliée avec sa sœur après des années. (She made up with her sister after years.)
Formed from libre plus -ment. Common: parler librement, circuler librement.
Always carries a negative undertone: qu'est-ce que tu insinues? Reflexive s'insinuer dans means to creep or slip into.
Feminine: natale. Common: mon pays natal, ma ville natale. The masculine plural is natals, not nataux.
Masculine despite the -ment ending. Common: trouver un arrangement avec qn, to come to an agreement with someone.

cards.de: to resign (from a post), to quit a job
cards.note: Used without a direct object: il a démissionné de son poste. The noun is la démission.
Nouns in -eur that name a quality are feminine (la couleur, la douceur).
Very colloquial, also used as an adjective: c'est dingue! For a woman: une dingue. Être dingue de qn means to be crazy about someone.

cards.de: the site, the space (parking or pitch)
cards.note: Masculine, like all nouns in -ment. Typical use: un emplacement de parking.
Masculine and rather literary. Don't confuse it with tourmente (storm, turmoil).

cards.de: to embody, to play (a role, an idea)
cards.note: Built on chair (flesh), so literally to give flesh to. Cet acteur incarne un jeune médecin dans le film. (This actor plays a young doctor in the film.) Reflexively, s'incarner dans qc.
Always followed by de: une vingtaine de personnes. Also used for age: il a la vingtaine, he's in his twenties.
Feminine. It means carpet laid over the whole floor; a single rug is un tapis.
From the verb user (to wear out). Also figurative: une expression usée, a hackneyed phrase.
Masculine. It also means a photographic shot or a negative.

cards.de: to unleash, to set off (a storm of feeling)
cards.note: From chaîne, so literally to let off the chain. Very often reflexive: la tempête se déchaîne.
Feminine subite, adverb subitement. Un changement subit de température a surpris tout le monde. (A sudden change in temperature surprised everyone.) Don't confuse it with the verb subir (to undergo).
Feminine sournoise. Un air sournois describes a shifty, devious look.

cards.de: earthly, land- (relating to the earth or to land)
cards.note: Same form for both genders. Contrasts with maritime or aérien, as in transport terrestre.
Nouns ending in -ie are almost always feminine. Common phrase: dans la catégorie de ...

cards.de: the carrier, the bearer (person carrying something)
cards.note: Feminine la porteuse. Also medical: être porteur d'un virus, to be a virus carrier.
Irregular plural: des amiraux, just like général becomes généraux.
La ville a été bombardée pendant la guerre. (The city was bombed during the war.) Also figurative: bombarder qn de questions, to bombard someone with questions.
Un billet valable un mois, a ticket valid for a month. Also means sound or acceptable: une excuse valable.
Often used with de to qualify a noun: une voiture de prestige, un hôtel de prestige.
Feminine, like all nouns in -ie. In France, une académie is also a regional school administration district.
Conjugated like finir. Ce voyage a enrichi mon vocabulaire espagnol. (This trip enriched my Spanish vocabulary.) The reflexive s'enrichir means to get rich.
Usually plural: passer les menottes à qn. In the singular, une menotte is a little hand, a diminutive of main.

cards.de: to pick up (a signal, a station)
cards.note: Je n'arrive pas à capter la radio dans cette vallée. (I can't pick up the radio in this valley.) Ici on ne capte pas means there's no reception here. Also capter l'attention de qn, to catch someone's attention.
Colloquial and affectionate. Used to sign off a message: Bisous!

cards.de: gradually, as you go along (fixed phrase)
cards.note: Only used in this set phrase; fur no longer exists on its own. With a clause: au fur et à mesure que j'avance.
Watch the accent change: j'imprègne, nous imprégnons. La pluie a imprégné mon manteau toute la journée. (The rain soaked my coat all day.) S'imprégner de qc means to soak something up.
Pattern: répliquer qc à qn. Il m'a répliqué qu'il n'avait pas le temps. [He retorted that he didn't have time.] It means answering sharply, not to replicate in the technical sense.
Faire des concessions à qn. It also means a dealership, as in une concession automobile.
The final c is pronounced, so it sounds like zingue. Colloquially it also means the bar counter: boire un coup sur le zinc.
Don't confuse it with l'âge, which is age in years. Une maison de retraite is a home for the elderly.
Same form in the masculine and the feminine. As a noun: un révolutionnaire, une révolutionnaire.

Pattern: harceler qn de questions. Les journalistes harcèlent le ministre de questions. [The journalists are pestering the minister with questions.] The noun le harcèlement covers harassment and bullying.
Usually followed by de: indigne de confiance. The opposite is digne.

cards.de: the pout (a face pulled in displeasure)
cards.note: Feminine. Very common in faire la moue, to pull a face or pout.

cards.de: to cool down (make cooler), to refresh
cards.note: La pluie a rafraîchi l'air ce soir. [The rain cooled the air down this evening.] Reflexive se rafraîchir means to have something refreshing. Also used on a computer: rafraîchir la page.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. In the plural, les hostilités means fighting or hostilities.
Feminine, like all nouns ending in -tion. The verb is bénir.
Words ending in -tion are feminine. Les installations sportives means sports facilities.
Pattern: alerter qn de qc. Un voisin a alerté la police du bruit. [A neighbour alerted the police about the noise.] The noun is une alerte.
Masculine and invariable in the plural. You live au rez-de-chaussée, and the floor above it is le premier étage.

cards.de: to treat (to good food), to spoil someone with a meal
cards.note: Ce soir, je vous régale au restaurant. [Tonight, dinner out is on me.] Colloquially c'est moi qui régale means it's on me. Se régaler means to really enjoy the food.
Typical pairing: une voix rauque. The form is the same in the masculine and feminine.
Feminine, like every noun ending in -tion. The verb is décrire (je décris).
The final d is silent. Battre un record means to break a record.

cards.de: the shooting, the filming (of a film)
cards.note: Masculine, with the ending -age. From tourner un film, to shoot a film.
Feminine form: artificielle. Familiar from l'intelligence artificielle.
The accent shifts: je complète, nous complétons. Very common in compléter un formulaire.
Feminine: la catholique. Used as an adjective, pas très catholique colloquially means a bit dodgy.
The source of the old English word periwig. Porter une perruque means to wear a wig.
Related to émouvoir (to move emotionally). Feminine émouvante, often in un film émouvant.
Conjugates like employer: j'aboie, nous aboyons. Le chien aboie contre le facteur.
Only used reflexively, and the passé composé takes être. Elle s'est exclamée qu'elle n'y croyait pas. [She exclaimed that she didn't believe it.]
From condamner qn à qc, to sentence someone to something. Feminine une condamnée.
Clearly disapproving, closer to poor than to merely average. Same form for both genders.
Masculine despite the -a ending. Vivre comme un pacha means to live like a king.

cards.de: the start of the school year (after the summer holidays)
cards.note: In France la rentrée is the big September restart, used for politics and culture too.
Feminine. It also means a connection when changing trains: prendre la correspondance.
Also the name of a dance style: le bal musette, played on the accordion.
Feminine, like abstract nouns in -eur of this kind. Note entrer en vigueur, to come into force.
Démontrer que takes the indicative. Cette étude démontre que le climat change vite. [This study proves that the climate is changing fast.] Careful: to dismantle is démonter.
Feminine form: sauve. Fixed phrase sain et sauf (safe and sound). As a preposition, sauf means except.
Tu dois activer ta carte avant de payer. [You have to activate your card before paying.] Reflexive s'activer means to hurry up or to busy oneself.
Almost always followed by à: contrairement à ce qu'on pense.
Le chien flaire une piste. Figuratively: flairer un piège, to sense a trap.
More often reflexive: s'engouffrer dans qc means to pour or rush into a place, as in la foule s'engouffre dans le métro.
Feminine form: insignifiante. Common pairings: un détail insignifiant, une somme insignifiante.
Formed from calme. Elle m'a répondu calmement, sans se fâcher. (She answered me calmly, without getting angry.) Often used as parler calmement, attendre calmement.

cards.de: to remain, to persist (still be there)
cards.note: Also used for scraping by: subsister avec un petit salaire. Il subsiste un doute means a doubt remains.
Almost always reflexive: la fleur s'épanouit, elle s'épanouit dans son travail. As an adjective: un visage épanoui, a beaming face.
Related to étreindre, to clasp tightly. Sounds more elevated than un câlin.
Le ciel est couvert means the sky is overcast. As a noun, le couvert is a place setting: mettre le couvert, to set the table.

cards.de: to dry out (make something go dry)
cards.note: Accent shifts like in acheter: je dessèche, nous desséchons. Reflexive se dessécher when skin or soil dries out.
An ir verb like finir: il refroidit. Laisse refroidir la soupe avant de manger. [Let the soup cool down before eating.]
Faire son testament means to make one's will. Also biblical: l'Ancien Testament.
Feminine form: impuissante. Common structure: être impuissant face à qc, to be powerless in the face of something.
Nouns ending in ance are feminine. Typical phrase: un sentiment d'impuissance.

cards.de: the slice of bread (spread with butter or jam)
cards.note: A staple of French breakfast: une tartine de confiture. The verb tartiner means to spread.
Same form for both genders: le terroriste, la terroriste. Also works as an adjective: un attentat terroriste.
Économiser de l'argent, économiser ses forces. For putting money aside you can also say mettre de l'argent de côté.
Feminine form: la banquière. Careful: la banque is the bank as an institution, le banc is a bench.
From la cendre, ash. Nouns ending in ier are usually masculine.

cards.de: to invoke, to cite (a law, an argument)
cards.note: Takes a direct object: invoquer une raison, invoquer la loi. Also used for calling on a deity.
persister à faire qc means to keep stubbornly doing something. Il persiste à dire qu'il a raison. [He persists in saying that he's right.] Also used of weather or problems: le froid persiste.
Stronger than le bruit. Common phrase: faire un vacarme épouvantable.
The same word means lustre or shine in formal usage: le lustre d'un meuble.
faire un souhait means to make a wish. À tes souhaits! is what you say when someone sneezes, like bless you!
Typical uses: formuler une demande, formuler des critiques.
Invariable, because it really names the chestnut: des yeux marron, une veste marron.
The larger species is called le goéland. The noun is feminine: la mouette.
The adjective from Pâques: l'agneau pascal, les vacances pascales.
From le fusil, rifle. Common in the news: une fusillade a éclaté.
Sounds exactly like résonner (to echo). Tu raisonnes comme un enfant. [You're reasoning like a child.] raisonner qn means to make someone see sense.
la tôle ondulée is corrugated iron. In slang, la tôle also means jail.
The h is silent, pronounced like rom. Do not confuse it with le rhume, a cold.
Feminine, but the article becomes l' before the vowel. It lives in la ruche and makes le miel.
From brûler. Les brûlures d'estomac means heartburn.
Past participle of déchirer (to tear). Mon jean est déchiré au genou. [My jeans are torn at the knee.] Figuratively: être déchiré entre deux choses, to be torn between two things.
Set phrase: têtu comme une mule, as stubborn as a mule.
Used both for mental focus and for the strength of a substance, just like in English. Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine in French.
Feminine, like other nouns ending in -té. Very common: l'humidité de l'air, the humidity of the air.

cards.de: oddly, strangely, in a strange way
cards.note: Formed from bizarre. Often starts a sentence: Bizarrement, personne n'a répondu.
au minimum means at least. The plural is usually les minimums, more rarely les minima.
Takes de before the thing you love. Mon frère est passionné de musique classique. [My brother is really into classical music.]
Borrowed from English; the plural is les barmans or les barmen. The female form is la barmaid.
Feminine form soucieuse. With de it means keen to: soucieux de bien faire, anxious to do things well.
Feminine. It also means the air force: l'aviation militaire.
Cette voiture consomme beaucoup, this car uses a lot of fuel. Don't mix it up with consumer, to burn up or destroy by fire.
The same word is also an adjective: un jouet mécanique, a wind-up toy.

cards.de: the tuft, the clump (of grass, hair)
cards.note: Feminine. Common phrases: une touffe d'herbe, une touffe de cheveux.

cards.de: the frame (of a pair of glasses)
cards.note: Feminine, built from monter. It also means a mount, an animal you ride.
Masculine. The big toe is le gros orteil. French keeps toes and fingers separate: fingers are les doigts.
The matching verb is récolter. Faire la récolte means to bring in the harvest.
The adjective is indulgent: indulgent envers qn, lenient towards someone.
Il pleut à torrents means it's pouring with rain.
Le montant total de la facture is the total amount of the bill.
Conjugated like dire: je redis, vous redites. Trouver à redire à qc means to find fault with something.
Formed from gai. Les enfants chantaient gaiement dans le jardin. (The children were singing cheerfully in the garden.)
Masculine and normally used in the plural, with the same spelling in both numbers. Les débris de verre are splinters of glass.
Faire une dépression means to develop depression. The same word also names a low pressure weather system.

cards.de: to blaze, to go up in flames
cards.note: From la flamme. La vieille grange a flambé en dix minutes. [The old barn went up in flames in ten minutes.] Figuratively, les prix flambent means prices are shooting up.
From sot, meaning silly. Dire des sottises means to talk nonsense.
The past participle of écrire, feminine écrite. Je veux cette réponse par écrit. [I want that answer in writing.]
It already ends in e, so the masculine and feminine forms are identical. Used for soil, for living things and for germ free material.
From détenir, to hold or detain. The feminine form is la détenue.

cards.de: that is, namely (introducing an explanation or a figure)
cards.note: Trois heures, soit 180 minutes. On its own, soit! means fine, all right. And soit ..., soit ... means either ... or.
The tree is le bananier. Une peau de banane is a banana skin.
From étrange, strange. Étrangement, il n'a rien dit pendant le repas. (Strangely, he said nothing during the meal.) Do not confuse it with étranger, which means foreign or foreigner.
It contains la gorge, the throat. Le fermier a égorgé le mouton. [The farmer cut the sheep's throat.] Like all verbs in ger, it keeps the e: nous égorgeons.

cards.de: the application (of a law or a rule)
cards.note: It also means an app on your phone, informally une appli. Mettre en application means to put into practice.
From terrifier, to terrify someone. The feminine is terrifiante.
Rather formal, often in avec lassitude. Related to las/lasse, meaning weary.
Careful: un marine is a marine, the soldier. Bleu marine, navy blue, never changes form.
Usually plural: nos semblables. As an adjective, semblable means similar.
Pronounced either zo or zo-o. The official term is le jardin zoologique.
Rayez votre ancienne adresse sur le formulaire. [Cross out your old address on the form.] It also means to scratch, as in rayer la voiture. The participle rayé means striped.
Used as an adjective in date anniversaire. Far more common as a noun: l'anniversaire, a birthday.
The feminine is la mendiante. The verb is mendier, to beg.
The final d stays silent. Rusé comme un renard means as cunning as a fox.

cards.de: the crossing (journey across, e.g. of a sea)
cards.note: From traverser (to cross). La traversée de l'Atlantique.
The male animal is le mulet. Têtu comme une mule works just like the English as stubborn as a mule.
Nouns ending in -ment are always masculine. The verb is siffler.
Feminine form poussiéreuse. From the noun la poussière (dust).
Feminine la productrice. Don't confuse it with le réalisateur, which is the film director.
The female goat is la chèvre. Le bouc émissaire means scapegoat.
Past participle of décevoir. Je suis déçu du résultat. [I'm disappointed with the result.] You say être déçu de qc (by something) or par qn (by someone).
Same form in the masculine and the feminine. Often used to mean absurdly ridiculous.

cards.de: to wait patiently, to be patient
cards.note: More polite than attendre. On the phone: Veuillez patienter un instant.
Literally after tomorrow. Mon frère arrive après-demain matin. (My brother arrives the day after tomorrow morning.) Its counterpart is avant-hier, the day before yesterday.
Elle me masse les épaules après le travail. [She massages my shoulders after work.] Se faire masser le dos means to have your back massaged.
Feminine veuve. Used as nouns, le veuf and la veuve mean widower and widow.
Very common in the phrase en permanence, meaning constantly or all the time. At school, la permanence is the supervised study room for free periods.
Feminine puante; it belongs to the verb puer (to stink).
From la saveur (flavour). Savourer un moment de calme.
Je transpire beaucoup quand je cours. [I sweat a lot when I run.] Transpirer is the neutral word; suer sounds blunter and earthier.
Masculine plural orientaux, feminine orientale. The opposite is occidental.
It is feminine, but l'oie hides the gender, so learn it as une oie. Don't confuse it with le foie (liver).
À proximité de la gare means near the station. Nouns ending in -ité are feminine.
Conjugated like finir: je maudis, nous maudissons, past participle maudit. Il maudit le jour où il a accepté ce travail. (He curses the day he took that job.)
Masculine despite the -e ending: un squelette.
Une soucoupe volante = a flying saucer. As a noun, le volant means steering wheel.
Literally "not heard", from the old verb ouïr (to hear). Une chance inouïe = incredible luck.
Masculine, and usually used without an article: manquer d'oxygène = to be short of air.
Feminine and plural only. Figuratively: les entrailles de la terre = the bowels of the earth.

Figuratively, broder sur qc means to embellish or exaggerate a story, just like "embroider" in English. Ma grand-mère aime broder des fleurs sur les nappes. (My grandmother likes to embroider flowers on tablecloths.)
French nouns ending in -sion are feminine. The verb is envahir, to invade or overrun.

cards.de: the shell (of an egg or nut)
cards.note: In printing, une coquille also means a typo. Careful: a shellfish or seashell is un coquillage, and a mussel is une moule.
It can also be completely neutral, meaning to handle. Il faut manipuler cette machine avec précaution. (You have to handle this machine carefully.)
Set phrase: les congés payés, paid holiday. Well paid is bien payé. Ce stage n'est pas payé, mais il est intéressant. (This internship isn't paid, but it's interesting.)
Used as être obligé de faire qc, to have to do something. Je suis obligé de partir, I have to go.
Built as récompenser qn de qc or pour qc. The noun is une récompense, a reward. Le prof a récompensé les élèves pour leurs efforts. (The teacher rewarded the pupils for their efforts.)
It comes from la mauve, the mallow flower. Unlike some colour words, it does take a plural s: des rideaux mauves.
Masculine. From entre and poser, so literally the place where goods are put in between.

cards.de: the work (a task to be done)
cards.note: It sounds slightly old-fashioned but survives in phrases like aller vite en besogne, to jump the gun.
The masculine plural is loyaux; the feminine forms are loyale and loyales.
Usually se baser sur qc, to go on something, or être basé sur qc, to be based on something. Le film est basé sur une histoire vraie. (The film is based on a true story.)
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Watch out for the adjective sensible: it means sensitive, not "sensible".

cards.de: the indirect route, the means (par le ... de = by means of)
cards.note: Two common phrases: de biais, at an angle or sideways, and par le biais de, by way of.

cards.de: the thrashing, the beating (une ... de coups)
cards.note: It comes from voler, to fly. Also à la volée, in mid air or on the fly, and une volée de moineaux, a flock of sparrows.
Also grammatical: le genre masculin. Feminine form masculine, opposite féminin.

cards.de: to race down, to hurtle down (stairs, a slope)
cards.note: It takes a direct object with no preposition: dévaler l'escalier, dévaler la pente.
chargé de qc means loaded with something, but être chargé de faire qc means to be put in charge of doing something. Elle est arrivée chargée de cadeaux. (She arrived loaded with presents.)
Normally masculine; une aigle refers only to the female bird or to an eagle on a coat of arms.
Learn the set phrase de surcroît, meaning what is more or on top of that.
Coucou! is also a casual hello between friends.
Slightly old fashioned; today people usually say la veste. The trousers are le pantalon.
Plural: les poteaux. Un poteau indicateur is a signpost.
It also means the pastry itself: manger une pâtisserie.
The typical headgear of the French police and the Foreign Legion.
Le gros gibier is big game. Also figurative: gibier de potence, a gallows bird or crook.
Colloquial. Also used as an adjective: il est complètement cinglé.
The matching verb is lacer ses chaussures. Une route en lacets is a winding road with hairpin bends.
Feminine. The adjective is énigmatique, mysterious.
Note the double g. Reflexive s'aggraver means to get worse. Fumer risque d'aggraver ta toux. (Smoking is likely to make your cough worse.)
Feminine: la réalisatrice. For theatre you say le metteur en scène.
Formed from silencieux, silencieuse. It means quietly or without saying a word. Il est entré silencieusement dans la chambre du bébé. (He came silently into the baby's room.)
The same form for masculine and feminine: un regard terne, une couleur terne. Also of people: une vie terne, a drab life.
Common uses: un rire forcé, un atterrissage forcé. Colloquially c'est forcé means that was bound to happen.

cards.de: the orbit (of a satellite or planet)
cards.note: Feminine: mettre un satellite en orbite. In anatomy it also means the eye socket.
Nouns ending in -logie are always feminine. Common phrase: les nouvelles technologies.
Almost always reflexive: se fiancer avec quelqu'un. Related nouns: le fiancé, la fiancée.
Nouns ending in -ion are feminine. Faire sa première communion. Figuratively: une communion d'idées, a meeting of minds.
From le coude, the elbow. It takes à: s'accouder à la fenêtre, to lean on the windowsill.
The final s is silent and the plural looks the same: un colis, des colis. Envoyer un colis.
It covers both a pastime and a lapse of attention. Une erreur par distraction, a careless mistake.
Related noun: la récolte, the harvest. Also used figuratively: récolter des informations, des ennuis.
The feminine form is la marraine, godmother. As in English, it also means a mafia boss.

cards.de: to give rise to (to cause, to generate)
cards.note: More formal than causer; its original sense is to father children. Cette décision risque d'engendrer des conflits. (This decision may give rise to conflicts.)
Usually plural: les négociations sont en cours. Verb: négocier avec qn.
être opposé à qc means to be against something. Also used as a noun: l'opposé, the opposite. Mon frère habite sur le trottoir opposé. (My brother lives on the opposite pavement.)
Masculine: avoir un alibi solide, to have a watertight alibi.
Feminine, despite ending in a consonant sound. Known from un film de cape et d'épée, a swashbuckler film.
Colloquial: je flippe avant l'examen. The noun le flipper, however, means a pinball machine.

cards.de: the show-off (someone making themselves seem important)
cards.note: Rare as a noun. The usual phrase is faire l'intéressant, to show off.
From éternel, éternelle. Double l plus -ement, like naturellement. Je te serai éternellement reconnaissant. (I will be eternally grateful to you.)
Normally used in the plural: consulter les archives. The noun is feminine.

cards.de: to set alight (to set on fire)
cards.note: Reflexive s'enflammer means to catch fire, and figuratively to get carried away with enthusiasm. Une étincelle a suffi à enflammer le papier. (One spark was enough to set the paper alight.)
Also means a projector in a cinema. Sous les projecteurs means in the spotlight.
Feminine form souterraine. As a noun, le souterrain is an underground passage.
Masculine and always used with the article: le chômage. être au chômage means to be unemployed.
Don't confuse it with une boîte, a box. You say faire de la boxe.
Masculine, like all nouns ending in -ment. At an airport, l'enregistrement is check-in.

cards.de: the pack (main group in a cycling race)
cards.note: Also used in the military: le peloton d'exécution is a firing squad.
Used with dans: croquer dans une pomme. Chocolat à croquer is plain eating chocolate.
Feminine: une marmite. It is bigger than une casserole, a saucepan.
aller au supermarché, to go to the supermarket. A bigger one is un hypermarché.
Common phrases: une technologie avancée, à un âge avancé. The verb avancer means to move forward.

cards.de: the business (informal, for trade or dealings)
cards.note: An informal English borrowing; les affaires is the neutral word. It keeps the English pronunciation.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. The related adjective is indigné, outraged.
Typical uses: scruter l'horizon, scruter le visage de qn. A little more formal than regarder.
The final -t is silent. Common phrases: un petit budget, le budget de l'État.
Takes a direct object with no preposition: critiquer qn/qc. The noun la critique is feminine. Elle critique toujours ma façon de conduire. (She always criticises the way I drive.)
In cooking, faire dorer means to brown something golden. It comes from or, gold. L'artisan a doré le cadre du miroir. (The craftsman gilded the mirror frame.)
Irregular: j'instruis, participle instruit. S'instruire means to educate yourself. Ce documentaire nous instruit sur la vie des abeilles. (This documentary teaches us about the life of bees.)
Feminine form: une magicienne. A stage magician is often called un prestidigitateur.
Set phrases: sauter à pieds joints, les mains jointes. Ci-joint means attached or enclosed in a letter.

cards.de: to describe (as), to call, to qualify
cards.note: The construction is qualifier qn/qc de + adjective. Se qualifier pour means to qualify for something. Les journaux qualifient cette décision d'historique. (The papers are describing this decision as historic.)
Used reflexively with body parts: se brosser les dents, se brosser les cheveux. The brush itself is une brosse.

cards.de: guilt (the feeling or state of being guilty)
cards.note: Common phrase: un sentiment de culpabilité. A financial debt, by contrast, is une dette.
Also used for goods and books: sold out, out of print. The verb is épuiser. Après cette longue journée, je suis complètement épuisé. (After this long day, I'm completely exhausted.)
From the adjective officiel, officielle plus -ment. The opposite is officieusement, unofficially. Le résultat sera annoncé officiellement demain. (The result will be officially announced tomorrow.)
Always written with hyphens. Slightly more formal than tout de suite. Le directeur a exigé une réponse sur-le-champ. (The director demanded an answer on the spot.)
The plural is usually glaciaux (glacials also occurs). Also figurative: un accueil glacial, an icy welcome.
Masculine: une allée de gravier. Used collectively, so normally in the singular.
This h is an h aspiré, so you say le harem, never l'harem, and there is no liaison.

cards.de: the candle (old-fashioned tallow or wax candle)
cards.note: Today people usually say la bougie. Idiom: devoir une fière chandelle à qn, to owe someone a huge debt of gratitude.

cards.de: the marvellous (the element of magic or fairy tale in literature)
cards.note: An adjective used as a noun. As an adjective, merveilleux, merveilleuse means wonderful.
Related to the verb survivre à qc. Common phrases: instinct de survie, chances de survie.
It also means about forty: une quarantaine de personnes, avoir la quarantaine (to be in your forties).
A softened version of taper. You say tapoter sur qc or tapoter l'épaule de qn. Il tapote sur la table en attendant sa réponse. (He taps on the table while waiting for her answer.)
Also trousse de toilette, a toiletry bag. In the plural: être aux trousses de qn, to be hot on someone's heels.
All nouns ending in -té are feminine. The adjective is généreux, généreuse.

cards.de: to sing quietly to oneself, to hum
cards.note: A diminutive form of chanter, like sautiller from sauter. Elle chantonne toujours en faisant la vaisselle. (She always hums while doing the dishes.)

cards.de: to lean (something with its back against)
cards.note: Formed from le dos, the back. Usually reflexive: s'adosser à un mur or contre un mur.
The feminine is la savante. As an adjective, savant means learned or clever.
The same form for both genders, only the article changes: un architecte, une architecte.
Masculine, with a silent h, so l'hélicoptère with liaison. The colloquial short form is un hélico.
Plural: les roseaux. Pascal famously called man a roseau pensant, a thinking reed.
Common phrase: faire référence à qc, to refer to something. Also un ouvrage de référence, a standard work.
Plural: les locaux, often a company's premises. As an adjective, local means local in the geographical sense.
Derived from dormir. Une ville-dortoir is a commuter town.
Nouns ending in -isme are masculine. It also means body or agency: un organisme public.
Usually seen as l'élite, so learn the gender: feminine. Common: les troupes d'élite, une école d'élite.
Typical uses: parler d'un ton assuré, d'un pas assuré. As a noun, l'assuré is the insured person.

cards.de: the shell (hard shell of a nut or egg)
cards.note: Un œuf à la coque is a soft boiled egg. A ship's hull is also la coque.

cards.de: to stab (with a knife or dagger)
cards.note: From le poignard, a dagger. Figuratively: poignarder qn dans le dos, to stab someone in the back. Dans le film, le voleur poignarde le gardien. (In the film, the thief stabs the guard.)
Masculine: l'écureuil. Careful with the pronunciation: the ending sounds like the one in feuille.
Common: en collaboration avec qn. Historically, la Collaboration refers to collaboration with the Nazis.
The related verb is se peigner, to comb one's hair. Colloquially: se donner un coup de peigne.
Slightly informal; transpirer is the neutral word. Je sue dès que je monte les escaliers. (I sweat as soon as I climb the stairs.) Very common: faire suer qn, to annoy someone.
Linked to the adjective serein, calm or untroubled. Common: avec sérénité.
Tes explications m'embrouillent complètement. (Your explanations confuse me completely.) Reflexive s'embrouiller means to get tangled up or lose the thread. The opposite is débrouiller.

cards.de: the furnace (large cooking range or smelting furnace)
cards.note: Plural in x: les fourneaux. Un haut fourneau is a blast furnace.
Masculine despite the -a ending. Common: tomber dans le coma, être dans le coma.
From la pile, a pile (also a battery). S'empiler means to pile up.
Unchanged in the feminine: une bête farouche. Of willpower or resistance it means fierce: une volonté farouche.
The final s is silent, so singular and plural sound identical. Un marais salant is a salt marsh where salt is harvested.
Used with money, water or time: gaspiller son argent, l'eau, son temps. The noun is le gaspillage.
Capitalised for the person, lower case as an adjective: un livre polonais. The language is le polonais, also lower case.

cards.de: to whiten, to bleach (also: to turn white)
cards.note: An -ir verb like finir: je blanchis, nous blanchissons. Le soleil a blanchi les rideaux. (The sun has bleached the curtains.) Also blanchir de l'argent, to launder money.
Found in fauteuil roulant (wheelchair) and tapis roulant (treadmill). Feminine: roulante.
Literally "under the sea". Plural: des sous-marins. As an adjective: la vie sous-marine.
Very often figurative: Elle a esquissé un sourire avant de partir. (She gave the faintest of smiles before leaving.) The noun is une esquisse.
Feminine: la jardinière, which also means a window box for plants.
Lower case as an adjective, capitalised as a noun: un Africain. Feminine: africaine.

cards.de: the sense of touch, the feel (of something)
cards.note: An infinitive used as a noun, so it is always masculine. Common phrase: doux au toucher (soft to the touch).
Built with sur: trébucher sur une pierre. It takes avoir in compound tenses.
From the adjective faible; the adverb comes from the feminine form plus -ment. La lampe éclairait faiblement la pièce. (The lamp lit the room faintly.)
Same form for men and women. As a noun: un/une célibataire (a single person).
Built with de: Ils l'ont expulsé du pays la semaine dernière. (They deported him from the country last week.) The noun is une expulsion.
Note the ending -ène with an accent grave; the form is the same for masculine and feminine. The noun is une obscénité.

cards.de: the small town (large village with a market)
cards.note: Smaller than une ville. It appears in faubourg (suburb) and in Strasbourg; the final g is silent.
Official language, more neutral than la mort: un acte de décès is a death certificate. Singular and plural look and sound the same.
Almost only used in un ange gardien. Feminine: gardienne. As a noun, le gardien is a guard or a goalkeeper.
Built with de: Je garnis le plat de tomates et d'olives. (I garnish the dish with tomatoes and olives.) An -ir verb like finir: je garnis, nous garnissons.
Nouns ending in -sion are always feminine. Common phrase: avoir de la compassion pour qn.
Opposite: immobile. Careful, a mobile phone is un portable, while le mobile also means a motive for a crime.
The counterpart to moralement or mentalement. Also used for sheer possibility. C'est physiquement impossible de finir ce travail ce soir. (It is physically impossible to finish this work tonight.)
La pluie accentue encore la tristesse de ce lieu. (The rain makes the sadness of this place even stronger.) s'accentuer means to grow stronger. Also used for stressing a syllable.

cards.de: to bawl, to yell (singing or shouting)
cards.note: Colloquial and disapproving. brailler une chanson = to bellow out a song.
Feminine pieuse, plural pieux. un mensonge pieux = a white lie.
Elle puise de l'eau dans le puits chaque matin. (She draws water from the well every morning.) puiser dans ses économies means to dip into one's savings.
As a noun, un combattant is a fighter, and un ancien combattant is a war veteran.
Feminine. Figuratively: être dans une impasse = to be at a deadlock.
sous garantie = under warranty. The matching verb is garantir.
Feminine inhabituelle. Opposite of habituel, formed with the prefix in-.
It also means the founding of something. In the plural, les fondations are the foundations of a building.
From prévoir via prévisible, with the prefix im-. Same form in masculine and feminine.
Only used impersonally: Personne ne sait ce qui adviendra demain. (Nobody knows what will happen tomorrow.) It follows venir and takes être; quoi qu'il advienne means whatever happens.
être parent de qn means to be related to someone: Je suis parent de cette famille par ma mère. (I am related to that family through my mother.) Feminine parente.
Past participle of résoudre. être résolu à faire qc = to be determined to do something.
Stronger than sale and usually about morals: un détail sordide, une affaire sordide.
Present participle of séduire (to seduce). Son idée me paraît très séduisante. (His idea seems very appealing to me.) Also used for people and offers.
Same form in masculine and feminine. Very common: une centrale nucléaire, a nuclear power station.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. From pauvre (poor).
Plural des verrous. The related verb is verrouiller (to bolt, to lock).
Figuratively: ne pas mâcher ses mots, to not mince your words.
Also figurative: piloter un projet means to run a project. Mon oncle pilote un petit avion le dimanche. (My uncle flies a small plane on Sundays.)
Watch the u: cinq becomes cinquième. Also a noun: un cinquième, a fifth.
Construction: insensible à qc, insensitive to something. Opposite of sensible, which means sensitive, not "sensible".
faire la lessive means to do the laundry. The same word also means washing powder.

cards.de: what is needed, the necessary things
cards.note: Set phrase: faire le nécessaire, to do what is needed. As an adjective it means necessary.

cards.de: warm, warm-hearted (of a person or welcome)
cards.note: Feminine chaleureuse. From chaleur (heat), but only used in the figurative sense.
Borrowed from English, plural des gentlemen. Pronounced roughly [dʒɛntləman].

cards.de: to begin, to start out (a thing or a career)
cards.note: Le film débute par une scène de nuit. For people: débuter dans un métier, to start out in a profession.
Stronger than supporter, it suggests putting up with suffering over time. Il a enduré la douleur sans se plaindre. (He endured the pain without complaining.)
Masculine despite the final -e. More formal than bâtiment, often used for churches and monuments.

cards.de: to inlay (set decoration into a surface)
cards.note: incruster qc de pierres means to set something with stones: L'artisan a incrusté la boîte de nacre. (The craftsman inlaid the box with mother of pearl.) Reflexive s'incruster is colloquial for overstaying your welcome.
Masculine. Figuratively: un gouffre financier, a money pit.
Feminine: paternelle. Counterpart: maternel. Common phrase: l'autorité paternelle.
Feminine, like nearly all nouns ending in -tion. Slightly formal and stronger than enthousiasme.
Feminine: primitive. It often just means "original, first version", not only "primitive".
Feminine. Verb: inspecter qc. L'inspection is also the name of the school inspectorate.
Feminine: fascinante. The sc is pronounced like ss. Verb: fasciner qn.
Feminine: relative. Construction: relatif à qc, relating to, concerning.
Common phrase: avec facilité. In the plural it means concessions or terms, e.g. facilités de paiement.
Feminine: gluante. From la glu (glue), so it suggests an unpleasant, tacky coating.
Feminine: latine. As a noun: le latin = the Latin language.
Masculine. The adjective is rectangulaire (rectangular).
Masculine despite the ending in -ice. Common exclamation: quel supplice! = what torture!
Feminine: bavarde. The verb is bavarder = to chat, to natter.
Feminine form: la messagère. Related to le message.
Feminine. In formal style la morgue can also mean arrogance.
Feminine: touchante. From toucher, which covers both to touch and to move emotionally.
Past participle of convaincre. Je suis convaincu qu'il dit la vérité. (I am convinced that he is telling the truth.) Also used as être convaincu de qc.
The form stays the same in the feminine. l'école élémentaire is primary school.
Same form in the feminine: une question complexe. As a noun: le complexe, including an inferiority complex.
Do not confuse it with the verb briser (to smash): il brise. Common phrase: une brise légère.
Typical use: les mains moites when you are nervous. For damp laundry use humide instead.
In slang un pétard also means a joint. Faire un pétard: to set one off.
L'homme des cavernes is the caveman. More neutral and far more common: la grotte.
In sentences it is nearly always a quantity: de l'ail, une gousse d'ail (a clove). The word is masculine.
Usually le court de tennis. It sounds exactly like the adjective court (short).
Feminine: rêveuse. From rêver (to dream): rêver de qc.
Feminine: sportive. Un événement sportif is a sporting event.
Mettre qc en sûreté means to put something somewhere safe. For everyday safety and security, French usually uses la sécurité.
Elle est fâchée contre moi depuis hier. (She has been angry with me since yesterday.) Être fâché avec qn means to have fallen out with someone.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. Dire des méchancetés: to say nasty things.
Same form for masculine and feminine: le parti socialiste, une idée socialiste.

cards.de: the are (unit of area, 100 square metres)
cards.note: Masculine; one hectare is 100 ares. It sounds like l'air but is a measure of area.
Feminine: une orpheline. Orphelin de père means fatherless.
Very common in plisser les yeux (to squint) and plisser le front (to frown). Il plisse les yeux pour lire le panneau. (He squints to read the sign.) The noun is le pli, a fold or crease.
Careful: the French word means touchy, not susceptible. It also appears in être susceptible de faire qc, to be liable or likely to do something.
The musical instrument is also le triangle.

cards.de: the chorus girl (dancer in a revue)
cards.note: An English loanword with a narrow meaning in French: only a revue dancer, never any girl, which is une fille.

cards.de: to challenge someone (also: to be stopped by the police)
cards.note: Always written with a double l: j'interpelle, nous interpellons. La police a interpellé deux hommes ce matin. (The police stopped two men this morning.) Figuratively, ça m'interpelle means that strikes a chord with me.
Feminine, like most nouns in -ive. Colloquially shortened to la loco.
Also used figuratively for a ruthless businessman: un requin de la finance.
It follows paraître: il réapparaît keeps the circumflex before the t. Le soleil a réapparu après l'orage. (The sun reappeared after the storm.)
Very common as an exclamation: Impeccable! Colloquially shortened to impec.
Nouns ending in -ie are almost always feminine in French. The adjective is stratégique.
Colloquial. Il râle toujours quand le train est en retard. (He always moans when the train is late.) Someone who is always moaning is un râleur, une râleuse.
A word of its own, not derived from cheval. Feminine despite the -ent ending.
Literally pour boire, for drinking. You say laisser un pourboire, to leave a tip.

cards.de: to drug someone (secretly give them drugs)
cards.note: Someone drugged her drink at the party: Quelqu'un l'a droguée pendant la soirée. (Someone drugged her during the party.) Reflexive se droguer means to take drugs.
As an adjective, fauve means tawny or reddish brown. Familiar from the painters known as les fauves.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Also used figuratively for dull people or colours.
The title is always feminine, even for men: Votre Altesse, Monseigneur.
Used as être stupéfait de qc. Do not confuse it with un stupéfiant, a narcotic.
Past participle of émouvoir. Il était très ému pendant le discours de sa fille. (He was very moved during his daughter's speech.) Common phrase: être ému aux larmes, moved to tears.
Feminine form meurtrière: une arme meurtrière. As a noun, le meurtrier means the murderer.
Nouns ending in esse are always feminine. Also used for the delicacy of food or colours.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Common phrase: une voix monotone.
Feminine in French. In traffic: priorité à droite, give way to the right.
Masculine plural verticaux, feminine verticale.
Plural éventails. Figuratively: un large éventail de choix, a wide range of options.
Masculine in French. The final t is silent.
Note the double b in the French spelling. The final n is nasal, not pronounced separately.
Regular er verb. L'enfant sanglotait dans les bras de sa mère. (The child was sobbing in his mother's arms.) The noun is un sanglot, a sob.
Une plage de galets is a pebble beach, as opposed to une plage de sable.
The final s is silent. Historically it also names the French Resistance in the Second World War.
Feminine. Parler avec aisance means to speak with ease.
Only one t in French. Pronounced like balè, with a silent t.
Feminine form prodigieuse. More elevated than étonnant.

cards.de: to set out in detail (list item by item)
cards.note: From le détail. Pouvez-vous détailler les frais du voyage? (Can you set out the costs of the trip in detail?) Common as a participle: un plan détaillé.
Usually feminine nowadays: t'as une clope? Very informal.
Informal. Mon entretien a complètement foiré hier. (My interview went completely wrong yesterday.) Also transitive: foirer un examen.
Masculine even though it ends in e. Les horaires d'ouverture are the opening hours.
Set phrase: tenir à qc comme à la prunelle de ses yeux, to guard something like the apple of one's eye. La prunelle also means sloe.
From promettre qc à qn. Proverb: chose promise, chose due.
In the plural, les finances means funds or public finances: le ministre des Finances.
Feminine noun. Typical phrase: les dunes de sable.
Very common at the start of a sentence: honnêtement, je ne sais pas. Watch the circumflex and the double n.

cards.de: to encourage (prompt someone to do something)
cards.note: Construction: inciter qn à faire qc. La pub incite les jeunes à acheter n'importe quoi. (Advertising encourages young people to buy anything.) Slightly more formal than pousser qn à faire qc.
A loanword from English, pronounced the French way: [gangstɛʁ]. Un film de gangsters.
Masculine, like all nouns ending in -ment. From enseigner qc à qn; l'enseignement supérieur is higher education.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. Phrase: par opposition à, as opposed to.
The opposite of facilement. On peut difficilement dire le contraire.
Feminine la pèlerine, though that word also means cape. A pilgrimage is le pèlerinage.
Same form in the masculine and the feminine. Une chauve-souris is a bat.
From la prison. Often in the passive: il a été emprisonné pendant dix ans.
An English loanword, feminine in French. Plural ladys or ladies.
Feminine form furtive. Common phrase: un regard furtif, a furtive glance.
Also fixed in set phrases: un effet secondaire (side effect), l'école secondaire (secondary school).
Feminine: la boxeuse. The sport itself is la boxe.
Common: une affaire louche, un type louche. As a noun, la louche means a ladle.
Used with de: une trentaine de personnes. Il a la trentaine means he is in his thirties.
Plural takes an x: des lambeaux. Very common in en lambeaux, in tatters.
Ends in -the but is masculine. The adjective is mythique.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. La préparation à un examen.
Feminine. The person is un adolescent, shortened to un ado in everyday speech.
From hôte (host, guest). Very common: une hôtesse de l'air, a flight attendant.
Fairly formal; in conversation people say pourtant or cependant instead. Il était fatigué; néanmoins, il a terminé le match. (He was tired; nevertheless, he finished the match.)

cards.de: to sculpt, to carve (in stone or wood)
cards.note: The p is silent: [skylte]. Mon grand-père sculpte des animaux dans le bois. (My grandfather carves animals out of wood.) Related words: la sculpture and le sculpteur.
Masculine. Pronounced the French way [pœzl], not as in English. Faire un puzzle.
A strong word, often used about weather or deeds: un temps abominable, un crime abominable.

cards.de: the other person (the other, one's fellow human being)
cards.note: Used as a noun: le respect de l'autre. Plural les autres (other people); l'un et l'autre.

cards.de: to tease someone, to wind someone up (colloquial)
cards.note: Colloquial, construction charrier qn. Mes amis me charrient à cause de mon accent. (My friends tease me because of my accent.) Literally it means to cart or haul; tu charries! means you're going too far.

Construction: munir qn/qc de qc. Il faut munir chaque salle d'un extincteur. (Each room must be provided with a fire extinguisher.) Very common reflexively: se munir de son passeport, to bring your passport with you.

cards.de: to round off (a number or a shape)
cards.note: Used for numbers and shapes: arrondir à l'euro près. Idiom: arrondir ses fins de mois, to earn a bit extra on the side.
Only one p at the end, and the t stays silent. Common: partir au galop, to set off at a gallop.
Masculine plural: matinaux. Of people, être matinal means to be an early riser.
The same word also means heir to the throne, or a politician's chosen successor.
Also figurative: se tromper lourdement, to be badly mistaken. Il est tombé lourdement sur le sol. (He fell heavily on the ground.)
As an adjective it never changes: un yaourt nature, des crêpes nature. Of people, informally, it means natural or unaffected.
Plural: des tonneaux. Faire un tonneau means to roll a car over.

cards.de: to copy (also to copy off someone)
cards.note: Il a copié mes réponses pendant le contrôle. (He copied my answers during the test.) At school: copier sur son voisin, to copy off the person next to you. On a computer: copier-coller.
Être en déplacement means to be away on business. Also les frais de déplacement, travel expenses.
Avoir la nausée means to feel sick. Figuratively: jusqu'à la nausée, ad nauseam.
Quality nouns ending in -eur are feminine: la blancheur, la douceur, la chaleur. Job words in -eur are masculine.
Double r, as in correct. Example: parler correctement le français.
A participle of disparaître used as a noun; feminine une disparue. Official phrase: être porté disparu, to be reported missing.
Écrire à la craie, to write in chalk. Un bâton de craie is a single stick of chalk.
Conjugated like paraître: il reparaît, il reparut. Compound tenses take avoir.

La rivière a submergé les champs en une nuit. (The river flooded the fields in one night.) Often passive: être submergé de travail, to be swamped with work. Like manger, it keeps the e before a and o: nous submergeons.
Pattern: dédier qc à qn. Elle a dédié son premier roman à sa sœur. (She dedicated her first novel to her sister.) Use it for dedicating a book or song; for devoting time, say consacrer.
Le cheval galope. Also used of children charging about: les enfants galopent dans le couloir.

cards.de: the gut (of an animal, coarsely also of a person)
cards.note: Plural in x: les boyaux. It also means a narrow passage or a tube; the medical term is l'intestin.
Feminine, like most nouns in -ure. Common: la structure d'une phrase, une structure d'accueil (a reception facility).

Le chef accommode ses plats au goût des clients. (The chef adapts his dishes to the customers' taste.) Very common reflexively: s'accommoder de qc means to put up with something. In cooking: accommoder les restes, to use up leftovers.
Built on plat (flat), with only one p. Il faut aplatir la pâte avec un rouleau. (You have to flatten the dough with a rolling pin.) An -ir verb like finir: il aplatit, nous aplatissons.

Derived from cheval. Elle chevauche un vieux cheval blanc tous les dimanches. (She rides an old white horse every Sunday.) Very common reflexively: se chevaucher means to overlap, for example appointments.
Le prof a groupé les élèves par niveau. (The teacher grouped the students by level.) Often reflexive: se grouper, to get together. Regrouper is even more common for putting things together.
Adjectives ending in -aire have the same form for masculine and feminine. Set phrases: la police judiciaire, un casier judiciaire (criminal record).

cards.de: to furrow, to knit (the brow, the eyebrows)
cards.note: Used almost only in froncer les sourcils, to frown. Mon père fronce les sourcils quand je rentre tard. (My father frowns when I come home late.) The c becomes ç before a and o: je fronçais.
Colloquial, from the verb planquer (to hide). It can also mean a cushy job: c'est une planque.
Feminine: la cantine. Everyday school phrase: manger à la cantine.
Un fourgon cellulaire is a prison van, un fourgon blindé an armoured money van. A smaller one is la camionnette.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. The verb is traduire qc en français, irregular like conduire.
A regular -er verb. Ce parti gouverne le pays depuis dix ans. (This party has governed the country for ten years.) The related noun is le gouvernement.
Used as an adjective it follows the noun: un élève modèle, une mère modèle.
agresser qn, with no preposition. On l'a agressé dans le métro hier soir. (He was mugged on the metro last night.) The attack itself is une agression.
