All nouns ending in -té are feminine. Common phrase: avec intensité.
La banque a débité mon compte de cinquante euros. (The bank charged fifty euros to my account.) The opposite is créditer. Colloquially also débiter des bêtises, to spout nonsense.

cards.de: freelance work paid by the piece (journalism)
cards.note: travailler à la pige means to work as a freelance journalist. In slang pige also means year: il a 40 piges.

cards.de: to turn pale, to go white
cards.note: Conjugated like finir: je pâlis, nous pâlissons. Elle a pâli de peur en voyant l'araignée. (She turned pale with fear when she saw the spider.)
The h is silent, so it becomes l'humilité. Fairly formal in tone, often avec humilité.
In everyday speech it often just means a bad headache: j'ai la migraine.
The final s is not pronounced, and the singular and plural look the same. A court case, by contrast, is un procès.
Also means a parry in sport and fencing. Common phrase: défiler à la parade.
L'ascenseur est en réparation means the lift is under repair. In legal contexts it also means compensation or redress.

cards.de: to address someone as "tu" (use the informal you)
cards.note: Used as tutoyer qn; the opposite is vouvoyer. The y becomes i before a silent ending: je tutoie, nous tutoyons.
The feminine form is la boulangère. Aller chez le boulanger means to go to the baker's.
Almost always plural and masculine, where English uses a singular uncountable noun. The related verb is applaudir qn.
Nouns ending in -ure are usually feminine. An architect is un architecte, or une architecte for a woman.
Careful: in French this is the verb, not the person. A kidnapper is un kidnappeur.

cards.de: the search (of a person or place, a frisking)
cards.note: The verb is fouiller qn or qc. In the plural, les fouilles means archaeological excavations.

cards.de: the ravine, the gully (narrow, deep valley)
cards.note: It is masculine: un ravin. Often heard as la voiture a fini dans le ravin.
Past participle of battre. Notre équipe a été battue en finale. (Our team was beaten in the final.) Set phrase: les sentiers battus, the beaten track.

cards.de: the introduction, the presentation (of a person or a project)
cards.note: All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. Faire les présentations means to introduce people to each other.
The feminine doubles the l: rituelle. As a noun, le rituel means the ritual.

cards.de: to request, to apply for (formally ask for something)
cards.note: Formal register: solliciter qc auprès de qn. J'ai sollicité un rendez-vous auprès du directeur. (I requested a meeting with the director.) Also solliciter qn, to approach someone with a request.
Feminine, like all nouns in -tion. Une délégation de pouvoir is a transfer of authority.
Formed from the adjective tendre. Elle embrasse tendrement son fils avant de partir. (She kisses her son tenderly before leaving.)

cards.de: to make out, to distinguish (perceive with difficulty)
cards.note: Construction: discerner qc de qc, to tell one thing from another. Dans le brouillard, je discerne à peine la route. (In the fog, I can barely make out the road.)

cards.de: the sheaf, the spray (bundle of corn or flowers)
cards.note: Une gerbe de fleurs is a large spray of flowers, for example at a grave. In slang, gerber means to throw up.

cards.de: to worry, to bother (cause someone concern)
cards.note: Informal. Cette histoire d'argent me tracasse depuis des jours. (This money business has been bothering me for days.) The reflexive se tracasser means to worry.
From épice, spice. The shopkeeper is l'épicier or l'épicière.

cards.de: to dissolve (a substance in liquid, or a parliament)
cards.note: Irregular: je dissous, past participle dissous, feminine dissoute. Je dissous le sucre dans l'eau chaude. (I dissolve the sugar in the hot water.) Also political: dissoudre l'Assemblée nationale.
From dur. Common phrase: être durement touché, to be hard hit.
From effrayer, to frighten. L'enfant était effrayé par le bruit de l'orage. (The child was frightened by the sound of the storm.)

cards.de: to crumple, to crease (also: to offend someone)
cards.note: Tu vas froisser ta chemise si tu la laisses dans le sac. (You'll crumple your shirt if you leave it in the bag.) Also froisser quelqu'un, to hurt someone's feelings, and se froisser un muscle, to strain a muscle.

cards.de: the younger brother, the youngest (of siblings)
cards.note: Feminine la cadette; the opposite is l'aîné. Idiom: c'est le cadet de mes soucis, that's the least of my worries.
Watch the accent grave: secrètement. Same meaning as en secret.
Feminine somptueuse. Un dîner somptueux, a lavish dinner.
Feminine fréquente. Note the adverb is fréquemment, pronounced with an a sound.
Regular -er verb. Ma grand-mère tricote un pull pour l'hiver. (My grandmother is knitting a jumper for the winter.) Related: les aiguilles à tricoter, knitting needles.

cards.de: to turn out (to be), to prove (to be)
cards.note: Almost always reflexive: il s'est avéré impossible de partir. The adjective follows directly, with no word for 'to be'.

cards.de: the gypsy (Roma, especially in Spain and southern France)
cards.note: Feminine une Gitane. Often felt to be derogatory today; the neutral term is un Rom.
Derived from la lettre. Also used informally as an intensifier, just like in English. Après la randonnée, j'étais littéralement épuisé. (After the hike, I was literally exhausted.)
Feminine une réfugiée. Common: les réfugiés politiques, demander l'asile.
Stronger than pâle, usually from fear or shock: blême de peur. Same form for both genders.
Common: travailler à une cadence infernale; marcher en cadence, to walk in step.
From gonfler, to inflate. Mon genou est encore gonflé après la chute. (My knee is still swollen after the fall.) Informally, tu es gonflé! means you've got some nerve!

cards.de: the leader, the executive (of a country or company)
cards.note: From diriger, to lead. Often in the plural: les dirigeants politiques, political leaders.
Typical uses: un animal domestique, les tâches domestiques. As a noun, un domestique is a servant.

cards.de: to desert, to abandon (a place, a post)
cards.note: Can stand alone (il a déserté) or take a direct object: déserter son poste, les touristes ont déserté la ville.
Rather formal or disapproving. Il exhibe sa richesse devant tout le monde. (He shows off his wealth in front of everyone.) Reflexive s'exhiber means to show oneself off.
Masculine. Don't confuse it with the adjective fourré, filled: un chocolat fourré.
Nouns ending in -tion and -sion are feminine: la transmission, la mission, la permission. It covers both broadcasting and the gearbox of a car.
From la vitre, the pane of glass. Common: une porte vitrée, une véranda vitrée.
Same form for both genders. Adverb: automatiquement.

cards.de: to confer, to bestow (a title, a right)
cards.note: Used as conférer qc à qn, formal register. Ce diplôme lui confère le droit d'enseigner. (This diploma gives him the right to teach.) Less often it means to confer with someone: conférer avec qn.
Il faut filtrer l'eau avant de la boire. (You have to filter the water before drinking it.) Also intransitive in the sense of leaking out: la nouvelle a filtré, the news leaked out.
Feminine crétine. As a noun, un crétin means an idiot and is clearly insulting.
Very colloquial: il a bousillé sa voiture. The neutral verbs would be casser or abîmer.
Also political (la détente internationale) and technical: la détente is the trigger of a gun.
Spelled the same in singular and plural: les remous. Figuratively it means a stir or commotion around an affair.
Only used reflexively: s'affairer autour de quelqu'un, s'affairer en cuisine.

cards.de: to win over (bring round to one's side)
cards.note: Reflexive with à: se rallier à un avis means to come round to an opinion.
Feminine la bienvenue, which also means the welcome itself: souhaiter la bienvenue à quelqu'un.
Feminine la déléguée. Le délégué de classe is the class representative; verb: déléguer qc à qn.
Mostly in the phrase avec insistance, meaning insistently. Verb: insister sur quelque chose.
It contains cercle (circle): la police a encerclé le bâtiment.
Plural: des chefs-d'œuvre. The f in chef stays silent here, pronounced che-dœuvre.
In France, la licence is also the first university degree, taken after three years.

cards.de: police (as in investigation), detective (as in novel)
cards.note: Feminine policière: une enquête policière. Un roman policier is a crime novel.
être quitte envers quelqu'un. The phrase quitte à faire qc means even if it means doing something.
Feminine la rousse, adjective roux/rousse. In cooking, le roux is the flour and butter base for sauces.

cards.de: the globe (the earth as a sphere)
cards.note: Le globe terrestre is the earth, le globe oculaire is the eyeball.
From the verb gronder, which also means to scold: gronder un enfant.
La bûche de Noël is the Christmas yule log cake. Informally, ramasser une bûche means to take a tumble.
Conjugated like employer: y becomes i, il tournoie. Often used of leaves, birds or dust.
It also means sewing as an activity: faire de la couture. Familiar from la haute couture.
The opposite is déménager (to move out, to move house). Structure: emménager dans un appartement.
From pendre (to hang): les jambes pendantes. Spelled the same as the preposition pendant (during).
réconforter qn, with no preposition. Ses mots gentils m'ont beaucoup réconforté. (His kind words comforted me a lot.) Also physical: a hot tea réconforte.
Today people normally say bébé. The loanword survives in words like baby-foot (table football).
Feminine: une collaboratrice. Historically the word also means a collaborator under the wartime occupation.
Les soldats ont pillé les magasins de la ville. (The soldiers looted the shops in the town.) Noun: le pillage. Do not confuse it with piler, to crush.
The form stays the same in the feminine. The tréma on the i shows that o and i are pronounced separately.
From la cloche (bell). As a verb, clocher informally means to be wrong: il y a quelque chose qui cloche.
Masculine, with an accent circonflexe on the o. The adjective symptomatique has no accent.

cards.de: to make holes in, to riddle with holes
cards.note: From le trou (hole). Les mites ont troué mon pull en laine. (The moths have made holes in my wool jumper.) Often used as a participle: des chaussettes trouées.
Masculine. The kitchen one is évier, the bathroom one is lavabo.
From la pitié (pity). Same form for masculine and feminine.
Conjugated like asseoir: je me rassieds or je me rassois. Common in the imperative: rasseyez-vous!

cards.de: the person you are talking to, the contact person
cards.note: Feminine: une interlocutrice. Common in business: mon interlocuteur chez le client.
The tréma on the i means o and i are pronounced separately. Note le héros has h aspiré, but l'héroïne does not.
Le pianiste a improvisé un morceau pour nous. (The pianist improvised a piece for us.) Also reflexive: s'improviser cuisinier means to suddenly take on the role of cook.

cards.de: the prefect (state's representative in a French département)
cards.note: The préfet represents the national government in a département. Feminine: la préfète.
Same form for both genders: une scientifique. As an adjective it means scientific.
From lourd (heavy). Ces livres alourdissent beaucoup mon sac. (These books make my bag much heavier.) Often figurative: alourdir la facture, to push the bill up.
Slightly formal in tone. Common phrase: éprouver de la gratitude envers qn.
Il était allongé sur le lit et lisait un roman. (He was lying on the bed reading a novel.) It can also mean elongated.
Feminine noun. Also the boarding ramp of a plane or ship, and figuratively a bridge between two areas.

cards.de: the chap, the fellow (colloquial, often pitying)
cards.note: Colloquial and old-fashioned. In exclamations: bougre d'idiot, you complete idiot.
Feminine: radieuse. Un sourire radieux, un temps radieux.
Feminine noun. In film, cascade also means a stunt, hence cascadeur, a stuntman.
Je vais farcir le poulet avec du pain et des herbes. (I'm going to stuff the chicken with bread and herbs.) Hence tomates farcies. Colloquially, se farcir qc means to put up with something.
Use passionné for people (enthusiastic) and passionnant for things.
Same form for both genders. Crème solaire is sunscreen, énergie solaire is solar energy.

cards.de: the fall, the drop (in prices, figures)
cards.note: Feminine noun. The opposite is la hausse. Common phrase: être en baisse.
A colloquial borrowing from English. More neutral: le patron.
Feminine: paysanne. As a noun, le paysan means the farmer or peasant.
From craquer, to crack or creak. Nouns ending in -ment are always masculine.
From ramer, to row. Une rame de métro also means an underground train.

cards.de: the conception, the view (the way one sees something)
cards.note: Nouns ending in -tion are feminine. It also means design and, in biology, conception.
Mon frère est distrait et oublie toujours ses clés. (My brother is absent-minded and always forgets his keys.) Feminine: distraite. It belongs to the verb distraire (to distract, to entertain).
The same noun can also mean an enclosing wall or enclosed grounds. As an adjective, enceinte means pregnant.
Adjectives ending in -ible have the same form for both genders. Often: un changement imperceptible.
Almost always reflexive: se lover dans un fauteuil. Nothing to do with the English word lover.
Personne ne peut prédire l'avenir. (Nobody can predict the future.) Conjugated like dire, but vous prédisez (not prédites). Pattern: prédire qc à qn.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine. Common phrase: en proportion de (in proportion to).
It also refers to a person's physical constitution. For someone's state or mood, use l'état instead.
Nouns ending in -sion are feminine. Compare the adjectives: compréhensif (understanding, of a person) and compréhensible (understandable).
From bête (stupid), keeping the accent circonflexe. J'ai bêtement oublié mes clés à la maison. (I stupidly forgot my keys at home.) Also common: tout bêtement (quite simply).
Sans médicaments, son état va empirer. (Without medicine, his condition will get worse.) It is intransitive and takes no se: la situation empire. The opposite is s'améliorer.
Usually plural: réduire les dépenses. The verb is dépenser de l'argent.
Feminine: sereine. Also used of weather: un ciel serein (a clear sky).
Feminine: inoffensive. It means not dangerous, not inoffensive in the sense of not causing offence.
It sounds exactly like vert, verre and vers. Un ver de terre is an earthworm.
Je ne peux pas te blâmer pour cette erreur. (I can't blame you for this mistake.) Note the accent circonflexe on the a. Pattern: blâmer qn pour qc or blâmer qn de qc.

cards.de: to direct (point in a certain direction)
cards.note: Le conseiller va t'orienter vers un autre service. (The adviser is going to direct you to another department.) The reflexive s'orienter means to find your bearings.
Feminine: paresseuse. The noun la paresse means laziness.
Informal: Quel bazar dans ta chambre! It also means a bazaar or market.
Remember the circumflex: bâche. Common: une bâche en plastique.
Le froid fait durcir le pain en une nuit. (The cold hardens the bread overnight.) An -ir verb like finir. Figuratively: durcir sa position, to take a tougher line.
escorter qn jusqu'à la sortie. The noun is une escorte.
Feminine doubles the l: culturelle. Common: un centre culturel.
Only used reflexively: se repentir de qc. Il se repent de ce qu'il a dit à sa sœur. (He repents of what he said to his sister.) Formal in tone, often with religious overtones.

cards.de: the end, the leaving (in the phrase au ... de)
cards.note: Almost only in au sortir de: au sortir de l'hiver, at the end of winter. An infinitive used as a noun.

cards.de: to fiddle with, to paw at
cards.note: Colloquial: Arrête de tripoter ton téléphone. Can also have a sexual sense.

cards.de: the head teacher, the principal (of a collège)
cards.note: Feminine: la principale. Le principal also means the main thing: C'est le principal.
Masculine and rather literary: un cri d'effroi. Related adjective: effroyable, dreadful.
Both spellings soûl and saoul are correct, pronounced [su]. Feminine: soûle.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Common: les personnes vulnérables, vulnerable people.
L'école veut équiper toutes les salles d'ordinateurs. (The school wants to equip every room with computers.) Pattern: équiper qn/qc de qc. Reflexive s'équiper means to kit yourself out.

cards.de: to locate, to track down (a position)
cards.note: localiser un appel, un téléphone. The noun is la localisation.
Le bateau a commencé à dériver vers la côte. (The boat started to drift toward the coast.) Also dériver de qc, to derive or stem from something. Related noun: la dérive, drift.
Capitalised as a noun, lower case as an adjective: un acteur britannique. Feminine: une Britannique.
Nouns ending in -ment are always masculine. Common: un claquement de porte, de doigts, de dents.

cards.de: the calm, the peace of mind
cards.note: Watch the double l. Common: en toute tranquillité, in complete peace.
Feminine fédérale, masculine plural fédéraux. L'État fédéral is the federal state.
Spelt with the ligature œ. The noun is la manœuvre, feminine.

cards.de: the manor house, the country seat
cards.note: Smaller than un château: an old noble house in the countryside.
Arrête d'éparpiller tes affaires dans le salon. (Stop scattering your things around the living room.) Reflexive s'éparpiller means to scatter, and also to spread yourself too thin.

cards.de: to step over, to climb over (something in your way)
cards.note: J'ai dû enjamber une grande flaque pour entrer. (I had to step over a big puddle to get in.) From la jambe (leg). A bridge can also enjamber a river, meaning to span it.
Very vulgar. Usually used as a noun: un enfoiré = a bastard, an arsehole.
The verb is condamner qn à qc. The m in condamner is silent.

cards.de: not at all, in no way
cards.note: Formal register. It pairs with ne: il n'est nullement surpris.
As a colour adjective it never changes: des cheveux argent. The form argenté, argentée is more common.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Être lucide means to be of sound mind or to see things clearly and soberly.
Same form for masculine and feminine, with an accent circonflexe on the a. Also used of food: une soupe infâme = a revolting soup.

cards.de: to sit on eggs, to brood (of a bird)
cards.note: La poule reste au nid pour couver ses œufs. (The hen stays in the nest to brood her eggs.) Also figurative: couver un rhume = to be coming down with a cold, couver qn = to fuss over someone.
Like all nouns ending in -té, it is feminine. The adjective is nu, nue.

cards.de: come back, returned (past participle of revenir)
cards.note: Il est revenu de vacances hier soir. (He came back from holiday last night.) Revenir forms its compound tenses with être: elle est revenue. As a noun, le revenu means income.

cards.de: the snatch, the fragment (of a conversation)
cards.note: Almost always plural: des bribes de conversation = snatches of conversation.
Used as contracter une maladie. Also of muscles: se contracter = to tighten up, to tense.
Ces gros nuages vont assombrir le ciel. (Those big clouds are going to darken the sky.) Often reflexive: le ciel s'assombrit. Figuratively too: son visage s'est assombri, his face clouded over.
Used as rincer un verre, se rincer la bouche. Spelled with ç before a and o: nous rinçons.
Formal or official register. Décréter que takes the indicative: il a décrété que c'était fini.
From carreau, a single tile. Nouns ending in -age are almost always masculine.
Je préfère miser sur le cheval numéro trois. (I'd rather bet on horse number three.) Used as miser sur qc, and figuratively: je mise sur elle, I'm counting on her.
Used as restaurer un tableau. The reflexive se restaurer means to have a bite to eat.
Une librairie sells books. A library where you borrow them is une bibliothèque.
Feminine. The verb needs à: il ressemble à son père.
Feminine form guerrière. As a noun, un guerrier means a warrior.
Masculine plural is coloniaux, like all adjectives ending in -al.
From flotter. Also used figuratively: une virgule flottante, des capitaux flottants.
Very colloquial for chambre, typical student slang.
Do not confuse it with intolérant, which describes a narrow-minded person. Common: une douleur intolérable.
From raisonner, to reason. Common phrase: suivre le raisonnement de qn.
Always feminine, even for a man: Elvis était une idole.
Feminine. Common: une tasse en porcelaine.
Feminine form virile. For grammatical or biological gender you say masculin; viril is about the impression given.
Ends in -e for both genders. Rester inerte means to lie there without moving.
Pronounced roughly as in English, [dʒaz]. Common: un concert de jazz.
The opposite is sucré. Colloquially it also means pricey: la facture est salée.
Le prof doit évaluer nos exposés cette semaine. (The teacher has to assess our presentations this week.) Pattern: évaluer qc à, to value something at a given amount.
Written with a hyphen, like après-demain (the day after tomorrow). Je l'ai vue avant-hier au marché. (I saw her the day before yesterday at the market.)
Dans le film, ils veulent flinguer le témoin. (In the film, they want to gun down the witness.) Slang, from le flingue (gun). The neutral verbs are abattre or tuer.
A diminutive of la cuve. Also the toilet bowl: la cuvette des toilettes.
Feminine form porteuse. Typical: un mur porteur. As a noun, le porteur is a porter.
Cette injustice va révolter tout le village. (This injustice will outrage the whole village.) Cela me révolte means that outrages me. Reflexive se révolter contre qn/qc means to rebel.
From poser. Common phrases: une voix posée, un garçon posé. Don't confuse it with pausé.
Usually plural: les égouts, the sewer system. Don't confuse it with le goût (taste).
As an adjective, commode means handy or convenient; il n'est pas commode means he is difficult to deal with.
From la pitié (pity). Usually negative: un résultat pitoyable.
Le feutre also means felt as a material and a felt hat. Un feutre noir = a black marker.
Rather formal or literary. In everyday speech people say étoile or planète.

cards.de: to mark the boundaries of (an area)
cards.note: Je vais me borner à répondre à ta question. (I'll limit myself to answering your question.) Very often reflexive like this: se borner à faire qc. On its own, borner means to mark the boundaries of an area.
Colloquial: les carottes sont cuites = it's all over, the game is up.
The matching verb is scier (to saw). Don't confuse it with ski.
Typical phrase: passer à l'offensive = to go on the attack. The adjective is offensif, offensive.
Mon choix est arrêté, je partirai lundi. (My mind is made up, I'll leave on Monday.) Also des idées arrêtées = fixed opinions. As a noun, un arrêté is an official order.
Verb: ravitailler qn en qc = to supply someone with something.
Usually plural: avoir des préjugés contre qn = to be prejudiced against someone.
Les machines vont damer la piste ce soir. (The machines are going to pack down the ski run tonight.) Une piste damée = a groomed ski run. Idiom: damer le pion à qn = to outdo someone.
Un air détaché = an indifferent look. Careful: des pièces détachées are spare parts.
Masculine despite the -e ending. La télévision par satellite = satellite TV.

Le bruit des travaux peut perturber les élèves pendant l'examen. [The noise from the building work can disrupt the pupils during the exam.] Être perturbé means to be unsettled, and trafic perturbé means disrupted traffic.
Les oiseaux aiment se percher sur ce vieux mur. [Birds like to perch on this old wall.] Usually se percher sur qc; perché also means high up, as in un village perché.
The final c is pronounced. Solide comme un roc = rock solid. A single rock you can climb is rather le rocher.
The final s stays silent: [taji]. Typical in forest and hunting descriptions: se cacher dans les taillis.
Used as a colour adjective it never changes: des rubans cerise. The tree is le cerisier.
The past participle of accomplir. Common in un musicien accompli and le fait accompli.
Accent shifts like préférer: je digère, nous digérons. Figuratively: je n'ai pas digéré son refus, I never got over his refusal.
Direct object for chairing: présider une réunion. With à when you oversee something: présider à une cérémonie.
Un chien égaré dort devant notre porte. [A stray dog is sleeping in front of our door.] It comes from s'égarer, to lose one's way, and un regard égaré is a wild, distraught look.
Masculine plural anormaux, feminine anormale. Don't mix it up with anonyme.
Le soleil est éblouissant ce matin. [The sun is dazzling this morning.] From éblouir, to dazzle; it also works for people, as in une beauté éblouissante.
Le souci commence à le miner. [Worry is starting to eat away at him.] It also has the literal sense of mining a piece of ground.
From mourir. As a noun un mourant is a dying person; d'une voix mourante means in a fading voice.
Feminine: à l'aurore means at daybreak. Aurore boréale is the northern lights.
Tu peux ajuster le siège à ta taille. [You can adjust the seat to your height.] The pattern is ajuster qc à qc, and it is also used for aiming: ajuster sa cible.
Lower case as an adjective: un couteau suisse. Capitalised for the person: un Suisse, une Suissesse.
The feminine doubles the l: irréelle. Une scène irréelle.

cards.de: the colleague (fellow member of a profession, e.g. doctor, lawyer)
cards.note: More formal than collègue and only used between members of the same profession. The feminine is une consœur.
Il n'arrête pas de marmonner dans sa barbe. [He keeps muttering under his breath.] It sounds grumpy, as in marmonner des excuses; murmurer is the neutral option.
Accent circonflexe, as in prêtre. Prêcher dans le désert means to preach to deaf ears.
Also used of the sea and of sleep: une mer agitée, une nuit agitée. The verb agiter means to shake.
From mitrailler, to fire on with a machine gun. The bigger weapon is la mitrailleuse, the machine gun.
Notre hôtel est bien placé, juste à côté de la gare. [Our hotel is well situated, right next to the station.] From the verb placer, and often found as bien placé or mal placé.
Feminine, despite ending in -e after a vowel. Useful phrase: être en extase devant qc, to be in raptures over something.

cards.de: to get someone drunk (also: to annoy someone)
cards.note: Ses amis ont essayé de le saouler à la fête. [His friends tried to get him drunk at the party.] Two spellings are accepted, saouler and soûler; colloquially, tu me saoules means you're getting on my nerves.
Almost always reflexive: s'aventurer dans la forêt. Don't confuse it with oser, to dare to do something.
Une cure de désintoxication is a detox or rehab programme. Careful: the healing itself is la guérison.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine. The verb is provoquer qn.

cards.de: carrying (in: to be in good health)
cards.note: Used almost only in the set phrase être bien portant, to be in good health.
Masculine: le baptême. The p is silent, so it sounds like [ba-tem]. Verb: baptiser.
Les journaux adorent déformer les faits. [Newspapers love to twist the facts.] The literal sense works too: la chaleur déforme le plastique.
The feminine form is la gérante. From the verb gérer, to manage or run.
Part of the motto liberté, égalité, fraternité. In sport, être à égalité means to be level or tied.

cards.de: to supply, to feed (with food, electricity, water)
cards.note: Alimenter qc en électricité. Also figurative: alimenter la discussion, to fuel the discussion.

cards.de: the editorial team (also: the writing of a text)
cards.note: At school it also means an essay. Verb: rédiger, to write or draft.
Masculine. Set phrase: créer un précédent, to set a precedent. As an adjective it means previous.
Always plural and feminine: toutes mes condoléances.
It stays invariable after a colour word: des yeux bleu foncé. The opposite is clair.
Une rue animée is a busy street. Un dessin animé is a cartoon.

cards.de: to grow (to increase, to get bigger)
cards.note: Les prix continuent de croître cette année. [Prices keep rising this year.] It is more formal than grandir and often used for figures; the past participle crû takes an accent to keep it apart from cru (raw).

cards.de: mounted (fixed on or fitted onto something)
cards.note: L'appareil photo est monté sur un trépied. [The camera is mounted on a tripod.] Construction: monté sur qc; it is also used for riding, as in un policier monté.
A collective noun with no ordinary plural; bestiaux serves as the plural.
Construction: se cramponner à qc/qn. Figuratively: se cramponner à un espoir, to cling to a hope.
The ending -ique stays the same in both genders. Very common: les produits chimiques.
All nouns ending in -tion are feminine. Un parc d'attractions is a theme park.
Colloquial clipping of cinéma, masculine. On va au ciné?

cards.de: the scheme, the trick (colloquial, often a bit shady)
cards.note: Colloquial and slightly negative: il a trouvé une combine. Do not confuse it with la combinaison (combination, overall).
The related adjective is paresseux, paresseuse (lazy).
Ils vont reconstruire le pont l'année prochaine. [They are going to rebuild the bridge next year.] Conjugated like construire: je reconstruis, participle reconstruit.

cards.de: to flop down (sink exhausted into an armchair)
cards.note: Almost always reflexive: s'affaler dans un fauteuil, s'affaler sur le canapé. Fairly colloquial.
French ends in -e where English has -a. Common phrase: faire de la propagande.

cards.de: the worry (a concern on your mind)
cards.note: Often plural: ses préoccupations quotidiennes. The verb is se préoccuper de qc.
Pronounced like mante, the h is silent. Thé à la menthe, sirop de menthe.
Masculine. It also exists as an adjective: rituel, rituelle.
Feminine. Do not mix it up with anecdotique, which means trivial or incidental. Raconter une anecdote.
The p stays silent: [skyl-tyr]. Same in sculpteur and sculpter.

r- plus habiller, with a silent h: je me rhabille. The opposite is se déshabiller. Example: Après l'examen, le patient s'est rhabillé en vitesse. (After the examination, the patient got dressed again quickly.)

cards.de: to flinch, to start (shudder with fright)
cards.note: Follows finir with irregular forms: je tressaille, nous tressaillons. Often tressaillir de joie, tressaillir de peur.
Feminine noun. Set phrase: monter en croupe, to get up behind someone on a horse.

cards.de: to beat up (give someone a hiding)
cards.note: Trois types ont essayé de le tabasser dans la rue. [Three guys tried to beat him up in the street.] Colloquial, so keep it for friends; se faire tabasser means to get beaten up.
A bit old-fashioned in France, but very common in Canada. The everyday word is le pull.
Same form for both genders. Careful: the noun une alerte means an alert or alarm.
Feminine form: insolente. Typical use: être insolent envers quelqu'un.
Masculine in French. In slang un joint also means a joint (cannabis cigarette).
Same form in singular and plural: les curieux. Feminine: la curieuse.
Same form for both genders. Common phrases: en sens inverse, à l'inverse de.
Nouns ending in -tion are always feminine. Colloquially une correction can also mean a beating.
Je suis intéressé par ce poste depuis longtemps. [I have been interested in this job for a long time.] The pattern is être intéressé par quelque chose. Careful: it can also mean self-interested.
Same form for both genders. Often heard as un résultat lamentable.
Best known from des sables mouvants, quicksand.
Feminine: la préférée. As an adjective: mon plat préféré, my favourite dish.
Irregular plural: les rivaux. Feminine: la rivale.
Cette vieille machine est difficile à mouvoir. [This old machine is hard to move.] It is formal and rare, so everyday French uses bouger; reflexive se mouvoir means to move oneself about.
Masculine. Common: le mécanisme de défense, un mécanisme de sécurité.
Tree names ending in -ier are masculine, while the fruit is feminine: une olive.
déguster un vin, des huîtres. Colloquially il a dégusté means he really took a beating.
Used for money, athletes and psychology: un transfert d'argent, le transfert d'un joueur.
Feminine cérébrale, masculine plural cérébraux. Typical: une hémorragie cérébrale.
Much more common as an adjective and very colloquial: c'est débile means that's stupid.
Formed from désespéré. Often: chercher désespérément quelque chose.
Takes à: cela me répugne, je répugne à mentir (I am loath to lie).
Set phrase: avoir les traits tirés, to look worn out. Literally the participle of tirer (to pull).
Usually plural: le jardin est envahi par les ronces. The berry itself is la mûre.
Reflexive: s'intégrer dans/à un groupe. Also intégrer une école = to be admitted to a school.
Il faut scier cette planche en deux. [We need to saw this board in two.] From la scie (the saw); colloquially, ça m'a scié means that floored me.

cards.de: to feel, to palpate (examine by touch)
cards.note: Typical at the doctor's: le médecin palpe le ventre. Unlike toucher, palper means feeling something to examine it.

Je n'ose pas contredire mon patron devant tout le monde. [I don't dare contradict my boss in front of everyone.] It takes a direct object, with no preposition, and is conjugated like dire except vous contredisez.

cards.de: to decline (politely turn down an offer)
cards.note: décliner une invitation, une offre. Also décliner son identité (to state your name) and to decline a word grammatically.
Masculine, like many animal names ending in -ier. The young is un marcassin.
dire son chapelet means to say the rosary. Figuratively: un chapelet d'injures, a string of insults.
Used for water (une eau limpide) and for texts or explanations. Same form in the masculine and feminine.
Tu devrais resserrer cette vis avant de partir. [You should tighten that screw before leaving.] Also figurative: resserrer les liens, to strengthen ties.
Don't mix it up with verre or verdure. It is a garden of fruit trees, not a vegetable patch (le potager).

cards.de: to flinch, to grumble (usually in the negative)
cards.note: Elle a tout accepté sans broncher. [She accepted everything without batting an eyelid.] You will almost only meet it in sans broncher, meaning without a murmur.

cards.de: the bunch (of grapes on the stem)
cards.note: Usually une grappe de raisin. A single grape is un grain de raisin.
Feminine nazie, plural nazis. Also used as a noun: un nazi.
un manuel scolaire is a school textbook. As an adjective, manuel means manual: travail manuel.
Normally plural: un steak avec des frites. Une frite is a single chip.
An adjective used as a noun; feminine une heureuse. Familiar from les heureux élus, the lucky chosen few.
Feminine turque, pronounced the same as the masculine form. The language: le turc.
Feminine sensuelle. Don't confuse it with sensible (sensitive) or sensé (sensible, reasonable).
Feminine une clocharde; it is colloquial and rather disparaging. The neutral terms are un SDF or une personne sans abri.
As a colour adjective it never changes: des murs orange. The fruit is une orange.
Same form for both genders. The person is un psychologue and the subject is la psychologie.
Plural originaux. As an adjective, original can also mean quirky or inventive: une idée originale.
Although curieux means curious, this adverb means strangely. It often opens a sentence: Curieusement, personne n'a répondu.
Same form in the feminine: une rebelle. Also an adjective: une mèche rebelle, an unruly lock of hair.
Vulgar, derived from chier. Feminine chiante. Milder options are ennuyeux or pénible.

cards.de: to wobble, to sway, to flicker
cards.note: Used of people and of light. La flamme de la bougie vacille dans le vent. (The candle flame flickers in the wind.)

cards.de: in a low voice, under one's breath
cards.note: The word mi-voix survives only in this set phrase: parler à mi-voix.
Same form for masculine and feminine: un spectacle grandiose, une vue grandiose.
Formed from maigre; the opposite is grossir. Il a maigri de trois kilos cet été. (He lost three kilos this summer.)
Feminine noun, usually used in the plural: des algues sur la plage.
A literary word; the adjective is voluptueux. Nouns ending in -té are always feminine.
Pronounced roughly as in English. Jouer au poker means to play poker.
Used with à: une lampe suspendue au plafond. It also means suspended in the sense of temporarily halted.
Feminine jumelle, plural jumeaux: des frères jumeaux, ma sœur jumelle. Les jumelles also means binoculars.
Conjugated like croître, past participle accru. Cette réforme devrait accroître nos revenus. (This reform should increase our income.) Often reflexive: les tensions s'accroissent.
Faire naufrage means to be shipwrecked. The survivor is un naufragé.
Feminine protectrice: une attitude protectrice. It can also sound condescending: un ton protecteur.
Typical of someone drunk or exhausted: il titubait jusqu'à la porte.
The adjective goes after the noun: une bombe atomique, l'énergie atomique.

cards.de: the hubbub, the din (of a crowd)
cards.note: An imitative word, masculine in French. Un brouhaha de voix dans la salle.

cards.de: to bristle, to make stand up (fur, hair)
cards.note: Usually reflexive: le chat se hérisse. The h is aspirated, so le hérisson (hedgehog) takes no liaison.
Opposite: majeur. As a noun, un mineur is either a minor (under 18) or a miner.
Common phrase: connaître tous les coins et recoins, to know every nook and cranny.
Opposite: instable. The noun is la stabilité.
Feminine form mate, as in une peinture mate. In chess: échec et mat.
Related to plaire, and slightly formal. Nous avons passé une soirée très plaisante. (We spent a very pleasant evening.) Often used in the negative: peu plaisant.
Un enfant prodige is a child prodigy. Don't confuse it with prodigue, meaning wasteful.
The opposite of monter. Mon frère démonte son vélo dans le garage. (My brother is taking his bike apart in the garage.) Figuratively it also means to throw someone off balance.
Un chien errant is a stray dog. The related verb is errer.
French names notes with the scale do, ré, mi, fa, sol, la, si instead of letters. Don't confuse it with the prefix mi- as in mi-temps.
Past participle of tuer. Le soldat a été tué pendant la bataille. (The soldier was killed during the battle.) Used as a noun too: les tués, those killed.
Feminine in French. Une ville de garnison is a garrison town.

cards.de: the bad one, the bad guy (person)
cards.note: The adjective used as a noun: les bons et les mauvais. Very common as an adjective too: de mauvaise humeur.
Plural: les corbeaux. Familiar from the fable Le Corbeau et le Renard.
Un mètre cube is a cubic metre. A dice for playing games is le dé.
Feminine. Related words: l'infirmier and l'infirmière, a nurse.

cards.de: to hurry, to hasten (do something eagerly)
cards.note: Only used reflexively: s'empresser de faire qc. Elle s'est empressée de répondre à mon message. (She hurried to answer my message.) It sounds slightly formal.

cards.de: the deputy (person who stands in for an office holder)
cards.note: l'adjoint au maire is the deputy mayor. The feminine form is une adjointe.
From le diable (the devil). Adjectives ending in -ique keep the same form in the masculine and the feminine.

cards.de: to simmer, to let something cook slowly
cards.note: Also used figuratively for plotting: qu'est-ce que tu mijotes? means what are you cooking up?
From nourrir (to feed). Nowadays it usually means a childminder who looks after children during the day.
Almost always reflexive: se blottir contre quelqu'un. Le chat se blottit contre moi quand il fait froid. (The cat snuggles up against me when it's cold.)
The noun is feminine: la mafia. A single mafioso is un mafieux.

cards.de: to fit out, to convert (a room or space)
cards.note: Do not confuse it with emménager (to move into a home). Nous voulons aménager le grenier en chambre. (We want to convert the attic into a bedroom.) Also used for arrangements: aménager le temps de travail.
Literally a throat support. The plural is des soutiens-gorge: only the first part takes an s.

cards.de: the sudden intrusion, the bursting in
cards.note: Mostly used in faire irruption dans une pièce, to burst into a room. Do not confuse it with éruption (an eruption).
From faible (weak). Cette longue maladie a affaibli mon grand-père. (This long illness has weakened my grandfather.) The reflexive s'affaiblir means to grow weaker.

cards.de: pilot, trial (used as an adjective, e.g. a pilot project)
cards.note: It follows the noun: un projet pilote, une classe pilote. As a noun, un pilote is a pilot or driver.
être confiant dans l'avenir means to feel confident about the future. Related to la confiance (trust).
le réservoir d'essence is the petrol tank. Figuratively you can say un réservoir de talents, a pool of talent.
la vie conjugale means married life. The masculine plural is conjugaux.
From une étincelle (a spark). Often used in des yeux étincelants, sparkling eyes.
Despite the -ile ending, this noun is masculine. Familiar from larmes de crocodile, crocodile tears.
Ce temps gris me déprime complètement. (This grey weather really depresses me.) It is also used intransitively: il déprime means he is feeling down. Very common as être déprimé.
Watch the accent: pêcher means to fish. It takes contre: pécher contre quelque chose.
The noun is feminine: la réforme. Common in the news: une réforme des retraites, a pension reform.
Feminine sotte, plural sots. It sounds rather formal or old-fashioned; everyday French uses bête.

cards.de: to spy on (to keep under surveillance)
cards.note: Takes a direct object with no preposition like the English "on". Related nouns: un espion, une espionne. Arrête d'espionner mes messages! (Stop spying on my messages!)
It appears in the standard formal letter ending: veuillez agréer mes salutations distinguées.

cards.de: to exempt (to excuse from a duty)
cards.note: The pattern is dispenser qn de qc. Le médecin l'a dispensé de sport pendant un mois. (The doctor excused him from PE for a month.)
Travailler dans le privé, as opposed to le public. Informally it can also mean a private detective.
Nouns ending in -tude are always feminine. A common phrase is dans l'incertitude, in the dark about something.
Takes a direct object: chatouiller qn. Arrête de chatouiller ton petit frère! (Stop tickling your little brother!) Despite the sound, it has nothing to do with chat.
Nouns ending in -tion are feminine. At school it also means an elective subject: prendre une option.

cards.de: the complex (group of buildings, psychological complex)
cards.note: Avoir des complexes means to have hang-ups. As an adjective, complexe means complicated.
The feminine form is identical. It works for people and things alike: une odeur tenace.
The feminine is industrielle with a double l. As a noun, un industriel is an industrialist.
Feminine radicale, plural radicaux. It often just means complete: un changement radical.

cards.de: to rivet (to join metal with rivets)
cards.note: Mostly used figuratively, in the past participle. Les enfants ont les yeux rivés sur l'écran. (The children have their eyes glued to the screen.)
The feminine is administrative. A common phrase is les démarches administratives, the official paperwork.
In everyday speech people usually say le couloir; corridor sounds slightly old-fashioned.
It originally meant timeliness, and the sense of "chance" was borrowed from English. The neutral word is une occasion.

cards.de: to curl up, to huddle up
cards.note: Only used reflexively, often se recroqueviller sur soi-même, to curl up into a ball. Example: Le chat se recroqueville près du radiateur. (The cat curls up next to the radiator.)
Répéter comme un perroquet means to parrot everything you hear.
A diminutive of roue. It also means the casino game and the dentist's drill; des patins à roulettes are roller skates.
The feminine is la gagnante. Also used as an adjective: le numéro gagnant, the winning number.
The related verb is escorter qn, to escort or accompany someone.
Se porter volontaire means to volunteer. As an adjective, volontaire means strong-willed or deliberate.
The feminine is confidentielle. It comes from la confidence, a secret told in confidence.

cards.de: the weak point (flaw or gap in a system)
cards.note: In geology it means a fault line. Sans faille means flawless or unwavering.
The adjective is modeste. A common phrase is en toute modestie, in all modesty.
The feminine is voleuse. As a noun, le voleur is the thief, and au voleur! means stop, thief!
It ends in a silent e but is still masculine. Also figurative: le tumulte de la ville.

cards.de: the audition (for a role or place)
cards.note: It also means the questioning of a witness, and the sense of hearing. Passer une audition means to audition.
The same form serves both genders. Also figurative: être très diplomatique, to be very tactful.
Plural only and feminine, with a formal ring to it. The everyday word is l'enterrement.
The opposite is un avantage. Common phrase: si vous n'y voyez pas d'inconvénient, if you have no objection.
More common in speech than quasi and means the same as presque. Le travail est quasiment terminé. (The work is pretty much finished.)
A false friend of English surname: your last name is le nom de famille.
Formed from doux. Un peu de miel adoucit le goût du citron. (A little honey softens the taste of the lemon.) Reflexive s'adoucir: le temps s'adoucit, the weather is getting milder.

cards.de: the embers (glowing coals in a fire)
cards.note: Often used in the plural: cuire sur les braises. Also des yeux de braise, burning eyes.
A borrowing from English, pronounced roughly deelur. The frenchified spelling dealeur is also accepted.
Feminine. A key collocation is l'huile d'olive, olive oil.
It also means an estate or inheritance. Common use: une succession de problèmes, a string of problems.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. In the plural, les brutalités means acts of violence.
Feminine and formal, usually with the elided article l': dans l'allégresse générale.

cards.de: to entitle, to give a title to
cards.note: Usually reflexive: le livre s'intitule... (the book is called...). Related to le titre.

cards.de: to suffocate, to be unable to breathe
cards.note: Also transitive: la fumée me suffoque. Figuratively: suffoquer de colère (to choke with rage).
Feminine anxieuse, plural anxieux. Pattern: anxieux de faire quelque chose.
The -ti- sounds like s: balbussié. Il a balbutié quelques mots avant de se taire. (He stammered a few words before falling silent.)
Plural des plates-formes, or des plateformes in the modern spelling. Also used online: une plateforme de streaming.

cards.de: the fix, the tight spot (trouble you are in)
cards.note: Almost only in être dans le pétrin (to be in a jam). Literally the trough for kneading dough (pétrir).
From aisé (easy, comfortable). On trouve aisément ce livre en librairie. (You can easily find this book in bookshops.) A little more formal than facilement.

Articule! is what you say to someone mumbling. Le professeur articule chaque mot très lentement. (The teacher pronounces each word very slowly.) Also to link parts together: articuler qc autour de qc.

cards.de: enslaved to, a slave to (dependent on something)
cards.note: Same form for both genders. Pattern: être esclave de qc, for example esclave de la mode.

cards.de: the supper (late evening meal, usual in Belgium/Quebec)
cards.note: In France the evening meal is le dîner; there le souper sounds old-fashioned or means a late meal after the theatre.
From lâche (cowardly, but also slack, loose). Nouns ending in -té are feminine.
Do not confuse it with une amande (almond). Common uses: payer une amende, une amende de 90 euros.

cards.de: the high school student (upper secondary pupil)
cards.note: Feminine: une lycéenne. The lycée covers the last three school years; before that you are a collégien.

cards.de: to link back, to attach, to assign (to connect again)
cards.note: Pattern: rattacher qc à qc. Ce village est rattaché à la commune voisine. (This village is attached to the neighbouring district.) Reflexive se rattacher à means to be connected with something.
Shortened to la récré in everyday speech. Not the same as free time in general (le loisir).
Formal register, often tirer qn de sa torpeur (to rouse someone from their stupor). The ending -eur is feminine here.

cards.de: to dishonour, to bring shame on
cards.note: From l'honneur (m), and rather formal or literary. Il pense que ce mensonge a déshonoré sa famille. (He thinks this lie brought shame on his family.)

cards.de: to illustrate, to demonstrate with an example
cards.note: Illustrer qc par un exemple. Reflexive s'illustrer means to distinguish oneself, to make a name.
The -e ending serves both genders. In everyday speech people often say de toutes les couleurs.
Slang for la main, as in serrer la pogne à qn. Use la main in neutral speech.
Feminine marchande: la marine marchande (merchant navy), une galerie marchande. As a noun, un marchand is a trader or shopkeeper.
Typical of stars and lights. Ce soir, les étoiles scintillent au-dessus du lac. (Tonight the stars are twinkling above the lake.) The noun is le scintillement.
Regular -er verb. Often figurative: tisser des liens (to build relationships), une toile tissée par l'araignée.
Feminine noun. Typical use: une épidémie de grippe se propage.
Suggests embarrassed, unclear speech: il a bredouillé une excuse.
Feminine in French: prendre une aspirine (one tablet) or de l'aspirine.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. Often plural: remplir les formalités administratives.

cards.de: the team (English loanword used in French)
cards.note: A borrowing from English, masculine. L'équipe (f.) is far more common.
Feminine malsaine. Also figurative: une ambiance malsaine (an unhealthy, nasty atmosphere).
The final t is silent. Typical: rendre un verdict, le verdict tombe.

cards.de: to bounce (a ball: to bounce back)
cards.note: An -ir verb like finir. Le ballon a rebondi sur le mur et il est tombé dans le jardin. (The ball bounced off the wall and fell into the garden.) Figuratively, l'affaire rebondit means the matter takes a new turn.
Used with à: antérieur à qc (earlier than something). The opposite is postérieur.
Dorénavant, je ferai mes devoirs le soir. (From now on, I'll do my homework in the evening.) Slightly formal in tone; in everyday speech people say désormais or à partir de maintenant.

cards.de: to clear, to force (a way through)
cards.note: Almost always reflexive: se frayer un chemin à travers la foule. Also frayer avec qn, to mix with someone.
Masculine. Common collocation: se faire un chignon, to put your hair in a bun.
Feminine noun. Also used for internet: la fibre (optique), fibre optic.

cards.de: the inspector (on a train: ticket inspector)
cards.note: Feminine form: la contrôleuse. Watch the circumflex in contrôle.

cards.de: to deprive of something (used almost only as the participle dépourvu)
cards.note: The verb itself is obsolete; what survives is être dépourvu de qc, to be lacking something, and prendre qn au dépourvu, to catch someone off guard.
Irregular plural: les baux. Typical: signer un bail de trois ans.

cards.de: to pour out (tip liquid or rubbish somewhere)
cards.note: Reflexive se déverser dans means to flow into: la rivière se déverse dans la mer. Figuratively: déverser sa colère sur qn.
The l doubles like in appeler: je grommelle, nous grommelons. Common phrase: grommeler entre ses dents.
Feminine form orpheline. It also works as a noun: un orphelin, une orpheline.
As a noun, le triple means three times as much: il gagne le triple.
The general word for sheep is le mouton. La brebis galeuse is the black sheep of a family.
Past participle of libérer. It takes de: libéré de ses obligations.
Note the double m and single n, unlike English. Common: une lettre de recommandation, sur la recommandation de qn.
Short for la centrale électrique, so it is feminine. Une centrale nucléaire is a nuclear power plant.
It can also mean thoughtlessness: agir avec légèreté. Opposite: la lourdeur.
Do not confuse it with illustré, which means illustrated. Used ironically in un illustre inconnu.
Informal short form of les mathématiques and always plural: je suis bon en maths.
Plural moineaux. Colloquially un drôle de moineau means an odd character.
Slightly literary or old-fashioned. Feminine vaillante; ne pas être vaillant means to feel under the weather.
Feminine noun. Often seen on menus: crevettes roses, cocktail de crevettes.
Related noun: le consulat, the consulate. The feminine is usually la consule.
Typical uses: des pluies incessantes, un bruit incessant. Linked to the phrase sans cesse.
A feminine noun. Also used figuratively for an endless stream of people: une procession de touristes.
Masculine noun. Common: le cycle de l'eau, un cycle de conférences.
The final t is silent. Familiar from col matelot, a sailor collar.
A formal, often religious word: demander miséricorde. The adjective is miséricordieux.
Masculine despite the final e. Common uses: par contraste avec, faire contraste.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Typical: une infime partie, une quantité infime.
A colloquial English borrowing; the neutral words are un enfant or un gamin.
Feminine chanceuse, plural chanceux. From la chance; for happy in the sense of glad, use heureux.
Spelled with ç before a and o: nous amorçons, j'amorçais. Le gouvernement amorce une réforme de l'école. (The government is initiating a school reform.) It also means to bait a hook.
Used as contaminer qn/qc, être contaminé par un virus. L'eau de la rivière a contaminé tout le village. (The river water contaminated the whole village.) The noun is la contamination.
All words ending in -isme are masculine. The person is un communiste.
No accent and feminine: sa cote de popularité monte. Don't confuse it with la côte (rib, coast) or le côté (side).
A regular -er verb from le sel. N'oublie pas de saler les pâtes avant de les cuire. (Don't forget to salt the pasta before cooking it.) Colloquially, une addition salée is a bill that stings.
Feminine une pionnière. Typical: un pionnier de l'informatique.
From la goutte (drop). Un chat de gouttière is a plain moggy with no pedigree.

cards.de: unawareness (used in the phrase: without someone's knowledge)
cards.note: Found almost only in à l'insu de qn, meaning without that person knowing. The opposite is au su de qn.
The final p is silent. Sirop contre la toux is cough syrup.
Feminine ingrate. It also means unrewarding: une tâche ingrate is a thankless task.
Nouns ending in -ie are feminine. La petite bourgeoisie is the lower middle class.
Feminine battante: sous une pluie battante, in driving rain. As a noun, un battant is a door leaf or a real fighter.
Built as compenser qc par qc. Il compense son manque d'expérience par beaucoup de travail. (He makes up for his lack of experience with a lot of work.) Pour compenser means to make up for it.

cards.de: to tumble down (fall down the stairs)
cards.note: Colloquial. Mon petit frère a dégringolé dans l'escalier ce matin. (My little brother tumbled down the stairs this morning.) Also used for prices: les prix dégringolent, prices are plummeting.

cards.de: the fortnight (period of about fifteen days)
cards.note: Une quinzaine de jours is the usual way to say a fortnight. With de it can also mean about fifteen of something.
Same form for masculine and feminine. The related noun is l'érotisme.
Takes a direct object. Les travaux entravent la circulation dans le centre-ville. (The roadworks are hindering traffic in the city centre.) The noun une entrave means an obstacle or a shackle.
Feminine form lourde. Il fait lourd means the weather is muggy, and un poids lourd is a lorry.
Une parcelle de terrain is a piece of land. Figuratively: une parcelle de vérité, a grain of truth.
Masculine plural fondamentaux, feminine fondamentale. C'est fondamental means it is absolutely essential.
The psy is pronounced psi with both letters audible, unlike English. The short form la psy is colloquial.
Here ch sounds like sh. La chirurgie esthétique is cosmetic surgery.
Always feminine. It means a light hunting or sporting rifle; a heavy military rifle is le fusil.
Usually used with an article: servir dans l'infanterie. A foot soldier is un fantassin.
A regular -er verb. Si tu inverses les deux chiffres, tu obtiens le bon résultat. (If you reverse the two digits, you get the right answer.) inverser les rôles means to swap roles.
Il a raclé la casserole pour enlever le fond brûlé. (He scraped the pan to get the burnt bits off.) se racler la gorge means to clear your throat, a very common phrase.
Same form for both genders. Also used of amounts: une somme respectable, a sizeable sum.
bulletin scolaire is a school report. Also le bulletin météo, the weather forecast, and le bulletin de vote, the ballot paper.

Literally to take out of the nest (nid). J'ai déniché une vieille lampe au marché pour dix euros. (I unearthed an old lamp at the market for ten euros.) Colloquially used for finding a bargain: dénicher une perle.
Masculine, like almost all words ending in -age. From the verb nettoyer, to clean.

cards.de: to officiate (to perform a ceremony or duty)
cards.note: A verb from church language, often used jokingly: il officie en cuisine. It looks identical to un officier, an officer.

cards.de: to relight, to switch back on
cards.note: The prefix re- shows repetition: allumer, to light or switch on, gives rallumer la lumière.
Feminine une artisane. Figuratively: l'artisan de la victoire, the architect of the victory.
Feminine une coureuse. As an adjective or noun, coureur can also mean a womaniser.

cards.de: the equal (a person of equal standing)
cards.note: Plural égaux, feminine une égale. Phrase: traiter qn d'égal à égal, to treat someone as an equal.
Also figurative: son sourire m'a désarmé. The prefix dés- reverses armer.
Masculine, and note the double n. Say chercher un mot dans le dictionnaire.
Don't confuse it with le genre, meaning type or kind. The daughter-in-law is la belle-fille.
Same form for both genders, only the article changes: une compatriote.
Feminine form experte. The usual construction is être expert en informatique.

cards.de: the stone, the pit (of a fruit, e.g. a cherry stone)
cards.note: Plural: les noyaux. Also means the nucleus of a cell and, figuratively, the hard core of a group.

cards.de: successful, well done (of an event or dish)
cards.note: From the verb réussir. Common: une soirée réussie, un plat très réussi.

cards.de: to deign, to condescend (to do something)
cards.note: Formal and often ironic: daigner faire qc, with no preposition. Il n'a pas daigné répondre.

cards.de: big (as an adverb: to think big, to open wide)
cards.note: Used as an adverb it stays invariable: voir grand, ouvrir grand la fenêtre.

cards.de: to suppress, to put down (a revolt, a feeling)
cards.note: réprimer une révolte, réprimer un sourire. The related noun is la répression.
favoriser qn/qc takes a direct object, with no preposition. Cette loi favorise les petites entreprises. (This law promotes small businesses.) It can also mean to give someone preferential treatment.
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. Also used of severity: la dureté d'un regard.
Careful: la couturière is a dressmaker, not a designer. For a woman designer you say une grande couturière.
grignoter qc, or with no object: j'ai envie de grignoter. Figuratively it means to gain ground bit by bit.
Feminine noun. Common collocation: pratiquer une autopsie.
Same form for both genders. La voûte céleste means the vault of heaven.
Used as différer de qc/qn. Mon opinion diffère un peu de la tienne. (My opinion differs a little from yours.) The same verb also means to postpone: différer une décision.

cards.de: the gendarmerie (police force in rural areas)
cards.note: It covers areas outside the big cities, where the force is called la police instead. An individual officer is un gendarme.
Nothing to do with rheumatism, despite the look of the word. Say attraper un rhume or j'ai un rhume.
From sec, sèche. Also figurative: la sécheresse d'un ton.
Plural: les sérails. Figuratively it means a closed circle of power: élevé dans le sérail.
Plural only, and masculine. Both parts take the plural ending: mes grands-parents.
Note the article: avoir la grippe. The idiom prendre qn en grippe means to take a dislike to someone.
Literally the impermeable one, from perméable. In everyday speech people often shorten it to un imper.

cards.de: coming from, descended from (a family, a background)
cards.note: Almost always used with de: être issu d'une famille modeste. Feminine form: issue.

cards.de: the circle of people around someone
cards.note: From entourer, to surround. It covers family, friends and acquaintances: dans son entourage proche.

cards.de: the strapping fellow, the burly chap
cards.note: Colloquial and usually friendly in tone: un grand gaillard de deux mètres.

cards.de: to swing back and forth, to oscillate
cards.note: Also used figuratively: les prix oscillent entre 10 et 15 euros.
A school term: il a redoublé sa troisième. Followed by de it means to redouble: redoubler d'efforts.
Formal and rare today. The plural aïeux means ancestors, while aïeuls means grandparents.
Colloquial: ça m'épate. Set phrase: épater la galerie, to show off.
Same form in masculine and feminine. Common pairings: un brouillard dense, une circulation dense.
The final c is silent: [ɛskʁo]. The related noun is une escroquerie, a scam.
Slightly formal; in daily life people say une entrée or un hall.
The opposite of nouer, to tie. Elle dénoue ses lacets avant d'entrer dans la maison. (She unties her laces before going into the house.) Figuratively, dénouer une crise means to defuse a crisis.
Feminine, like most nouns in -ie. The usual phrase is suivre une thérapie, to be in therapy.
Feminine douce, plural doux. Il fait doux means the weather is mild; en douce means secretly.
Related to la rage, fury. Mon frère adore me faire enrager devant tout le monde. (My brother loves driving me mad in front of everyone.) It is mostly found in that phrase, faire enrager quelqu'un.
Masculine plural monumentaux. Also colloquial for mistakes: une erreur monumentale.
The construction is être touché par qc. Je suis vraiment touché par votre message. (I am really moved by your message.) Also used in fencing and sport: touché! = hit!
Feminine miraculeuse. From le miracle; it really means miraculous, not just lovely.
Common phrase: faire une déposition, to give a statement.
Only used reflexively: je me suis rendormi. The prefix re- here means again.
The plural is regular, des carnavals, not carnavaux.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Typical use: une ambiance lugubre.
Feminine. Also l'écorce terrestre, the earth's crust.
Feminine noun. Notre galaxie, la Voie lactée (the Milky Way).
Feminine soyeuse. From la soie, silk: des cheveux soyeux.
Feminine cochonne. Colloquial: une histoire cochonne, a dirty joke.
Feminine hagarde. Almost always in un regard hagard, un air hagard.
Watch the spelling with emment, which is pronounced like amment. Comme je l'ai dit précédemment, la réunion est annulée. (As I said previously, the meeting is cancelled.)
Usually reflexive, and the imperative ressaisis-toi! means get a grip! Example: Il a pleuré cinq minutes, puis il s'est ressaisi. (He cried for five minutes, then he pulled himself together.)
Conjugated like vendre: je revends, il revend. Also in avoir qc à revendre, to have plenty of something.
Common: une bonne entente entre collègues. It can also mean a deal or arrangement between companies.
The h is silent, so l'honnêteté and en toute honnêteté. Nouns ending in té are feminine.
Double c and double s. Used for places and for goals alike: un rêve inaccessible.
Colloquially un torchon also means a rag or a badly written piece: ce journal est un torchon.
From the adjective distrait. Il écoutait distraitement la radio en cuisinant. (He was listening to the radio absent-mindedly while cooking.) Typical with écouter, regarder, répondre.
All French nouns ending in -tion are feminine. The related verb is méditer sur qc, to meditate on something.
Usually plural: se promener sous les arcades. Set phrase: l'arcade sourcilière, the brow ridge.
From the verb dresser. Used of animals, dressé means trained: un chien bien dressé.
Same form for both genders. The opposite is transparent, and it also works figuratively for murky situations.
Un pirate informatique is a hacker; used as an adjective it gives une radio pirate, a pirate radio station.
Feminine: formelle. It very often also means definite or categorical: un refus formel, je suis formel.
Recruter qn pour un poste. The noun le recrutement covers hiring and recruitment.
A little more elevated than bien sûr. Assurément, nous ferons tout notre possible. (Certainly, we will do everything we can.) Works alone as an emphatic reply: Assurément !

More common reflexively: se gaver de qc, to stuff yourself with something. Les enfants se sont gavés de bonbons pendant la fête. (The kids stuffed themselves with sweets during the party.) Colloquially, ça me gave means that annoys me.

cards.de: to assent (agree, often with a nod)
cards.note: It takes à: acquiescer à qc. Elle a acquiescé d'un signe de tête sans rien dire. (She nodded her assent without saying anything.) Fairly formal, common in written narration.
There is also a verb, petit-déjeuner. In Belgium and Quebec breakfast is called le déjeuner.

cards.de: the armour (a knight's suit of armour)
cards.note: Don't confuse it with une arme (weapon) or l'armée (army).
The related verb is se méfier de qn/qc, to distrust someone or something. Méfie-toi ! means Watch out!
Borrowed from English and masculine. Set phrase: en stock, in stock.
Constructions: confronter qn à or avec qc. Reflexive: se confronter à un problème.

cards.de: the wing (stage scenery area in a theatre)
cards.note: Usually plural: dans les coulisses means behind the scenes.
Feminine form: la jurée. Jurors sit in the cour d'assises.
Set phrase: avoir le trac, to have stage fright.
As an adjective it is invariable and follows the noun: la côte ouest, la façade ouest.
A neutral medical term; the related adjective is spermatique.
In the plural it is a legal term: les assises, la cour d'assises = the criminal court.
The plural is unchanged: les avant-bras.
Same form for both genders. As a noun, un exemplaire means a copy of a book or document.

cards.de: the pole (long pole, e.g. for jumping)
cards.note: le saut à la perche = pole vault. The same word also means perch, the fish.
Past participle of vouloir. Ne t'inquiète pas, ce n'était pas voulu. (Don't worry, it wasn't on purpose.) Also en temps voulu = in due time.
Used as être ravi de faire qc. Polite on meeting someone: ravi de vous rencontrer.

cards.de: the cheer of bravo (shout of applause)
cards.note: Plural des bravos = cheers. As an exclamation simply Bravo !
être décidé à faire qc = to be determined to do something. Elle est décidée à partir vivre à l'étranger. (She is determined to go and live abroad.) C'est décidé ! = It's settled!
Always with de: bénéficier d'une réduction. The verb is never reflexive. Les étudiants bénéficient d'un tarif réduit au cinéma. (Students benefit from a reduced rate at the cinema.)
It comes from la grille (grating), nothing to do with grilling. Nouns ending in -age are masculine.

cards.de: the kitty (pet name for a cat)
cards.note: Informal, much like kitty or puss in English. La minette is the feminine form; of people, minet(te) also means a preened young trendy type.
Very colloquial: rester peinard means to keep a low profile, un boulot peinard is an easy job.
The feminine is la souveraine. There is also the adjective souverain, as in un État souverain.
Provoquer qn en duel means to challenge someone to a duel. Do not confuse it with the adjective duel (dual).
The h is silent, so l'hallucination, une hallucination. Avoir des hallucinations.
Elle m'a souri tristement avant de partir. (She smiled at me sadly before leaving.) Set phrase: tristement célèbre means notorious.
Also used figuratively: avoir le blues means to feel down.

cards.de: the news flash (from a news agency)
cards.note: Related to se dépêcher (to hurry). Une dépêche de l'AFP is an agency report.
Used figuratively just as in English: un homme de ce calibre, a man of that calibre.
Abstract nouns ending in -eur are feminine. For measurements: trois mètres de largeur, three metres wide.
Usually plural: les déchets ménagers, household waste. Don't confuse it with déchéance, decline or decay.
France's smallest administrative unit, headed by the maire. Don't confuse it with the adjective commun, shared or common.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine. En toute sincérité means quite frankly.
Enrichir son vocabulaire means to build up your vocabulary. The noun is masculine despite the -e ending.
The opposite of serrer, to tighten. Ne pas desserrer les dents means not to say a word.
Often figurative: ouvrir une brèche dans qc, to open up a gap in something. Être sur la brèche means to be hard at it.

cards.de: to dispute (to challenge, to call into question)
cards.note: Used as contester qc à qn. The participle contesté means controversial. Il conteste la décision de l'arbitre. (He is disputing the referee's decision.)
From la bûche, the log. Spelled the same is the colloquial verb bûcher, to cram or swot.
Feminine form triomphante. Typical phrase: un air triomphant, a triumphant look.
Colloquial. Feminine costaude, more rarely costaud.
From l'effroi, dread. Stronger than terrible and fairly formal in tone.
Same form for both genders: une interprète. It also means performer, a singer or actor.
From the adjective lisse, smooth. Lisser ses cheveux means to straighten your hair. Elle lisse sa robe avant d'entrer. (She smooths down her dress before going in.)

cards.de: to mobilise (to rally forces or people)
cards.note: Also reflexive: se mobiliser pour une cause, to rally behind a cause.
Irregular like cueillir: j'assaille, participle assailli. Les journalistes ont commencé à assaillir le ministre de questions. (The journalists started bombarding the minister with questions.)

cards.de: the failure (person who fails at life)
cards.note: Feminine une ratée. Colloquial and derogatory, from the verb rater, to miss or fail.
Capitalised as la Renaissance for the artistic period. From renaître, to be reborn.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Figuratively: un labyrinthe administratif, a maze of red tape.
Feminine form: souveraine. As a noun, le souverain means the sovereign or ruler.
From le poil, body hair. As a noun, le poilu refers to a French soldier of the First World War.
The form is the same for both genders. Common: un point stratégique, une position stratégique.

cards.de: to terrify (to fill someone with fear)
cards.note: Construction: terrifier qn. The participle terrifié is used far more often than the verb itself. Ce film a terrifié mon petit frère. (That film terrified my little brother.)
For the height of an object, use la hauteur instead. Typical: à une altitude de 3000 mètres, prendre de l'altitude.

cards.de: the rolling (low rumble, roll of a drum)
cards.note: un roulement de tambour is a drum roll. Quite separately, travailler par roulement means to work in shifts.
The final s belongs to the word, so singular and plural look identical. Common: un abus de confiance, l'abus d'alcool.
More formal and more vague than la peur, which is fear of something specific. Adjective: anxieux, anxieuse.
Pronounced [stɛk]. un steak haché is a burger patty or beef patty.
Feminine form: puérile. It sounds formal and disapproving; everyday French prefers enfantin.
Ma question était purement théorique. (My question was purely theoretical.) Set phrase: purement et simplement, meaning quite simply or flatly.
La devise de la France est Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité. In the plural, les devises means foreign currencies.
Feminine form: inhumaine. The prefix in- negates humain, just as in- does in English.
Feminine form: la mécanicienne. Colloquially shortened to le mécano.

cards.de: to ripple (to undulate, move in waves)
cards.note: Related to une onde, a wave. Des cheveux ondulés means wavy hair. Le blé ondule doucement dans le vent. (The wheat ripples gently in the wind.)
From bavarder (to chat). Often used in the plural: assez de bavardages!

cards.de: the nursery (day care for babies and toddlers)
cards.note: The same word also means a Nativity scene. For older children it is l'école maternelle.
Typical: on ne peut pas attendre indéfiniment. Do not confuse it with infiniment (infinitely, extremely).
Nouns ending in -té are always feminine. Adjective: timide (shy).
Always reflexive: s'abstenir de qc or de faire qc. In elections it means to abstain from voting. Je préfère m'abstenir de tout commentaire. (I prefer to refrain from any comment.)

cards.de: to stamp, to put postage on (a letter)
cards.note: It also means to set free: affranchir un esclave. Reflexively, s'affranchir de qc means to free yourself from something. J'ai oublié d'affranchir la lettre avant de la poster. (I forgot to stamp the letter before posting it.)
The feminine form is menteuse. Used as a noun, un menteur / une menteuse means a liar.
This word is feminine in French. Common combinations: une omelette au fromage, une omelette aux champignons.
Usually used as faire de la plongée. La plongée sous-marine is scuba diving.
Il a poliment refusé notre invitation. (He politely declined our invitation.) Formed from poli, since adjectives ending in -i add -ment directly, with no feminine e.
Very common as un communiqué de presse, a press release.
Used transitively, impatienter qn means to make someone impatient. Les clients commencent à s'impatienter devant la caisse. (The customers are starting to grow impatient at the till.)
A borrowing from English. In military usage the usual word is le char (d'assaut).
It also covers interpreting between languages and a performance of a piece. Related noun: un interprète.
In the plural, les parasites also means static or interference on radio or TV.
It also means the sprocket on a bike. Idiom: avoir pignon sur rue, to be well established or respected.

cards.de: to infiltrate (plant someone inside a group)
cards.note: Reflexively, s'infiltrer dans qc means to get inside or seep in, including water. La police a réussi à infiltrer le réseau. (The police managed to infiltrate the network.)

cards.de: to dive back in, to plunge in again
cards.note: Usually replonger dans qc. Informally it can also mean to relapse, for example into drug use. Après les vacances, il a replongé dans le travail. (After the holidays, he plunged back into work.)
Example: Ma cheville a enflé. In everyday speech you will often hear gonfler instead.
Rather literary in tone, typically une frêle silhouette. The masculine and feminine forms are identical.

cards.de: the roadstead (sheltered anchorage in a harbour)
cards.note: Worth remembering the phrase tomber en rade: informally, to break down or be stranded.
Rare as an adjective: il est très artiste. For artistic in the sense of relating to art, use artistique.
It appears almost only in the fixed phrase metteur en scène. For film, le réalisateur is also used.
In everyday use, Je suis navré simply means I'm very sorry. Je suis navré, mais la salle est déjà complète. (I'm very sorry, but the room is already full.)
Works for materials (stiff) and for people or rules (strict). The form does not change in the feminine.
Common in une jupe ample (a full skirt) or un geste ample (a sweeping gesture). It describes generous width, not size in general.

cards.de: to doze off, to nod off
cards.note: Usually reflexive: il s'est assoupi devant la télé. Transitive assoupir means to lull or to dull.
Slangy version of perdre: j'ai paumé mes clés. Se paumer means to get lost.
Adjectives ending in -ique stay the same in the feminine: une plante exotique.
Feminine: la bien-aimée. It sounds formal or literary; in everyday speech people say mon chéri.
Feminine: vigoureuse. The related noun is la vigueur, strength.
The ending -âtre on colours adds a negative, unattractive tone; compare jaunâtre and rougeâtre.

cards.de: the leaf, the panel (of a double door)
cards.note: Une porte à deux battants is a double door. Used of a person, un battant means a fighter or go-getter.
The e shifts to è when stressed: je décèle, nous décelons. Often used about faults or illnesses. Le médecin a décelé un problème au cœur. (The doctor detected a heart problem.)
Nouns ending in -té are almost always feminine. In the plural, les variétés can also mean light entertainment or variety shows.
With an object, bouder qn means to give someone the cold shoulder. The noun is la bouderie. Mon fils boude dans sa chambre depuis une heure. (My son has been sulking in his room for an hour.)
The feminine une entraîneuse is now used in sport, but it used to mean a bar hostess. The verb is entraîner, to train or coach.
Unusual plural in -als: des chantiers navals, not navaux.
Feminine: scandaleuse. The ending -eux always becomes -euse in the feminine.
It is masculine and refers to the shell or the shellfish. The edible mussel is la moule.
Le train est arrivé relativement tôt ce matin. (The train arrived relatively early this morning.) Also used as relativement à quelque chose, meaning with regard to something.
Present participle of fumer. Une soupe fumante is a steaming bowl of soup.
Feminine: une habituée. As an adjective: être habitué à quelque chose, to be used to something.
Feminine, like almost all nouns ending in -tion. The verb is citer, to quote.

cards.de: the deposit (security payment, e.g. for a flat)
cards.note: Feminine. Verser une caution means to pay a deposit; se porter caution means to stand surety for someone.
Feminine: charnelle. From la chair, flesh, and it sounds formal or literary.
Masculine, plural flashs. It also means a news bulletin: un flash info.

An -ir verb following the finir pattern. Cette coiffure te rajeunit means that hairstyle makes you look younger. Ces lunettes la rajeunissent de dix ans. (Those glasses make her look ten years younger.)
Masculine. Do not confuse it with repaire (a hideout); perdre ses repères means to lose one's bearings.

cards.de: student (as an adjective, e.g. student life)
cards.note: Used as an adjective in la vie étudiante, student life. As a noun it is un étudiant, une étudiante.
Feminine: crasseuse. From la crasse, ingrained dirt, and stronger than sale.
Conjugated like conduire. Déduire qc de qc means to infer something from something. De son silence, j'en déduis qu'il n'est pas d'accord. (From his silence, I deduce that he doesn't agree.)
Feminine: respectueuse. It takes de: être respectueux de quelque chose.

cards.de: the sphere (geometric shape, also a domain)
cards.note: Feminine. Figuratively: la sphère privée, the private sphere.
As a fraction it is masculine: trois cinquièmes. At school, la cinquième is a year group.
Le crime organisé is organised crime. Of a person: il est très organisé.
The feminine form is identical. Common phrase: laisser quelqu'un perplexe, to leave someone baffled.
Feminine une épicière. The shop is l'épicerie, where you buy basic foodstuffs.
The form stays the same in the feminine: une coutume barbare. It also works as a noun: un barbare.
The pattern is doter qn/qc de qc. Often passive: la salle est dotée d'un écran.
