cards.de: Give me your phone number, please.
cards.fr: ___ ton numéro de téléphone, s'il te plaît.
cards.note: In the affirmative imperative the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen, and me becomes moi.
devenir, like venir and revenir, takes être. The participle adds an e with a feminine subject.
naître and mourir form the passé composé with être. A woman writes je suis née.

cards.de: How many books did you read this summer?
cards.fr: Combien de livres as-tu ___ cet été ?
cards.note: combien de livres is the direct object and comes before the verb, so the participle agrees: lus (masculine plural). This agreement is common in questions with combien de and quel.
Passive in the passé composé: avoir + été + participle. The participle agrees with the subject, hence construite with la maison.

cards.de: He was bitten by a dog.
cards.note: se faire + infinitive says that something happened to someone. The participle fait never changes here.
In the passive only être is conjugated; the participle agrees with the subject in gender and number.
s'en aller follows aller, with the reflexive pronoun and en added: nous nous en allons, vous vous en allez, ils s'en vont.

cards.de: Suddenly someone knocked at the door.
cards.note: Markers like soudain or tout à coup signal a single completed event, which calls for the passé composé.
The plus-que-parfait is used after si for an unreal past. Verbs of movement like venir form it with être, and the participle agrees.
The conditionnel présent goes in the main clause after si + imparfait. pouvoir has the irregular stem pourr- plus imparfait endings.

cards.de: You have to do your homework.
cards.fr: Il faut que tu ___ tes devoirs.
cards.note: il faut que always takes the subjonctif. faire uses the stem fass-: que je fasse, que tu fasses.
savoir is irregular: que je sache, que tu saches, que nous sachions.
The conditionnel stem is pourr-: je pourrais, tu pourrais, nous pourrions. Don't confuse it with je pouvais (imparfait).
Conditionnel passé: avoir in the conditionnel plus dû. English "should have known" comes out as dû savoir, with the second verb in the infinitive.
se souvenir de qc. English remembers something with no preposition, but French always needs de.
commencer à faire qc is the normal pattern. commencer de also exists but sounds formal.
décider de faire qc. But se décider à faire qc means to finally make up your mind.

cards.de: I call my brother every Sunday.
cards.fr: Je téléphone ___ mon frère chaque dimanche.
cards.note: téléphoner à qn, even though English calls someone with no preposition. Only appeler qn works without one.
essayer de faire qc. Contrast it with réussir à faire qc, which takes à.

cards.de: My daughter helps me prepare the meal.
cards.fr: Ma fille m'aide ___ préparer le repas.
cards.note: aider qn à faire qc. The person is a direct object, and the following infinitive needs à.

English says "they got married" with no reflexive pronoun and no agreement, but French reflexive verbs always take être in the passé composé and the participle agrees with the subject: ils se sont mariés, elles se sont mariées.

cards.de: Give me a spoonful of sugar, please.
cards.fr: Donne-moi une cuillère ___ sucre, s'il te plaît.
cards.note: Quantities and contents take de. By contrast, une cuillère à soupe or à café names the type of spoon.

cards.de: My sister is studying in Germany.
cards.fr: Ma sœur fait ses études ___ Allemagne.
cards.note: Feminine country names, the ones ending in -e, take en: en Allemagne, en Espagne, en Italie.

cards.de: He lived in Iran for two years.
cards.fr: Il a vécu deux ans ___ Iran.
cards.note: Masculine countries beginning with a vowel still take en: en Iran, en Irak, en Israël.

cards.de: Are you coming to my place tonight?
cards.note: chez is followed by a stressed pronoun: chez moi, chez toi, chez nous, chez eux.

cards.de: On the plane you are not allowed to make phone calls.
cards.fr: ___ l'avion, on ne peut pas téléphoner.
cards.note: For being inside a vehicle, use dans plus the article: dans l'avion, dans le métro. En avion would instead mean travelling by plane.

cards.de: The train leaves in an hour.
cards.note: dans plus a time expression always points to a future moment once that time has passed. For the length of time something takes, use en une heure.
afin que requires the subjonctif: Je vous envoie le plan afin que vous puissiez nous trouver. pouvoir is irregular: puisse, puisses, puisse, puissions, puissiez, puissent.
The stem is irregular: devr-. je devrais means "I should" and is the polite way to give advice.
The -e ending serves both genders. Common uses: un animal sauvage, une grève sauvage, le camping sauvage.
The masculine and feminine forms are identical. As a noun: un aveugle, a blind man.
The reflexive se noyer means to drown yourself, as in accidentally. The identical noun le noyer is the walnut tree.
Pronounced [statü], with the final -e silent. Don't mix it up with statut, meaning status.
It already ends in -e, so the masculine and feminine forms are identical: un art moderne, une ville moderne.
The masculine plural is irregular: brutaux. The adverb is brutalement.
A little more formal than calmer. S'apaiser means to die down (a storm, an argument).
The feminine is amère. Used for taste and for feelings alike: un souvenir amer.
Masculine plural: internationaux; feminine: internationale.
jouer aux dés means to play dice. A dé à coudre is a thimble.
Invariable, even in the plural: des robes sexy. Informal.
Feminine illégale, masculine plural illégaux. The opposite is légal.
Formal, common in news reports: périr dans un incendie. Conjugated like finir.
One form for both genders. It is also the grammatical term for neuter: le genre neutre.
It takes à: parallèle à qc. Only one accent, on the second e.
Common uses: atténuer la douleur, atténuer les effets. Reflexive s'atténuer means to subside.

cards.de: to succumb (to give in, to yield)
cards.note: Always followed by à: succomber à la tentation. It also means to die of something: succomber à ses blessures.
ralentir follows the finir pattern and adds -iss- in the plural: nous ralentissons, vous ralentissez, ils ralentissent.
The participle is ralenti and it takes avoir. It stays unchanged because there is no preceding object.

cards.de: My brother is thirty years old.
cards.note: English has only one word "year", but French uses an for counting (deux ans, trente ans) and année for a stretch of time you experience (une bonne année, toute l'année). Note also that age uses avoir, not être.
In the future tense prendre drops the e of the infinitive: nous prendrons une décision demain.
poser un lapin à qn means to stand someone up, to not show up for a meeting.

cards.fr: Cette montre coûte les ___ de la tête.
cards.note: Coûter les yeux de la tête means to be very expensive. The plural yeux is fixed here, never l'œil.

cards.de: In November I often feel down.
cards.fr: En novembre, j'___ souvent le cafard.
cards.note: This idiom always uses avoir, never être. Être le cafard does not exist.

cards.hint: Je ne crois pas que tu ... le cafard.
cards.note: ne pas croire que triggers the subjonctif: Je ne crois pas que tu aies le cafard.

cards.de: There is nobody in the hall.
cards.fr: Il n'y ___ personne dans la salle.
cards.note: Il y a contains the verb avoir, so there is no accent. Compare il y avait.

cards.de: When he comes in, everyone goes quiet.
cards.fr: ___ il entre, tout le monde se tait.
cards.note: Nothing is elided here, but a liaison appears: the d of quand sounds like a t, so quand il sounds like kan-til.

cards.de: The ceremony takes place on the eleventh of November.
cards.fr: La cérémonie a lieu ___ onze novembre.
cards.note: There is no elision before onze, oui, huit or un as a number: le onze, le oui, le huit.

cards.de: He comes from Germany and works in Lyon.
cards.fr: Il vient ___ et travaille à Lyon.
cards.note: De becomes d' before a vowel or silent h: d'Allemagne, d'accord, d'hiver. After et, by contrast, there is never a liaison.
Masculine: le soleil. Note the weather phrase il y a du soleil, literally there is some sun.

cards.de: the cup (trophy or dish), also a haircut
cards.note: Feminine. Do not confuse it with le coupé, a masculine word for a type of car.
Masculine: il cherche un emploi. It also appears in emploi du temps, which means timetable, not use of time.
Feminine, even though the English approach looks identical and neutral: une nouvelle approche du problème.
Feminine: la paupière, with the -ière ending you also see in la lumière and la rivière. Fermer les paupières means to close one's eyes.
Always feminine in French, even about a man: il est une star du cinéma. For a star in the sky you need une étoile instead.
Masculine: du pain et du beurre. Remember le beurre but la crème, which go together at the table but not in gender.

cards.de: the bowl (round cup, for example for milky coffee)
cards.note: Masculine: un bol de café. Informally, avoir du bol means to be lucky.
Every noun ending in -tion is feminine, so la section. It also means a branch of an organisation: la section locale du parti.

cards.de: a piece of rubbish, waste (also used of a vile person)
cards.note: Feminine, like other nouns in -ure: la voiture, la nature, la peinture. Usually plural: sortir les ordures.
Masculine: une mine de charbon. Most nouns in -on are masculine, which helps here.
Feminine: avoir mauvaise haleine means to have bad breath, and hors d'haleine means out of breath.
Masculine. With instruments French uses jouer de: jouer du violon, not jouer le violon.

cards.de: the seed (single grain of a plant)
cards.note: Feminine: semer des graines means to sow seeds. Do not confuse it with le grain, a grain of sand or of wheat.
Nouns ending in -ment are masculine: la crise du logement, the housing crisis.
Masculine: ouvrir or fermer le robinet. Nouns in -et are almost all masculine.

cards.de: the edge of the wood (forest edge)
cards.note: Feminine, like most nouns in -ière: à la lisière du bois. For the edge of a table you need le bord.
Masculine: il a caché son embarras. The idiom avoir l'embarras du choix means to have too many good options.
Nouns in -age are usually masculine. Despite chanter, it has nothing to do with singing: faire du chantage à quelqu'un means to blackmail someone.
Feminine like all -tion nouns: un prix de consolation is a consolation prize.

cards.de: the furrow (line cut in a field, groove)
cards.note: Masculine: le sillon, like le wagon, le poumon, le talon. Creuser un sillon works for ploughing and also for leaving one's mark.
After a negation, du, de la, des and un, une all become de. Exception with être: Ce n'est pas du café.

cards.de: I would like some water, please.
cards.note: Before a vowel or a silent h, du and de la become de l'. The partitive article marks an unspecified quantity.

cards.de: At the weekend he does sport.
cards.note: With faire plus an activity French uses the partitive article: faire du sport, faire de la musique, faire des études. English uses no article at all here.

cards.de: She has a lot of patience with the children.
cards.fr: Elle a beaucoup ___ patience avec les enfants.
cards.note: After quantity words like beaucoup, peu, trop and assez you only ever use de, never du, de la or des.
After aimer, adorer, détester and préférer French uses the definite article, because you mean the thing in general. The partitive only fits an actual quantity, as in manger du chocolat.
In the negative, une voiture becomes de voiture. So un and une disappear just like du, de la and des.

cards.de: That isn't wine, it's grape juice.
cards.fr: Ce n'est pas ___ vin, c'est du jus de raisin.
cards.note: After ne pas être the article stays, because you are correcting a statement rather than denying a quantity. So Ce n'est pas du vin, not pas de vin.
La plupart is the big exception among quantity words and takes de plus the article, so des or du. Beaucoup, by contrast, takes de alone.

cards.de: You have to be lucky to win the lottery. (literally: to have luck)
cards.fr: Il faut ___ pour gagner au loto.
cards.note: Many set phrases with avoir keep the partitive article: avoir de la chance, avoir du courage, avoir de la patience. In a sentence, avoir is conjugated.

cards.de: You can call me, any time at all.
cards.note: n'importe quand stresses that it really doesn't matter when. For a vague "some day" in the future, un jour is the natural choice.

cards.de: Do you want to drink something else?
cards.note: "Something else" is simply autre chose, with no quelque and no de. With an adjective you add de: autre chose de plus léger.

cards.de: We have dinner at eight o'clock.
cards.note: Verbs in -ger keep the e before endings with o or a, so that the g stays soft: nous mangeons, je mangeais.
The past participle of devoir is dû with a circumflex, which keeps it apart from the article du.

cards.task: Put into the past: Il a dit que ...
cards.answer: Il a dit qu'il viendrait demain.
cards.note: After a main verb in the past, the futur shifts to the conditionnel. This use is called the futur du passé.
avant que takes the subjonctif, while après que takes the indicative. The form of pleuvoir is qu'il pleuve.
avant que + subjonctif. A stylistic ne often appears with it: avant que tu ne partes, and it is not a negation.
il faut becomes il faudrait in the conditionnel, meaning "one ought to" or "we should". To advise one person directly, tu devrais works better.
The verb is dépendre de qc, so the preposition is de, not "on". de + le contracts to du.

cards.de: She has been playing the piano for ten years.
cards.fr: Elle joue ___ piano depuis dix ans.
cards.note: Instruments take jouer de, while sports and games take jouer à. de + le contracts to du.

cards.de: I come from Portugal, but I live in Switzerland.
cards.answer: Je viens du Portugal, mais j'habite en Suisse.
accept: Je viens du Portugal mais j'habite en Suisse.
cards.note: For origin, use de with feminine countries (de France), du with masculine ones (du Portugal) and des in the plural (des États-Unis).
With masculine country names, de + le contracts to du: du Maroc, du Portugal, du Japon.

cards.de: She likes neither fish nor meat.
cards.answer: Elle n'aime ni le poisson ni la viande.
cards.note: ni … ni replaces the partitive du/de la, but the definite article stays. The ne is obligatory.
After a negation, du, de la and des all become de or d'. Only after être does the article stay: ce n'est pas du vin.
After ne … plus, a noun takes only de, never du or de la.

cards.fr: Il est sept heures et demie du soir.
cards.note: In everyday speech you count to twelve and add du matin, de l'après-midi or du soir. Officially you count to 24 and drop et quart, et demie and moins.

cards.de: The museum is open from Tuesday to Sunday.
cards.answer: Le musée est ouvert du mardi au dimanche.
accept: Le musée est ouvert du mardi jusqu'au dimanche.
cards.note: For spans of days, French keeps the article: du mardi au dimanche. Same idea with clock times: de 9 h à 18 h.
les rayons du soleil, les rayons X. In a shop, le rayon means the department or the shelf.
avoir du talent means to be talented. The final t is silent.
Masculine. faire du bruit means to make noise, and un bruit can be a single sound.
Masculine noun. Figuratively: le démon du jeu, a gambling addiction.
Masculine despite the -e ending. Common phrase: faire du charme à qn, to charm someone.

cards.de: to spread out, to spread (butter etc.)
cards.note: étaler du beurre sur le pain. Colloquially s'étaler means to stretch out or to fall flat.
The same word means a mountain pass: le col du Grand-Saint-Bernard. Don't confuse it with le cou, the neck.
avoir du chagrin means to be sad, and un chagrin d'amour is heartbreak.
Traditionally masculine only; today you also hear une autrice or une auteure. Also l'auteur du crime, the perpetrator.
More common in speech than la bicyclette. You say faire du vélo or aller à vélo.

cards.de: to point (aim a finger at something)
cards.note: pointer qc du doigt, to point at something with your finger. At work, pointer also means to clock in.
Irregular plural: les signaux. Donner le signal du départ, to give the starting signal.
Also la plante du pied, the sole of the foot. The verb is planter, to plant.
From le sang, blood. Je saigne du nez depuis ce matin. (My nose has been bleeding since this morning.)

cards.de: the set, the scenery (in a theatre)
cards.note: Masculine. Also used figuratively: cela fait partie du décor means it is just part of the scenery.
Playing an instrument uses jouer de: jouer du piano.
Feminine. Du sucre en poudre is caster sugar, and la poudre also means face powder.
From serrer (to squeeze, to tighten). Also figurative: un emploi du temps serré is a tight schedule.
Related to une enveloppe, an envelope. Common pattern: envelopper qc dans du papier.
Also in faire du stop, meaning to hitchhike.
It also means growing or cultivation: la culture du blé. The matching adjective is culturel.
faire du sport means to do sport. Used as an adjective it never changes: une tenue sport, casual sporty clothes.
Weather takes il y a: il y a du brouillard. Figuratively, être dans le brouillard means to be clueless.
Usually plural: les vivants et les morts. Also remember du vivant de qn, during someone's lifetime.
Masculine and borrowed straight from English. A rock star is une star du rock.
Regular plural: des clous. Le clou du spectacle is the highlight of the show.
Formal, often biblical. Known phrase: dormir du sommeil du juste, to sleep the sleep of the just.
Also a display case in a museum. Faire du lèche-vitrines means to go window shopping.

cards.de: the stage (of a journey or a process)
cards.note: Feminine, so une étape. Common uses: procéder par étapes, la première étape du Tour.
Almost only found in set phrases: contre son gré (against one's will), de bon gré (willingly), au gré du vent.
The accent shifts: je lèche, nous léchons. Le chien adore lécher les mains des enfants. (The dog loves licking the children's hands.) Faire du lèche-vitrines means to go window shopping.
Conjugated like vendre: je fends, il fend. Typical use: fendre du bois, to chop wood.
Spelled with a circumflex like goût, taste. Structure: éprouver du dégoût pour quelque chose.
Do not confuse it with la pause, a break, as the two sound almost identical. It also means laying or fitting: la pose du carrelage.

cards.de: to date, to go back (to a period)
cards.note: dater de qc means to date from a period: cette église date du XIIe siècle.
Spelled with two n, as in English. voir le bout du tunnel means to see light at the end of the tunnel.
Built from régulier, using the è of the feminine form régulière. Je fais régulièrement du sport.
A dish in sauce: du poulet en sauce. Colloquially, mettre la sauce means to step on the gas.
The animal is le crabe. Common: un cancer du poumon, avoir le cancer.
Derived from jeter: un jet d'eau. The phrase du premier jet means at the first attempt.
Used with de: la moitié du gâteau. As an adverb, à moitié means half: la bouteille est à moitié vide.
Feminine noun. Often par ironie du sort, by a cruel irony of fate.
Masculine noun. Typical use: le divan du psychanalyste.
Almost only in set phrases: faire tout son possible means to do one's utmost, and dans la mesure du possible means as far as possible.
Always provenir de qc. Conjugated like venir and takes être in the passé composé: ces mots proviennent du latin.
It also means crochet work: faire du crochet. In boxing, un crochet is a hook.
The s is pronounced: [as]. Also figurative: un as du volant, an ace behind the wheel.
From le fusil, rifle. Les soldats ont menacé de fusiller les prisonniers. (The soldiers threatened to shoot the prisoners.) Figuratively, fusiller qn du regard means to glare daggers at someone.
Construction: avoir la nostalgie de qc. Homesickness is usually le mal du pays instead.
Masculine noun. People usually ask Tu as du feu? rather than asking for a briquet.

cards.de: north, northern (used with a noun, e.g. north coast)
cards.note: Invariable: la côte nord, la façade nord. As a noun, le Nord, l'Amérique du Nord.
Feminine noun. Idiom: tirer son épingle du jeu, to get out of a situation cleverly.
Past participle of peindre, feminine peinte. Mon frère a peint sa chambre en bleu. (My brother painted his room blue.) Du papier peint means wallpaper.
To ski is faire du ski, and a ski resort is une station de ski.
avoir du cran means to have guts, rather colloquial. Originally a notch: monter d'un cran, to go up a level.
Languages are masculine in French: le latin, le grec. Faire du latin means to study Latin.
A verb used as a noun, so masculine: le parler du Midi. Do not mix it up with la langue.

cards.de: the decline; the distance (in time or emotional)
cards.note: Prendre du recul means to step back and get some perspective. From reculer, to move backwards.
The opposite is licencier. L'entreprise va embaucher dix personnes cet été. (The company is going to hire ten people this summer.)
Often plural: les contours du visage, the contours of the face. The verb contourner means to go around something.
It also means the plot of a film or novel: l'intrigue du film. The noun is feminine.

cards.de: the stripe (rank braid on a uniform)
cards.note: The noun is masculine: un galon. Prendre du galon means to be promoted.
Feminine, like most nouns ending in -ide. A famous one: la pyramide du Louvre.
Usually plural: les vibrations du moteur. The matching verb is vibrer.
Colloquial: avoir du culot means to have some nerve. Do not confuse it with cul.
Je chausse du 42 means I take a size 42 shoe. Il faut chausser des bottes pour marcher dans la boue. (You need to put on boots to walk in the mud.) Reflexive se chausser, to put one's shoes on.

cards.de: the setting (of the sun: le ... du soleil)
cards.note: An infinitive used as a noun, so masculine. Also l'heure du coucher, bedtime; the opposite is le lever du soleil.
Masculine despite the -ice ending. Signer un armistice; l'Armistice du 11 novembre 1918.
éloigné de qc: une maison éloignée du centre. Un parent éloigné is a distant relative.
Faire du tricot means to knit. The verb is tricoter.
Faire du zèle means to be overzealous and usually sounds critical.
It sounds exactly like signe (sign). A well known phrase: le chant du cygne, the swan song.

cards.de: the heart of the matter (in: entrer dans le ... du sujet)
cards.note: The noun survives mainly in set phrases: entrer dans le vif du sujet, piquer au vif, une plaie à vif.
Avoir du tempérament means to be full of spirit. Acheter à tempérament, by contrast, means to buy in instalments.
A borrowing from English, but pronounced "lidœr". Also used in sport and business: le leader du marché.

cards.de: the rising (of the sun or moon)
cards.note: Le lever du soleil. It also means getting up in the morning: au lever, dès le lever.

cards.de: the middle of nowhere (small village, dismissive)
cards.note: Colloquial, borrowed from Arabic. Typical phrases: un bled perdu, au fin fond du bled.
In film and theatre it also means the cast: la distribution du film.
Common: le port du masque est obligatoire. The adverb is obligatoirement.
Payer une rançon. Figuratively: la rançon du succès, the price of success.
Administrative language: un décret du gouvernement. The verb décréter means to decree or order.
The y becomes i before a silent ending: je broie. Je broie les grains de café chaque matin. (I grind the coffee beans every morning.) Idiom: broyer du noir, to be down in the dumps.
Typical: du saumon fumé. Nous avons mangé du saumon fumé pour Noël. (We ate smoked salmon at Christmas.) With glass or glasses, fumé means tinted.
Usually plural: les écailles du poisson. The verb écailler means to scale a fish.
The diaeresis splits the syllables: ma-is, unlike mais (but). Partitive article: du maïs.
Always followed by de: une odeur émane de la cuisine. Also figurative: le pouvoir émane du peuple.
French takes a decision rather than making one: prendre une décision. Likewise prendre rendez-vous, prendre du poids (to put on weight).
